title: [4A] Implement EngineResources broker: OnceLock host, runtime presets, thread envelope, two-phase memory ledger
description:
## Background
`EngineResources` is the one process-owned asupersync runtime/admission/memory domain behind the synchronous `NlpEngine` facade. Every engine holds a lease to it; creating ten engines must not create ten runtimes, ten compute teams, or ten independent memory promises. It exists because the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops with KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, q 3072→6144; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) is memory- and thread-hungry: bf16 KV alone is 176 KiB/token/sequence (180,224 B), so uncoordinated engines would oversubscribe RAM and threads instantly. This bead productionizes the G0 broker/seam probes into the real broker.

## Contract
- One documented `OnceLock` broker. `NlpEngine::builder()` snapshots configuration and acquires `Arc<EngineResources>` from it. Advanced callers may install the single process host before the first engine; arbitrary public construction of a second host is not exposed (tests get an isolated `cfg(test)` constructor).
- First initialization fixes the resource-host fields: runtime preset, effective compute-team width, blocking width, aggregate process memory ceiling. A later incompatible request fails with a **field-level `ResourceConfigConflict`** naming the exact conflicting field and both values — never a second host, never silent inheritance.
- **Runtime presets are the pinned builder's actual profiles** — `current_thread` (one-shot CLI / deterministic-first), `low_latency` (interactive generate), `high_throughput` (batch daemon) — selected per entrypoint and recorded in telemetry. A preset name is NEVER a safe thread count: at the pin `high_throughput()` doubles the deterministic default runtime-worker count, so pairing it blindly with a physical-core-wide scoped team oversubscribes small hosts. Record the preset's concrete builder values; override worker/blocking counts when the measured envelope requires it.
- **Aggregate runnable-thread envelope**: admission proves (runtime workers + maximum concurrently running blocking coordinators + every scoped CPU child + separately ratified long-lived service/helper threads) against the host policy; the full thread inventory is emitted in `robot health` and performance receipts.
- **Two-phase memory reservations as tracked obligations**: reserve before allocation → commit after success → abort on failure/cancel. Obligation-leak response policy: panic in lab/CI, logged-with-escalation in production, never silently ignored. The ledger charges weights, KV/pages, activation/logit scratch, prefix/grammar caches, job buffers, and staging across every engine lease; exact same-digest read-only weights/native packing may share one `Arc`, every other copy is charged. Per-engine local ceilings are allowed; the process ceiling is authoritative. No engine lock is held while waiting for admission.
- **Deadline monitoring** with meaningful checkpoint messages surfaced through `robot health`; **bounded cancel-attribution depth** so cancellation storms stay cheap.
- **`ReentrantCall` typed error**: a public sync call made from one of the same runtime's worker threads fails fast — never nested `block_on`. Async hosts call the blocking API from their own blocking boundary.
- Production `EngineResources` configures a real blocking-pool handle; the pinned `spawn_blocking` inline fallback is lab/test behavior and never a production success path (executor-heartbeat proof required).
- Post-wrapper-cancel pool closures stay registered in an actual-completion set retaining their admission/memory/output guards until their latch fires; region/process shutdown treats that set as outstanding drain work.
- Config layering: code defaults, then the CLI's one-time `FNLP_*` snapshot; the library never reads ambient environment.
- Resource discovery: logical parallelism may use `std::thread::available_parallelism`; cgroup/job-object-aware memory, topology, NUMA, QoS need a ratified safe FrankenSuite surface or the feature refuses/requires an explicit budget. Never reach through to `libc`/`sysinfo`.

## Constraints
G1>G2 profile-scoped; deny-not-forbid unsafe (this module is safe code); no Rayon anywhere in the release graph; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; leaf kernels never spawn; asupersync doctrine: never enter the seam under an engine lock, never nest a runtime, preserve `Outcome::{Ok,Err,Cancelled,Panicked}` to the policy boundary; budgets are typed meet-composed children with reserved cleanup budget, never ambient milliseconds.

## Evidence / gates
Capacity-certificate gauntlet artifact: one process admission domain, aggregate thread inventory, no Rayon/global-pool escape, obligation accounting. Racing first-install / compatible-reuse / field-level-conflict tests green. `many_docs_without_deadlock` watchdog. Recorded in the invariant-gate suite and the performance receipts (thread inventory section).

## Tests
Unit: field-by-field `ResourceConfigConflict` (each fixed field mismatched individually, error names the field); compatible reuse returns the same host; `ReentrantCall` from a worker thread; `cfg(test)` isolated constructor. Property: reservation ledger never exceeds the ceiling under random reserve/commit/abort interleavings; abort always restores the exact prior balance; obligation leak in lab panics with the leaked obligation id logged. Concurrency: racing first initialization from N threads yields exactly one host; asupersync Lab scenarios assert quiescence and zero leaked obligations, seed-bound chaos over cancel/budget storms with crashpack replay on failure. E2E: `robot health` emits the full thread inventory + preset name + concrete worker values as versioned JSON. Detailed logging: every reserve/commit/abort carries obligation id, bytes, engine lease id; conflicts log both requested and fixed values. Model-gated tests report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- A_G0_SEAM (cross-epic): the G0 spawn_blocking/scoped_cpu seam probe ratifies pool-handle, heartbeat, and latch semantics this broker enforces.
- A_G0_CENSUS (cross-epic): the OQ-35 census fixes preset worker values, budget units, and obligation leak-response semantics at the pin.
- A_SCAFFOLD (cross-epic): crate, error map, robot skeleton, and CI must exist to host the broker.

title: [P2] Implement .fnlpq canonical writer: prelude, hash-checked header, ordered sections, digest taxonomy
description:
## Background
The `.fnlpq` container is franken_nlp's only on-disk weight format: a self-describing, versioned strict envelope (adapted from the `.focrq` pattern, newly specified — no ABI-by-analogy). This bead builds the canonical WRITER: fixed prelude, hash-checked canonical header JSON, ordered binary sections, and the normative digest taxonomy. Everything downstream (reader, converter, packager, pull, activation, receipts) consumes these exact bytes, so canonical serialization is specified here, not delegated to an unspecified map serializer. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Fixed prelude (canonical little-endian): magic `b"FNLPQ\0\0\x01"` (exactly 8 bytes, a valid Rust byte literal); `format_version: u32`; `required_flags: u32`; `header_len: u64`; `section_count: u64`; `tensor_count: u64`; `file_len: u64`; `header_sha256: [u8; 32]`.
- Canonical header JSON (exactly `header_len` bytes, hash-checked before parsing): `arch_target` ∈ {Generic, Aarch64Sdot, Aarch64I8mm, X86Vnni256, X86Vnni512, X86Avx2}; ordered `source_files: [{name, len, sha256}]`; `recipe_id` / `converter_commit` / `census_digest` / `source_root_sha256`; `logical_model_sha256` / `packing_set_sha256` / `license_bundle_sha256`; `sections: [{id, kind, absolute_offset, len, sha256, alignment}]`; `tensors: [{name, dtype, shape, data_section, data_offset, data_len, scale_section?, scale_offset?, scale_len?, group_size?, tier?}]`; optional `bit_allocation_table`; `packing_manifest`; frozen relevant config fields.
- Ordered binary sections: tensor bytes + scale/row-sum metadata; **exact `tokenizer.model` bytes** (2,782,298 bytes, SHA-256 fb41d04798b714520a9b075727b0226538b7330254299062742c50ec8374bc36); exact tokenizer/config/template source bytes; the Apache-2.0 + attribution + modification-notice bundle. Required tokenizer/template/license section kinds occur exactly once.
- Canonical bytes are specified: fixed Rust structs plus sorted lists/`BTreeMap` only where the schema declares key order; duplicate keys/names reject; one pinned UTF-8 escape form for JSON strings; integers/digests carry authoritative numeric/byte values; floating scales live in binary sections with fixed IEEE-bit encoding, never JSON numbers; NaN/Inf reject; padding is zero; the writer never accepts arbitrary `serde_json::Value` maps. Authority-bearing names/ids/filenames restricted to explicit printable-ASCII grammars (tensor dotted names, lowercase recipe ids, portable single-component filenames) — no Unicode-normalization dependency. JSON never carries raw binary blobs; no base64 dependency. Every section has one kind, absolute range, alignment, digest; only explicitly declared zero-filled alignment gaps.
- **Digest taxonomy (normative; the ambiguous bare name `semantic_digest` is RETIRED):** `source_root_sha256` (canonical ordered source-file identity) · `logical_model_sha256` (domain-framed over ordered logical tensor `(name, dtype, shape, canonical logical bytes)` records plus exact materialized config/tokenizer/template identities — the packing-independent computational model identity) · `packing_set_sha256` (exact representation/layout set) · `license_bundle_sha256` (exact license/attribution/notice section bytes; legal identity, never model semantics) · `fnlpq_file_sha256` (exact complete file bytes) · `release_manifest_sha256` (exact canonical manifest bytes). Native repacking changes `fnlpq_file_sha256`/`packing_set_sha256` without changing `logical_model_sha256`; a notice-only correction changes `license_bundle_sha256` and file/release identities without claiming a new computational model.
- High-precision tensors (embed_tokens, all norms by default) stored BF16 verbatim — byte-identical round-trip; f16 narrowing is lossy and only ever a ledgered divergence.
- Scale context: 4,169,800,704 params = 8,339,601,408 bf16 payload bytes; logits f32 row is 664,576 B at vocab 166,144.

## Constraints
- Direct non-suite deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2; serde/serde_json sit only at the approved metadata layer above the binary envelope. No Rayon anywhere in the release graph; the writer is serial/streaming. No unsafe island needed (deny-not-forbid policy stands). G1>G2: canonical bytes are exact before any speed work. License settled Apache-2.0; the embedded bundle carries factual attribution only ("Model origin: Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B; author attribution per the pinned model card: Nanbeige Team; source revision f56ec5a…; Apache-2.0; transformed by franken_nlp under recipe `<id>`") — never a synthesized copyright notice the upstream never published.

## Evidence / gates
- **Golden serializer fixture** covering EVERY field, escape, key order, alignment gap, and section kind — committed, byte-compared in CI; any canonical-bytes change is a deliberate format_version event.
- §5.4 canonical-serialization gate (writer half): identical logical input → identical bytes across runs and hosts.
- Digest-taxonomy fixtures: repack flips `fnlpq_file_sha256`/`packing_set_sha256` with `logical_model_sha256` invariant; notice-only edit flips `license_bundle_sha256` + file identity only. Close cites the fixture paths and green CI run.

## Tests
- Unit: prelude field encoding/offsets (little-endian), header hash over exactly `header_len` bytes, pinned escape form, BTreeMap key order, duplicate-key/name rejection, NaN/Inf scale rejection, zero padding, section order/alignment-gap declaration, printable-ASCII grammar rejection cases.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary valid logical models → serialize → reparse → structurally identical; flip any byte → prelude/header/section digest mismatch detected. On failure log seed, first divergent offset, and section id.
- E2E: tiny synthetic model written then re-read with DETAILED LOGGING of the full section table (id, kind, offset, len, digest) at debug level. Real-artifact write is model-gated and reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL when the 8,360,887,509-byte closure is absent.
- Named artifacts: the golden serializer suite is `tests/fnlpq_writer_golden.rs` with committed goldens under `tests/fixtures/fnlpq/golden/` (every field, escape, key order, alignment gap, and section kind; OQ-31 field-inventory ids cross-referenced); the write→read round-trip leg is driven by `scripts/e2e_convert_roundtrip.sh` (named in the round-trip gate bead), whose logs carry per-stage timestamps, per-section byte counts + digests, and expected-vs-actual pairs on any mismatch.

## Dependencies & rationale
- [P0] crate scaffold (franken_nlp-uxw): the writer lands in the scaffolded crate's module tree behind `cli_main()` and the shared error map; no code bead can precede the scaffold.
- [P-1] 201-tensor census generator (franken_nlp-7xa): the header embeds `census_digest` and the tensor table is validated against the machine-readable census; the golden serializer fixture cannot be frozen before that census identity exists.
- The envelope specification is fully inlined above; the reader (separate bead) consumes this bead's golden fixtures as its parse oracle.

title: [P2] Implement .fnlpq checked reader: prelude-first validation, u64 range caps, fuzz corpus, opt-in mmap island
description:
## Background
The `.fnlpq` READER is the hostile-input half of the format: a checked byte-range index over one owned buffer (default) or an opt-in audited mmap island. It must fail loudly and safely on malformed, truncated, or adversarial files BEFORE allocating from attacker-controlled counts — the model file is a 4+ GB download and the reader is the first code to touch it. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Prelude validation happens before ANY variable allocation:** magic `b"FNLPQ\0\0\x01"`/version/required_flags must be known; declared `file_len` must equal the actual regular-file length; `header_len` must fit a compile-time hard cap and checked `prelude_len + header_len`; `section_count`/`tensor_count` are NOT trusted until the bounded header hash (`header_sha256`) and canonical parse both succeed. Header corruption is therefore detected before allocating from attacker-controlled counts.
- Checked `u64` range arithmetic for every section/tensor against `file_len` and the actual file: no overlap with the prelude/header or each other; only explicitly declared zero-filled alignment gaps; required tokenizer/template/license section kinds occur exactly once.
- Caps cover: section count, tensor count, tensor rank, each dimension, header/config/template/tokenizer/license section size, and total mapped bytes. Unknown required flags or enum values REJECT — no "best effort" parsing of a newer format.
- Quantized tensors carry inline scales (per-out-channel int8; per-group int4 + tier metadata) with exact expected scale counts derived from shape and group size. NaN/Inf/non-positive scales, overlapping ranges, duplicate names, misalignment, and non-canonical nibble padding all reject.
- Reader = checked byte-range index over one owned buffer by DEFAULT; `FNLP_MMAP=1` opt-in mapping is an enumerated audited unsafe island (scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, never `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn`, every op in explicit `unsafe {}` with a local `// SAFETY:` proof) with separate range/lifetime/immutability tests. Only the approved serde/JSON metadata layer sits above the binary envelope.
- An arch-specific artifact never silently "falls back" to a different packing: an incompatible `arch_target` is a hard error naming the required derivation (`fnlp models derive`).
- Expected real-file scale: 4,169,800,704 params, 8,339,601,408 bf16 payload bytes in the bf16-verbatim configuration; 201 logical tensor names in the census.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no memmap2 crate — the mmap island uses the ratified suite/std surface per docs/PLATFORM_SURFACES.md or stays disabled. No Rayon in the release graph. Deny-not-forbid unsafe; the mmap island is the ONLY unsafe surface this bead may touch and a policy test rejects any unlisted island. G1>G2. Malformed input must produce typed errors mapped to documented exit codes 0–10 at the CLI boundary, never panics.

## Evidence / gates
- **Malformed-header fuzz corpus**: committed corpus + fuzz harness covering truncation at every prelude/header/section boundary, bit flips, count inflation, overlap, gap fraud, oversized dims, unknown flags, duplicate names, bad scales, wrong `file_len`. Zero panics/OOM/UB; every rejection is a typed error. Corpus and harness paths cited at close.
- Structural check gate: header/section digests permit a fast bounded structural check; the full-file bit-rot recheck is `fnlp models verify --full` (later bead) — this bead provides both range-checked entry points.
- Mmap island gate: separate range/lifetime/immutability tests green; policy test proves the island is enumerated.

## Tests
- Unit: each prelude violation class; each cap; each overlap/gap case; exactly-once section kinds; scale-count formula per dtype/shape/group_size; nibble-padding canonicality; unknown-flag rejection.
- Property/fuzz: writer-generated valid files always parse and re-serialize to identical logical content; arbitrary mutations never crash and always yield typed errors. DETAILED LOGGING: on rejection log the violated invariant, absolute offset, and section/tensor id; fuzz failures log the reproducing seed.
- E2E: owned-buffer and FNLP_MMAP=1 paths both load the golden writer fixture and produce identical logical tensors; real-model load is gated and reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL absent the artifact.
- Named artifacts: the fuzz harness is `tests/fnlpq_fuzz.rs` with its committed corpus under `tests/corpus/fnlpq/` (one file per hostile class from the OQ-31 checklist, ids preserved; every CI-found failure is committed with its reproducing seed in the filename). The harness ends each run with a machine-parseable `FUZZ_SUMMARY` line (cases run, rejects by class, zero-panic assertion).

## Dependencies & rationale
- .fnlpq canonical writer: the reader's parse oracle is the writer's golden fixture set and canonical-byte spec; building the reader first would freeze guesses.

title: [P2] Build checked safetensors range index with pre-exposure source digest verification
description:
## Background
`fnlp convert` must read two pinned safetensors shards totaling 8,339,624,720 bytes without ever trusting their headers. This bead builds the checked safetensors RANGE INDEX: a validating parser over the safetensors header + byte ranges that exposes bounded, digest-verified range reads — the production alternative to the pinned `ft-serialize::load_safetensors_from_bytes`, which copies a whole shard into owned tensor storage and therefore remains a parity/fixture baseline ONLY (its whole-blob behavior is not the converter's peak-memory contract). Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Parse and validate the safetensors JSON header of each shard: duplicate tensor names reject; dtype must be a known enum (BF16 for all 201 weight tensors at the pin); checked shape-product × dtype-size must equal the declared byte range length; offsets are monotone-checked, non-overlapping, in-bounds against the actual file length; header length field itself is cap-checked before reading.
- **Exact source digests verified BEFORE exposing any range:** `model-00001-of-00002.safetensors` = 4,973,547,960 bytes, SHA-256 09d265d5ec837bc64462796b7f8c110be9a135a55ed7a6eb5d07e0e90c976a94; `model-00002-of-00002.safetensors` = 3,366,076,760 bytes, SHA-256 31019e7870a044f44bc3f7e981f8c5ecd42d341e5ca6cfdbfd07fb95d95be389; `model.safetensors.index.json` = 16,519 bytes, SHA-256 30d8da0fa8b97abc6d9eddfd017a0cb7a649bcbd58caa57804c56c767db5c0f1. Logical tensor payload is 8,339,601,408 bytes; the 23,312-byte difference from the shard lengths is container-header metadata, not unexplained model data.
- The index resolves the safetensors index.json name→shard mapping, cross-checks it against both shard headers, and exposes `read_range(tensor, row_panel) -> &[u8]`-style bounded access: one tensor or bounded row-panel at a time, checked u64 arithmetic throughout, no whole-shard materialization required by the API shape.
- Census hook: enumerate exact `(name, dtype, shape, len)` for all tensors so the converter can diff against the §2.6 201-tensor census (MISSING / SHAPE-MISMATCH / EXTRA), including the OQ-1 tripwire (any mHC/ngram/depth/LoopSplit tensor name → design-assumption abort).

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite (`ft-serialize` may be consumed for the FIXTURE baseline only; the production range path is ours). No Rayon in the release graph; index construction and hashing are serial/streaming. No unsafe. G1>G2. Typed errors, never panics, for every malformed-header class.

## Evidence / gates
- Differential fixture gate: on small synthetic safetensors fixtures, range-index reads byte-equal the pinned `ft-serialize` whole-blob loader for every tensor — proving the range path against the audited baseline without inheriting its memory behavior.
- Hostile-header rejection suite green (see Tests). Close cites fixture paths + suite run.
- Digest-refusal gate: a wrong-digest or wrong-length shard/index refuses before any tensor parse, with the expected/actual digest pair in the error.

## Tests
- Unit: header cap, duplicate names, unknown dtype, shape-product overflow (checked mul), offset overlap/gap/out-of-bounds, index↔shard-header mismatch, wrong file length, wrong digest.
- Property/fuzz: mutated headers never panic/OOM; valid synthetic files round-trip through range reads equal to whole-blob reads. Log violated invariant + offset + tensor name on every rejection; log per-shard hash timing at debug.
- E2E (model-gated): index both real shards, verify all three digests, enumerate 201 tensors, diff against census, sum ranges to exactly 8,339,601,408 payload bytes; report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without the closure. Named artifacts: the hostile-header suite is `tests/safetensors_hostile.rs` (mutation corpus under `tests/corpus/safetensors/`); the model-gated leg runs as stage 1 of `scripts/e2e_convert_roundtrip.sh`, logging per-shard timestamps, byte counts and digests expected-vs-actual, and the census-diff verdict into that script's machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants, orchestrator wires): A_SCAFFOLD — needs the crate/CI/error-map skeleton; A_CENSUS — the 201-tensor machine-readable census supplies the expected (name, shape) table this index diffs against.
