title: [P2] Build bounded tensor-streaming converter core (fnlp convert --recipe) with peak-RSS gate
description:
## Background
`fnlp convert` is the sovereign path (G3: public pull is convenience, never a requirement): pinned HF snapshot → canonical Generic `.fnlpq`, bounded in memory, deterministic in bytes. This bead is the converter CORE: the streaming tensor pipeline, the peak-RSS contract, source-closure verification, census diff, staging/receipt/atomic-rename, and the `--recipe` CLI. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Pipeline in canonical manifest order, one tensor or bounded row-panel at a time: source range (checked safetensors range index) → checked BF16 decode → bounded f32 work panel → quantize/pack per recipe → write exact precomputed output range into the `create_new` staging file.
- **Memory contract: NEVER materialize the 8.34 GB weight shards and their ~16.7 GB f32 expansion together.** Peak converter RSS is a measured gate derived from: largest source panel + largest f32 panel + quant/packing scratch + bounded output buffer + parser metadata + margin. The formula AND its computed value are PRINTED BEFORE conversion starts and enforced as a gate during conversion.
- **Operator-facing progress + confirm:** conversion emits a per-tensor progress line to stderr (`[k/201] name shape panels bytes-written running-peak-RSS ETA`, ETA derived from processed-vs-total logical payload bytes — 8,339,601,408 at the pin); the preflight footprint block (closure bytes to read 8,360,887,509; staged output bytes; peak scratch; peak-RSS formula value; final disk) is printed first and, on an interactive TTY without `--yes`, requires an explicit y/N confirm (non-TTY/robot runs proceed without prompting and log the footprint). Robot mode mirrors progress as versioned NDJSON events under stdout-data rules. Every refusal states WHAT failed, the OBSERVED vs EXPECTED value (digest, shape, or byte count), and the NEXT command to run.
- Source-closure verification FIRST: refuse a missing or wrong-digest member of the named ten-file conversion closure (exactly 8,360,887,509 bytes at the pin) before parsing any tensor. `--source-manifest docs/truth-pack/nanbeige4.2-3b.source.json` names the closure.
- `--strict-source-dir` semantics: unrelated files in the source directory are ignored by default; strict mode rejects ALL extras; but extra safetensors shards, alternate indexes, or conflicting config/tokenizer files — anything that could alter load semantics — ALWAYS reject even without strict mode.
- WeightsManifest census diff vs the §2.6 201-tensor census: MISSING / SHAPE-MISMATCH / EXTRA → LOUD named diff, refuse to proceed. EXTRA is the OQ-1 tripwire: any mHC/ngram/depth tensor name aborts with a design-assumption error.
- Tensor remap (HF dotted → internal): `model.embed_tokens.weight`→`embed` (bf16 verbatim); `model.layers.{0..21}.input_layernorm/post_attention_layernorm.weight`→`layer[i].norm1/norm2` (bf16 verbatim, widened to f32 only in kernels); `.self_attn.{q,k,v,o}_proj.weight`→`layer[i].attn.*` (int8 stage 2b); `.mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight`→`layer[i].mlp.*` (int8 stage 2a); `model.norm.weight`→`final_norm` (bf16 verbatim); `lm_head.weight`→`lm_head` (int8 stage 2c). No biases exist (attention_bias=false; mlp_bias=false default; census has no bias tensors) — a bias tensor appearing is a loud converter error.
- **CLI is `--recipe <id>` (e.g. `nanbeige42-int8-v1`), NOT `--quant`.** Emits `--arch generic` only; native packings are separate derived caches (`fnlp models derive`) and never change the Generic digest. Reference invocation: `fnlp convert --source <dir> --source-manifest docs/truth-pack/nanbeige4.2-3b.source.json --recipe nanbeige42-int8-v1 --arch generic -o nanbeige4.2-3b.fnlpq-v1.int8.generic.fnlpq`.
- Emits a machine-readable conversion receipt: ordered source-root digest, 201-tensor census digest, converter commit, recipe, rounding/packing ids, measured peak RSS/scratch/disk, output length, output SHA-256, license identity. Then reloads the staged `.fnlpq`, reconstructs every logical tensor, runs structural/census/round-trip and kernel selftests, syncs, and atomically renames under the filesystem-transaction contract. Preflight computes PEAK (not final) free space and repeats immediately before conversion; invalid old files are quarantined with observed digest, never silently overwritten.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; the pinned ft-serialize whole-blob loader is fixture/parity baseline only, never the production memory contract. No Rayon anywhere in the release graph; conversion is serial/streaming (bounded panels, not parallel shards). No unsafe. G1>G2. Deterministic: pure function of ordered source bytes + versioned recipe (full spec in the portable-quant-v1 bead). "Optimal" is never inferred from bit width; it means cleared locked gates.

## Evidence / gates
- Peak-RSS gate: measured RSS ≤ printed formula value on the real conversion (model-gated) and on synthetic large-panel fixtures (always-on).
- Two-clean-directory determinism gate (Phase-2 exit): converting the same closure twice in independent clean directories yields identical Generic `fnlpq_file_sha256`.
- Refusal gates: missing/wrong-digest member; conflicting weight/config/tokenizer extras (with and without `--strict-source-dir`); census MISSING/SHAPE-MISMATCH/EXTRA diffs each named in the error and exit code per error.rs.

## Tests
- Unit: closure verification order (digests before tensor parse), strict/non-strict extra-file matrix (unrelated ignored; semantic-conflict always rejects), remap table completeness (201 names), panel-boundary arithmetic, staging create_new + rename, receipt field completeness.
- Property/fuzz: synthetic multi-tensor safetensors fixtures with adversarial panel sizes — output ranges never overlap, every output byte written exactly once, RSS proxy under formula.
- E2E: tiny synthetic closure converts end-to-end with DETAILED LOGGING (per-tensor: name, shape, panel count, output range, running peak RSS estimate); real-closure conversion is model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without it. The runnable driver is `scripts/e2e_convert_roundtrip.sh` (shared with the round-trip gate bead): per-stage timestamps, byte counts + digests at every verification point, expected-vs-actual on mismatch, and a machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Checked safetensors range index: supplies the only approved bounded source-read path and the census enumeration.
- .fnlpq canonical writer: the converter's output surface; staging bytes must be canonical before receipts mean anything.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SCAFFOLD — CLI/error-map/robot skeleton; A_CENSUS — the 201-tensor census digest is embedded in header + receipt.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **Source-closure verification gate.** Deliverable: refuse-first verification — a missing or wrong-digest member of the named ten-file closure (exactly 8,360,887,509 bytes at the pin, named by `--source-manifest docs/truth-pack/nanbeige4.2-3b.source.json`) refuses before parsing any tensor; `--strict-source-dir` semantics (unrelated extras ignored by default, ALL extras rejected in strict mode, semantics-altering extras — extra shards, alternate indexes, conflicting config/tokenizer — ALWAYS rejected). Test evidence: unit closure-verification order (digests before tensor parse); the strict/non-strict extra-file matrix. Next milestone assumes: only a fully verified closure ever reaches tensor parsing.
2. **Census diff + remap table.** Deliverable: WeightsManifest diff vs the §2.6 201-tensor census with LOUD named MISSING / SHAPE-MISMATCH / EXTRA refusal (EXTRA as the OQ-1 tripwire: any mHC/ngram/depth tensor name aborts with a design-assumption error); the complete HF-dotted → internal remap (embed, norm1/norm2, attn.{q,k,v,o}, mlp.{gate,up,down}, final_norm, lm_head with their bf16-verbatim vs int8-stage assignments); a bias tensor appearing is a loud converter error. Test evidence: unit remap-table completeness (201 names); refusal gates each named in the error with exit code per error.rs. Next milestone assumes: a validated, fully mapped tensor inventory drives the pipeline.
3. **Bounded streaming pipeline.** Deliverable: canonical-manifest-order processing, one tensor or bounded row-panel at a time — source range (checked safetensors range index) → checked BF16 decode → bounded f32 work panel → quantize/pack per recipe → exact precomputed output range into the `create_new` staging file. Test evidence: unit panel-boundary arithmetic; property/fuzz on synthetic multi-tensor safetensors fixtures with adversarial panel sizes — output ranges never overlap and every output byte is written exactly once. Next milestone assumes: correct bounded byte production for the RSS gate to measure.
4. **Peak-RSS formula printed + enforced.** Deliverable: the measured memory gate — formula (largest source panel + largest f32 panel + quant/packing scratch + bounded output buffer + parser metadata + margin) AND its computed value PRINTED BEFORE conversion and enforced during conversion; the 8.34 GB shards and their ~16.7 GB f32 expansion are never materialized together. Test evidence: RSS proxy under the formula on synthetic large-panel fixtures (always-on); measured RSS ≤ printed value on the real conversion (model-gated). Next milestone assumes: a memory-safe conversion run to wrap in CLI/preflight.
5. **`--recipe` CLI + preflight/quarantine.** Deliverable: the `--recipe <id>` surface (NOT `--quant`), `--arch generic` only, supporting the reference invocation; preflight computing PEAK (not final) free space, repeated immediately before conversion; invalid old files quarantined with observed digest, never silently overwritten. Test evidence: CLI-surface tests for the reference invocation; preflight and quarantine fixtures. The preflight footprint block + TTY y/N confirm (`--yes` bypass) and the per-tensor progress/ETA/running-peak-RSS stderr stream land in this milestone, with tests covering TTY, non-TTY, and robot-mode paths. Next milestone assumes: a runnable end-to-end command producing staged canonical bytes.
6. **Receipt + reload-verify + atomic activation.** Deliverable: the machine-readable conversion receipt (ordered source-root digest, 201-tensor census digest, converter commit, recipe, rounding/packing ids, measured peak RSS/scratch/disk, output length, output SHA-256, license identity); then reload of the staged `.fnlpq`, reconstruction of every logical tensor, structural/census/round-trip and kernel selftests, sync, and atomic rename under the filesystem-transaction contract. Test evidence: unit staging `create_new` + rename and receipt field completeness; tiny synthetic closure E2E with DETAILED per-tensor LOGGING (name, shape, panel count, output range, running peak-RSS estimate). Next milestone assumes: a complete self-verifying conversion whose bytes can be checked for determinism.
7. **Two-clean-directory determinism gate.** Deliverable: the Phase-2 exit evidence — converting the same closure twice in independent clean directories yields identical Generic `fnlpq_file_sha256`, establishing conversion as a pure function of ordered source bytes + versioned recipe (full spec in the portable-quant-v1 bead). Test evidence: the two-clean-directory gate run recorded; real-closure conversion model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without it.

title: [P2] Produce int8-mlp stage artifact: per-output-channel symmetric MLP quant + preregistered parity gate
description:
## Background
First of three staged IMMUTABLE int8 artifacts (int8-mlp → int8-mlp-attn → int8-all), each a separate content-addressed `.fnlpq` with its own parity gate and ledger entry. Stage 2a quantizes the bulk: the MLP gate/up/down projections, 22 layers × 3 matrices × (10752×3072) = 2,179,989,504 params ≈ 2.18 B — everything else stays BF16 verbatim (embed, all norms, attention, lm_head). The loop reuses each quantized tensor in BOTH passes, so sensitivity is joint; staging isolates where quality moves. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Recipe id `int8-mlp` under the converter's `--recipe` CLI: per-output-channel symmetric quantization (`quantize_per_output_channel_i8`), zero-point 0, one f32-derived scale per output channel stored in the artifact's scale sections with fixed IEEE-bit encoding.
- Canonical algebra: logical activations and weights are signed i8; `y[o] = sx * sw[o] * Σk(qx[k]·qw[o,k])` (no model biases exist; the notation reserves the contract). Every SIMD path must preserve this logical reduction order — this bead defines the canonical int8 scalar path that later backends are compared against.
- Overflow proof at the MLP shapes: at K=10752 (down_proj), full-domain S8×S8 ≤ 176,160,768; raw U8×S8 ≤ 350,945,280; |128·Σw| correction ≤ 176,160,768; conservative raw+correction sum 527,106,048 — all inside i32 with >4× headroom vs 2^31−1. K=3072 (gate/up) bounds are proportionally smaller; compile-time formula tests cover every model K.
- Output is a separate immutable content-addressed artifact: distinct `logical_model_sha256`, distinct `fnlpq_file_sha256`, its own conversion receipt and ledger entry. It never overwrites or mutates the bf16 or any sibling artifact.
- Quantization is deterministic per the portable-quant-v1 spec (RNE ties-to-even, negative-zero handling, NaN/Inf reject, specified clamp domain/order, no fast-math/contraction).

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon in the release graph. G1>G2 profile-scoped: this stage's fidelity claims live under `strict-quantized-vN` numerics profiles; deliberate int8 divergence from bf16 is a separate preregistered decision and never inherits a blanket BF16-token-identity claim. Raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` is banned everywhere (kernel-side rule; the artifact stores exact quantized values that make the exact AVX2 constructions possible). Measured-faster wins later; correctness artifact first.

## Evidence / gates
- **Parity gate vs a PREREGISTERED logit budget:** the int8-mlp L3 logit tolerance is registered BEFORE measurement; the gate compares against the bf16 reference forward on the frozen fixture set. L4 token agreement vs bf16 is measured and LEDGERED (exact only where the recipe actually preserves it), never presumed.
- L1 same-recipe integer exactness: quantize→dequantize fixtures and scalar int8 matvec vs i64 oracle, exact.
- Ledger entry in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md-adjacent quant ledger records recipe id, budgets, measured deltas. Close cites gate run + receipt digest.

## Tests
- Unit: per-channel scale computation (absmax, zero-row behavior, RNE), zero-point-0 symmetric range use, scale count = out_features exactly (10752 for gate/up, 3072 for down), i32 bound formula tests for K ∈ {3072, 10752}.
- Property/fuzz: random f32 rows → quantize → int8 matvec vs i64 oracle exact; dequant error ≤ scale/2 per element; adversarial full-K ±127 vectors.
- E2E (model-gated): full int8-mlp conversion + parity run over frozen prompts with DETAILED LOGGING of per-layer max-abs logit delta and first token divergence position if any; SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without the closure/oracle fixtures. Runnable as `scripts/e2e_stage_parity.sh --stage int8-mlp` (one shared driver serves all three stage artifacts): per-stage timestamps, artifact digests logged at the conversion/load/parity boundaries, the per-layer delta table with preregistered-budget consumption reported expected-vs-actual, first divergence position on any miss, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` NDJSON line; prints SKIPPED_NO_MODEL naming the exact missing prerequisite.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Converter core: stage recipes execute inside the bounded streaming pipeline; no separate quantization binary exists.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_FWD — the parity gate needs the reference forward (bf16 profile) to produce comparison logits.

title: [P2] Produce int8-mlp-attn stage artifact: add q/k/v/o quant with own parity gate
description:
## Background
Second staged immutable int8 artifact. Recipe `int8-mlp-attn` adds the attention projections to the already-gated int8 MLP: q/k/v/o across 22 layers = 22 × (3072×6144 + 3072×1024 + 3072×1024 + 6144×3072) = 22 × 44,040,192 = 968,884,224 ≈ 0.97 B params quantized on top of stage 2a's 2.18 B. Embed, all norms, and lm_head remain BF16 verbatim. Staging matters because attention feeds RoPE/GQA numerics on BOTH loop passes — a quality regression here must be attributable to attention quant alone. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Recipe id `int8-mlp-attn`: per-output-channel symmetric `quantize_per_output_channel_i8`, zero-point 0, for `layer[i].attn.{q,k,v,o}` in addition to the stage-2a MLP set. Scale counts: q→6144, k→1024, v→1024, o→3072 per layer, exact.
- **Separate immutable content-addressed artifact** with its own header digests, conversion receipt, and ledger entry. ROLLBACK = activating the prior stage artifact (`fnlp models activate` on int8-mlp or bf16): a runtime environment variable can NEVER restore bf16 attention weights from an artifact that contains only quantized ones — the bytes are not in the file. Runtime switches govern only genuinely runtime choices (e.g. KV int8).
- Canonical algebra identical to stage 2a: `y[o] = sx * sw[o] * Σk(qx[k]·qw[o,k])`; K values here are 3072 (q/k/v) and 6144 (o); i32 bounds follow the K=10752 worst-case proof (S8×S8 ≤ 176,160,768 at K=10752; smaller Ks strictly tighter) with compile-time formula tests for K ∈ {3072, 6144}.
- Deterministic per portable-quant-v1 (RNE ties-even, negative-zero, NaN/Inf reject, clamp order, no fast-math/contraction).

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon in the release graph. G1>G2 profile-scoped: fidelity claims under `strict-quantized-vN`; never a blanket BF16-token-identity claim. head_dim is 128, NOT hidden/heads=64 — any scale/shape table built on 64 is a loud error (q_proj is 3072→6144 because 48 heads × 128). Immutable artifacts: no in-place upgrade of an int8-mlp file into int8-mlp-attn.

## Evidence / gates
- **Own parity gate vs its own preregistered logit budget** (registered before measurement), run against the bf16 reference forward AND against stage 2a to isolate the attention-quant delta. L4 token agreement ledgered, not presumed.
- L1 integer exactness for the attention matvecs vs i64 oracle at K ∈ {3072, 6144}.
- Rollback evidence: a test proves activating the prior artifact restores prior bytes/digests exactly, and that no env var alters which weights load. Close cites gate runs + both receipts.

## Tests
- Unit: per-layer scale-count exactness (6144/1024/1024/3072), remap completeness for the attn set, artifact-separation (distinct content addresses, no shared mutable state).
- Property/fuzz: quantize→matvec vs i64 exact on random and adversarial ±127 rows for K ∈ {3072, 6144}.
- E2E (model-gated): full int8-mlp-attn conversion; parity vs bf16 and vs int8-mlp on frozen prompts with DETAILED LOGGING (per-layer attention-output max-abs delta, logit budget consumption, divergence positions); SKIPPED_NO_MODEL otherwise. Runnable as `scripts/e2e_stage_parity.sh --stage int8-mlp-attn` (the shared three-stage driver named in the int8-mlp bead): per-stage timestamps, digests at conversion/load/parity boundaries, budget consumption expected-vs-actual, a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line, and SKIPPED_NO_MODEL naming the missing prerequisite.

## Dependencies & rationale
- int8-mlp stage artifact: staging discipline requires 2a gated before 2b exists, so attention deltas are attributable.
- hf-bf16-eager reference forward (franken_nlp-pnu, direct): the 2b parity gate compares int8-mlp-attn logits/greedy tokens against the reference forward under this stage's own preregistered budgets — the parity oracle is a direct blocker of this bead's gate, not merely inherited through 2a.

title: [P2] Produce int8-all stage artifact: quantized lm_head, row-sum correction metadata, parity gate
description:
## Background
Third and final staged immutable int8 artifact. Recipe `int8-all` adds `lm_head` (166,144 × 3072 = 510,394,368 ≈ 510 M params) to the gated int8 MLP+attention set, completing "int8-everything-quantizable" — the near-lossless correctness oracle for later int4 work (expected ≈4.7 GB with bf16 embed). lm_head is special: it is row-sliced for scoring (per-row independence must survive quantization) and it is the tensor the x86 VNNI u8×s8 route needs row-sum correction metadata for. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Recipe id `int8-all`: per-output-channel symmetric `quantize_per_output_channel_i8`, zero-point 0, adding `lm_head` (scale count exactly 166,144). Embed and all norms remain BF16 verbatim; lm_head/embedding quantization are measured, separately-published recipe stages, never silent defaults.
- **Row-sum metadata for the u8 correction:** VNNI consumes u8×s8, so x86 forms `u = qx XOR 0x80` and exactly subtracts `128·Σk qw[o,k]`; the per-output-row sums `Σk qw[o,k]` are computed at conversion time and stored in the packing/scale metadata sections so runtime kernels never re-derive them. Stored for every quantized tensor in the artifact, lm_head included.
- Overflow proof restated: at K=10752 worst case, S8×S8 ≤ 176,160,768; raw U8×S8 ≤ 350,945,280; |128·Σw| ≤ 176,160,768; conservative independent raw-plus-correction 527,106,048 < 2^31−1 (>4× headroom). lm_head K=3072 is strictly tighter; compile-time formula tests cover every model K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}.
- Per-row self-containment: per-output-channel scales make each lm_head row (row bytes + its scale + its row sum) independently loadable for §6.10 row-sliced scoring; the artifact layout must not interleave rows in a way that breaks bounded row-range reads.
- Separate immutable content-addressed artifact, own receipt/ledger entry; rollback = activate int8-mlp-attn / int8-mlp / bf16; env vars can never restore bf16 lm_head bytes absent from the file.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon in the release graph. G1>G2 profile-scoped under `strict-quantized-vN`. Raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` remains banned in every consumer; the artifact's exact values + row sums are precisely what make the exact AVX2 low-7/high-bit and widened-i16 constructions provable. Logits remain f32 (664,576 B per position at vocab 166,144) after dequant regardless of weight quant.

## Evidence / gates
- **Own parity gate vs its own preregistered logit budget** (registered before measurement) against the bf16 reference forward and vs int8-mlp-attn to isolate the lm_head delta; L4 token agreement ledgered.
- Row-sum correctness gate: for every quantized tensor, stored row sums equal an i64 recomputation exactly (full census sweep, not sampled).
- Row-slice gate: dequantized row-sliced logits ≡ full-projection logits for the same rows, exact in integer domain, bitwise in f32 assembly order.
- Close cites all three gates + receipt digest + ledger entry.

## Tests
- Unit: scale count 166,144; row-sum i64 recomputation equality; XOR-0x80 correction algebra identity `Σ(u−128)·w = Σq·w` on exhaustive small-K; row-range read arithmetic.
- Property/fuzz: random rows — u8×s8 + correction ≡ s8×s8 ≡ i64 oracle, exact, including ±127 adversarial rows at K=3072.
- E2E (model-gated): full int8-all conversion; parity + row-slice differential on frozen prompts with DETAILED LOGGING (logit budget consumption per checkpoint, row-sum verification count, first divergence if any); SKIPPED_NO_MODEL otherwise. Runnable as `scripts/e2e_stage_parity.sh --stage int8-all` (the shared three-stage driver): per-stage timestamps, digests at conversion/load/parity/row-slice boundaries, row-sum verification counts and budget consumption expected-vs-actual, a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line, and SKIPPED_NO_MODEL naming the missing prerequisite.

## Dependencies & rationale
- int8-mlp-attn stage artifact: staging discipline — lm_head delta must be attributable on top of a gated 2b.
- hf-bf16-eager reference forward (franken_nlp-pnu, direct): the 2c parity gate (including lm_head logit/argmax/token-agreement rows over the 166,144-row head) runs against the reference forward; the parity oracle is a direct blocker of this stage's own gate, not merely inherited through 2a/2b.

title: [P2] Specify portable-quant-v1 determinism + cross-OS/ISA digest gate or canonical-publisher fallback
description:
## Background
Deterministic quantization is a TARGET WITH A GATE, not a prose assumption. `portable-quant-v1` is the written determinism specification that makes the canonical Generic conversion a pure function of (ordered source-file bytes + versioned recipe), plus the cross-target CI gate that proves it — or the honest, narrower fallback when it fails. Without this, "canonical artifact" and every digest in the release chain is fiction. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
The spec document + conformance tests pin ALL of:
- BF16 decoding semantics; absolute-value/max (absmax) behavior; zero-row behavior; scale precision.
- Rounding mode: round-to-nearest, ties-to-even (RNE), exactly.
- Negative-zero handling; NaN/Inf REJECT (a NaN/Inf source weight is a hard conversion error, never a quiet clamp).
- Clamp domain AND clamp order (clamp-then-round vs round-then-clamp is specified, one way, forever for v1).
- f32 operation order with NO contraction (no FMA fusing where the spec says separate ops), no fast-math, no host-approximate conversions.
- int4 nibble order; group traversal order; serializer order; padding bytes are zero. (int4 fields are specified now so v1 does not need a v2 for Phase 5.)
- If an eval/calibration set ever enters recipe selection (AA-Q1), its license, digest, order, preprocessing, and split ids join the recipe identity.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon. The converter must implement quantization ONLY through spec-conformant scalar/checked routines; any SIMD quantization path must be bit-identical to the spec path on the full input domain or it cannot be used in conversion. G1>G2: a faster converter that changes one output byte is reverted and ledgered in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

## Evidence / gates
- **Cross-target gate:** CI converts the same fixture closure on every supported OS/ISA — at minimum ONE aarch64 host (Apple Silicon) and ONE x86-64 host — and compares the complete Generic `fnlpq_file_sha256`. Byte-identical → the portable-determinism claim holds.
- **Fallback (explicit, honest):** if full-model cross-target identity fails, release tooling designates ONE pinned canonical-publisher target; local conversion on other hosts claims semantic/quality equivalence — NOT hash identity — until the cause is removed. The narrowed claim is recorded in docs/CLAIMS.json and surfaced by `fnlp models`/docs; the failure cause gets a tracked issue.
- Phase-2 exit line: `portable-quant-v1` cross-OS/ISA Generic-digest identity (≥1 aarch64 + ≥1 x86-64) OR the documented canonical-publisher-target fallback with its narrower local-conversion claim. Close cites the CI matrix run or the fallback ADR.

## Tests
- Unit: RNE tie cases (x.5 at even/odd), negative-zero quantization, NaN/Inf rejection, clamp-order fixtures at the domain edges (±127 boundaries), zero-row scale behavior, nibble-order and padding goldens.
- Property/fuzz: random bf16 inputs quantized twice in-process → identical; spec scalar path vs any candidate vectorized path → bit-identical over full i8 domain sweeps and adversarial floats (denormals, near-tie values). Log the first differing element index, input bits, and both outputs on any mismatch.
- E2E: fixture-closure conversion digest comparison across the host matrix (CI); real-closure cross-target run is model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL where the closure is absent. The named matrix driver is `scripts/e2e_convert_determinism_matrix.sh`: runs the fixture-closure conversion per host, logs per-host `fnlpq_file_sha256` expected-vs-actual with toolchain/OS/ISA fingerprint and per-stage timestamps, and ends with a machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line (hosts, digests, identical|divergent verdict) — the artifact CI archives for the identity-or-fallback decision.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Converter core: the spec constrains and is exercised by the converter's quantize/pack stage; the gate runs the converter on fixtures.

title: [P2] Gate bf16 byte-identical round-trip and census-on-load digest verification
description:
## Background
Two load-bearing trust gates on the format itself: (1) BF16 tensors survive convert→load→re-serialize BYTE-IDENTICALLY (the bf16-not-f16 rule inherited: f16 narrowing is lossy and only ever a ledgered divergence); (2) census + logical-model digest verification runs ON LOAD, so wrong/stale/corrupt weights fail loudly BEFORE any kernel sees a pointer. Together they make "the artifact you loaded is the artifact that was gated" a checked property, not an assumption. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **BF16 round-trip gate:** for every BF16-verbatim tensor (embed_tokens 166,144×3072, all 44 layer norms, final_norm, and in the bf16 artifact everything else), convert→load→re-serialize asserts exact byte equality against the canonical source bytes. Any single differing byte fails the gate with tensor name + offset.
- **Census-on-load:** loading any `.fnlpq` verifies (a) the 201-name census — every expected (name, dtype, shape) present, nothing extra, shapes exact (e.g. q_proj 6144×3072 because head_dim 128 is EXPLICIT, never 64); (b) `logical_model_sha256` recomputed over the ordered logical tensor records + materialized config/tokenizer/template identities equals the header claim. Failure is a typed load error naming the first divergent record; NO kernel, cache, or engine handle is constructed first.
- Bounded structural fast path: header/section digests give a fast structural check on every load; the full-file bit-rot recheck stays explicit (`fnlp models verify --full`, packaged in the models-CLI bead) — this bead must make the load-time check cheap enough to be always-on (hash logical records streamed during section reads, no second full pass by default; measured and reported).
- Applies to all artifacts: bf16, int8-mlp, int8-mlp-attn, int8-all — each stage's distinct `logical_model_sha256` is what census-on-load pins.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon; hashing is serial/streaming. No unsafe (owned-buffer path); the mmap island inherits the same checks. G1>G2: load-time verification is not skippable by any env var in release builds; an explicit documented fast-load debug flag may exist only for lab builds and must be absent from release binaries.

## Evidence / gates
- §5.4 round-trip gate green: convert→load→re-serialize byte equality on synthetic fixtures (always-on) and the real closure (model-gated).
- Census/digest refusal fixtures: truncated tensor, flipped payload byte, renamed tensor, wrong-shape tensor, stale header digest — each refused before kernel construction, each with the named first divergence.
- Phase-2 exit contribution: this bead plus the reader close the "conversion-twice identity" loop by making equality checkable at the logical layer, not only whole-file SHA-256.

## Tests
- Unit: bf16 byte-identity on single-tensor fixtures; hash-domain framing (name/dtype/shape/bytes record encoding) golden; first-divergence reporting.
- Property/fuzz: random valid artifacts — load→re-serialize identical; single-byte payload mutations always caught by logical or section digest (no silent pass), with the catching layer logged.
- E2E: full synthetic-model round-trip with DETAILED LOGGING (per-tensor byte counts, streamed-hash timing, verification verdict); real-model round-trip model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. The named runnable driver is `scripts/e2e_convert_roundtrip.sh`: synthetic closure → convert → load → re-serialize → byte-compare, then the census-on-load refusal legs (truncated / flipped-byte / renamed / wrong-shape / stale-digest). Its logs carry per-stage ISO-8601 timestamps, per-tensor byte counts and digests at every verification point, expected-vs-actual pairs on any mismatch (tensor name + first divergent offset), and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` NDJSON line (stages, verdicts, bytes, wall times); the real-closure leg logs SKIPPED_NO_MODEL with the missing prerequisite named.

## Dependencies & rationale
- .fnlpq canonical writer: re-serialization requires canonical bytes to compare against.
- .fnlpq reader: load path + range checks are the substrate the census/digest verification runs on.

title: [P2] Build release packager: fixed 1,957,046,720-byte parts, receipts, draft-release runbook
description:
## Background
GitHub Releases cap asset sizes, so the canonical Generic `.fnlpq` ships as deterministic fixed-size chunks plus receipts. This bead builds `fnlp release package-model` / `fnlp release verify-model-package` (maintainer-facing CLI) and the draft-release runbook. It deliberately copies FrankenOCR's proven invariants: versioned immutable filenames, exact chunk size, per-part + whole SHA-256, no wildcard uploads, never `--clobber`. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Split the exact `.fnlpq` byte stream into **1,957,046,720-byte** chunks (the safely-under-2-GiB size proven in FrankenOCR), ONLY the final chunk shorter. Names append zero-padded ordered suffixes `.part00`, `.part01`, …; the v1 manifest caps part count at **64**, so two digits are sufficient and unambiguous. Concatenation in manifest order IS the original file — no archive or compression layer. (The ≈4.7 GB int8-all artifact is expected to split into 3 parts; the cap, not the expectation, is the contract.)
- Logical filename is artifact-version/quant/packing-bearing: `nanbeige4.2-3b.fnlpq-v1.int8.generic.fnlpq`. Binary SemVer and model-artifact SemVer are independent; a patch binary release must not rename or republish identical 4+ GB bytes. A different source revision, format, recipe, tokenizer/template closure, or logical bytes gets a NEW artifact version/name/tag; bytes under an existing tag/name are NEVER replaced. A bad release is superseded by a new catalog, not rewritten.
- Staging directory contents: the parts, `MODEL_ASSET_RECEIPT.json` (binds the conversion receipt, split command/tool version, ordered reconstruction, whole-file result, parity/quality receipts, and intended release inventory), `SHA256SUMS`, `RECONSTRUCTION.txt` (exact byte-concatenation instructions), and the exact approved license/NOTICE/modification bundle. Small records committed or attached; the multi-GB `.fnlpq` and parts stay gitignored.
- `verify-model-package`: rehash the retained staging set, reconstruct by concatenation, byte-compare the whole result against the converter output digest, and validate the receipt's internal cross-references.
- **Draft-release runbook** (docs/, maintainer-facing): hash staging set → reconstruct/compare → create DRAFT GitHub Release → upload with EXACT EXPLICIT PATHS per asset (never a wildcard, never `gh release upload --clobber`) → query remote inventory → re-download each asset into a clean directory → repeat part/whole verification → only that receipt authorizes publishing the draft. Revocation is not recall: an old offline binary with an embedded old manifest may still install an old immutable release; tooling must state this rather than claim old bytes vanished.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon; split/hash is serial/streaming with bounded buffers (never whole-part in RAM). No unsafe. License settled Apache-2.0: the packaged bundle carries the exact license text, verbatim upstream notices, and the factual modification notice (recipe id + source revision + source digests) — byte-compared against the truth-pack copy. G1>G2: packaging is deterministic; same input bytes → same part bytes, names, and receipts.

## Evidence / gates
- Split/reassembly identity gate: for fixture files at sizes {0-boundary, exact multiple of 1,957,046,720 (synthetic sparse), one-byte-over, tail-only}, split → concatenate → byte-identical, part count and names exact.
- Receipt validation gate: `verify-model-package` rejects a tampered part, missing part, renamed part, wrong-order manifest, or edited receipt field, each with a named error.
- Runbook dry-run gate against a FAKE local release layout (no network): full runbook executes with every check green. Close cites fixture runs + runbook path.

## Tests
- Unit: chunk-size arithmetic (exact 1,957,046,720 boundaries), zero-padded suffix generation, 64-part cap enforcement, SHA256SUMS format, receipt schema completeness.
- Property/fuzz: random-length fixtures (weighted around boundaries) split+reassemble byte-identically; any single-byte part corruption is caught by the named part digest before whole-file comparison. Log part name, expected/actual digest on every failure.
- E2E: package→verify→reconstruct a synthetic multi-part artifact with DETAILED LOGGING (per-part length/digest/timing); real int8-all packaging is model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. The named runnable driver is `scripts/e2e_release_package_verify.sh`: package → verify → tamper-one-part → verify-must-fail → reconstruct → byte-compare, logging per-stage timestamps, per-part name/length/digest with expected-vs-actual on every failure (the exact failing part named), reconstruction byte count vs `fnlpq_file_sha256`, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` NDJSON line; the real int8-all leg logs SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- .fnlpq canonical writer: the packager's input is a finished canonical artifact and its conversion receipt; part digests bind to `fnlpq_file_sha256`.

title: [P2] Embed release-bound canonical manifest with pre-network compatibility enforcement
description:
## Background
Default `fnlp pull` trusts exactly one thing: the release-bound manifest EMBEDDED in the installed binary. This bead defines the canonical schema-versioned manifest, embeds its exact bytes + SHA-256 in every compatible binary (also attached to the model release for audit), and builds the pre-network validation layer that rejects incompatibility BEFORE any multi-GB request or cache creation. Hashes prove byte integrity, not publisher identity — the manifest is trusted only relative to the installed binary. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Canonical schema-versioned manifest records: model/artifact ids; immutable release tag; logical filename/length/SHA-256 (`nanbeige4.2-3b.fnlpq-v1.int8.generic.fnlpq`); exact ordered part name/length/SHA-256/HTTPS mirror URLs; ordered source-file digests + `source_root_sha256`; recipe/converter/format compatibility; tokenizer/template/census/logical-model/packing digests; license-bundle digest; packing policy; revocation/supersession state. Canonical bytes + `release_manifest_sha256` embedded in the binary at build time and attached to the release.
- **Immutable release-tag URLs ONLY:** `releases/download/<exact-tag>/<asset>` — never `main`, `latest`, or another mutable branch; never captured expiring object-storage redirects. Redirect targets are validated at request time by the pull layer.
- **Pre-network enforcement (all BEFORE any artifact request, cache creation, or network I/O):** exact schema/recipe/format compatibility; portable single-component filenames; unique case-folded names; canonical part ids/order; HTTPS-only URLs; checked part-size sum equals declared whole length; count/size/string caps (≤64 parts, capped name/URL lengths); required license/census digests present. An incompatible historical recipe fails here, cleanly.
- Escape hatch contract (consumed by the pull bead): `--manifest <local-path-or-https-url>` MUST be paired with `--expected-sha256`; `FNLP_MANIFEST_URL` is NOT a hidden library read. The expected digest binds the manifest only to the extent the caller obtained it through a trusted channel; manifest + digest supplied together by the same attacker prove only self-consistency — document this honestly in help text.
- Caps and compatibility are enforced with the same duplicate-key-rejecting JSON primitives as the format header; unknown required schema versions reject.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon. No unsafe. No network code in THIS bead — it is pure data/validation; asupersync HTTP enters only in the pull bead. Embedding must not balloon binary size beyond the manifest's real bytes; the audit copy on the release is the same canonical bytes (byte-compared in CI).

## Evidence / gates
- Golden manifest fixture: canonical bytes stable across builds; embedded copy == release-attached copy == fixture, byte-compared.
- Rejection matrix green: each pre-network invariant above has a fixture that fails BEFORE any I/O layer is invoked (asserted via an I/O-refusing test harness stub in the validation layer's seam).
- Phase-2 exit contribution: "malicious-format/manifest tests green". Close cites the matrix + golden fixture paths.

## Tests
- Unit: every schema field; part-size sum arithmetic (u64 checked); case-folded uniqueness; single-component filename grammar; HTTPS/tag-URL shape; caps at 64/limits; revocation/supersession state parsing.
- Property/fuzz: mutated manifests never panic and always fail with a typed pre-network error naming the violated invariant; valid manifests round-trip canonically. Log invariant name + JSON pointer path on every rejection.
- E2E: binary embeds fixture manifest; `fnlp models --json` (later bead) surfaces its identity; a fake incompatible-recipe manifest fails before any socket exists (asserted by the no-network test harness). No model gating needed — manifests are small.
- Named artifact: the pre-network rejection matrix lives at `tests/manifest_rejection_matrix.rs` with the I/O-refusing harness stub; every rejection logs the invariant name + JSON pointer path with the expected vs observed value inline, and the suite ends with a machine-parseable summary line (fixtures run / rejected-as-designed counts).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Release packager: part names/lengths/digests and receipt structure are produced by packaging; the manifest schema binds those exact outputs.

title: [P2] Implement streaming fnlp pull: verified parts, sequential mirror fallback, budgeted resume
description:
## Background
`fnlp pull` is the ONE Rust artifact manager: the installed binary's streaming download/verify/reassemble/activate path over asupersync HTTP/TLS (`tls-webpki-roots`) — the ONLY networked Rust/product code path in the project (no reqwest/hyper, ever; `install.sh`/`install.ps1` invoke this exact binary and never parse manifests, concatenate parts, invent cache filenames, or duplicate integrity logic). Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Identity encoding enforced** (no transfer/content-encoding transforms of part bytes); response frames stream directly into ONE same-filesystem staging file while updating per-part AND whole SHA-256 incrementally; a part is never buffered in RAM.
- **Part geometry is fixed:** parts are exactly 1,957,046,720 bytes each with only the final part shorter (the manifest caps the count at 64, so zero-padded two-digit `.part00`, `.part01`, ... suffixes are sufficient and unambiguous); concatenation in manifest order IS the original `.fnlpq` — no archive or compression layer exists to interpret.
- **Sequential mirror fallback, explicitly:** mirrors are tried in deterministic manifest order with an explicit ordered `for`/`await` loop. At the asupersync pin, `combinator::first_ok_outcomes` merely CLASSIFIES an already-completed outcome vector, and `ExecPlan::first_ok` drives EVERY child to completion before selecting the first success in input order — the pinned `first_ok` is NOT a race and no losers exist to cancel, but neither surface is the required sequential short-circuit, so neither is used for fallback. A concurrent hedge is research-only: it would require a separately ratified first-SUCCESS contract, a duplicate-byte budget, and cancel-then-drain proof for every loser.
- **Budgets:** each mirror attempt gets child connect/header/idle/total-time and remaining-byte caps that can fail it early enough to reach the next mirror; ALL attempts meet under one enclosing pull deadline/cost/byte budget (typed meet-composed asupersync budgets, reserved cleanup budget kept). Transient failures may use the foundation's retry future only where OQ-35 ratifies it; `RetryPolicy` bounds attempts/backoff and is never described as bounding transferred bytes. Each attempt rolls back to the last verified part boundary.
- **Resume journal** binds manifest digest, final path, committed length, and verified part index. On restart the manager REHASHES every committed part before trusting the prefix. Intra-part Range resume is used ONLY after an asupersync fixture proves `206` + exact `Content-Range`; otherwise the unverified tail is truncated and that part restarts.
- Manifest authority: default = release-bound embedded bytes; `--manifest` requires `--expected-sha256`; redirects host-allowlisted; credentials never forwarded cross-origin; redirect targets validated at request time. All pre-network compatibility checks run first (embedded-manifest bead).
- Completion: sync; fully parse/census-check the staged `.fnlpq`; verify embedded source/license/logical-model identity; derive the native packing via its own resumable `create_new` staging transaction; differential-check it; run required selftests; sync and rename to a previously nonexistent content-addressed destination (same filesystem; never rely on rename-replace — not portable to Windows); append the activation record. Existing files count as cached only after exact length + whole SHA-256. Failure/cancel/disk-full/crash/malicious mirror leaves the previously active chain head intact; concurrent pulls converge on the same content address. Installed remote parts are NOT retained (no second 4+ GB copy).
- Capability/typing: the pull child `Cx` gets only the spawn/time/IO and TLS entropy its pinned path proves necessary — never REMOTE; `Outcome::{Ok,Err,Cancelled,Panicked}` and all eleven pinned `CancelKind` variants (`User`,`Timeout`,`Deadline`,`PollQuota`,`CostBudget`,`FailFast`,`RaceLost`,`ParentCancelled`,`ResourceUnavailable`,`Shutdown`,`LinkedExit`) preserved to the CLI policy boundary. `bracket` may structure the normal awaited path, but its drop-path release is bounded best-effort — durable cleanup authority is RAII + explicit awaits + the part-boundary journal + orphan staging recovery + the append-only activation protocol.
- Five-quantity report before transfer: network download bytes / canonical Generic bytes / derived packing-set bytes / peak install bytes / steady-state retained bytes; peak free-space enforced before pull AND before native-pack derivation.
- **Operator-facing progress + resume UX:** during transfer, stderr shows per-part progress (`part 02/03 41.7% 815,000,000/1,957,046,720 bytes`), cumulative verified-vs-remaining bytes for the whole artifact, and the current mirror; every mirror failure states the mirror URL, the OBSERVED failure (HTTP status / timeout class / budget exhausted, observed vs expected value inline), and the next mirror tried; on interrupt/failure the final message states exactly what is preserved (verified parts) and the NEXT command (re-run `fnlp pull` — it resumes from the last verified part boundary after rehash). On an interactive TTY without `--yes`, the five-quantity report is followed by an explicit y/N confirm; non-TTY (installer) runs proceed and log the report instead. Robot mode mirrors progress/failure as versioned NDJSON events; human decoration never enters robot output.

## Constraints
- Deps: asupersync HTTP/TLS + clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 only; no Rayon in the release graph; leaf hash/copy loops never spawn. No unsafe. G1>G2. Typed exit codes 0–10 at the CLI boundary. `fnlp pull [--quant int8|int4] [--arch auto|...] [--model-dir ...]` surface; `--model-dir` wins, then explicit `FNLP_MODEL_DIR`, then platform default `${HOME}/.cache/franken_nlp/models/` (Unix) / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\franken_nlp\models\` (Windows, `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\...` fallback).

## Evidence / gates
- Tiny deterministic multi-part fixtures: mirror fallback order, streamed assembly, part/whole mismatch, overlong/short bodies, malicious names/redirects, resume at every part boundary, cache-hit rehash, 206/Content-Range proof before intra-part resume, budget-exhaustion-to-next-mirror timing. (Hostile-root/crash/concurrency matrix is its own bead; this bead must pass the pull-specific rows.)
- Phase-2 exit: a private/fake-release clean-cache pull resolves with no `--model`; malicious-manifest/pull/resume tests green. Close cites fixture suite + journal-replay evidence.

## Tests
- Unit: incremental part/whole hash equivalence vs one-shot; journal record encode/decode; rollback-to-boundary arithmetic; redirect allowlist; identity-encoding rejection of transformed bodies.
- Property/fuzz: byte-stream perturbations (truncation, corruption, reorder, stall) at random offsets — every outcome is typed, staging never becomes the final name, committed-prefix trust only after rehash. DETAILED LOGGING: per-attempt mirror, budget consumption, bytes, digest state at each boundary; seed-bound where the lab transport is ratified.
- E2E: fake local HTTPS release → clean-cache pull → activation → discovery; second pull = byte-perfect cache hit with ZERO network (socket-refusing harness). Real-release pull is model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. The named runnable driver is `scripts/e2e_pull_fake_release.sh`: per-stage timestamps, per-part bytes + digests at every verification boundary, expected-vs-actual on mismatch with the exact failing part/offset, the zero-network assertion result, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` NDJSON line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Release-bound embedded manifest: supplies the trusted inventory + pre-network validation this manager obeys.
- .fnlpq reader: the staged artifact must fully parse/census-check before activation.
- Filesystem transaction + activation journal: staging, locks, rename, and the append-only activation chain are that bead's contract; pull is its first consumer.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_G0_SEAM — G0 ratified the asupersync HTTPS Range/redirect/cancellation/resume semantics this design assumes.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **Part geometry + incremental hashing core.** Deliverable: the fixed-geometry module — parts exactly 1,957,046,720 bytes (final part shorter, ≤64 parts, zero-padded `.part00`… suffixes), concatenation in manifest order IS the `.fnlpq`, with incremental per-part AND whole SHA-256 updated as bytes stream. Test evidence: unit incremental-vs-one-shot hash equivalence; rollback-to-boundary arithmetic units. Next milestone assumes: correct part math and digest state for the streaming writer.
2. **Single-mirror streaming download into staging.** Deliverable: identity-encoding-enforced transfer (no transfer/content-encoding transforms) streaming response frames directly into ONE same-filesystem staging file — a part is never buffered in RAM — with per-attempt connect/header/idle/total-time and remaining-byte caps that can fail an attempt early. Test evidence: tiny deterministic multi-part fixtures for streamed assembly, part/whole digest mismatch, overlong/short bodies; identity-encoding rejection of transformed bodies. Next milestone assumes: a working single-attempt transfer that fails early with typed outcomes.
3. **Sequential mirror fallback + enclosing budgets.** Deliverable: the explicit ordered `for`/`await` loop over mirrors in deterministic manifest order (neither `combinator::first_ok_outcomes` nor `ExecPlan::first_ok` is used; concurrent hedge stays research-only), all attempts meeting under one enclosing pull deadline/cost/byte budget with reserved cleanup budget, `RetryPolicy` only where OQ-35 ratifies it (bounding attempts/backoff, never bytes), each attempt rolling back to the last verified part boundary. Test evidence: fixtures for mirror fallback order and budget-exhaustion-to-next-mirror timing. Next milestone assumes: attempts fail cleanly to the next mirror with the verified prefix intact.
4. **Resume journal + rehash-on-restart + Range gating.** Deliverable: the journal binding manifest digest, final path, committed length, and verified part index; restart REHASHES every committed part before trusting the prefix; intra-part Range resume only after an asupersync fixture proves `206` + exact `Content-Range`, otherwise the unverified tail is truncated and the part restarts. Test evidence: resume at every part boundary; cache-hit rehash; the 206/Content-Range proof fixture; journal record encode/decode units. Next milestone assumes: committed-prefix trust is durable across restarts.
5. **Manifest authority + redirect/credential policy + CLI surface.** Deliverable: default release-bound embedded manifest bytes; `--manifest` requires `--expected-sha256`; host-allowlisted redirects validated at request time; credentials never forwarded cross-origin; all pre-network compatibility checks run first (embedded-manifest bead); `fnlp pull [--quant int8|int4] [--arch auto|...] [--model-dir ...]` with `--model-dir` > `FNLP_MODEL_DIR` > platform default resolution. Test evidence: malicious-name/redirect fixtures; redirect-allowlist units. Next milestone assumes: only trusted inventories and URLs reach the transfer machinery.
6. **Completion pipeline: verify → derive → activate.** Deliverable: sync; full parse/census-check of the staged `.fnlpq`; embedded source/license/logical-model identity verification; native packing derived via its own resumable `create_new` staging transaction plus differential check; required selftests; sync + rename to a previously nonexistent content-addressed destination (never rename-replace); activation record appended; cache hit only after exact length + whole SHA-256; installed remote parts not retained. Test evidence: E2E fake local HTTPS release → clean-cache pull → activation → discovery; second pull is a byte-perfect cache hit with ZERO network (socket-refusing harness); failure/cancel/disk-full/malicious-mirror rows leave the previously active chain head intact (full hostile matrix stays in its own bead; pull-specific rows pass here). Next milestone assumes: a durably activated model exists so capability typing and reporting can be finished around it.
7. **Capability typing, five-quantity report, typed exit codes.** Deliverable: pull child `Cx` granted only proven spawn/time/IO + TLS entropy (never REMOTE); `Outcome::{Ok,Err,Cancelled,Panicked}` and all eleven pinned `CancelKind` variants preserved to the CLI policy boundary (typed exit codes 0–10); the five-quantity report (network download / canonical Generic / derived packing-set / peak install / steady-state retained bytes) printed before transfer with peak free-space enforced before pull AND before native-pack derivation. Test evidence: property/fuzz byte-stream perturbations (truncation, corruption, reorder, stall) at random offsets — every outcome typed, staging never becomes the final name, committed-prefix trust only after rehash; per-attempt mirror/budget/bytes/digest logging; Phase-2 exit run — private/fake-release clean-cache pull resolves with no `--model`, close citing fixture suite + journal-replay evidence. The per-part progress stream, mirror-failure reason lines, resume-instruction message, and TTY y/N confirm (`--yes` bypass) land in this milestone, with TTY/non-TTY/robot-mode tests.

title: [P2] Implement filesystem transaction + append-only activation journal (ActivationFork fail-closed)
description:
## Background
Every durable mutation of the model root — staging a download, installing a converted artifact, deriving a native packing, activating or rolling back — goes through ONE filesystem transaction layer plus an APPEND-ONLY activation journal. Crash, disk-full, cancellation, or a malicious mirror must never leave an ambiguous or corrupted active model. This bead is the authority the pull/derive/models beads build on. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Root policy:** the model root must be owner-controlled and not writable by an untrusted principal. One NON-REENTRANT lock handle guards each content address. Staging and activation records use `create_new` (exclusive creation). Symlink/reparse-point/device targets and hostile parent permissions REJECT. All temporary and final paths stay on ONE filesystem. Where safe handle-relative/no-follow operations are unavailable, shared/adversary-writable roots are UNSUPPORTED — refused, not papered over with a racy pre-check (TOCTOU is not mitigated by stat-then-open).
- **Commit protocol:** write staged file → fsync file → rename to a PREVIOUSLY-NONEXISTENT content-addressed final name on the same filesystem (never depending on rename-replace semantics, which are not portable to Windows) → fsync directory where supported.
- **Append-only activation journal:** under the model-root lock, construct a canonical record body containing: checked monotonic sequence number, artifact/native/config digests, and previous-record digest; compute `record_digest = SHA-256("fnlp-activation-v1" || body)`; write/sync a `create_new` staged envelope containing body + digest; rename it to a unique sequence-and-digest final name; sync the directory. Discovery recomputes EVERY digest and follows the one contiguous chain from the unique genesis record.
- **Fail-closed reads:** staged/torn/gapped/disconnected records are ignored. Two valid successors of one head = **`ActivationFork`** — a typed integrity error that keeps the LAST UNAMBIGUOUS HEAD; discovery never chooses a winner by filename or digest order. Sequence overflow is a typed error, not a wrap.
- **Activate and rollback BOTH append a new record** — neither overwrites an old pointer or artifact. Prior immutable stage artifacts (bf16, int8-mlp, int8-mlp-attn) remain activatable; this is the rollback mechanism that actually exists (env vars can never restore bytes absent from a file).
- Orphan/live staging is distinguishable by its lock; stale state is quarantinable (`fnlp doctor` later) — this bead provides the primitives and detection, not the doctor UX.
- Phase-0 G0 item (9) ratified the platform substrate (pinned-nightly `std::fs::File::{lock,try_lock}` probe, rename/directory-durability behavior per target family); implement against those ADRs, and if a target family lacks a facility, it is explicitly blocked/compiled out per docs/PLATFORM_SURFACES.md — never emulated unsafely.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; std::fs only — no libc reach-through, no memmap2, no notify/inotify crates. No Rayon. No unsafe. `bracket`'s drop-time release is bounded best-effort at the pin, so durable cleanup is synchronous RAII + explicit awaits + this journal + recovery — never "the destructor will handle it". Durable spool/journal writes that require acknowledgement use `GenServer::call` or reserve→permit with explicit commit acknowledgement; `cast().await` proves enqueue only.

## Evidence / gates
- Crash-state matrix (shared with the test-matrix bead, but the primitive-level rows land here): process kill / disk-full / power-cut simulation at EVERY sync/rename/journal state → recovery always finds either the old head or the new head, never ambiguity, never a torn active pointer.
- ActivationFork fixture: two hand-forged valid successors of one head → typed `ActivationFork`, last unambiguous head retained, both forks preserved on disk for forensics.
- Append-only proof: activate→rollback→activate produces a strictly growing chain; no file in the journal directory is ever opened for write twice. Close cites matrix run + fixture paths.

## Tests
- Unit: record-body canonical encoding; `record_digest` domain framing (`"fnlp-activation-v1" || body`); sequence monotonicity/overflow; previous-digest linkage; genesis uniqueness; lock non-reentrancy (same-process re-entry refused, typed).
- Property/fuzz: random interleavings of {stage, sync, rename, append, crash} over a simulated-failure fs shim — invariant: discovery result ∈ {old head, new head}; forged/truncated/bit-flipped records always ignored or fork-error, never adopted. Log the full chain walk (sequence, digest, verdict per record) on every discovery.
- E2E: real-filesystem (tmpdir) kill-during-rename and kill-during-append runs on macOS + Linux CI; symlink/reparse/device and hostile-permission rejection walks with DETAILED LOGGING of the refused path + reason. No model gating — operates on synthetic content. Named artifact: the primitive-level crash/hostile rows live at `tests/fs_txn_crash_matrix.rs` (the rows the distribution-stack matrix bead later re-drives end-to-end); every row logs per-stage timestamps plus the full chain-walk verdict and ends with a machine-parseable summary line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- [P0] crate scaffold (franken_nlp-uxw): the transaction layer lands in the scaffolded crate behind the shared error map; no code bead can precede the scaffold.
- [P0] G0 probes 1-3+9 (franken_nlp-upv): item (9) ratifies the exact platform substrate this bead implements against — the pinned-nightly `std::fs::File::{lock,try_lock}` probe and per-target rename/directory-durability ADRs. Implementing before those ADRs exist would bake in guessed crash semantics; the dependency is a real blocker, not epic-ordering prose.
- None intra-epic: this is the foundation layer consumed by pull, derive, and the models CLIs (they depend on it, not vice versa).

title: [P2] Implement fnlp models derive: content-addressed native packing with byte-differential proof
description:
## Background
Public hosting stays 1× per quant tier: the released artifact is arch-neutral Generic, and each host derives its own native packing LOCALLY. `fnlp models derive --arch {aarch64-sdot,aarch64-i8mm,x86-vnni256,x86-vnni512,x86-avx2}` creates a disposable, content-addressed native cache from the Generic root; the Generic file remains the reconstruction/provenance root and its digest never changes. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Content address = `(whole_artifact_sha256, packing_id, tile_table_version)`** — packing ids include the tile-table version, so a tile-table change is a new cache, never an in-place mutation. Derived caches live under content-addressed subdirectories of the model root.
- **Byte-differential proof:** every derived packing must reconstruct IDENTICAL logical tensors — CI and the derive command itself verify reconstruction against the Generic root's logical tensors (per-tensor byte compare of the logical form, plus row-sum/scale metadata consistency). Derivation changes `fnlpq_file_sha256`/`packing_set_sha256` of the derived object and NEVER `logical_model_sha256`.
- **Resumable `create_new` staging** through the filesystem-transaction layer: interrupted derivation resumes or restarts cleanly; the cache appears atomically at its content-addressed name or not at all; the Generic root is opened read-only.
- **PackingSet authority:** a `PackingSet` lists the representations actually installed; dispatch may only select a kernel whose required representation IS installed — per-shape dispatch cannot assume mutually incompatible SDOT/I8MM/VNNI-256/VNNI-512/AVX2/autovec layouts all exist for free. Multiple representations are allowed only when the duplicate byte cost is explicit and reported. An arch-specific artifact never silently falls back to a different packing; an incompatible arch target is a hard error NAMING the required derivation command.
- Derivation is deterministic per packing id (same Generic bytes + packing_id + tile_table_version → same cache bytes); a maintainer packaging command cannot publish a native cache as the canonical artifact (type-level separation of Generic vs derived paths).
- Footprint honesty: derive reports its addition to the five-quantity footprint (derived packing-set bytes, peak during derivation with staging, steady-state retained); `--no-native-cache` users keep Generic-only on the compatible slower path.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon; derivation streams tensor-by-tensor with bounded panels (same memory discipline as the converter). No unsafe. Measured-faster wins is the DISPATCH rule — capability alone never decides the winner; this bead only guarantees the representations dispatch may choose from are real, installed, and logically identical. G1>G2: a packing that fails byte-differential reconstruction is discarded, never shipped.

## Evidence / gates
- Reconstruction identity gate: for every supported packing id on synthetic artifacts (all five arch targets), derive → reconstruct → per-tensor byte equality with the Generic logical tensors, plus metadata (scales, row sums) equality.
- Atomicity gate: kill during derivation at staged/sync/rename points → Generic untouched, cache either absent or complete-and-verified; re-run converges.
- Dispatch-safety fixture: a dispatch table row referencing an uninstalled representation is rejected at load (consumed later by kernel beads; the refusal lands here). Close cites gate runs.

## Tests
- Unit: content-address derivation (digest/packing_id/tile_table_version triple), read-only Generic access, duplicate-cost reporting, incompatible-arch hard error text naming the derive command.
- Property/fuzz: random synthetic tensor sets × all packing ids → reconstruct equal; corrupted derived cache detected by its own digests at open (never trusted because the triple matches).
- E2E: derive on the host's actual arch from a synthetic Generic artifact with DETAILED LOGGING (per-tensor pack timing, bytes in/out, reconstruction verdict); real-artifact derive is model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable driver: `scripts/e2e_derive_native.sh` — derive → reconstruct → byte-compare → kill-and-resume leg, logging per-stage timestamps, per-tensor bytes in/out and digests, expected-vs-actual logical bytes on any reconstruction miss (tensor name + first divergent offset), and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Filesystem transaction + activation journal: staging/rename/lock/atomicity substrate for cache creation.
- .fnlpq reader: derivation reads the Generic root through the checked range index and census verification.

title: [P2] Ship fnlp models/licenses/provenance CLIs + robot selftest with five-quantity footprint
description:
## Background
The user-facing truth surfaces for the artifact lifecycle: `fnlp models` (and `models verify --full`), `fnlp licenses`, provenance reporting, and `fnlp robot selftest`. These commands make the honest-state doctrine operational: five-quantity footprints, separated provenance states, factual attribution, and a selftest that is evidence — not universal proof. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **`fnlp models` (+ `--json`):** installed/active digests (full taxonomy: source_root/logical_model/packing_set/license_bundle/fnlpq_file), recipe, format version, source revision, packing set, license path, bytes, provenance/attestation status, durability grade, and source class ∈ {public-catalog, private-manifest, locally-converted}. Reports the revocation limitation honestly (revocation is not recall: an old offline binary can still install an old immutable release; never claim old bytes vanished). `fnlp models verify --full` is the explicit full-file bit-rot recheck (whole-file SHA-256 vs activation receipt). Human output is an ALIGNED fixed-column table (stable column order: name, recipe, arch/packing, bytes, provenance, durability, state), honoring NO_COLOR/CI/TERM=dumb; `--json` is the canonical machine form and the table is derived from it, never the reverse. Every failure message from these surfaces states WHAT failed, the OBSERVED vs EXPECTED value (both digests on a verify miss), and the NEXT command to run (e.g. `fnlp models verify --full`, `fnlp models derive --arch <target>`, or re-run `fnlp pull`).
- **Five-quantity footprint report** — printed by `fnlp pull`, the installer path, `robot plan`, and any footprint claim: (1) network download bytes, (2) canonical Generic bytes, (3) derived packing-set bytes, (4) peak install bytes (staging plus any previously active artifact), (5) steady-state retained bytes. Local steady-state disk is NOT 1×: Generic + active derived packing + receipts. Never conflate the five.
- **`fnlp licenses`:** prints the full §5.7 bundle — exact Apache-2.0 text, every applicable upstream notice VERBATIM, and the prominent modification notice naming the transformation (recipe id + source revision + source digests). Attribution is factual provenance only: "Model origin: Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B; author attribution per the pinned model card: Nanbeige Team; source revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; Apache-2.0; transformed by franken_nlp under recipe `<id>`." NEVER a synthesized `© 2026 Nanbeige Team` line the upstream never published. `fnlp --version` carries the one-line attribution; `fnlp models --json` exposes the full provenance bundle.
- **Provenance reporting** distinguishes THREE states separately, never one boolean: binary provenance (attestation status of the installed binary), manifest provenance (embedded release-bound vs private-manifest-with-caller-digest), artifact provenance (verified digests + activation receipt binding the full-file digest verified at installation). `fnlp robot health` prints recipe, catalog/manifest/artifact/source/packing/license digests, and source class.
- **`fnlp robot selftest`:** a FINITE on-CPU differential rerun — dispatched kernels vs canonical scalar/i64 references on fixed fixture shapes (including K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752} int8 rows) — emitting a provenance-stamped NDJSON verdict. It is EVIDENCE on this host at this moment, not universal proof; output wording must say so (no "verified correct" without scope).

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. No Rayon; selftest runs serial or under the one owned scoped_cpu discipline — leaf kernels never spawn. Robot mode: versioned NDJSON, stdout data / stderr diagnostics, stable exit codes 0–10, honor NO_COLOR/CI/TERM=dumb; human mode never mixes decoration into robot output. Presets are data. License settled Apache-2.0 — no fail-closed "license uncertainty" language anywhere in these surfaces.

## Evidence / gates
- Byte-compare gate: `fnlp licenses` output vs the truth-pack bundle copy (and vs the artifact's embedded bundle) — exact, including the modification notice.
- Five-quantity consistency gate: numbers reported by pull, `robot plan`, and `models` agree with measured fixture artifacts (Generic bytes, derived bytes, staged peak) on synthetic fixtures.
- Robot schema contract test: `models --json`, `robot health`, `robot selftest` events validate against the frozen JSON schema fixture. Close cites all three.

## Tests
- Unit: provenance three-state matrix (8 combinations render distinctly); durability-grade wording; revocation-limitation text presence; digest-taxonomy field mapping.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary installed-state fixtures (missing cache, stale receipt, forked journal, partial derive) → `models` reports each condition truthfully with a typed state, never a false "healthy" boolean.
- E2E: synthetic install → `models`/`licenses`/`robot health`/`robot selftest` full pass with DETAILED LOGGING (every digest printed and cross-checked against fixture expectations); real-artifact runs model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable driver: `scripts/e2e_models_surfaces.sh` — runs all four surfaces against a synthetic install plus each degraded-state fixture, logging per-stage timestamps, every digest expected-vs-actual, table-alignment goldens and schema-validation verdicts, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line.

## Dependencies & rationale
