- Native packing derivation: `models` reports PackingSet contents and footprint quantities that derivation produces.

title: [P2] Build hostile-root/crash/concurrency test matrix with deterministic VirtualTcp fixtures
description:
## Background
The hostile-root / crash / concurrency TEST MATRIX for the whole distribution stack: pull, filesystem transactions, activation journal, and native-pack derivation under every failure the design claims to survive. Where the OQ-35 census ratified the asupersync lab's `VirtualTcp` transport at the pin, network fixtures run DETERMINISTICALLY — virtual sockets, virtual time, seed-bound fault injection — so every mirror-failure/resume/cancellation interleaving replays from a seed instead of flaking on a local socket server. Real-socket smoke coverage is retained but ceases to be the primary vehicle. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
Matrix rows (each a named, replayable test):
- **Crash/kill/disk-full at EVERY sync/rename/journal state**: staged-unsynced, staged-synced, mid-rename, renamed-dir-unsynced, journal-envelope-staged, journal-renamed — recovery finds old head or new head, never ambiguity.
- **Journal adversarial rows:** sequence overflow (typed error, no wrap), sequence gap (chain stops at gap), fork (two valid successors → `ActivationFork`, last unambiguous head kept, no filename/digest tiebreak), torn/truncated/bit-flipped records (ignored, logged), genesis duplication.
- **Old-head preservation:** every failure row asserts the previously active chain head remains discoverable and its artifact bytes untouched.
- **Concurrency:** concurrent pulls of the same content address converge to one verified artifact (no torn merge, no double-activation); lock re-entry refused typed; orphan staging from a killed peer is detected and quarantinable, never adopted without verification.
- **Hostile roots:** symlink/reparse-point/device targets, hostile parent permissions, shared/adversary-writable roots → refused (unsupported), with the exact policy error; no racy stat-then-open pre-check accepted as mitigation.
- **Pull network rows (VirtualTcp where ratified; real-socket smoke otherwise):** mirror-order fallback, per-mirror budget exhaustion mid-body, stall (idle budget), truncated/overlong bodies, corrupted part (per-part digest catch), malicious redirect (cross-host credential strip + allowlist), resume at every part boundary, intra-part resume only with proven 206/Content-Range, restart-rehash of committed parts, cache-hit full rehash, enclosing pull budget exhaustion with reserved cleanup budget honored.
- **Derivation rows:** kill during pack staging/rename; corrupted derived cache detected at open; Generic root untouched throughout.
Every deterministic row must REPLAY FROM ITS SEED (lab runs record seed + trace fingerprint + crashpack id); a failing interleaving may never survive as a one-off CI ghost.

## Constraints
- Test-only bead: no production code beyond test hooks/shims already specified by the beads under test. Simulated-failure fs shim and VirtualTcp fixtures live in test code. No Rayon anywhere (including dev-dependency test helpers in the release graph — test-only helpers stay out of release features). Lab oracles cover async state, NOT native scoped_cpu OS-thread interleavings — the pull/journal stack is async+fs, which is exactly the lab's ratified domain; anything requiring native-thread coverage defers to the bounded team-state model beads (Phase 0/3), and this bead must not claim that coverage.

## Evidence / gates
- Full matrix green in CI with row inventory committed (row name → seed(s) → verdict), satisfying the Phase-2 exit line "malicious-format/manifest/pull/resume/concurrency/install tests green" for its rows.
- Replay proof: for at least one deliberately-injected failure per family, the recorded seed reproduces the identical trace fingerprint on re-run.
- Real-socket smoke: one end-to-end fake-release pull over a real localhost TLS socket stays green per platform. Close cites the row inventory + replay artifacts.

## Tests
(This bead IS tests; deliverables:)
- The matrix harness with per-row DETAILED LOGGING: row id, seed, injected fault point, fs/journal state timeline, discovery verdict, digest states.
- Named runnable driver: `scripts/e2e_pull_hostile_matrix.sh` executes the full matrix (row filters supported) and emits one machine-parseable NDJSON verdict line per row (row id, seed, fault point, wall time, verdict, crashpack id when failing) plus a final `E2E_SUMMARY` line; per-row logs carry per-stage timestamps and expected-vs-actual digest/offset detail — a pull-row failure names the exact part and byte offset that diverged.
- Fixture corpus: forged journal records, malicious manifests/redirect scripts, boundary-length parts (empty tail, 1-byte tail, exact 1,957,046,720-byte part).
- CI wiring: rows run on Linux + macOS (+ Windows for rename/reparse semantics rows); model-gated rows none — everything here is synthetic; nothing may report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Streaming fnlp pull: the network/resume/budget rows exercise its real implementation, not a stand-in.
- Filesystem transaction + activation journal: the crash/journal/hostile-root rows exercise its real implementation.
- Native packing derivation: the derivation atomicity rows exercise its real implementation.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_G0_CENSUS — the OQ-35 census ratifies (or records absent) VirtualTcp/lab determinism this matrix's primary vehicle depends on.

title: [4A] Build sealed-formation scoped-CPU team: entry gate, capacity-1 lanes, panic drain, completion latch
description:
## Background
All CPU-bound inference for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT with q 3072→6144; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) runs inside one admitted `Cx::spawn_blocking` closure owning one `Cx::scoped_cpu` region per request or bounded batch epoch. The pinned `ScopedCpu::spawn` checks the numeric worker cap but does NOT check the scope's drain latch before creating a child, so an unprotected protocol could spawn a worker after cancellation began. This bead builds the sealed-formation team that makes that impossible by construction.

## Contract
- **Sealed formation**: the coordinator creates the entire fixed team while workers wait at an entry gate, irrevocably ends the spawn phase (seal), and only then releases workers into the persistent bounded command loop. No fallible kernel work starts before the seal; the coordinator never calls `spawn` again after it. Because the pinned `ScopedCpu::spawn` enforces the cap but not the drain latch, the protocol itself must prevent post-latch spawns — and a test must prove no post-start/post-latch worker can appear under cancellation or panic.
- The coordinator may execute one deterministic shard itself while creating at most `effective_compute_team_width − 1` children (the pinned `worker_cap` is a cap on spawned children, per the G0 probe arithmetic — never assume it includes the caller).
- **Capacity-1 command/reply lanes per worker**; preallocated worker-owned output shards; deterministic ordinal handoff/assembly at stage boundaries so mutable aliases never cross workers. Assembly bytes and rendezvous cost are measured explicitly, not assumed free.
- **Disconnect-safe panic drain**: a disconnected per-worker reply lane identifies a panicked/exited child; the coordinator stops siblings and joins the scope rather than deadlocking on a fixed-count barrier.
- **Completion latch owns everything until closure exit**: the blocking closure owns the compute-admission lease, memory reservation, and output buffers until its `scoped_cpu` region has joined and the closure exits; the latch fires only then. Wrapper-task cancellation never releases or reuses those resources early (the pinned contract says an already-running pool closure may outlive its cancelled wrapper — it stays tracked in EngineResources' actual-completion set).
- **Checkpoints**: every worker checkpoints its `CpuCx` before its first command and at tile/morsel boundaries; every stage declares a maximum uninterruptible work quantum. Cancellation closes admission, sends stop on the command lanes, and joins the entire scope.
- Leaf kernels never spawn; no layer/microkernel creates threads or tasks. A faster direct-write design may replace lane assembly only through a safe disjoint-range FrankenSuite abstraction, never a new unsafe island.

## Constraints
No Rayon anywhere in the release graph; deny-not-forbid unsafe (this module is safe); deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; never enter the seam under an engine lock; never recursively create a team; never nest a runtime; `Outcome::{Ok,Err,Cancelled,Panicked}` preserved through child join and latch resolution; reserve→permit two-phase channel idiom (a held permit is an obligation, never carried across an unrelated await); G1>G2.

## Evidence / gates
Hostile interleaving test: cancellation/panic cannot produce a post-start or post-latch worker. The repository-owned bounded team-state automaton (formation/seal/command/cancel/panic/join) covers the native OS-thread half that asupersync Lab explicitly does NOT enumerate; native hostile stress/replay validates the automaton's seam against the real implementation. Gauntlet capacity certificate: one admitted team, exact coordinator/child width, full join on cancel/panic, region-close quiescence. p50/p95/p99 cancellation-observation latency measured against declared quanta.

## Tests
Unit: seal is irrevocable (post-seal spawn attempt is a compile-shape or typed-protocol error); ordinal assembly reproduces a known permutation deterministically; capacity-1 lane refuses a second in-flight command. Property: for random command schedules, output assembly is byte-identical to sequential execution. Concurrency/model: bounded exhaustive team-state automaton run in CI; injected worker panic at every protocol state → coordinator stops siblings, full join, `Panicked` outcome preserved; injected cancel at every state → no post-latch worker, latch fires only after join. E2E: `many_docs_without_deadlock` (docs ≫ compute width). Detailed logging: worker ordinal, protocol state transitions, latch events, and join order logged per run; failing seeds replay from the logged seed. Model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. The bounded team-state automaton and its native stress seam validation ship as the named deliverable `tests/team_state_model.rs` (shared with the 4A daemon proof program); each run logs scenario id + seed on one machine-parseable line, replayable from the log alone.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (EngineResources broker bead): the team is admitted through, latch-tracked by, and width-inventoried in `EngineResources`.
- A_G0_SEAM (cross-epic): the G0 seam probe ratifies coordinator/child arithmetic, latch semantics, and heartbeat proof this protocol builds on.

title: [P2] Prove model-gated e2e: fetch, convert twice, package, pull, no-flag inference, zero-network cache hit
description:
## Background
The end-to-end lifecycle proof that closes Phase 2: pinned source → deterministic conversion → packaging → release → pull → discovery → real inference → cache-hit — the WHOLE §5 pipeline exercised as one model-gated test, with ordinary CI reporting SKIPPED_NO_MODEL rather than fake-passing. This is the receipt release certification runs; it is also the drill every regression must survive. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
Sequential stages, each with its own assert + artifact:
1. **Fetch/verify:** the revision-scoped source closure passes `--check-only` full rehash — all ten files, exactly 8,360,887,509 bytes total (shards 4,973,547,960 + 3,366,076,760; index 16,519; config 1,019; tokenizer.json 18,450,979; tokenizer.model 2,782,298; tokenizer_config 10,990; added_tokens 174; special_tokens_map 623; generation_config 187), each SHA-256 exact.
2. **Convert twice, clean directories:** two independent clean-directory conversions with `--recipe nanbeige42-int8-v1` produce byte-identical Generic artifacts (`fnlpq_file_sha256` equal). Peak-RSS printed and within formula both times.
3. **Package:** split into exact 1,957,046,720-byte parts; receipts written.
4. **Reassemble:** concatenation in manifest order is byte-identical to the converter output.
5. **Pull from fake release:** a local fake HTTPS release serves the parts; clean-cache `fnlp pull` streams, verifies per-part + whole digests, activates, derives native packing, passes census/selftest.
6. **No-flag discovery:** a fresh engine/CLI run finds the installed exact versioned basename (`nanbeige4.2-3b.fnlpq-v1.int8.generic.fnlpq`) with NO `--model` flag.
7. **Frozen real inference:** the frozen inference fixture (pinned prompt, greedy, pinned recipe/profile) reproduces its expected tokens exactly.
8. **Second pull = byte-perfect cache hit with ZERO network:** rerun `fnlp pull` → full-rehash cache hit, no bytes downloaded; the inference run opens NO network (socket-refusing harness / network-denied environment).
Release certification additionally arms: fallbacks pointed at `/nonexistent`, artifact digest recorded in the certification receipt, and the cross-OS/ISA digest identity (or documented canonical-publisher fallback) + remote re-download identity + attestation checks per §5.6.6 items 1–7 (attestation tooling itself is Phase 6; this bead must leave named hook points and assert the items it can run locally).

## Constraints
- Ordinary CI: reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL for stages needing the closure — NEVER fake-passes, never downloads the closure implicitly (source acquisition stays explicit and out-of-band). The fake-release stage and all synthetic-scale rows (tiny closure analog) run in ordinary CI unconditionally. No Rayon. Exit codes 0–10 honored; the harness distinguishes stage-failure exit codes from SKIPPED status in its NDJSON report.

## Evidence / gates
- The Phase-2 exit lines this bead closes: two-clean-directory conversion identity; package/reassemble identity; private/fake-release clean-cache pull resolving with no `--model`; frozen inference reproduction; zero-network second pull. Public weight assets may be published only after §5.6's remote replay + real-inference receipt is green — this harness IS that receipt generator for the local half.
- Certification artifact: an NDJSON run report binding stage verdicts, digests at every boundary (source root, Generic file, parts, reassembled, installed, activated), peak-RSS values, and the inference token stream hash. Close cites a full armed run OR the harness + synthetic run if the closure is unavailable to the implementer (bead then closes on harness completeness with the armed run tracked by release certification).

## Tests
(This bead IS an e2e test; deliverables:)
- The staged harness with per-stage DETAILED LOGGING: stage id, wall time, bytes processed, every digest computed vs expected, SKIPPED_NO_MODEL markers with the exact missing prerequisite named.
- Named entrypoint: `scripts/e2e_model_lifecycle.sh` (modes: `--armed` for release certification; default synthetic-scale) — emits one NDJSON record per stage (stage id, ISO-8601 start/end, bytes, digests expected-vs-actual, verdict or SKIPPED_NO_MODEL) and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line binding the certification-receipt fields; a failing stage names the exact boundary artifact (part, file, or digest) that diverged.
- Synthetic-scale mirror of all 8 stages (tiny closure → tiny artifact → 3-part split at a scaled chunk size parameterized ONLY in the synthetic path — the real path always uses 1,957,046,720) running unconditionally in CI.
- Negative rows: tampered part before pull (refused), edited artifact after activation (census-on-load refuses), network attempted during stage 8 (harness fails the run).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Hostile-root/crash/concurrency test matrix: e2e certification presumes the failure matrix is green; running the lifecycle drill before the matrix would certify on sand.

title: [4A] Implement admission certificate + process memory ledger with robot plan term printout
description:
## Background
Memory admission precedes allocation and is process-aggregate. For the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, q 3072→6144; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) the numbers are brutal: bf16 KV is 180,224 B = 176 KiB per token per sequence across the 44 slots, so one 8192-token sequence needs ≈1.38 GiB of KV and 64 such sequences ≈88 GiB before activations. The engine must queue/reject before promising that combination, and it must explain the rejection without allocating.

## Contract
- **Admission certificate**: a sequence (or batch row) is admitted only when its worst-case next-step KV/pages, activation rows, logits/candidate rows (full f32 logit vector = 664,576 B per row), grammar/source state, output buffering, and one explicit safety margin fit BOTH the engine's local ceiling AND `EngineResources`' aggregate process ledger. Batch width `M` = min(certificate, measured throughput cap) — never a naked 16–128 guess.
- **Memory-budget decomposition** into named terms: `--memory-budget-total` (maximum modeled process commitment; plain `--memory-budget` aliases it) · `--memory-reserve-os` (non-allocatable safety reserve) · fixed residency (mapped/owned active packing, tokenizer, immutable caches, runtime/pool) · elastic engine budget (KV, activations, logits, grammar/source state, queues, output buffers) · optional replicated-weight/NUMA residency · unmodeled/emergency reserve.
- **`robot plan --ctx --batch --quant` prints every term**, whether file-backed pages count as mapped versus resident, exact committed/peak bytes, and the exact rejection reason — all WITHOUT allocating.
- The admission invariant never compares KV alone against a "budget" that silently excludes the 4–10 GB model/packing residency (params 4,169,800,704 = 8,339,601,408 bf16 payload bytes; int8 roughly halves that).
- Default per-sequence context cap is 8192; the model's 262,144 max positions is an observed limit, not a usability promise.
- Int8 KV accounting is honest: 88 KiB/token payload + 2,816 B/token f32 K/V scales (or 1,408 B f16) + padding + page-table overhead — "approximately halves total KV" may be said only after including that overhead.
- Cancellation aborts/resolves the two-phase reservation and releases committed pages deterministically; per-sequence state is explicit.

## Constraints
Two-phase reservations are tracked obligations under the leak policy (panic in lab/CI, logged escalation in prod); no engine lock held while queued for admission; no general-allocator calls to answer `robot plan` (checked arithmetic only); deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon in the release graph; cgroup/job-object-aware memory authority via ratified safe suite surface or explicit-budget refusal — never libc/sysinfo reach-through; G1>G2.

## Evidence / gates
Overflow/admission proofs in the invariant-gate suite: every budget term uses checked arithmetic (no silent wrap); admission decisions replayed as fixtures; `robot plan` golden outputs for the exact 8192/1.38 GiB and 64×8192/88 GiB scenarios; aggregate multi-engine reserve/commit/abort accounting test green. Ledger entries land in the gauntlet capacity certificate.

## Tests
Unit: each budget term computed independently with known inputs; alias `--memory-budget` ≡ `--memory-budget-total`; rejection reason names the first violated term. Property: for random budget/request vectors, admitted ⇒ sum of worst-case terms ≤ ceiling; abort restores exact ledger balance; checked arithmetic rejects near-overflow inputs instead of wrapping. E2E: `robot plan --ctx 8192 --batch 64 --quant int8` prints all terms + rejection without allocating (assert via allocation-count harness on that path); multi-engine scenario where two engines cannot each promise the same RAM. Detailed logging: every admission decision logs the full term vector and result. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_robot_plan_admission.sh` (model-free): drives the 8192/1.38 GiB and 64×8192/88 GiB scenarios plus near-overflow inputs, asserting every term printed, the first-violated-term rejection reason, and zero allocation on the plan path; one machine-parseable row per scenario. Model-gated tests report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (EngineResources broker bead): the aggregate ledger, two-phase obligations, and process ceiling live in `EngineResources`; admission is its client.

title: [GOV] Create docs/CLAIMS.json claim registry + CI wording enforcement
description:
## Background
Proof state must be machine-checkable, not buried in prose. `docs/CLAIMS.json` is the registry of every public benchmark/quality/portability/security/determinism/artifact claim, and CI is its enforcement arm: README/help/release wording can never be stronger than what the registry records as proven. This governs the whole project (portable-quant-v1 identity claims, footprint claims, parity claims, task-quality claims). Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- `docs/CLAIMS.json` schema per claim: `id`; exact wording scope; `state ∈ {targeted, observed, evidenced, withdrawn}`; validity domain (host/profile/recipe/dataset scoping); evidence artifact digests; expiry/revalidation trigger; and the public surfaces allowed to repeat it (README, `--help`, release notes, robot schema descriptions).
- **CI enforcement:** an extractor scans README/help templates/release templates for claim-id annotations, and REJECTS (a) wording stronger than the registry state, (b) any public NUMERIC or SUPERLATIVE claim that does not carry an explicit claim id. The checker does NOT pretend natural-language equivalence is decidable — the id-annotation requirement is precisely what makes enforcement mechanical.
- Registry plumbing: canonical schema; version migration policy (no compatibility shims before 1.0 — regenerate deliberately); duplicate-id rejection; state-transition rules (e.g. `evidenced` requires ≥1 evidence digest; `withdrawn` retains history, never deletes).
- Seed entries at landing: the profile-scoped fidelity claims (hf-bf16-eager owns HF-match; diagnostic-f32 not required to token-match bf16; quantized profiles carry preregistered budgets), the portable-quant-v1 identity-or-fallback claim, and the five-quantity footprint claim shape — each in `targeted` state until their gates run.
- Fidelity/task claims name their probability space and scope: score spaces are `full_vocab_sequence_logprob` / `trie_local_conditional_probability` (depth-1 form `single_step_candidate_conditional`) / `sequence_score_softmax`; task-quality claims name dataset, prompt hash, recipe id, thinking mode.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 (validator is repo tooling; may live behind a dev/tool target but its JSON parsing uses the same duplicate-key-rejecting primitives). No Rayon. "Verified" without scope, validity domain, and evidence grade is forbidden wording everywhere. License settled Apache-2.0 — claims about licensing use the factual-attribution form only.

## Evidence / gates
- CI job green on the seeded registry; a deliberately-planted stronger-than-state README fixture FAILS the job (negative fixture committed and frozen).
- Schema validation of the registry itself in CI (unknown keys reject; duplicate ids reject).
- Close cites: registry path, CI job name, negative-fixture path, and the extractor's annotation grammar doc.

## Tests
- Unit: state machine transitions; id grammar; evidence-digest format; expiry-trigger parsing; annotation extractor on fixture README/help snippets (stronger-wording, missing-id-numeric, superlative-without-id all rejected; compliant text passes).
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary registry JSON mutations → typed validation errors, never panics; extractor never false-passes a numeric token adjacent to a percent/×/tok/s unit without an id annotation in fixture corpora. Log the offending file/line/claim-id on every rejection.
- E2E: full-repo run of the enforcement job with DETAILED LOGGING (files scanned, ids resolved, states checked); no model gating — pure docs/tooling. Named entrypoint: `scripts/check_claims.sh` (invoked by `scripts/check.sh` in CI and by the governance umbrella driver `scripts/e2e_governance_validate.sh`); every rejection logs file:line, claim id, and registry state vs offending wording (expected-vs-actual), and the run ends with a machine-parseable summary line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SCAFFOLD — CI (`scripts/check.sh`) and repo layout must exist for the enforcement job to hook into.
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract target(s) claims_registry green in the 24/26-green no-fail-fast suite (only canonjson + dependency_policy red)

title: [P1] Write minimal dependency-free SentencePiece protobuf reader with fuzzed limits
description:
## Background
franken_nlp is a pure-Rust, memory-safe, CPU-hyper-optimized library + CLI (`fnlp` / `franken_nlp`) that runs exactly ONE model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d — as a local NLP toolbox. The model is a dense Llama-family decoder WITH A LOOP: 22 physical layers executed twice per token (44 logical layer executions), KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots per position, final RMSNorm after EACH pass (loop 2 consumes loop-1 normalized output). head_dim is 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

The pinned `tokenizer.model` is a SentencePiece protobuf (`ModelProto`) whose trainer spec declares `model_type=2` (BPE) with an identity normalizer and byte pieces. The dependency allowlist (clap, serde/serde_json, sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite) contains NO protobuf crate and never will, so we write a minimal, dependency-free protobuf reader for exactly the fields the tokenizer needs — the same discipline as franken_ocr's in-crate HF-JSON BPE reader. Every downstream tokenizer surface (encode/decode engine, `fnlp tokens`, the UntrustedDocument boundary) parses the model file through this one reader.

## Contract
- New module under `src/tokenizer/` (e.g. `spm_proto.rs`): a hand-written wire-format reader for the SentencePiece `ModelProto` subset we consume. No code generation, no `prost`/`protobuf` crates, `std` only.
- ACCEPTED FIELD SET is explicit and closed: `pieces` (repeated SentencePiece: `piece` string, `score` f32, `type` enum covering NORMAL/UNKNOWN/CONTROL/USER_DEFINED/BYTE/UNUSED), the `trainer_spec` fields needed to assert `model_type=2` (BPE), the `normalizer_spec` fields needed to assert the identity normalizer, and the special-piece id fields (unk/bos/eos/pad). Every other field number is skipped by wire type (varint, 64-bit, length-delimited, 32-bit); groups (wire types 3/4) reject as unsupported.
- HARD LIMITS, each an explicit named constant with a typed error: maximum varint length (10 bytes; an unterminated or >10-byte varint rejects), maximum message nesting depth, maximum piece count (must comfortably admit the pinned 166,144-piece vocab; cap on the order of 2,000,000), maximum single piece string length, maximum total input byte length, and a maximum-total-allocation bound so a hostile length prefix cannot force a huge up-front allocation (allocate incrementally, never `Vec::with_capacity(attacker_len)`).
- REJECT CLEANLY (typed error, no panic, no partial state): unterminated varints; varint/length overflow; length-delimited fields running past the buffer; conflicting DUPLICATE occurrences of a singular field (last-wins is NOT acceptable — duplicate singular fields with differing payloads are a parse error); piece strings that are invalid UTF-8; truncated input; trailing garbage where a message must end.
- Output is a typed `SpmModel` (pieces + scores + types + special ids + asserted model_type/normalizer facts) consumed by the BPE engine bead; this bead does not implement encode/decode.
- The reader must parse the pinned tokenizer.model bytes byte-identically on every target (pure integer/string parsing; no float reinterpretation beyond exact f32 bit reads of score fields).

## Constraints
- Dependency universe is closed: clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite only; NO protobuf/tokenizers/tiktoken crates (doctrine: tokenizer is ours). `unsafe_code = "deny"`; this module gets no unsafe island.
- No Rayon anywhere in the release graph; parsing is single-threaded and allocation-bounded.
- Forced tokens ≠ forced bytes and G1 > G2 are downstream concerns; this bead's binding rule is fail-closed parsing: any malformed input rejects with a typed error, never a best-effort model.
- Never create sibling "V2" files; this is the one reader.

## Evidence / gates

Recorded in the conformance harness output; the L0 tokenizer gate downstream is the end proof.

title: [4A] Build typed step DAG scheduler: shared linear groups, ragged attention, morsels, decode preemption
description:
## Background
The NLP workloads are corpus-shaped: thousands of short documents × one shared task prompt. Sequential batch-1 decode of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) logically visits ≈3.7 GB of packed weight payload per token per document; a compatible M-row layer-major operation amortizes those logical visits toward 3.7 GB/M. This bead is the typed step DAG scheduler (`batchsched.rs`) — the structural throughput lever. The loop is the architecture: never size or schedule this as a conventional 22-layer model.

## Contract
- **Loop-major step plan**: `for loop in 0..2 { for layer in 0..22 { batched ops over compatible rows } final_norm(rows) }` — one logical batched operation per physical layer per loop over all compatible rows, versus 2M independent batch-1 layer operations. Per-(loop, layer) KV binding `layer + loop×22` resolved at engine build; no hash-map lookups in the hot loop.
- **Typed step DAG**: `norm/quantize → shared linear group → per-row or ragged attention group → shared output/MLP group`, preserving each row's dependencies and KV destination. Compatibility keys are defined per node and belong to the model-checked scheduler spec.
- **Shared linear groups are keyed `(recipe, numerics profile, loop, layer, op kind)` — attention shape NEVER keys linear stages.** Q/K/V/O and MLP linear work batches rows with different context lengths because the fixed K/N weight shapes (K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}) match regardless of position. Requiring one identical whole-layer "attention shape" would fragment a heterogeneous corpus toward batch-1 and surrender exactly the weight-stream amortization batching exists for.
- **Ragged attention groups** receive explicit sequence lengths/page tables and group rows more narrowly only where the kernel requires it. Prefill and decode rows mix only at operator boundaries proven semantically compatible; no kernel receives a padding or mask convention merely because two rows were convenient to place together.
- **Bounded prefill morsels**: long prefills are chunked so one 200K-token document cannot monopolize a step. **Decode max-wait preemption**: decode latency has an explicit maximum-wait budget and can preempt further prefill admission between morsels.
- Static range assignment is the deterministic fallback; any work-stealing candidate must preserve per-row reduction order and beat the fixed schedule in the ledger.
- **Determinism mechanism, stated precisely**: under `strict-quantized-vN`, batch composition must not change any sequence's tokens. Integer paths (int8 GEMM/GEMV, i32 accumulation) are exact regardless of blocking, hence batch-invariant by construction; f32 paths (norms, softmax, attention accumulation, dequant-scale application) must keep per-row reduction order identical between M=1 and M>1 kernel variants — a kernel-selection rule the gate enforces, not an accident. `fast-vN` carries its own contract and may not reuse strict-profile cache entries.
- Receipts report both logical weight visits and measured DRAM/cache traffic; the amortization crossover is a deliverable, never "M=32 fixes it".
- `--batch 1` (and the library default) preserves the simple sequential latency path.

## Constraints
The scheduler issues work only inside the sealed scoped-CPU team; leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon in the release graph; admission precedes scheduling (certificate bead); checkpoints at tile/morsel boundaries with declared max uninterruptible quanta; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; G1>G2 — a faster schedule that changes greedy tokens for the same recipe/profile is reverted and memorialized in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

## Evidence / gates
Scheduler automaton/interleaving tests green (deterministic Lab runs for the async half + the bounded team-state model for the OS-thread half). The batch-M ≡ batch-1 token-exact determinism gate under `strict-quantized-vN` (also surfaced in the 4A daemon bead) depends on this scheduler's reduction-order rule. Morsel/preemption behavior measured with p50/p95/p99 decode-wait distributions in the perf ledger.

## Tests
Unit: DAG construction for a mixed prefill/decode row set — linear groups keyed exactly `(recipe, profile, loop, layer, op kind)`, ragged attention receives explicit lengths; KV binding table = layer + loop×22 for all 44 slots. Property: random row mixes → every row's op sequence equals its batch-1 op sequence (order-preserving projection); no step exceeds the morsel bound; decode wait never exceeds its budget in simulated schedules. Integration: batch-M vs batch-1 token-exact on fixture rows under strict profile; loop-boundary fixture (loop-1 post-norm feeds loop-2 layer-0). Detailed logging: per-step group composition, morsel ids, preemption events, and reduction-order variant selected — all replayable. Scheduler Lab scenarios (the async half) live in the named deliverable `tests/lab_scheduler_scenarios.rs`; every scenario run logs scenario id + seed machine-parseably so failures replay from the log alone. Model-gated e2e: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without weights.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (sealed-team bead): all batched steps execute on the sealed formation team's command lanes.
- (admission-certificate bead): rows enter the DAG only after certificate admission; M derives from it.
- A_GQA (cross-epic): the native 48:8 GQA/decode attention kernel is the ragged-attention substage this DAG drives.
- A_DISPATCH (cross-epic): the measured dispatch table selects the kernel variant per (ISA, shape, regime) for every DAG node.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **Loop-major step plan + KV binding table.** Deliverable: the `for loop in 0..2 { for layer in 0..22 { batched ops over compatible rows } final_norm(rows) }` skeleton with per-(loop, layer) KV binding `layer + loop×22` resolved at engine build — no hash-map lookups in the hot loop. Test evidence: unit KV-binding table = layer + loop×22 for all 44 slots; the loop-boundary fixture (loop-1 post-norm feeds loop-2 layer-0). Next milestone assumes: correct loop/layer/KV addressing for DAG construction.
2. **Typed step DAG construction with compatibility keys.** Deliverable: the `norm/quantize → shared linear group → per-row or ragged attention group → shared output/MLP group` DAG preserving each row's dependencies and KV destination, with linear groups keyed exactly `(recipe, numerics profile, loop, layer, op kind)` — attention shape NEVER keys linear stages, so fixed K/N shapes (K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}) batch rows of different context lengths; compatibility keys live in the model-checked scheduler spec. Test evidence: unit DAG construction for a mixed prefill/decode row set with exact keying; property — every row's op sequence equals its batch-1 op sequence (order-preserving projection). Next milestone assumes: a correct DAG shape onto which attention grouping attaches.
3. **Ragged attention groups.** Deliverable: attention groups receiving explicit sequence lengths/page tables, grouped more narrowly only where the kernel requires it; prefill and decode rows mix only at operator boundaries proven semantically compatible; no kernel receives a padding or mask convention merely from co-placement. Test evidence: unit — ragged attention receives explicit lengths in constructed DAGs for mixed row sets. Next milestone assumes: semantically safe attention grouping so scheduling/preemption can chunk work freely.
4. **Bounded prefill morsels + decode max-wait preemption + static-range fallback.** Deliverable: morsel chunking so one 200K-token document cannot monopolize a step; an explicit decode maximum-wait budget that can preempt further prefill admission between morsels; static range assignment as the deterministic fallback (any work-stealing candidate must preserve per-row reduction order and beat the fixed schedule in the ledger); checkpoints at tile/morsel boundaries with declared max uninterruptible quanta. Test evidence: property — no step exceeds the morsel bound and decode wait never exceeds its budget in simulated schedules; scheduler automaton/interleaving tests green (deterministic Lab runs for the async half, bounded team-state model for the OS-thread half); p50/p95/p99 decode-wait distributions recorded in the perf ledger. Next milestone assumes: deterministic bounded scheduling on which the determinism gate is meaningful.
5. **Strict-profile batch-invariance determinism gate.** Deliverable: the enforced kernel-selection rule — under `strict-quantized-vN`, integer paths (int8 GEMM/GEMV, i32 accumulation) are exact regardless of blocking, and f32 paths (norms, softmax, attention accumulation, dequant-scale application) keep per-row reduction order identical between M=1 and M>1 variants; `fast-vN` carries its own contract and never reuses strict-profile cache entries. Test evidence: integration batch-M ≡ batch-1 token-exact on fixture rows under the strict profile (model-gated e2e: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without weights); G1>G2 enforcement — a faster schedule that changes greedy tokens is reverted and memorialized in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md. Next milestone assumes: token-exact batching, so receipts and perf reporting cannot drift semantics.
6. **Receipts, replayable logging, and the `--batch 1` path.** Deliverable: receipts reporting both logical weight visits and measured DRAM/cache traffic with the amortization crossover as a deliverable (never "M=32 fixes it"); per-step group composition, morsel ids, preemption events, and reduction-order variant selected — all replayable; `--batch 1` (and the library default) preserving the simple sequential latency path. Test evidence: detailed-logging replay fixtures; ledger entries showing the measured crossover; batch-1 path exercised by the existing unit/property suites.

title: [4A] Implement KV slab allocator: refcounted slabs, COW fork tails, zero inner-loop allocation
description:
## Background
KV for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; 8 KV heads; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) is 44-deep: 180,224 B = 176 KiB per token bf16. A 16-token page across all 44 slots totals ≈2.75 MiB — far too much to clone on a small fork. If pages were indivisible 44-slot allocations, every continuation-trie fork and every cancellation would amplify memory retention. This bead builds the slab allocator that makes forks, cancellation, and admission accounting structural.

## Contract
- **Logical page group ≠ physical allocation**: a 16-token range (initial candidate; measured) is a logical page group. Physical slabs are independently allocated and reference-counted by `(token range, loop-layer group, K|V, dtype)` — or another measured bounded grouping. Candidate groupings compared for page-table overhead, TLB behavior, prefill writes, decode scans, fork fan-out, and cancellation: one loop-layer; 2/4/8 loop-layers; K and V together or separate; all-44-slots-in-one-page as a measured candidate, never the baseline.
- **COW fork tails**: sealed immutable pages plus small fork-tail slabs (down to one token) are weighed against explicit tail copy/recompute; admission prices the actual parent-fill state and fan-out before branching.
- **Lazy allocation from a byte-capped pool**: KV pages are allocated only at admission/page boundaries from a pre-reserved pool; the inner token/layer loops perform ZERO general-allocator calls — enforced by an allocation-count test.
- Page tables, not one giant contiguous reservation, so cancellation and COW stay bounded; exact per-slab admission accounting (each slab's bytes charged to the aggregate ledger).
- Logical addressing `[loop-layer][head][position][128]` with 64-byte alignment; the physical paged order is selected by benchmark while preserving sequential position scans.
- Int8 KV (runtime-gated, later recipe stage) accounting is structural now: 88 KiB/token payload + 2,816 B/token f32 K/V scales per (loop-layer, KV head, token) (f16 scales 1,408 B) + padding + page-table overhead all counted.
- Refcount transitions on fork/drop/cancel are deterministic; dropping a fork releases only its tail slabs, never unrelated 44-slot storage.

## Constraints
Allocation only from the pre-reserved pool inside admitted envelopes (two-phase reservation upstream); no unsafe (safe Rust; any future mmap interaction stays in the enumerated island); system allocator only; no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; G1>G2; fork admission prices actual 44-deep tail bytes — "bounded" without a usable byte certificate is not a design.

## Evidence / gates
Allocation-count test proving zero general-allocator calls in inner loops. Per-slab admission accounting reconciles with the aggregate ledger byte-for-byte in a property test. Fork/cancel retention test: cancelling one fork releases exactly its slabs. Grouping benchmark rows (page-table overhead, scan traffic, fork amplification) recorded in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md before a default grouping is frozen.

## Tests
Unit: slab key `(token range, loop-layer group, K|V, dtype)` round-trip; refcount inc/dec on fork/drop; sealed-page immutability (writes to sealed pages are a type error or panic in debug). Property: random fork/append/cancel sequences → total charged bytes always equals live slab bytes; no leak, no double-free (refcount never negative); COW fork then parent-append never aliases. Integration: 2.75 MiB/16-token/44-slot arithmetic asserted from census constants, not re-derived ad hoc. Detailed logging: slab lifecycle events (alloc/seal/fork/release) with byte counts and owner request ids. Model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (admission-certificate bead): every slab allocation is priced against the certificate and aggregate ledger before the pool hands out bytes.
- A_FWD (cross-epic): the Phase-1 forward pass defines the 44-slot K/V write/read semantics (prefill append, decode scan) the slab layout must serve; slabs are sized/validated against its KV-append fixtures.

title: [GOV] Scaffold NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE, PERF_LEDGER, FEATURE_PARITY artifact-graph ledgers
description:
## Background
Three evidence ledgers scaffolded with a shared artifact-graph entry format: `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` (every rejected optimization — losers reverted with NO source landed, per the 5-pass loop), `docs/PERF_LEDGER.md` (every performance measurement, winners AND slower rows), and `docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md` (honest feature-parity matrix vs the reference stack). These are the memory of the measured-everything doctrine: a rejected idea that is not ledgered will be re-attempted and re-burned. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Shared artifact-graph entry format (all three files):** `claim_id` (links docs/CLAIMS.json where applicable), evidence description, fixture hashes, CPU feature string (exact — e.g. which of AVX2/VNNI-256/VNNI-512/SDOT/I8MM the host advertised), exact command + environment (thread count, allocator, numerics profile, recipe id), disposition.
- **NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md:** entry per rejected optimization: hypothesis, the 5-pass measurement loop results, why it lost (slower / violated parity / unprovable bounds), revert proof (no source landed), and the conditions under which re-evaluation is justified. Seed rows reserved for: raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` (banned by construction — pre-registered as rejected), and any Phase-2 converter shortcut that changed output bytes.
- **PERF_LEDGER.md:** entry per measurement campaign: regime (R0 cold/warm startup, R1 latency generate, R2 corpus scoring, R3 corpus generation, R4 long-context), host fingerprint, artifact recipe + packing set + kernel table + load mode, p50/p95/p99, thread/allocator/precision fairness controls, and the labeled bandwidth denominator (logical tensor bytes vs packed payload bytes vs measured DRAM bytes — never conflated; STREAM peak and vendor TOPS are context, not attainable denominators). Slower rows STAY in the ledger.
- **FEATURE_PARITY.md:** matrix rows per surface with state ∈ {present, partial, missing, n/a} — `partial` NEVER rounds up to `present`; each `partial` names what is missing and the gating bead/phase.
- All three get: schema header, linter (shared with the BEHAVIOR/DISCREPANCIES linter infrastructure where sensible), and frozen negative fixtures (entry missing CPU feature string; `partial` presented as `present`; perf row without fairness controls).

## Constraints
- Docs + validator tooling only; deps clap/serde/serde_json/sha2. No Rayon. Honest-measurement doctrine is binding: gauntlet comparisons use thread/allocator/precision fairness controls; a ledger row without its controls named is schema-invalid. Sibling-project wins (franken_ocr/frankensearch) are PRIORS, not this project's measurements — the schema has a `prior` disposition to record them distinctly.

## Evidence / gates
- Scaffolds + linter green in CI; frozen negative fixtures fail as designed.
- Cross-link check: every `claim_id` referenced exists in docs/CLAIMS.json (soft-pending until the cross-registry validator bead lands; this bead ships the local check).
- Close cites file paths, linter job, fixtures.

## Tests
- Unit: entry parsers for all three schemas; parity-state enum strictness; disposition enum (won | rejected | prior | deferred); CPU-feature-string presence; command+env presence.
- Property/fuzz: mutated entries → typed lint errors; no panic on arbitrary markdown around entries. Log file/line/entry-id per rejection.
- E2E: CI linter run over the real docs with DETAILED LOGGING; no model gating. The linter ships as `scripts/lint_ledgers.sh` wired into `scripts/check.sh` and the governance umbrella driver `scripts/e2e_governance_validate.sh`; rejections log file:line, entry id, and the missing/invalid field expected-vs-actual, ending with a machine-parseable summary line (entries linted per ledger, failures by class).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SCAFFOLD — docs tree + CI hook must exist.

title: [4A] Implement prefix cache: ExecutionIdentity keys, shipped-prefix default, fork-equals-cold gate, deterministic LRU
description:
## Background
Corpus workloads share one task prompt across thousands of documents. Prefilling that shared prefix once and forking page references copy-on-write is a first-order win for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), where every cached prefix token saves 176 KiB of recomputed KV across 44 slots. But a cache keyed too loosely is a correctness bug and a privacy leak. This bead builds the prefix cache in `kv.rs`.

## Contract
- **Key = exact prefix token ids + a named projection of `ExecutionIdentity`**: artifact/recipe digest, tokenizer/template/prompt hashes, thinking/tool mode, RoPE/numerics/KV dtype, and kernel-semantic version. Any field outside the projection must be provably irrelevant to KV bytes.
- **Default eligibility is shipped task/system prefixes ONLY — never arbitrary user document text**, so cross-request reuse cannot leak private content. User-prefix caching is explicit opt-in AND namespace-isolated (per engine/namespace; user-content caches stay isolated even when public immutable weights are shared).
- **Fork ≡ cold gate**: a forked prefix must equal cold prefill exactly (token-exact and KV-byte-exact under the same profile). This is an invariant, not a tolerance.
- **Deterministic LRU with a byte budget** is the v1 eviction policy. S3-FIFO becomes a candidate only after traces show scan pollution (AA-C1 gate); no speculative fancy eviction.
- `fast-vN` numerics may not reuse `strict-quantized-vN` cache entries (profile is in the key).
- Fork admission goes through the KV slab allocator's COW tails; eviction releases slab refcounts deterministically.

## Constraints
Cache privacy is an invariant gate; namespace-complete keys; no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; presets are data (shipped prefixes come from hashed preset packs); G1>G2 — a cache hit that changes tokens is a reverted bug, never a tolerance; byte budget charged to the aggregate ledger.

## Evidence / gates
Prefix-fork ≡ cold-prefill exact equivalence fixture (invariant-gate suite). Cache-privacy test: two engines/namespaces with different user opt-in state cannot observe each other's entries; a default-config run never caches document-derived prefixes. Deterministic-eviction fixture: same insertion sequence → same eviction sequence.

## Tests
Unit: key projection includes exactly the named ExecutionIdentity fields (adding/removing a field breaks a golden); opt-in flag gates user-prefix insertion; byte budget enforcement evicts deterministically. Property: random insert/hit/evict sequences → LRU order deterministic and byte budget never exceeded; fork-then-evict never invalidates live forks (refcounts protect). Integration: fork ≡ cold on fixture prompts (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without weights; scalar-spec-engine fixtures otherwise). Detailed logging: hit/miss/evict events with key digests (never raw user text) and byte accounting.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (KV slab allocator bead): COW forks and eviction operate on refcounted slabs; the cache cannot exist before them.
- A_EXECID (cross-epic): the canonical `ExecutionIdentity` type this cache's key projects from.

title: [GOV] Define .fnlpr receipt schema + emitters: completeness grades, HMAC content commitments
description:
## Background
`.fnlpr` receipts are the typed-evidence output of every significant run: canonical, schema-versioned JSON binding the semantic request, artifacts, code/profile, datasets/fixtures, checks executed, output identities, and evidence links. This bead defines the schema and the emitter library the engine/CLI call. The hard parts are honesty (completeness GRADES, not a boolean "verified") and privacy (public receipts never leak content hashes of private or low-entropy data). Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Completeness grades (every receipt declares exactly one):** `Replayable` (all authorized inputs/artifacts and any required commitment secret resolvable under the retention policy) · `StructuralReplay` (structure/cost/provenance replayable, private content absent) · `VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied` (identities retained; caller must supply bytes and any required secret) · `AuditOnly` (historical facts, no replay claim). "Verified receipt" WITHOUT a grade is forbidden; a digest/commitment proves identity, not future resolvability.
- **Privacy:** public/exported receipts NEVER expose a raw SHA-256 of private or low-entropy input/output (raw hashes of low-entropy content are dictionary-invertible). A durable job reuses its per-job HMAC commitments (§8.4 keys); an ad-hoc private run either creates an owner-only per-receipt 256-bit commitment secret or omits content identity and accepts the lower grade. The exported projection contains ONLY domain-separated HMAC commitments plus a NONSECRET commitment-key id; the secret and private bytes appear only under an explicit owner-authorized retention policy.
- **Binding set:** semantic request; artifact digests (full taxonomy: source_root/logical_model/packing_set/license_bundle/fnlpq_file as applicable); code identity (converter/binary commit); numerics profile; recipe id; prompt-template hash; dataset/fixture digests; checks executed with verdicts; output identities (or commitments); evidence links. Every cache/receipt key derives from the ONE canonical `ExecutionIdentity` type — no parallel ad-hoc identity tuples.
- **Concurrency-failure receipts:** bind the lab seed + trace fingerprint + crashpack id + the exact replay command, so a scheduler defect's receipt is `StructuralReplay`-grade BY CONSTRUCTION, not a prose apology.
- Canonical bytes: same duplicate-key-rejecting, order-specified JSON discipline as the `.fnlpq` header (fixed structs, pinned escape form, no arbitrary Value maps); schema-versioned with no pre-1.0 compatibility shims.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite (HMAC built on the approved sha2 surface — HMAC-SHA-256 per RFC 2104 implemented in-repo over sha2, no new crate). No Rayon. Receipts are metadata-only by default: no hidden input/output retention; content bytes only under explicit owner-authorized retention. Robot-mode receipts are NDJSON-embeddable; stdout data, stderr diagnostics.

## Evidence / gates
- Schema + golden receipt fixtures for all four grades; a graded-wording lint (the string "verified" may not appear ungraded in receipt-rendering code paths — enforced by a frozen fixture test).
- Privacy gate: an exported fixture receipt for a private low-entropy input contains NO raw SHA-256 of that input (test greps commitments only; the raw digest is computed in-test and asserted ABSENT from the exported bytes).
- Domain-separation gate: HMAC domains for input/output/config commitments are distinct constants; cross-domain collision fixture rejects.
- Close cites schema path, fixtures, lint job.

## Tests
- Unit: grade enum + required-field matrix per grade; HMAC-SHA-256 test vectors (RFC 4231); key-id nonsecrecy (key id present, key absent); ExecutionIdentity → receipt-key derivation determinism.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary receipt JSON mutations → typed schema errors; exported projection never contains a byte-substring equal to any registered private raw digest (property harness over random low-entropy corpora). Log the violating field path on every failure.
- E2E: a synthetic pipeline run emits receipts at each stage (convert/pull/inference stub) with DETAILED LOGGING of grade decisions and commitment-key ids; a simulated lab concurrency failure emits the StructuralReplay receipt with seed/fingerprint/crashpack/replay-command bound. No model gating — synthetic runs suffice; real-run receipts arrive with their host beads.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SCAFFOLD — crate/CI/error-map skeleton; A_EXECID — the canonical ExecutionIdentity type receipts key from; A_G0_CENSUS — OQ-35 census ratifies the lab seed/trace/crashpack surfaces the concurrency-receipt binding depends on.

title: [4A] Build grammar schema compiler: normative JSON-Schema subset, bounded numerics, fnlp schema check/sample
description:
## Background
G8 — valid-by-construction structured output — is a headline guarantee: every successful structured response validates, and failure is a typed no-result, never partial success. This bead builds the grammar schema compiler in `grammar/` that turns a user JSON Schema into a bounded typed-JSON automaton for constrained decoding on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144 — so a per-state legal mask is 20,768 bytes; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). It also ships the model-free CLI `fnlp schema check` / `fnlp schema sample`.

## Contract
- **Normative v1 subset (accept)**: root and nested `type` ∈ {object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, null}; `enum`/`const` over JSON scalars; object `properties`/`required` with MANDATORY `additionalProperties:false`; arrays with `items` and a finite effective `maxItems` (schema value or engine cap); finite string/output byte caps; the namespaced string annotation `"x-fnlp-source":"verbatim"` (activates the source product, gated on OQ-17).
- **Reject before model load, by keyword**: `$ref`, recursion, `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`not`, `patternProperties`, arbitrary `additionalProperties`, `uniqueItems`, `contains`, `minimum` (and sibling semantic numeric keywords), `multipleOf`, `format`, general `pattern`, and `verbatim-normalized` — each until it has a valid-by-construction implementation.
- **Bounded numerics without routing schema authority through f64**: `integer` is an exact signed/unsigned 64-bit value (optional stricter task ranges); `number` is an exact finite decimal `(sign, coefficient, base-10 exponent)` with ≤38 significant digits and normalized scientific adjusted exponent in [−308, 308]. Parsing uses checked `u128` coefficient arithmetic; overflow, excessive digits/exponent, or excessive lexeme length rejects; values never round. Every negative-zero spelling canonicalizes to `0`. Canonical output: `0` for zero; plain base-10 for integral values in the integer domain; lowercase normalized scientific notation for non-integral values (one leading digit, no redundant coefficient zeros, no `+` in the exponent).
- **Mathematical numeric equality for enum/const**: schema literals `1`, `1.0`, and `1e0` denote the SAME value (JSON Schema mathematical equality inside the bounded domain, not lexical or f64 equality), canonicalized to one spelling; the compiler rejects duplicate semantically equal enum members so generation and independent validation cannot disagree.
- **Strings**: RFC-8259-compatible escape/UTF-8 lexers; escape emission (which characters are emitted escaped vs raw) is specified as part of the canonical output contract.
- **Compile target**: a bounded typed-JSON automaton — ordered keys with optional/required transitions, enum tries, canonical number lexers. State/transition counts and estimated mask-cache bytes are computed with CHECKED arithmetic and compared against per-request caps BEFORE any allocation (checked state/mask-byte preflight).
- Canonical object-key order and JSON number spelling are part of the output schema contract. Every parser boundary rejects duplicate JSON object keys rather than accepting parser-dependent overwrite.
- **CLI**: `fnlp schema check` compiles + resource-checks with no model load; `fnlp schema sample` walks only the supported grammar to emit valid instances (DX + fuzz-seed reuse). Neither loads weights.

## Constraints
Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite — no llguidance or any grammar library; the tokenizer is ours; no Rayon; unsafe denied; G8 has G1 rank; unsupported keywords fail closed pre-model; every reachable nonaccepting state must have a path to acceptance within the configured remaining output bound or compilation rejects the request; forbidden claims: none of this is "any schema" support.

## Evidence / gates
Golden + hostile fixture families: integer/number cross-form equality (1 ≡ 1.0 ≡ 1e0), signed zero, exponent forms, coefficient/exponent boundaries, equivalent decimals, values adjacent to the 64-bit/38-digit limits. Rejection-by-keyword table golden. Preflight cap tests: a schema whose state/mask estimate exceeds per-request caps rejects before allocation. `schema check`/`schema sample` golden CLI outputs. Compiler fuzz: arbitrary input → compile-or-clean-error, never dead/unbounded state.

## Tests
Unit: every accepted keyword and every rejected keyword individually; duplicate-equal-enum rejection; negative-zero canonicalization; u128 checked overflow paths. Property/fuzz: random supported schemas compile and `schema sample` outputs re-validate; random byte inputs never panic the compiler; depth/length/empty-language boundaries; dead-state search finds none. E2E: `fnlp schema check` on the fixture corpus exits 0/typed-error correctly with NO model present (this surface must be fully green in ordinary CI — no SKIPPED_NO_MODEL needed here). Detailed logging: compile reports state/transition/mask-byte estimates and the rejecting keyword + JSON pointer on failure. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_schema_check_golden.sh` (model-free, green in ordinary CI): the fixture corpus through `fnlp schema check`/`schema sample`, one machine-parseable row per schema (accept/reject, rejecting keyword + JSON pointer, state/mask estimates, exit code).

## Dependencies & rationale
- A_SCAFFOLD (cross-epic): crate, CLI dispatch, typed error map, and duplicate-key-rejecting JSON primitives must exist to host `grammar/` and the `schema` subcommands.

title: [GOV] Implement OPERATION_COSTS.json structural witnesses + cross-registry validator
description:
## Background
`docs/OPERATION_COSTS.json` records exact STRUCTURAL WITNESSES — counters both the scalar and optimized engines emit — so equal semantic output can never hide accidentally duplicated model work (e.g. an engine quietly running the 2-pass loop twice, or projecting all 166,144 lm_head rows when a slice sufficed). This bead builds the witness schema, the emitter trait both engines implement, the CROSS-REGISTRY REFERENCE VALIDATOR spanning all governance artifacts, and frozen negative fixtures. Serves the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- **Witness fields (emitted by scalar AND optimized engines):** invocation kind; loop passes; physical-layer executions; token positions; lm_head rows evaluated; candidate-trie nodes; KV logical bytes and KV committed bytes; source-automaton transitions; cache hits BY DEPENDENCY SCOPE (ItemLocal / PartitionReduce / CorpusGlobal); generated tokens.
- **The loop invariant is numeric and exact:** a `target_full` invocation has EXACTLY 2 loop passes and 44 physical-layer executions per token position (22 physical layers × 2 loops; the two post-loop final-RMSNorm states are norm states, not extra layer executions). Any future AA-D1 loop-1 draft projection is counted SEPARATELY as `draft_loop1` (one pass plus its projection) and can NEVER be labeled a target invocation.
- **Anti-hiding property:** scalar-vs-optimized witness comparison is a gate — same semantic run, same structural counts (up to documented, witness-visible optimizations like row-sliced lm_head, where the count itself is the evidence: rows evaluated < 166,144 with the slice named). Hardware time/energy remain benchmark measurements and are NOT structural counters — the schema forbids them here.
- KV byte scale sanity anchors: bf16 KV is 180,224 B = 176 KiB per token per sequence across 44 slots (int8 payload 88 KiB + 2,816 B/token f32 K/V scales or 1,408 B f16); a 16-token KV range ≈ 2.75 MiB — witness totals must reconcile with these formulas on fixtures.
- **Cross-registry reference validator:** every `claim_id` in NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/PERF_LEDGER/FEATURE_PARITY resolves in docs/CLAIMS.json; every discrepancy rollback names an existing mechanism; every receipt evidence-link resolves; every OPERATION_COSTS witness schema version matches the emitters; BEHAVIOR_NOTES ids referenced by fixtures exist. Dangling references fail CI.
- **Frozen negative fixtures:** a witness stream claiming 1 pass for `target_full`; 44 executions across 2 positions (should be 88); `draft_loop1` labeled as target; a time-per-token field smuggled into structural counters; a dangling claim_id — each must fail, frozen forever.

## Constraints
- Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2. No Rayon. Registry files have canonical schemas, a version migration policy (no compatibility shims before 1.0; regenerate deliberately), and complement — never replace — L0–L5, task scorecards, hostile tests, or human review. Witness emission must be cheap enough for always-on robot mode (counter increments, no allocation in leaves; leaves never spawn).

## Evidence / gates
- Witness-invariant gate green: scalar fixture engine run over N positions emits passes=2N/positions, layer executions=44 per position exactly; negative fixtures fail.
- Cross-registry validator green over the real docs tree; a planted dangling reference fails (frozen fixture).
- Scalar-vs-optimized comparison harness wired (consumed by later kernel beads; the harness + schema land here). Close cites schema path, validator job, fixture inventory.

## Tests
- Unit: schema field completeness; target_full arithmetic (2 passes, 44 executions/position); draft_loop1 separation; dependency-scope enum; KV byte reconciliation formulas (176 KiB/token bf16; 88 KiB int8 payload).
- Property/fuzz: random witness streams → validator verdicts deterministic and typed; no panic on arbitrary JSON. Log the violated invariant + witness index on every rejection.
- E2E: CI run of the cross-registry validator over the full docs tree with DETAILED LOGGING (references resolved per registry, counts); engine-emission e2e uses the scalar fixture engine (synthetic weights) — real-model witness runs arrive with the engine beads; nothing here is model-gated. Named runnable driver: `scripts/e2e_governance_validate.sh` — runs the cross-registry validator plus the ledger/claims/behavior linters (shipped by their own beads) in one pass, logging per-registry timestamps, resolved/dangling reference counts, each planted negative fixture's expected-vs-actual verdict, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- docs/CLAIMS.json registry: the validator resolves claim ids against it.
- BEHAVIOR_NOTES/DISCREPANCIES scaffolds: validator checks their ids and rollback-mechanism references.
- NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/PERF_LEDGER/FEATURE_PARITY scaffolds: validator checks their claim_id links and entry schemas.
- .fnlpr receipt schema: validator resolves receipt evidence-links; witness ids appear in receipts.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SCAFFOLD — CI + docs tree must exist.

title: [4A] Build vocab-trie mask oracle + detokenization transducer with privacy-separated mask cache
description:
## Background
The hard part of constrained decoding is tokenization alignment: one token may cross several grammar states. For the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; SentencePiece BPE tokenizer; vocab 166,144 → a per-state legal mask is 20,768 bytes; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) the mask oracle must reason in detokenized BYTES, not raw SentencePiece piece text. This bead builds the vocab trie, the detokenization transducer, and the privacy-separated lazy mask cache.

## Contract
- **Vocab-trie mask oracle**: consumes detokenized byte transitions through a vocab trie over all 166,144 pieces, built when the approved tokenizer asset loads. SentencePiece word-boundary and byte-fallback behavior belong to the **detokenization transducer**; raw piece text is NEVER treated as emitted bytes.
- **Cache key**: `(tokenizer_digest, schema_digest, grammar_version)`. The global cross-request cache holds ONLY the reusable schema×tokenizer product.
- **Lazy, byte-budgeted per-state masks**: masks materialize on demand under a byte budget so an attacker cannot force `states × vocab` memory (166,144 bits = 20,768 B per dense state; the preflight from the grammar compiler bounds the estimate, this bead enforces it at runtime).
- **Privacy separation (hard rule)**: document-specific substring/source automata, occurrence indexes, logical-unescape products, and ANY mask containing source-derived transitions are request-owned and NEVER enter the global cross-request cache. An explicitly opted-in durable job may reuse them only inside its private namespace and storage policy.
- **Cache accounting separates immutable schema masks from source-derived state**, so an eviction trace or `robot health` report cannot reveal document substrings or equality relationships (memory + privacy: sizes of source-derived state are reported only in aggregate request-local terms).

## Constraints
Tokenizer is ours (embedded Apache-2.0 bytes, hash-checked against the artifact copy at load); no tokenizers/tiktoken/llguidance crates; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; checkpoints inside long mask expansions (declared max uninterruptible quantum — a 166,144-piece trie walk cannot monopolize cancellation); cache privacy is an invariant gate; G1>G2.

## Evidence / gates
Mask-oracle differential: for sampled grammar states, the lazy masked set equals the brute-force set computed by walking every vocab piece through the transducer. Byte-budget adversarial test: hostile schema/state sequences cannot exceed the mask budget. Privacy gate: after processing a document, the global cache contains zero source-derived entries (introspection test) and eviction traces expose no substrings. Cached-vs-uncached equality across (tokenizer_digest, schema_digest, grammar_version) key changes.

## Tests
Unit: byte-fallback pieces transduce to their exact bytes; word-boundary pieces produce the specified leading-space bytes; trie lookup for known pieces. Property/fuzz: every token-crossing class (token spans 2+ grammar states; state spans 2+ tokens; byte-fallback mid-string; non-ASCII/UTF-8 boundaries); random schemas × random walks — masked-legal tokens all extend to acceptance, masked-illegal tokens all fail. Concurrency: concurrent requests with different documents never observe each other's source-derived state. Detailed logging: mask materialization events with state id, bytes, budget remaining; cache hit/miss by key digest. Model-free surface — full green in ordinary CI; model-gated e2e reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (grammar schema compiler bead): the typed-JSON automaton and its state/mask preflight are the input this oracle masks against.
- A_TOK_L0 (cross-epic): the L0-exact SentencePiece tokenizer supplies the vocab pieces, digests, and byte-fallback semantics the transducer must mirror.

title: [4A] Build source-language product automaton: substring x typed-JSON x transducer with occurrence spec
description:
## Background
Source-grounded fields ("x-fnlp-source":"verbatim") promise that a successful value is a byte-exact substring of the original document BY CONSTRUCTION. That requires intersecting three machines during decoding on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; SentencePiece tokenizer with byte fallback; vocab 166,144; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half): the source substring automaton, the typed-JSON automaton, and the detokenization transducer. This bead builds that product automaton as SPECIFICATION, not implementation folklore.

## Contract
- **Product = bounded substring automaton over the original source bytes ∩ typed-JSON automaton ∩ tokenizer detokenization transducer.**
- **Escaping boundary**: the JSON lexer owns escaping; the source side sees logical UNESCAPED UTF-8 bytes. A source byte sequence containing `"` or `\` appears escaped in the JSON output while the source automaton matches the unescaped logical bytes.
- **Specified, not folkloric**: start-anywhere transitions (a match may begin at any source byte offset), finish transitions, empty-string handling, minimum-length constraints, repeated occurrences (the same substring appearing at multiple offsets), byte-fallback pieces, and offset recovery (mapping an accepted path back to candidate byte intervals) each get written spec text + fixtures.
- **Preflight**: source-index bytes are accounted before construction and the request rejects over budget (the index is request-owned state — see the mask-oracle privacy rule: it never enters the global cache).
- **Unsatisfiable required grounded field → typed task no-result** (exit-code-10 family; abstention is exit 0 + status abstained is a different surface). Nullable fields may emit `null` only if the schema permits it. There is NO silent unconstrained fallback — never emit an ungrounded string for a grounded field.

## Constraints
Forced tokens ≠ forced bytes (multiple tokenizations of one byte suffix have different KV/hidden states — the product constrains legality; it never licenses byte-level jump-forward); no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; checkpoints inside source-index construction (declared max uninterruptible quantum); request-owned memory only; G8 = G1 rank; G1>G2.

## Evidence / gates
Grounded-field property proofs (invariant-gate suite): every accepted grounded value independently occurs in the source under the named byte contract (verified by the independent validation module, which shares no state with this code). Occurrence-semantics fixtures: single occurrence, repeated occurrences, overlapping occurrences, empty/min-length edges. Unsatisfiable-field fixture returns the typed no-result. Budget-rejection fixture.

## Tests
Unit: escaping boundary (source bytes with quotes/backslashes/control chars round through JSON escapes; automaton matches logical bytes); start-anywhere and finish transitions; min-length enforcement. Property/fuzz: random source docs × random verbatim schemas — every constrained-decode walk that reaches acceptance yields a value that is a byte-exact substring; adversarial Unicode/escapes/repetition; empty-language cases reject at compile/preflight, not mid-decode; cancellation at every emitted token leaves no partial success. Integration: product with byte-fallback-only strings (non-BMP, invalid-start bytes in source handled per spec). Detailed logging: product-state transitions (state ids only, never raw source bytes in shared logs), preflight byte estimates, rejection reasons. Model-free construction tests green in CI; decode e2e is model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (grammar schema compiler bead): supplies the typed-JSON automaton side of the product.
- (mask-oracle/transducer bead): supplies the detokenization transducer and the request-owned-state privacy regime this product's indexes live under.

title: [4A] Build execution compiler: ProjectLegal, FeedForced proof witness, CopyFromSource, micro-prefill forced runs
description:
## Background
The execution compiler turns each grammar/source product state into exactly one exact primitive for the lm_head stage of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; untied lm_head 3072→166,144 — full f32 logits are 664,576 B, a dense legal mask is 20,768 B; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Doctrine: compile known structure, never approximate it — thresholds select between EQUIVALENT paths by measured cost, never by dropping candidates.

## Contract
- **Primitives** (each product state emits one): `ProjectLegal(all_legal_rows)` — evaluates EVERY legal lm_head row and no illegal row when the compiled legal set is below a measured threshold; exact for the conditioned distribution because omitted rows are impossible under the declared grammar; no heuristic may omit a legal row. `FeedForced(tokens)`. `CopyFromSource(state)`. Universal `FullProjection(mask)` — dense states AND the 20,768-byte legal mask into the full sampler scan.
- **FeedForced proof witness**: projection may be skipped ONLY when the intersection of (grammar/tokenizer legality ∩ EOS/min-length/stop policy ∩ banned-token policy ∩ repetition/presence/frequency processing ∩ logit bias ∩ tool/thinking phase policy ∩ every other enabled processor) leaves exactly one legal token id INDEPENDENTLY of its unknown raw logit, AND no logprob/legal-mass/margin/audit telemetry was requested. "The grammar alone has one edge" is insufficient — a later processor could ban or alter that edge. The compiled forced run stores a witness naming the processor-state facts that make projection irrelevant. Processor state that depends only on emitted ids (penalty windows) is STILL updated for every forced token. Any unsupported processor DISABLES the optimization rather than being ignored (OQ-8/OQ-32). If logprobs were requested, the projection is still performed.
- **Forced bytes ≠ forced tokens**: a uniquely determined byte suffix is NOT sufficient — multiple tokenizations of the same bytes lead to different hidden/KV states. Byte-level jump-forward, canonical retokenization, and token healing are EXCLUDED from this exact path.
- **Micro-prefill teacher forcing**: a maximal bounded run of uniquely forced token ids may be teacher-fed through a causal micro-prefill updating all 44 KV slots. The transformer work is never skipped. The micro-prefill must match sequential feeding at every token/KV point under the designated numerics contract, else the fallback is one-token feeding.
