OQ-19 measures whether exact-token runs occur often enough to keep this; rarity is acceptable negative evidence for docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.
- **Exactness invariants with universal fallbacks**: sparse `ProjectLegal` ≡ `FullProjection`-after-masking; forced ≡ sequential-KV feeding. Both are exact differential gates; the universal fallback (FullProjection / one-token feeding) always remains available, and no public task may depend on an optimized route whose fallback is not green.
- **Diagnostics, not truth**: optional full-projection audits may report pre-mask argmax legality, legal mass, and best-legal-minus-best-illegal margin. Sparse projection cannot know illegal logits → those fields are `not_computed`. These signals are never a fabrication detector, correctness probability, or calibrated confidence, and cannot alone authorize acceptance/escalation.

## Constraints
Compile known structure, never approximate it (doctrine #17); forced tokens still run all 44 effective layer executions; constraint pressure is not confidence (doctrine #18); no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; G1>G2 and G8 at the same rank; measured-faster wins for path selection among proven-equivalent paths only.

## Evidence / gates
Invariant-gate suite: sparse=full differential over random states (masked full projection vs sparse rows — logit-identical for legal rows, identical selection); forced=sequential-KV differential (micro-prefill vs one-token feeding — every KV slot byte-compared under the designated contract); witness-completeness test (each supported processor toggled adversarially so a forced edge becomes non-unique → optimization must disable). Phase-4A exit: no public task depends on an optimized route whose universal fallback is not green.

## Tests
Unit: witness construction for every processor combination; unsupported-processor disable path; `not_computed` propagation for sparse diagnostics. Property/fuzz: random grammars × processor stacks — selection outcomes identical between primitive path and universal fallback; penalty windows identical after forced runs vs sequential; forced runs with requested logprobs always project. Integration: CopyFromSource states hand off to the source product; cancellation checkpoints inside long forced runs. Detailed logging: every compiled primitive with state id, chosen path, threshold values, and witness contents; every fallback engagement logged with reason. Model-gated KV comparisons: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without weights (scalar spec engine covers structure in CI).

## Dependencies & rationale
- (mask-oracle/transducer bead): masks and byte transitions feed ProjectLegal/FullProjection legality.
- (source-product bead): CopyFromSource states and grounded legality come from the product automaton.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **`FullProjection(mask)` universal baseline.** Deliverable: the universal primitive — dense states AND the 20,768-byte legal mask into the full sampler scan, plus the optional full-projection audit fields (pre-mask argmax legality, legal mass, best-legal-minus-best-illegal margin) as diagnostics-not-truth. Test evidence: differential vs the unconstrained full scan (legal-row logits identical; masking changes only illegal-row eligibility; identical selection) and unit coverage that audit fields never authorize acceptance/escalation. Next milestone assumes: a green universal fallback exists for every optimized route to be differentially gated against.
2. **`ProjectLegal` sparse path + sparse==full gate.** Deliverable: sparse evaluation of EVERY legal lm_head row (no illegal row, no omitted legal row) selected below a measured threshold. Test evidence: the sparse ≡ `FullProjection`-after-masking differential over random states (logit-identical legal rows, identical selection) and unit tests for `not_computed` propagation on sparse diagnostics (illegal-logit fields). Next milestone assumes: both projection routes are proven equivalent, so forced-path work can gate against either.
3. **`FeedForced` single-token + processor-state witness + forced==sequential gate.** Deliverable: single-token forced feeding whose skip-projection decision requires the full witness — the intersection of grammar/tokenizer legality, EOS/min-length/stop, banned-token, repetition/presence/frequency, logit bias, tool/thinking phase, and every other enabled processor leaving exactly one legal id independently of its raw logit, with no logprob/legal-mass/margin/audit telemetry requested; penalty windows still updated per forced token; any unsupported processor disables the optimization (OQ-8/OQ-32); requested logprobs still project; forced bytes ≠ forced tokens (byte-level jump-forward, canonical retokenization, token healing excluded). Test evidence: witness-construction units for every processor combination; the witness-completeness test (each supported processor toggled adversarially so a forced edge becomes non-unique → optimization must disable); penalty-window equality after forced vs sequential; forced-with-logprobs always projects. Next milestone assumes: a proven one-token forced primitive exists as the fallback for any multi-token forced run.
4. **`CopyFromSource`.** Deliverable: the copy primitive for source product states, completing the one-primitive-per-product-state compiler surface. Test evidence: integration tests handing `CopyFromSource` states off to the source product; compiled-primitive logging (state id, chosen path) covers all four primitives. Next milestone assumes: every product state emits exactly one primitive, so whole-run compilation can be exercised.
5. **Micro-prefill maximal forced runs + KV-point equality.** Deliverable: bounded maximal runs of uniquely forced token ids teacher-fed through a causal micro-prefill updating all 44 KV slots (transformer work never skipped). Test evidence: the forced ≡ sequential-KV differential with every KV slot byte-compared under the designated numerics contract (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without weights; scalar spec engine covers structure in CI); cancellation checkpoints inside long forced runs; OQ-19 frequency measurement recorded, with rarity filed as negative evidence in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md if applicable. Next milestone assumes: both optimized routes (sparse projection, forced/micro-prefill) are exact-gated, leaving only path selection.
6. **Threshold selection plumbing + fallback wiring.** Deliverable: measured-cost thresholds selecting only among proven-equivalent paths, with the universal fallback (`FullProjection` / one-token feeding) always available, and full logging (every compiled primitive with state id, chosen path, threshold values, witness contents; every fallback engagement with reason). Test evidence: property/fuzz over random grammars × processor stacks — selection outcomes identical between primitive path and universal fallback; Phase-4A exit check that no public task depends on an optimized route whose fallback is not green.

title: [4A] Build independent validation module sharing zero automaton state with grammar
description:
## Background
"Independently checked" must not be circular: if the validator shared automaton code with the grammar compiler, both could agree on the same bug and G8 would be theater. This bead builds the `validation/` module — the second, deliberately separate implementation that every successful structured response of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; vocab 166,144; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) must pass before it is reported as success.

## Contract
- **Scope**: JSON parsing, schema validation, source-membership verification, and offset verification (`source[byte_start..byte_end] == text` on UTF-8 boundaries, half-open intervals, byte + Unicode-scalar coordinates).
- **Independence rule (hard)**: `validation/` shares ZERO automaton states, transition tables, mask cache, or acceptance routines with `grammar/`. The ONLY shared items are immutable declarative schema types (the parsed schema description). Enforced by a policy test on module dependencies.
- **Duplicate-key rejection**: the validator's JSON parser rejects duplicate object keys (as does every parser boundary in the product) rather than accepting parser-dependent overwrite semantics.
- **Bounded numbers, independently implemented**: the validator implements the normalized-decimal comparison (integer = exact 64-bit; number = (sign, coefficient, exponent) with ≤38 significant digits, adjusted exponent in [−308,308], checked arithmetic, mathematical equality where 1 ≡ 1.0 ≡ 1e0, negative-zero → 0) INDEPENDENTLY of the grammar lexer — same spec, separate code.
- **Differential fuzz kills agree-on-same-bug**: the fuzz harness feeds BOTH (a) grammar-compiler-generated outputs and (b) independently generated hostile byte strings to BOTH the grammar path and the validator, asserting agreement on accept/reject and flagging any input where both accept but a reference JSON semantics check fails.
- Grounded values pass the independent source-membership/offset verifier here — not the grammar-side product automaton.

## Constraints
Only immutable declarative schema types cross the grammar/validation boundary; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite (the validator's parser is ours or serde_json configured for strictness — duplicate-key rejection must be proven, not assumed); no Rayon; unsafe denied; G8 = G1 rank.

## Evidence / gates
Independence policy test green (no forbidden imports between grammar/ and validation/ beyond declarative types). Differential fuzz corpus running in CI with zero common-mode acceptances. The L5 gate consumes this module: constrained-greedy task bytes validate here before golden comparison. Offset-verifier property proofs recorded in the invariant-gate suite.

## Tests
Unit: duplicate-key rejection; UTF-8 boundary offset checks (reject non-boundary byte_start/byte_end); scalar-index computation vs byte index on multilingual fixtures; numeric equality across spellings (1/1.0/1e0), 38-digit and 64-bit boundary values, negative zero. Property/fuzz: random valid instances from `schema sample` all validate; mutated instances fail closed; hostile byte strings (truncated UTF-8, nesting bombs within caps, huge lexemes) → clean typed rejection, never panic; differential agreement with the grammar path. Detailed logging: every validation failure names the JSON pointer, expected constraint, and offending bytes' location (never logging full private document content in shared logs). Model-free: fully green in ordinary CI.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (grammar schema compiler bead — types only): the immutable declarative schema types are defined there; this bead consumes them and NOTHING else from grammar/.

title: [4A] Build exact continuation trie + named score spaces with KV fork-tail admission
description:
## Background
Finite-candidate scoring (classify labels, judge choices, enum fields) compiles multi-token candidate sets into a continuation trie so each unique prefix state is evaluated once on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; untied lm_head 3072→166,144; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22 — so every trie fork carries 44-deep KV tail state; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half; 16-token bf16 KV page group ≈2.75 MiB). This is dynamic programming over the COMPLETE candidate language — not beam search — and its scores are only "exact" relative to a named score space.

## Contract
- **Complete finite-language DP, no pruning ever.** Every candidate is scored; terminal/EOS is an explicit scored edge when one label prefixes another.
- **Three named score spaces, never blurred**: (1) `full_vocab_sequence_logprob` — the sum of true model log-probabilities; requires the full 166,144-row normalizer at EVERY distinct hidden state even when only candidate rows are retained; (2) `trie_local_conditional_probability` — per-node normalization over only the legal outgoing candidate edges; exact for the locally conditioned process and computable from sliced rows, but NOT the model's unconditional sequence probability; its depth-1 degenerate form over a single-step candidate set is labeled `single_step_candidate_conditional`; (3) `sequence_score_softmax` — softmax over a named terminal sequence score (summed selected logits, mean, or terminal token), a task estimator, not a model probability. Every response emits `score_space`, `normalization_scope`, the length/EOS rule, and whether full-vocabulary denominators were computed; the words "probability", "captured mass", and "confidence" are unavailable unless the corresponding quantity was actually computed. Trie traversal cannot convert space (2) or raw-logit scores into space (1) merely by visiting every candidate.
- **KV fork-tail byte admission BEFORE allocation**: the compiler estimates unique-node work AND actual KV fork-tail bytes from trie breadth/depth, page fill, and the 44-slot geometry, then chooses among: exact breadth/frontier batching; depth-first snapshot/restore with bounded tail state; or naïve per-candidate scoring. Little prefix sharing or excessive fork memory selects the naïve fallback. Admission goes through the KV slab allocator's certificate.
- **A compact canonical short-ID encoding** is a separate quality/performance baseline, never assumed equivalent to semantic labels.
- **Ship gate**: the trie ships ONLY when scores/rankings equal the naïve implementation on EVERY execution mode under the same normalization, candidate order is irrelevant (permutation invariance), admission is certified, and the measured reuse win exceeds traversal/KV cost in the ledger.

## Constraints
Continuation tries never prune a candidate (doctrine #17); fork admission prices actual 44-deep tail bytes (doctrine #26); trie ≡ naïve is an exact gate with the universal naïve fallback; no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; G1>G2; score-space honesty is mandatory envelope data (§6.10 semantics).

## Evidence / gates
trie ≡ naïve score-space equality differential on every mode (breadth, depth-first, naïve) — exact per space; candidate-order permutation invariance fixture; fork-tail admission certificate fixtures (breadth/depth/page-fill arithmetic vs actual allocation); reuse-win ledger row in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md before default-on. Recorded in the invariant-gate suite (Phase 4A exit: trie/naïve score-space equality green).

## Tests
Unit: trie construction with shared prefixes and prefix-of-another-label terminals; depth-1 labeling emits `single_step_candidate_conditional`; score-space envelope fields present and correct. Property: random candidate sets → all modes produce identical scores/rankings per space; permuting candidates changes nothing; full-vocab space requested → normalizer computed at every distinct hidden state (assert via counted projections). Integration: admission rejects a breadth/fan-out bomb before allocation with exact byte reasoning. Detailed logging: per-node evaluation counts, KV bytes charged, mode selection rationale. Model-gated scoring e2e: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; scalar spec engine covers structure in CI.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (execution-compiler bead): trie edges execute through ProjectLegal/sliced projection primitives and share their exactness/fallback regime.
- A_FWD (cross-epic): the forward pass (prefill/decode over 44 slots) is what evaluates each unique trie prefix state.

title: [4A] Implement addressable seeded sampler: Seed256 draw addressing, fused greedy, top-k heap, exact top-p
description:
## Background
Sampling must be addressable: the same seed + semantic request + numerics profile must reproduce every draw regardless of batching, reordering, or resume. For the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; untied lm_head 3072→166,144 → the full f32 logit vector is 664,576 bytes; pinned upstream sampling defaults temperature 0.6 / top_k 20 / top_p 0.95; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) this bead implements the seeded sampler and the fused greedy path in `lmhead.rs`.

## Contract
- **Seed types**: library type `Seed256` (`[u8; 32]`). CLI accepts either the 64-char lowercase-hex form or a decimal u64, which expands EXACTLY as `SHA-256("fnlp-seed-u64-v1" || u64_be)`. At admission, use the caller's seed or fill one effective seed with exactly ONE pinned `Cx::random_bytes` call; emit the 64-hex effective seed in the result/receipt. `--seed` is legal only with sampling; an omitted seed is intentionally nondeterministic until the emitted effective seed is replayed.
- **Every random draw** = `SHA-256("fnlp-sampler-v1" || length-framed effective_seed || stable_request_key || sample_index || decode_step || draw_index)`. No shared mutable RNG stream exists. Interpret the first 53 digest bits as one big-endian integer n and map `u = n / 2^53`. Nucleus ordering, tie handling, cumulative arithmetic, half-open selection intervals, and the final-rounding fallback are frozen by golden fixtures.
- **`stable_request_key`** is the canonical INTERNAL digest of the complete semantic request (input bytes or their authoritative private commitment, task/recipe/prompt, artifact, options, numerics profile, and caller/job item id) — never a caller-chosen id alone. It is INTERNAL-ONLY: never emitted or logged; any exported identity for private input uses the keyed-commitment rule (domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 per the job/receipt privacy contract), never a raw low-entropy content digest.
- **Greedy path**: full 3072→166,144 GEMV fused with the COMPLETE ordered logit-processor stack and argmax under a specified lowest-token-id tie break and an explicit NaN/Inf policy; no materialized softmax over 166K. Greedy has no RANDOM authority (capability row).
- **top_k=20 heap path**: top-k/top-p still evaluate the FULL vocabulary. With the pinned default top_k=20, a deterministic size-20 heap/selection may precede softmax and top-p filtering.
- **Exact top-p without top-k**: exact nucleus requires the full normalizer and probability rank order until cumulative mass crosses p — the baseline retains the bounded 166,144-entry f32 logit vector (664,576 bytes), computes max/sum in a fixed order, and uses a deterministic stable partial/full sort. No universal exact one-pass top-p over arbitrary logits is promised; a one-pass streaming threshold is not exact and may not ship under that name.
- **`sampler_version` freezes everything** (draw formula, ordering, tie/rounding rules); it is part of ExecutionIdentity. Batch composition, reordering, and resume do not change draws (batch/reorder/resume invariant).

## Constraints
RANDOM capability: unseeded sampling draws entropy exactly once at admission then passes owned state; greedy and kernel leaves get no RANDOM; sha2 is an approved dependency; no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; G1>G2; determinism is scoped (semantic under named profile; canonical bytes additionally need ordered output/scrubbed metadata).

## Evidence / gates
Golden fixture suite freezing: u64→Seed256 expansion vectors; draw digests for framed inputs; nucleus ordering/tie/rounding cases; NaN/Inf policy cases; lowest-token-id tie break. Batch/reorder/resume invariance fixtures (same seed+request+profile across batch sizes and restart). Privacy gate: stable_request_key never appears in any emitted event, receipt, or log (scan test). Sampler-version bump test: changing any frozen rule without bumping sampler_version fails a golden.

## Tests
Unit: seed parsing (64-hex, decimal u64, invalid forms); one-random_bytes-call admission (counted); 53-bit mapping boundary values (n=0, n=2^53−1); size-20 heap equals full-sort top-20 on random logits including ties. Property: draws are a pure function of the six framed fields; permuting batch rows or resuming mid-sequence reproduces identical draws; top-p cutover at exact cumulative boundary uses the half-open rule. Fuzz: hostile logit vectors (all-NaN, all-Inf, all-equal) follow the explicit policy, never panic. E2E: `--seed` with greedy → typed error; sampled run emits 64-hex effective seed and replaying it reproduces the stream (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL). Detailed logging: draw indices and digests at trace level with the effective seed elided per privacy rule.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (execution-compiler bead): the sampler consumes projected/masked logits and fuses with the processor stack the compiler's witnesses reason about; forced-run interplay (penalties updated, projection on logprob request) must agree.
- A_G0_CENSUS (cross-epic): the OQ-35 census ratifies `Cx::random_bytes` availability/semantics and the RANDOM-once capability admission pattern.

title: [4A] Stand up fnlp batch daemon skeleton + deterministic lab/chaos/team-model proof program
description:
## Background
`fnlp batch` is the opt-in throughput surface: a long-running daemon that loads the one-model wedge once (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) and streams NDJSON documents through the layer-major scheduler. This bead ships the daemon SKELETON (framing, admission, cancellation, output) plus the deterministic-lab proof program that certifies the whole 4A concurrency stack. Durable jobs and daemon hardening are Phase 4C, not here.

## Contract
- **Framing**: NDJSON requests on stdin `{id, text, task_args?}`; bounded line/document/token/schema/output sizes checked BEFORE admission. Every nonempty input line receives a checked monotonic `request_seq` before parsing; every event or parse error caused by that line echoes it, so a reused caller id can never make completion-order output ambiguous; sequence overflow cleanly ends admission. Events (all with `schema_version`): `run_start`, `stage`, `doc`, `doc_error`, `token`, `flush`, `run_complete`, `run_error`.
- Default emits completion-order results with caller id + engine-assigned `request_seq`; canonical byte replay requires `--ordered`, a declared maximum reorder window, and telemetry-free output. Duplicate caller ids are rejected within a numbered epoch whose capped seen-id set resets only after a drained `flush`. One malformed document → one `doc_error` with its sequence position, without corrupting framing. Backpressure pauses stdin reads (bounded channels everywhere). EOF requests graceful drain.
- **Signals**: first SIGINT closes admission and requests cooperative cancellation; a second shortens the grace policy but is never described as safely preempting Rust/OS threads — the process emits no success receipt and reuses no in-process buffer before the compute completion latch fires.
- Weights load once; runtime preset `high_throughput` recorded in telemetry (preset name is never a safe thread count — the measured envelope governs).
- **The deterministic-lab proof program** (this bead owns it for the 4A stack): (a) oracle-checked Lab scenarios run to `run_until_quiescent_with_report()` asserting region/task/obligation/cleanup invariants, cancellation propagation, and loser drain; (b) seed-bound chaos — cancellation/delay/budget-exhaustion/wakeup storms — replacing hand-rolled hostile interleavings for the async state, with failing runs auto-attaching a crashpack (stable fingerprint + replay command) into the evidence ledger; (c) obligation-based futurelock detection recording a deterministic witness when a task holds obligations unpolled beyond the idle bound — stronger diagnosis than wall-clock timeout but NOT proof of semantic deadlock nor freedom outside the explored schedules/bound; (d) the repository-owned bounded team-state automaton exhausting formation/seal/command/cancel/panic/join states — because Lab does NOT enumerate native `scoped_cpu` OS-thread interleavings; (e) hostile native stress/replay validating the automaton's seam against the real implementation; (f) the `many_docs_without_deadlock` watchdog (batch of docs ≫ compute width).
- **Determinism gate**: batch-M ≡ batch-1 token-exact per sequence under `strict-quantized-vN` (this bead wires the gate end-to-end through the daemon; the scheduler bead owns the reduction-order rule).

## Constraints
stdout is data, stderr diagnostics; robot NDJSON is versioned and frozen-schema tested; asupersync doctrine #8 in full (one admission domain, sealed team, closure-owned latch, typed re-entry refusal); Lab oracles cover async state NOT native scoped_cpu interleavings (never overclaim); no Rayon; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; neither pinned first_ok surface is a sequential-mirror fallback (`combinator::first_ok_outcomes` only classifies already-completed outcomes in order; `ExecPlan::first_ok` drives all children concurrently to completion and never cancels/drains losers) — the daemon does no concurrent hedging absent a separately ratified first-success primitive; GenServer cast acknowledges enqueue only — required transitions use call/reserve→permit.

## Evidence / gates
Phase-4A exit gates: scheduler automaton/interleaving tests green; capacity invariants green; batch-M ≡ batch-1 exact. Crashpacks retained in the evidence ledger for any failing seed. Frozen robot-schema contract test covers the daemon events. Chaos/futurelock/team-automaton runs are CI jobs whose failing seeds must replay — a failure may never survive as an unreproducible CI ghost.

## Tests
Unit: request_seq monotonicity + overflow end-of-admission; duplicate-id rejection within epoch, reset after drained flush; malformed line → doc_error with correct seq; bounded-size rejection before admission. Property: interleaved valid/malformed lines never corrupt framing; completion-order output always carries correct (id, request_seq) pairs. Concurrency: Lab scenarios + seed-bound chaos storms + futurelock witness + bounded team automaton + native stress, all seed-replayable; SIGINT matrix (first/second, at every lifecycle stage) — no success receipt before latch. E2E: pipe N docs through a stub task with no model → framing green + SKIPPED_NO_MODEL for inference; armed model run gates release. `many_docs_without_deadlock` in CI. Detailed logging: every admission/cancel/drain transition with request_seq, epoch, and latch state; chaos seeds logged for replay. Named test deliverables: `tests/lab_scheduler_scenarios.rs` (oracle-checked Lab scenarios + seed-bound chaos storms + futurelock-witness runs) and `tests/team_state_model.rs` (bounded formation/seal/command/cancel/panic/join automaton + native stress seam validation); every lab/chaos case logs scenario id AND seed on one machine-parseable line so a failure replays from the log alone; bounded-size/admission rejections emit the exact violated bound (line/document/token/schema/output cap) in the typed doc_error payload, never a bare "too large".

## Dependencies & rationale
- (typed step DAG scheduler bead): the daemon feeds admitted rows to the scheduler; batching/preemption semantics come from it.
- (addressable sampler bead): sampled/streamed tokens and seed emission flow through daemon events; determinism gate needs the sampler's invariance.
- A_G0_CENSUS (cross-epic): the OQ-35 census ratifies Lab/chaos/crashpack surfaces, GenServer call/cast semantics, and supervision decisions the daemon skeleton builds on.

title: [4B] Implement Task trait, closed BuiltInTask enum, TaskIR core, and semantic/telemetry envelopes
description:
## Background
The task layer is why anyone installs the binary: it turns the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, q 3072→6144; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) into a local NLP toolbox. This bead builds the `Task` architecture core: the trait, the closed registry, `TaskIR`, and the two-envelope response contract. Every 4B/4C task compiles through this.

## Contract
- **Trait (exact shape)**:
```rust
trait Task {
    type Request;  // serde types; CLI + library + NDJSON share them
    type Response;
    fn spec(&self) -> &'static TaskSpec;      // name, version, JSON Schemas (request/response), presets
    fn plan(&self, req: &Self::Request, ctx: &PlanContext)
        -> Result<TaskPlan, FnlpError>;       // prompt build + decode strategy + grammar + budget
    fn finalize(&self, req: &Self::Request, plan: &TaskPlan, raw: DecodeOutput,
                validator: &IndependentValidator)
        -> Result<Self::Response, FnlpError>; // G8: independent validation + grounded-offset checks
}
```
The old `parse(raw)` sketch was doubly wrong: references must be `&Self::Request`/`Self::Response`, and a finalizer without the request, plan, and source text cannot verify grounded fields or offsets.
- **Closed `BuiltInTask` enum with STATIC dispatch.** The associated-type trait deliberately does not support a heterogeneous `Vec<Box<dyn Task>>`; no erasure layer is built. Public data-only recipes compile to TaskIR; they never become dynamically loaded Rust task implementations.
- **`TaskIR` compiles BEFORE model load** into: exact prompt-token segments; grammar/execution program; optional continuation trie; deterministic finite postconditions; resource bounds; and a stage dependency scope — `ItemLocal` | `PartitionReduce` | `CorpusGlobal`. The scope controls cache/reuse authority: adding one item may preserve local map results but invalidates any reduce/global result whose child set changed. The runtime executes this IR; it never interprets arbitrary code.
- **TaskPlan decode strategies**: `PrefillOnly { candidates }` (logit-sliced/trie-scored), `ConstrainedJson { schema }`, `ConstrainedPattern { grammar }`, `FreeText { stops, budget }`, `Distribution { scale }`. Tasks compose these; the engine doesn't know task semantics.
- **Semantic envelope vs telemetry envelope**: every response carries `schema_version`, task spec version, the ExecutionIdentity projection INCLUDING the prompt-template hash, thinking mode, deterministic token counts, calibration/policy identity, `score_space`, and result status. Timings, queue wait, selected tuning row, transient run id, page faults, host load, and energy live in a SEPARATE telemetry envelope. Canonical byte replay (`--ordered` + canonical metadata; the `--canonical` mode) omits the telemetry envelope entirely.
- Budget/cancel/resource failure is a typed no-result (exit 10 family), never partial success; an unconstrained "retry on parse failure" loop is a design bug.

## Constraints
Static dispatch, no plugin system; bounded TaskIR only (no code/tools/network/undeclared files/Jinja/shell/Python/WASM; unknown keys forward-reject); presets are data; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; G8 = G1 rank; determinism scoped by ExecutionIdentity; exit codes 0–10 with 10 = typed task no-result and abstention = exit 0 + status abstained.

## Evidence / gates
Compile-time: the trait compiles with the exact associated-type signatures; a doc-test proves the closed-enum dispatch covers every BuiltInTask variant (exhaustive match, no default arm). TaskIR golden fixtures per task: identical request → byte-identical IR (before model load). Envelope contract test: canonical mode output contains zero telemetry fields (frozen-schema fixture). Dependency-scope authority test: item addition preserves exact ItemLocal entries, invalidates changed PartitionReduce/CorpusGlobal.

## Tests
Unit: TaskSpec versioning; plan() rejection paths (bad request, over-budget) return typed errors; finalize() refuses raw output that fails the IndependentValidator. Property: TaskIR compilation is deterministic (same request+context → same IR bytes); scope-invalidation rules under random child-set mutations. E2E: a stub task exercises the full plan→execute→finalize path with the validator wired; canonical vs default envelope golden diff. Model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Detailed logging: every plan/finalize failure logs task, spec version, and typed error code; envelope assembly logs which identity fields were hashed.

## Dependencies & rationale
- A_EXEC (cross-epic): TaskPlan decode strategies execute through the 4A execution-compiler primitives.
- A_VALID (cross-epic): `finalize` takes `&IndependentValidator`; G8 requires the independent validation module.
- A_EXECID (cross-epic): the semantic envelope embeds the canonical ExecutionIdentity projection defined in Phase 0.

title: [4B] Build presets-as-data infrastructure: embedded provenance packs, --preset-file, versioned prompt diffs
description:
## Background
Task prompts and presets decide quality as much as kernels do, so they are versioned data, never code. A quality regression on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) must be attributable to weights vs kernels vs prompts — so all three are hashed. This bead builds the presets-as-data infrastructure that every 4B/4C task consumes.

## Contract
- **Embedded packs**: `tasks/presets/*.json`. Only repo-authored or provenance-cleared packs may ship/embed. EVERY preset file carries origin/license metadata and a content hash; imported material (e.g. the owner's own swiss_army_llama presets, reuse authorized with attribution) still gets an origin hash so later edits are auditable.
- **`--preset-file`**: users may supply their own preset file; user-supplied packs are loaded with the same schema validation but are never silently promoted into shipped defaults.
- **Prompt changes are versioned, diffable events with eval reruns** — never a drive-by string edit. The prompt-template hash lands in every response's semantic envelope (via the task-core bead), and a changed hash without a recorded version bump + eval rerun fails CI.
- Preset schema: typed fields per task (dimensions, labels, verbalizers, scaffolds), forward-rejecting unknown keys; duplicate-key-rejecting JSON parsing like every parser boundary in the product.
- Embedded packs are hash-checked at load; a mismatch between the embedded index and file content is a loud typed error, never a silent fallback.

## Constraints
Presets are data, prompts are versioned (doctrine #13); provenance mandatory (origin/license metadata + content hash per file); deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; unknown keys forward-reject; no network access ever (packs are embedded or local files).

## Evidence / gates
CI check: every file under `tasks/presets/` has origin/license metadata + content hash and parses against the preset schema. Golden: preset-pack index (name → hash) frozen; changing a prompt without bumping its version breaks the golden and demands an eval-rerun record. Envelope integration: a task response's prompt-template hash equals the loaded preset's recorded hash.

## Tests
Unit: pack parsing (valid/invalid/unknown-key/duplicate-key); hash verification failure path; `--preset-file` loading and precedence. Property: content-hash stability across load/serialize round-trips. E2E: run a stub task with a shipped pack and with `--preset-file` — envelope hash tracks the actual pack used. Detailed logging: pack load events with name, version, hash, origin. Model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL where inference is involved; pack validation is model-free and fully green in CI.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (task-core bead): TaskSpec/TaskIR define where presets plug in and the envelope that carries the prompt-template hash.

title: [4B] Implement typed prompt-segment ABI and UntrustedDocument trust boundary
description:
## Background
Prompts for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; SentencePiece tokenizer; im/think chat-template markers and XML/JSON tool branches — the think/tool markers are `special=false` at pin; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) must preserve typed structure so common prefixes are discoverable and the untrusted-document boundary is typed. This bead builds the prompt-segment ABI and wires the `UntrustedDocument` encoder into the task layer.

## Contract
- **Typed segments**: `global policy`, `task instruction`, `document`, `answer scaffold` — prompts preserve these types rather than becoming an opaque string too early. This permits content-addressed common-prefix discovery without forcing an instructions-last layout. Corpus-major sharing is the default proven layout; document-major `analyze` packs remain per-task empirical (Phase 7) and are NOT built here.
- **Trust boundary**: only trusted template code may inject role, thinking, or tool-control token ids. An `UntrustedDocument` segment is encoded through the Phase-1 constrained tokenizer path that excludes the COMPLETE `TemplateControlIds` registry — not merely tokens marked `special=true`, since the think/tool markers are `special=false` at pin — while preserving the document's decoded bytes via ordinary/byte pieces. If exact byte preservation without a forbidden id is impossible, preflight REJECTS instead of silently weakening the boundary. Literal marker text remains ordinary untrusted content (the model may see the words; it never sees the control ids).
- **Honest claim scope**: this proves marker containment ONLY — control-token/role-boundary smuggling is prevented; semantic prompt injection is NOT (instruction-shaped prose can still steer the model and is measured by the per-task matched clean/attack scorecards bead). No firewall claim anywhere.
- **Envelope marking**: every output envelope marks which fields derive from untrusted content; downstream agents must treat them as data.
- Segment types feed TaskIR's exact prompt-token segments; the ABI defines how segment hashes compose into the prompt-template hash.

## Constraints
Typed trust boundary without firewall claims (doctrine #22); forced tokens ≠ forced bytes; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; the complete TemplateControlIds registry (censused in Phase −1, OQ-20) is the exclusion set — never a hand-maintained subset; G8 = G1 rank.

## Evidence / gates
Lexicon-style property proofs: an untrusted segment's token ids exclude EVERY TemplateControlIds member AND decode to the original document bytes, or the encode rejects (both directions fuzzed). Envelope untrusted-derived marking present in the frozen response schema. Prefix-discovery fixture: two requests sharing global-policy+task-instruction segments produce identical leading token runs (the cache-eligible prefix).

## Tests
Unit: each segment type renders in order; role/think/tool ids appear only from trusted template code paths; preflight rejection when byte preservation is impossible. Property/fuzz: random documents (including literal marker text, e.g. the im/think marker strings as plain text) → encoded ids exclude all control ids and decode byte-exactly; adversarial Unicode and byte-fallback documents. E2E: a task request with a hostile document containing marker text produces output whose envelope marks untrusted-derived fields (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; encoding-side tests are model-free and green in CI). Detailed logging: encode rejections log the offending byte range and the forbidden id that could not be avoided (id, never raw private content in shared logs).

## Dependencies & rationale
- (task-core bead): segments are TaskIR prompt-token segments; the envelope marking lives in the semantic envelope.
- A_CTL_CENSUS (cross-epic): the complete TemplateControlIds registry census (special=false markers included) is the authoritative exclusion set.

title: [4B] Ship fnlp extract: schema-constrained structured extraction flagship
description:
## Background
`fnlp extract` is the flagship: schema-constrained structured extraction demonstrating G8 (valid-by-construction) end to end on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). It covers a broad set of bounded object/array extraction schemas — what most people actually need from "LLM + JSON".

## Contract
- **CLI**: `fnlp extract --schema s.json [doc.txt | -]`, `--json` everywhere, `-o file`. First-run ergonomics: invoking `fnlp extract` WITHOUT `--schema` is an exit-2 usage error whose message embeds a minimal worked example (a 3-field schema plus the exact command line to run it); schema-rejection errors always name the offending keyword + JSON pointer, and grounded/offset failures name the field and byte offset. Long map-reduce runs emit stage/progress events (chunk k of N) on stderr/robot `stage` events rather than going silent. User supplies the DOCUMENTED finite JSON-Schema subset (the 4A grammar compiler's normative v1: object/array/string/number/integer/boolean/null, enum/const, mandatory `additionalProperties:false`, finite `maxItems`, bounded 64-bit/38-digit numerics) plus text. Unsupported JSON-Schema features reject by keyword BEFORE model load — this is explicitly not "any schema".
- **G8**: a successful result is schema-valid by construction (constrained decode) AND independently checked (the `validation/` module — separate implementation, zero shared automaton state).
- **Verbatim grounding**: string fields may opt into `"x-fnlp-source":"verbatim"`; then a successful value is a byte-exact source substring BY CONSTRUCTION (the 4A source-language product automaton). Normalized dates/amounts remain ordinary semantic fields.
- **Repeated occurrences**: return ALL compatible intervals, or a separately constrained occurrence selector — string membership alone NEVER fabricates a unique offset.
- **Modes**: single-shot; `--ndjson` batch (daemon-compatible framing); map-reduce for over-context documents via the shared spine — deterministic token-budgeted chunking → batched map → task-specific deterministic reduce, every output linked to chunk ids/byte ranges; hierarchical reduction never claims exact equivalence to single-context inference. (`--verify-semantic` is Phase 5 and NOT built here; it stays absent, not stubbed.)
- **Failure honesty**: every non-success is a typed no-result — never a truncated object, never an unconstrained retry. Exit codes follow the frozen error.rs map (single authority, no duplicate table): unsatisfiable required grounded field, missing mandatory close delimiter, or output-budget exhaustion with no valid completable object → exit 10 (structured task no-result); timeout/cost-budget expiry → exit 5; cancellation → exit 6.

## Constraints
G8 = G1 rank; unsupported keywords fail closed pre-model; no silent fallback from grounded to ungrounded; thinking off by default for structured tasks; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; presets are data; stdout data / stderr diagnostics; exit codes 0–10 (10 = typed no-result).

## Evidence / gates
Phase-4B exit: G8 + grounded-field property/fuzz proofs green. L5: constrained-greedy task bytes exact against the frozen golden for the same artifact/recipe/profile/canonical mode. Field-F1 scorecard on the schema-diverse corpus (eval bead) — validity asserted at 100% by construction, accuracy measured. Extract rows in docs/FEATURE_PARITY.md.

## Tests
Unit: request parsing; schema-rejection paths surface the grammar compiler's keyword + JSON pointer; occurrence policy (all-intervals vs selector) round-trips the response schema. Property/fuzz: random supported schemas × synthetic docs → every success validates independently AND every verbatim field byte-matches source at its offsets; unsatisfiable required grounded field → typed no-result (10); cancellation at every token → no partial success (exit 6, per-code asserted). E2E: single-shot, `--ndjson`, and map-reduce modes on fixture docs (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; grammar/validation plumbing model-free in CI); golden envelope in canonical mode. Detailed logging: per-field grounding status, occurrence counts, and typed failure reasons; NDJSON doc_error framing preserved on per-doc failure. The flagship golden e2e ships as the named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_extract_golden.sh`: fixture docs × schema corpus through single-shot/--ndjson/map-reduce, one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, schema digest, dataset/prompt-hash/recipe/thinking-mode, grounding status, exit code), asserting the no-schema usage-error path, with SKIPPED_NO_MODEL rows explicit when unarmed.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (task-core bead): extract is a BuiltInTask compiling through TaskIR with ConstrainedJson strategy.
- (trust-ABI bead): documents enter as UntrustedDocument segments; envelope marks untrusted-derived fields.
- A_GRAMMAR (cross-epic): the normative schema subset compiler is the constrained-decode engine extract rides.
- A_EXEC (cross-epic): ProjectLegal/FeedForced/CopyFromSource primitives execute the extraction.
- A_VALID (cross-epic): independent validation is half of G8.

title: [4B] Ship fnlp ner: source-grounded typed spans with byte+scalar offsets and explicit ambiguity
description:
## Background
`fnlp ner` is the headline "what people used SpaCy for" surface, minus what a 3B LLM shouldn't do. It emits typed entity spans over the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) with offsets that are actually trustworthy — grounded by the same source machinery as extract. (`fnlp resolve` is Phase 4C, not here.)

## Contract
- **CLI**: `fnlp ner [--types ...] [doc.txt | -]`; typed spans over a configurable type set. An unknown `--types` entry is an exit-2 usage error listing the shipped type-set presets; anchoring failures name the mention text position and its candidate byte offsets.
- **Offsets**: half-open `{byte_start, byte_end, scalar_start, scalar_end}`; "scalar" means Unicode scalar-value index — NOT grapheme cluster, NOT UTF-16 code unit. Every accepted span satisfies `source[byte_start..byte_end] == text` with both ends on UTF-8 boundaries.
- **Grounding**: after OQ-17 passes, surface forms use the exact source-language constraint by default (the 4A product automaton — extraction shares this machinery).
- **Ambiguity is explicit**: repeated occurrences remain `ambiguous` with candidate intervals unless a separately constrained occurrence selector resolves them. Ordinary non-grounded recipe fields may be `unanchored`, but spans are NEVER silently relocated — a span that cannot anchor is ambiguous/unanchored/no-result, never approximated.
- **Confidence honesty**: `confidence` is a separately calibrated mention-correctness estimate — NOT a raw average of whichever tokens happened to encode the span. Until a calibration artifact exists (Phase 5), the field is absent or explicitly `uncalibrated`; it never dresses up raw logprobs.

## Constraints
G8 + grounded offsets at G1 rank; never fabricate unique offsets from string membership; no silent relocation after any normalization (coordinate maps or no-result); thinking off by default; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; exit codes 0–10; presets (type sets) are data.

## Evidence / gates
Phase-4B exit: grounded-field property/fuzz proofs green for ner spans. Invariant: anchored offsets survive deterministic coordinate conversion (byte ↔ scalar). Scorecard (eval bead): span-exact/type-relaxed F1 by language/type on WNUT-17/Few-NERD (after license archival) + the repo-authored modern-web/CJK set, with anchoring status reported. L5 constrained-greedy golden for fixture docs.

## Tests
Unit: byte/scalar offset computation on ASCII, multibyte, combining-mark, and emoji fixtures (scalar counts differ from grapheme counts — assert the scalar definition); half-open boundary edges (span at doc start/end); type-set configuration. Property/fuzz: for random docs, every accepted span byte-matches and lands on UTF-8 boundaries; repeated-surface docs yield `ambiguous` with complete candidate lists; adversarial Unicode (NFC/NFD lookalikes, ZWJ) never produces a non-boundary offset. E2E: `fnlp ner --json` on fixture docs (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL); golden response schema incl. ambiguity fields. Detailed logging: per-mention anchoring decision (anchored/ambiguous/unanchored) with candidate counts and typed reasons. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_ner_golden.sh`: multilingual fixture docs with one machine-parseable row per mention (fixture id, anchoring status, byte/scalar offsets, dataset/prompt-hash/recipe/thinking-mode, exit code), SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (extract bead): ner shares the grounded machinery extract stood up (source product wiring, occurrence policy, offset verification through validation/).
- A_GRAMMAR (cross-epic): the constrained output format (typed span JSON) compiles through the grammar engine.

title: [4B] Ship fnlp classify: verified verbalizers, named score spaces, independent multi-label
description:
## Background
`fnlp classify` is zero-shot classification exploiting exactly what the engine is good at: logit-sliced candidate scoring on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; untied lm_head 3072→166,144 — C-row sliced GEMV instead of all 166,144 rows; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Its probability semantics must be honest per the three named score spaces.

## Contract
- **CLI**: `fnlp classify --labels a,b,c [--multi] [doc.txt | -]`; labels + descriptions + text → single- or multi-label. Omitting `--labels` (and any preset selection) is an exit-2 usage error that LISTS the shipped preset packs (topic/intent/moderation/spam) with one worked `--labels` example; an unknown preset name lists the valid pack names.
- **Single-label**: prefer opaque single-token verbalizers VERIFIED in the exact answer-scaffold context — bucket/verbalizer token identity is census-verified after the exact scaffold and leading whitespace, never by tokenizing the label string in isolation. A single-token candidate-conditional softmax is exact for that declared finite choice (score space `single_step_candidate_conditional`).
- **Multi-token labels**: explicitly select ONE of the three named score spaces (`full_vocab_sequence_logprob` / `trie_local_conditional_probability` / `sequence_score_softmax`); the DEFAULT quality baseline is `full_vocab_sequence_logprob` unless a locked evaluation qualifies a cheaper estimator; frozen length/prior correction. The response envelope names the score space; "probability" language is unavailable unless the corresponding quantity was computed.
- **Multi-label** (`--multi`): INDEPENDENT yes/no (present/absent) verbalizers per label, calibrated and thresholded separately — NEVER a softmax that forces labels to compete. Multi-token verbalizers name their score space and calibrate separately.
- **Cost shape**: one shared document/task prefix (prefix cache where eligible) + batched label suffixes; multi-token candidate sets compile to the 4A continuation trie when its measured reuse wins; realized cost scales with unique trie states/label queries AND IS REPORTED. Never market "one prefill" when multi-label suffixes add work.
- Presets (topic/intent/moderation/spam packs) are data with provenance; the non-LLM n-gram language detector is a SEPARATE gated artifact and not part of this bead.

## Constraints
Score-space honesty is mandatory (three quantities never blurred; envelope carries score_space/normalization_scope); no competing-softmax multi-label; candidate sets are complete (no pruning — trie rule); thinking off by default; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; confidence language requires calibration (Phase 5) — until then raw scores are labeled as scores.

## Evidence / gates
Verbalizer census-verification fixture (single-token identity in scaffold context, including leading-whitespace behavior). trie-vs-naïve equality inherited from 4A applies to label sets (spot-check gate here). Scorecard (eval bead): accuracy/macro-F1/Brier/ECE/selective risk on license-gated SST-2/AG-News/Banking77-class corpora + owned multilingual smoke. Cost report fields (unique trie states, label-query count) present in telemetry envelope golden.

## Tests
Unit: label parsing; single- vs multi-label mode selection; scaffold-context verbalizer verification catches a label whose tokenization differs in context; score-space envelope fields. Property: multi-label independence — per-label decisions invariant to the other labels present; single-label candidate-conditional softmax sums to 1 over candidates. E2E: `fnlp classify --json` single and `--multi` on fixtures (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL); golden envelopes name score spaces. Detailed logging: per-label score, space, normalization scope; batched-suffix grouping decisions. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_classify_golden.sh`: single/multi-label fixtures plus the usage-error paths, one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, score_space, dataset/prompt-hash/recipe/thinking-mode, exit code), SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (task-core bead, franken_nlp-ngg): classify is a BuiltInTask using PrefillOnly{candidates} strategy and the envelope contract.
- A_SAMPLER (cross-epic, franken_nlp-9tz): lm_head slicing, full-vocab normalizer machinery, and fixed reduction order for candidate softmax live in the 4A sampler stack.
- A_TRIE (cross-epic, franken_nlp-k9e): the three named score spaces (`full_vocab_sequence_logprob` / `trie_local_conditional_probability` incl. `single_step_candidate_conditional` / `sequence_score_softmax`), the continuation trie, and its universal naïve fallback are that bead's deliverables — multi-token label scoring is impossible without them.

title: [4B] Ship fnlp redact: detector union, recall-first overlap, HMAC pseudonyms, --verify, --map-out
description:
## Background
`fnlp redact` removes/replaces PII-class spans by unioning anchored NER with deterministic rules on the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). It is defense-in-depth with cryptographically honest pseudonyms — explicitly NOT anonymization and never a compliance certificate.

## Contract
- **Detection**: union source-grounded/anchored NER spans with VERSIONED deterministic rule automata; rule patterns/locales and their per-detector precision/recall fixtures are DATA, not an unspecified regex oracle. Overlaps resolved by a versioned recall-first interval policy. Unanchored model guesses become WARNINGS, never destructive offsets.
- **Actions**: `mask | placeholder | pseudonymize`; pseudonyms are explicitly not anonymization.
- **Pseudonym contract (exact)**: RFC-2104/4231 HMAC-SHA-256 over the approved `sha2` primitive with RFC test vectors mandatory — never `SHA256(secret || value)`. Input = domain/version + length-framed namespace + entity type + bytes under a named canonicalization policy. Key: ≥32 bytes high-entropy, supplied via owner-only key file, inherited descriptor, or stdin — NEVER argv or telemetry; nonsecret key id/version accompanies it for rotation; key-stdin and document-stdin are mutually exclusive. The semantic job key/receipt retain only the nonsecret key commitment `HMAC_K("fnlp-pseudonym-key-commit-v1")`, so resume with the wrong secret fails BEFORE emitting mixed pseudonyms; a caller label alone is not sufficient identity. The secret is never logged, persisted in a receipt, or reused as the sampler seed.
- **Output encoding + collision policy**: default = 128 digest bits as lowercase hex with a type prefix. Collision handling is JOB-WIDE: before externally visible 128-bit output, preflight the COMPLETE canonical-value set under declared byte/cardinality budgets, using a bounded owner-only external sort/index when it exceeds memory; any truncation collision between DISTINCT values either fails closed or deterministically promotes the ENTIRE colliding class to the full digest. If the preflight/index cannot complete within budget: fail before output, or run the whole job in full 256-bit mode under an explicit flag. A truly streaming mode that cannot preflight uses full 256-bit pseudonyms FROM THE START — never retroactively changes an already-emitted token.
- **`--verify`**: reruns the FULL detector union over the redacted output of the same command; residual findings → nonzero exit + leak report. It is a useful clean-pass receipt, NOT a compliance certificate.
- **`--map-out` / `-o`**: through the local-output transaction — owner-controlled parent, exclusive `create_new` staging, no symlink/reparse/device target, owner-only permissions/ACL, sync + same-directory activation, no overwrite absent a separately explicit destructive policy. The map NEVER enters telemetry.

## Constraints
Recall-first is the declared bias and is reported as such; sha2 is the only crypto primitive (HMAC built on it, RFC-vector-tested); key material never in argv/telemetry/receipts; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; exit codes 0–10; per-detector fixtures are versioned data; G8 rank for structural output validity.

## Evidence / gates
RFC 4231 HMAC-SHA-256 test vectors pass. Per-detector precision/recall fixture suite green with per-detector metrics recorded (scorecard bead consumes them). Collision-policy fixtures: constructed 128-bit truncation collision → fail-closed or whole-class promotion, deterministically; budget-exceeded preflight → typed pre-output failure or explicit 256-bit mode. `--verify` residual-leak fixture returns nonzero + report. Output-transaction hostile tests (symlink/reparse/device target, existing file) fail closed.

## Tests
Unit: key sourcing paths (file/fd/stdin; argv rejected; <32-byte key rejected; key-stdin×doc-stdin exclusive); key-commitment mismatch on resume fails before output; canonicalization framing (namespace/type/bytes length-framed — no ambiguity between ("ab","c") and ("a","bc")). Property: same key+namespace+type+value → same pseudonym across runs; distinct values collide only via the handled truncation path; overlap resolution is recall-first per the versioned policy on random span sets. Fuzz: Unicode obfuscation fixtures (homoglyphs, ZWJ) exercise detector behavior and are REPORTED per detector, not asserted universally. E2E: redact→verify round trip on fixtures (model-gated NER half: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; rule half model-free green); `--map-out` transaction on a hostile directory matrix. Detailed logging: per-detector hit counts and policy decisions; NEVER the secret, NEVER raw pseudonym↔value maps in logs/telemetry. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_redact_golden.sh`: redact→verify round trips over the detector fixture corpus plus the hostile `--map-out` directory matrix, one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, per-detector hit counts, collision-policy outcome, verify verdict, exit code); rule-half rows run model-free, NER-half rows print SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicitly.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (ner bead): anchored NER spans are the model half of the detector union; redact consumes its grounded-offset machinery.
- A_TOK_L0 (cross-epic): exact tokenizer/byte semantics underpin span byte-fidelity for rule/NER union on multibyte text.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **Versioned rule automata + per-detector fixtures.** Deliverable: the deterministic rule detectors with VERSIONED patterns/locales and per-detector precision/recall fixtures as DATA (not an unspecified regex oracle). Test evidence: per-detector precision/recall fixture suite green with per-detector metrics recorded (the scorecard bead consumes them); Unicode-obfuscation fuzz (homoglyphs, ZWJ) exercised and REPORTED per detector, not asserted universally. Next milestone assumes: a measurable, model-free detector half exists.
2. **Detector union + recall-first overlap policy.** Deliverable: the union of source-grounded/anchored NER spans with the rule automata under the versioned recall-first interval policy; unanchored model guesses become WARNINGS, never destructive offsets; span byte-fidelity on multibyte text rests on the exact tokenizer/byte semantics (A_TOK_L0). Test evidence: property — overlap resolution is recall-first per the versioned policy on random span sets; NER half model-gated (SKIPPED_NO_MODEL), rule half model-free green. Next milestone assumes: a resolved span set ready for actions.
3. **HMAC-SHA-256 pseudonym core.** Deliverable: RFC-2104/4231 HMAC-SHA-256 built on the approved `sha2` primitive — never `SHA256(secret || value)` — over input = domain/version + length-framed namespace + entity type + bytes under a named canonicalization policy. Test evidence: RFC 4231 test vectors pass (mandatory); canonicalization framing units (no ambiguity between ("ab","c") and ("a","bc")); property — same key+namespace+type+value → same pseudonym across runs. Next milestone assumes: a correct keyed primitive for key-lifecycle handling.
4. **Key sourcing + commitment.** Deliverable: ≥32-byte high-entropy key via owner-only key file, inherited descriptor, or stdin — NEVER argv or telemetry; key-stdin and document-stdin mutually exclusive; nonsecret key id/version for rotation; job key/receipt retain only the nonsecret commitment `HMAC_K("fnlp-pseudonym-key-commit-v1")` so resume with the wrong secret fails BEFORE emitting mixed pseudonyms (a caller label alone is not sufficient identity); the secret is never logged, persisted in a receipt, or reused as the sampler seed. Test evidence: unit key-sourcing paths (file/fd/stdin; argv rejected; <32-byte key rejected; stdin exclusivity); key-commitment mismatch on resume fails before output. Next milestone assumes: a safe key lifecycle for externally visible encoding.
5. **Actions + output encoding + job-wide collision policy.** Deliverable: `mask | placeholder | pseudonymize` actions (pseudonyms explicitly not anonymization); default 128 digest bits as lowercase hex with type prefix; JOB-WIDE collision handling — preflight the COMPLETE canonical-value set under declared byte/cardinality budgets (bounded owner-only external sort/index beyond memory); any truncation collision between DISTINCT values fails closed or deterministically promotes the ENTIRE colliding class to full digest; budget-exceeded preflight fails before output or runs the whole job in explicit 256-bit mode; a truly streaming mode uses full 256-bit pseudonyms FROM THE START, never retroactively changing an emitted token. Test evidence: collision-policy fixtures (constructed 128-bit truncation collision → fail-closed or whole-class promotion, deterministically; budget-exceeded → typed pre-output failure or explicit 256-bit mode); property — distinct values collide only via the handled truncation path. Next milestone assumes: final redacted output whose residuals can be verified.
6. **`--verify` residual-leak rerun.** Deliverable: rerun of the FULL detector union over the redacted output of the same command; residual findings → nonzero exit + leak report; a clean-pass receipt, NOT a compliance certificate. Test evidence: the `--verify` residual-leak fixture returns nonzero + report; E2E redact→verify round trip on fixtures (model-gated NER half SKIPPED_NO_MODEL, rule half green). Next milestone assumes: a verifiable end-to-end flow to harden the output transaction around.
7. **`--map-out`/`-o` local-output transaction + logging discipline.** Deliverable: outputs through the local-output transaction — owner-controlled parent, exclusive `create_new` staging, no symlink/reparse/device target, owner-only permissions/ACL, sync + same-directory activation, no overwrite absent a separately explicit destructive policy; the map NEVER enters telemetry; detailed logging carries per-detector hit counts and policy decisions but NEVER the secret or raw pseudonym↔value maps; exit codes 0–10. Test evidence: output-transaction hostile tests (symlink/reparse/device target, existing file) fail closed; `--map-out` on the hostile directory matrix E2E; log-content assertions for the never-logged invariants.

title: [4B] Ship fnlp generate/chat: greedy default, nanbeige sampling preset, bounded thinking, streaming NDJSON
description:
## Background
`fnlp generate` / `fnlp chat` expose completion/chat over the native template of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; SentencePiece tokenizer; im/think chat markers with XML/JSON tool branches; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Greedy is the PRODUCT default (registered behavior note BN-GEN-DEFAULT-001 — an intentional product decision, never to be mistaken for HF parity, since upstream defaults sample).

## Contract
- **CLI**: `fnlp generate/chat [--think/--no-think] [--sample --preset nanbeige] [--seed <u64|64hex>]`.
- **Defaults**: greedy product default. `--sample --preset nanbeige` restores the upstream sampling defaults: temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95. `--seed` follows the 4A addressable sampler contract (u64 expands as SHA-256("fnlp-seed-u64-v1")||u64_be; effective seed emitted as 64-hex; --seed legal only with sampling).
- **Thinking**: `--think`/`--no-think` bounded — explicit token/time cap; thinking tokens never enter task JSON; prompt caches are keyed by mode; a missing close delimiter fails typed (no-result), never emits partial success.
- **Streaming**: NDJSON `token` events with `schema_version` and `request_seq` echo, integrated with the daemon framing contract.
- **`--tools`**: returns a TYPED unsupported-surface error until OQ-10's parser contract is EVIDENCED (a line-backed XML/JSON tool-call parser contract plus malformed-call fixture corpus). Tool declaration/rendering/parsing is compiled in only after that gate (Phase 4C). `fnlp` parses/emits tool-call data but NEVER executes tools — under any flag, ever.
- Chat uses the verbatim pinned template (Phase-1 builder over the OQ-7 AST matrix); user/document content enters via the trust-ABI segments.

## Constraints
No misleading success-shaped stubs: `--tools` is a versioned typed error the frozen robot schema describes, not a silent no-op; unseeded sampling draws entropy exactly once at admission (RANDOM capability); greedy has no RANDOM authority; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; determinism scoped (greedy exact under named profile; sampled replay via effective seed); BN-GEN-DEFAULT-001 must be visible in docs/BEHAVIOR_NOTES.md.

## Evidence / gates
Golden: `--sample --preset nanbeige` maps to exactly temperature 0.6/top_k 20/top_p 0.95 in the semantic envelope. `--tools` typed-error golden against the frozen robot schema. Thinking-cap and missing-close-delimiter fixtures return typed no-result. Streaming framing validated by the frozen NDJSON schema contract test. L4/L5 references: greedy stream exact under the named profile on oracle-reproducible prefixes (model-gated).

## Tests
Unit: flag matrix (--seed without --sample → typed error; --think bounds parsed; preset resolution); tool-call NEVER-execute assertion (no exec path exists — a policy test greps/denies process-spawn APIs in this module). Property: replaying an emitted effective seed reproduces the sampled stream (model-gated). E2E: generate and chat with/without thinking on fixtures; streaming token event sequence golden; SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without weights. Detailed logging: mode, preset values, seed emission (effective seed only in the result per privacy contract), thinking-cap events, stream backpressure events. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_generate_stream_golden.sh`: the generate/chat flag matrix incl. --think bounds, the --sample --preset nanbeige envelope check (0.6/20/0.95), the --tools typed-error golden, and stream-concatenation equality; one machine-parseable row per case (mode, preset values, prompt hash, exit code); SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (task-core bead): generate/chat are BuiltInTasks (FreeText strategy) sharing the envelope/typed-error contracts.
- A_SAMPLER (cross-epic): seeded sampling, preset parameter semantics, and greedy fusion live in the 4A sampler.
- A_TPL_L0 (cross-epic): the L0-exact chat-template builder renders prompts for chat/thinking modes.

title: [4B] Ship fnlp split + narrow normalize with byte-span preservation and coordinate maps
description:
## Background
`fnlp split` and the narrow `fnlp normalize` are non-LLM textutil surfaces (no model load) that feed every long-document and offset-preserving pipeline for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; SentencePiece tokenizer used only for token counting via `fnlp tokens`; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22 — which is why 44-deep KV makes long contexts expensive and splitting is a primary operating mode; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Offsets must survive or be honestly declared dead — never approximately relocated.

## Contract
- **`fnlp split`**: a VERSIONED conservative delimiter/newline splitter that preserves exact byte spans for every chunk and enforces byte + token budgets. Language coverage is measured, not claimed. Deterministic chunk coverage/overlap (same input + version → same chunks). No model load; token budgets use the embedded tokenizer.
- **`fnlp normalize` v1 (deliberately narrow)**: CRLF/CR→LF plus EXPLICITLY REQUESTED ASCII horizontal-whitespace trim/collapse operations ONLY; ALL other UTF-8 bytes remain unchanged. NFC/NFKC/case-folding are NOT in v1 (they require pinned generated Unicode tables with version/license/generator digest/conformance suite — a later bead, never a vague "Unicode normalize" label).
- **Coordinate honesty**: every transform states whether it preserves bytes, scalar positions, or neither. Wherever offsets must survive, an original↔normalized coordinate map is part of the contract and independently verified. Source-grounded NER/extraction never normalizes away from the original document unless such a lossless map is in the task plan; a span that cannot map back to exact original UTF-8 boundaries is `unanchored` or a no-result — NEVER approximately relocated.

## Constraints
Versioned transforms (splitter/normalizer version in every output); no model load; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; stdout data / stderr diagnostics; deterministic under a named version; exit codes 0–10.

## Evidence / gates
Property proofs in the invariant suite: concatenating split chunk bytes at their spans reconstructs the input exactly; every chunk within byte+token budgets; normalize touches only the specified bytes (a byte-level diff proves all other positions identical); coordinate map round-trips every surviving position. Golden: chunk boundaries for a multilingual fixture corpus frozen per splitter version. Scorecard hooks: `tokens`/`split`/`normalize` exact-parity and coordinate-property rows per the eval framework.

## Tests
Unit: CRLF/CR→LF cases incl. lone CR, CRLF at buffer edges; trim/collapse ops individually and combined; splitter budget enforcement at exact boundaries. Property/fuzz: random UTF-8 (and invalid-UTF-8 rejection paths) → split spans are a partition (half-open, non-overlapping unless overlap is requested, covering); normalize is idempotent; coordinate map bijective on surviving positions, and unmapped positions reported unanchored; adversarial length bounds. E2E: `fnlp split --json` and `fnlp normalize --json` goldens; deterministic across runs; model-free — fully green in ordinary CI (token-budget path uses the embedded tokenizer, still no artifact needed). Detailed logging: transform version, ops applied, byte counts, map size. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_split_normalize_golden.sh` (fully model-free, green in ordinary CI): drives split/normalize/tokens over the multilingual fixture corpus, one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, transform version, span-partition verdict, coordinate-map verdict, exit code).

## Dependencies & rationale
- (task-core bead): shares Request/Response typing, envelope, and CLI conventions even though these are non-LLM tasks.
- A_TOK_L0 (cross-epic): token budgets and `fnlp tokens` counting require the L0-exact embedded tokenizer.

title: [4B] Build task-eval framework core: DATASETS.md registry, license-gated acquisition, digest-bound scorecards
description:
## Background
Kernel parity proves faithful execution, not useful tasks. Task quality of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) must be measured on named, versioned datasets with license discipline — a quality regression gates a release exactly like a parity regression. This bead builds the eval framework CORE (registry, acquisition, scorecard plumbing); per-task scorecards are the sibling bead. The user-facing `fnlp eval/calibrate/qualify` surfaces are Phase 5, not here.

## Contract
- **Dataset registry**: every dataset FIRST enters `docs/eval/DATASETS.md` with: immutable source; exact license text/terms; allowed use/redistribution; preprocessing digest; unit of analysis; development/calibration/test id splits (disjoint); known contamination/leakage risks.
- **License-gated acquisition**: a script may download only when the terms permit automated access; otherwise the harness accepts a user-supplied file and verifies its digest. "Fetch by hash" is NOT a substitute for permission. Only repo-authored fixtures or explicitly redistributable data are committed to the repo.
- **Scorecard identity**: every scorecard states model recipe id, prompt hash, thinking mode, and dataset version — so regressions are attributable to weights vs kernels vs prompts vs data.
- **Release gating**: quality regressions gate releases at parity rank; the harness emits machine-readable scorecard artifacts the release gauntlet consumes.
- **Split discipline**: each calibrated task keeps disjoint development/calibration/test ids; test ids are locked (evaluated only under the locked protocol); calibration parameters may fit only calibration data.
- Harness mechanics: task-shaped NDJSON in, digest-bound metrics out; deterministic metric computation (preregistered point estimates and confidence intervals on locked data — no ad-hoc statistics).

## Constraints
No dataset enters CI without its DATASETS.md row; contaminated/unlicensed data never committed; external LLM judges (if ever used by a task's eval) are disclosed and never the sole gate; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; benchmark/oracle tooling stays outside the release dependency graph; scorecards are typed evidence (claims map to docs/CLAIMS.json where public).

## Evidence / gates
CI validator: every referenced dataset has a complete DATASETS.md entry (source, license text, digest, splits); missing/incomplete → red. Digest-verification test for user-supplied files. Scorecard schema golden (recipe id + prompt hash + thinking mode + dataset version mandatory fields). Split-disjointness checker green on every registered dataset.

## Tests
Unit: DATASETS.md parser/validator; digest mismatch → typed refusal; split-overlap detection; scorecard field completeness. Property: metric computations deterministic across runs and row orderings (order-invariant aggregation); tiny-sample handling emits INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than fake precision. E2E: run the harness over a stub task's NDJSON on a repo-authored fixture dataset → scorecard artifact validates against its frozen schema; model-gated task runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Detailed logging: dataset id/version/digest, split sizes, every excluded row with reason.

## Dependencies & rationale
- A_SCAFFOLD (cross-epic): CI plumbing, docs tree, and the validator harness location must exist to host the registry and checks.
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract target(s) eval_framework green in the 24/26-green no-fail-fast suite (only canonjson + dependency_policy red)

title: [4B] Stand up flagship scorecards + matched clean/attack injection suite for extract/ner/classify/redact
description:
## Background
Phase 4B ships four flagship tasks; this bead stands up their scorecards plus the matched clean/attack content-injection suite, all through the eval framework core, for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). The Phase-4B exit gate requires flagship scorecards published and per-task injection attack-success rows published WITHOUT a firewall claim.

## Contract
- **extract**: field-F1 on a schema-diverse fixture corpus; 100% validity by construction is ASSERTED (G8), accuracy is MEASURED — the scorecard reports both distinctly.
- **ner**: span-exact and type-relaxed F1, reported BY language and type, on WNUT-17 and Few-NERD ONLY AFTER their exact upstream licenses are archived in docs/eval/DATASETS.md, PLUS a repo-authored modern-web/CJK set. CoNLL/OntoNotes/Reuters/LDC-class corpora remain user-supplied where terms require. Anchoring status reported alongside F1.
- **classify**: accuracy, macro-F1, Brier, ECE, and selective risk on license-gated SST-2/AG-News/Banking77-class corpora plus owned multilingual smoke.
- **redact**: recall-first reporting with precision, unresolved-anchor rate, AND per-detector rule metrics — recall/precision per detector, overlap-policy behavior, Unicode obfuscation, checksum/Luhn behavior where applicable — plus residual-leak verification (the `--verify` rerun as a measured metric).
- **Content-injection suite**: matched clean/attack fixture pairs for EVERY document-consuming flagship task across five attack families: role-marker text, refusal steering, false-negative steering, value steering, and tool-call bait. Report per-task attack-success rates.
