The structural control-id property is an invariant (trust-ABI); content-injection resistance is ONLY an empirical per-task metric — a bad rate may block a consequential preset, but NO "prompt-injection safe"/firewall claim ships, ever.
- Every scorecard states model recipe id, prompt hash, thinking mode, dataset version (framework contract).

## Constraints
Licenses archived BEFORE any download/commit (license-gated acquisition path); only repo-authored or redistributable fixtures committed; attack fixtures are matched pairs (same content ± attack) so deltas are attributable; no universal linguistic-law claims from probes; scorecard regressions gate releases at parity rank; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; evaluation tooling outside the release graph.

## Evidence / gates
Phase-4B exit: flagship scorecards published; per-task injection attack-success rows published with no firewall claim (wording checked against docs/CLAIMS.json — no unregistered superlative/safety claim). DATASETS.md rows complete for WNUT-17/Few-NERD/classify corpora or those datasets remain user-supplied. Scorecard artifacts digest-bound and reproducible (same inputs → same metrics).

## Tests
Unit: metric implementations (span-exact vs type-relaxed matching incl. boundary/type-only errors; Brier/ECE binning; selective-risk curves; per-detector aggregation) against hand-computed goldens. Property: F1/Brier order-invariance over row permutation; matched-pair delta computation correct under missing rows (fail closed with named gaps). E2E: full scorecard run over fixture datasets with the armed model (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL in ordinary CI — the metric layer itself runs green on recorded outputs); injection suite emits per-family attack-success rates per task. Detailed logging: every fixture id, clean/attack pairing, per-family outcome; every dataset row exclusion with reason. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_flagship_scorecards.sh`: drives all four scorecards plus the injection suite, one machine-parseable row per (task, dataset, attack family) carrying dataset version+digest, prompt hash, recipe id, thinking mode, and attack-success rate; SKIPPED_NO_MODEL rows explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- (eval framework core bead): registry, license gates, scorecard schema, and split discipline all come from it.
- (extract bead): its task surface + fixtures are what the extract scorecard and injection suite exercise.
- (ner bead): span metrics and anchoring-status reporting need the shipped ner surface.
- (classify bead): calibration-adjacent metrics (Brier/ECE) run over its score outputs.
- (redact bead): per-detector metrics and residual-leak verification exercise its detector union and --verify.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **Metric layer + goldens.** Deliverable: the metric implementations all four scorecards share — field-F1; span-exact and type-relaxed F1 (boundary and type-only error handling); accuracy/macro-F1/Brier/ECE/selective-risk; per-detector aggregation. Test evidence: unit metrics against hand-computed goldens (span matching, Brier/ECE binning, selective-risk curves, per-detector aggregation); property — F1/Brier order-invariance over row permutation. Next milestone assumes: trusted metric primitives every scorecard can consume.
2. **Dataset acquisition + DATASETS.md license gating.** Deliverable: WNUT-17 and Few-NERD used ONLY AFTER exact upstream licenses are archived in docs/eval/DATASETS.md; license-gated SST-2/AG-News/Banking77-class corpora; the repo-authored modern-web/CJK set and owned multilingual smoke; CoNLL/OntoNotes/Reuters/LDC-class corpora remain user-supplied where terms require; only repo-authored or redistributable fixtures committed. Test evidence: DATASETS.md rows complete (or datasets remain user-supplied); every dataset row exclusion logged with reason; licenses archived BEFORE any download/commit. Next milestone assumes: lawful fixture corpora exist to run scorecards over.
3. **extract scorecard.** Deliverable: field-F1 on the schema-diverse fixture corpus, reporting 100%-validity-by-construction as ASSERTED (G8) distinctly from MEASURED accuracy; scorecard states model recipe id, prompt hash, thinking mode, dataset version. Test evidence: full scorecard run over fixture datasets (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL in ordinary CI; metric layer green on recorded outputs); digest-bound reproducible artifact. Next milestone assumes: the scorecard schema/framework contract exercised end-to-end once.
4. **ner + classify scorecards.** Deliverable: ner span-exact and type-relaxed F1 reported BY language and type with anchoring status alongside F1; classify accuracy, macro-F1, Brier, ECE, and selective risk over its score outputs; both carrying the framework metadata contract. Test evidence: same model-gated run pattern with recorded-output metric verification; digest-bound reproducibility (same inputs → same metrics). Next milestone assumes: the remaining flagship metric surfaces are wired.
5. **redact scorecard.** Deliverable: recall-first reporting with precision, unresolved-anchor rate, AND per-detector rule metrics (recall/precision per detector, overlap-policy behavior, Unicode obfuscation, checksum/Luhn behavior where applicable), plus residual-leak verification (the `--verify` rerun as a measured metric). Test evidence: per-detector aggregation against goldens; model-gated scorecard run; digest-bound artifact. Next milestone assumes: all four flagship scorecards are publishable.
6. **Matched clean/attack content-injection suite.** Deliverable: matched clean/attack fixture pairs (same content ± attack, so deltas are attributable) for EVERY document-consuming flagship task across the five attack families — role-marker text, refusal steering, false-negative steering, value steering, tool-call bait — reporting per-task attack-success rates; the structural control-id property stays an invariant (trust-ABI) while content-injection resistance remains ONLY an empirical per-task metric. Test evidence: property — matched-pair delta computation correct under missing rows (fail closed with named gaps); the suite emits per-family attack-success rates per task; logging of every fixture id, clean/attack pairing, and per-family outcome. Next milestone assumes: publishable per-task rows for the exit gate.
7. **Phase-4B exit publication + claims check.** Deliverable: flagship scorecards published and per-task injection attack-success rows published WITHOUT a firewall claim — a bad rate may block a consequential preset, but no "prompt-injection safe"/firewall claim ships, ever; scorecard regressions gate releases at parity rank. Test evidence: wording checked against docs/CLAIMS.json (no unregistered superlative/safety claim); scorecard artifacts digest-bound and reproducible (same inputs → same metrics).

title: [P1] Implement SP BPE encode/decode engine + L0 token-id-exact gate
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT with q 3072→6144, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Its tokenizer is SentencePiece **BPE** (`TrainerSpec.model_type=2`) with an identity normalizer, byte pieces, `add_bos_token=true`, `add_eos_token=false`, `legacy=false` [OBSERVED@pin]. The model card's own usage snippet passes `use_fast=False`, so the SLOW SentencePiece path is canonical. Everything downstream — template rendering, grammar, scoring, the untrusted-document boundary — sits on token-id-exact tokenization, which is why this bead carries gate L0 (anchor A_TOK_L0).

## Contract
- Implement the SP BPE encode/decode engine in `src/tokenizer/` over the `SpmModel` produced by the protobuf-reader bead:
  - Identity normalizer (no NFKC), SentencePiece whitespace conventions exactly as the slow reference behaves at the pin.
  - BPE merge/scoring semantics: greedy pair merging driven by piece scores exactly as SentencePiece BPE does; byte-fallback via the byte pieces for any input not representable by ordinary pieces.
  - Special-token handling: `add_bos=true`, `add_eos=false`, `legacy=false`; special/added-token injection and precedence matching the slow reference (added-token precedence is part of the OQ-6 edge surface and must match, not approximate).
  - Three distinct public operations, never blurred: `encode_ids(&str/bytes) -> Vec<u32>`; `decode_bytes(&[u32]) -> Vec<u8>` (the authority for grammar and source-grounding); `decode_text(&[u32]) -> Result<String, DecodeTextError> | lossy-mode result` — `decode_text` returns valid UTF-8 or an EXPLICIT decode error / explicitly-requested lossy result. Silent U+FFFD replacement inside an exactness path is forbidden.
- L0 GATE (this bead's exit): token-id-EXACT equality vs the pinned slow reference tokenizer over (a) the frozen multilingual + code + special-token adversarial corpus and (b) the fast-vs-slow reconciliation corpus (sequences where HF fast and slow tokenizers are known to agree/disagree; we match SLOW). Zero mismatches; a mismatch is a bug, not a tolerance.
- Decode conventions (whitespace marker ▁ handling, byte-piece reassembly, special-token text) reproduce the reference's own canonical behavior. `decode(encode(x)) == x` is NOT asserted as a general property — SP normalization makes it false in general; byte-losslessness is asserted only on paths where the reference itself is lossless (e.g. byte-fallback).

## Constraints
- Pure Rust, std + allowlist only (clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite); NO `tokenizers`/`tiktoken` crates. `unsafe_code = "deny"`, no unsafe island here. No Rayon in the release graph.
- G1 > G2, profile-scoped: L0 is exact, full stop — there is no "close enough" tokenization. Any speedup (e.g. precomputed merge tables) must preserve id-exactness and is differential-tested against the straightforward in-repo implementation.
- decode_text lossy mode is an explicit caller opt-in flag, never a default, and its output is marked lossy.
- Fail closed: unknown bytes route through byte-fallback or reject; no silent skipping.

## Evidence / gates
- **Gate L0 (tokenizer half)**: exact token ids over the adversarial corpus (multilingual scripts, code, emoji/ZWJ, mixed specials, long-run whitespace, byte-fallback-only inputs) and the fast-vs-slow corpus, both frozen as fixtures with digests. Fixture generation is the reference-fixtures script's tokenizer section; results recorded in the conformance harness. This bead is anchor **A_TOK_L0** — downstream epics (grammar, tasks, forward-pass prompts) key off it.
- Fuzz evidence: encode/decode never panic on arbitrary input (see Tests).

## Tests
- Unit: happy-path encodes with known id sequences; BOS injection on/off surfaces; byte-fallback round-trips; special-token injection & precedence cases; decode_bytes vs decode_text split; decode_text invalid-UTF-8 error and explicit-lossy behaviors; empty input; whitespace-only input.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary bytes/strings → `encode_ids` then `decode_bytes` never panics; on byte-fallback-lossless paths `decode_bytes(encode_ids(x)) == x`; arbitrary id sequences (including out-of-range ids, which must reject typed) → decode never panics.
- Differential e2e: the L0 corpus run — every fixture line logs input digest, expected ids digest, got ids digest, and the FIRST diverging index + a ±8-token context window on failure (detailed logging is mandatory; a bare "mismatch" is not acceptable output).
- CI posture: corpus fixtures are committed; no weight artifact needed; nothing here is SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Fixture REGENERATION is oracle-gated and out of scope for CI. Named artifact: `tests/l0_tokenizer_conformance.rs` (unit + property + the L0 corpus differential), emitting per-corpus-file `L0 corpus=<name> RESULT=PASS|FAIL lines=<n>` and a final `L0_TOKENIZER RESULT=<verdict> mismatches=<n>` summary.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on the [P1] SentencePiece protobuf reader bead: this engine consumes its `SpmModel` (pieces/scores/types/special ids); building BPE on an unverified parse would launder parse bugs into "tokenizer bugs".
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_FIXTURES — the pinned-oracle fixture corpus (reference tokenizer id sequences) is generated by the Phase −1 fixtures bead; the L0 differential needs those frozen files.

title: [P1] Ship fnlp tokens CLI with hash-checked embedded tokenizer
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). `fnlp tokens` is the first user-visible product surface of the Lexicon subsystem: exact token counting/inspection without loading any weights. It also enforces a load-time integrity rule the whole product relies on: the tokenizer bytes are EMBEDDED in the binary (the tokenizer is Apache-2.0, carried with attribution) and must be hash-checked against the artifact's own tokenizer copy so a binary and a `.fnlpq` artifact can never silently disagree about tokenization.

## Contract
- `fnlp tokens` (and identically under the long binary name `franken_nlp`): reads text from file args or stdin; emits EXACT token counts and, on request, the exact token ids (and optionally per-token decoded byte segments) from the L0-exact SP BPE engine.
- Modes: human mode (concise text output), `--json` (single JSON document), robot mode (versioned NDJSON per input, schema self-described by `robot schema`). stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics; honor `NO_COLOR`, `CI`, `TERM=dumb`. Exit codes follow the project map (0 success; typed failures per `error.rs`; exit 10 = typed no-result).
- Counting semantics are explicit flags, never guesses: `--bos on|off` (default on, matching the model's `add_bos=true`; the value used is echoed in `--json`/robot output), raw-text vs template-rendered counting is out of scope here (template beads own rendering); this command tokenizes exactly the bytes given.
- EMBEDDED-TOKENIZER INTEGRITY: the binary embeds the pinned tokenizer.model bytes with their SHA-256. At any load that also opens a model artifact, the artifact's embedded tokenizer copy is hashed and MUST equal the binary's embedded hash; mismatch is a typed fail-closed error naming both digests, the artifact path, and next steps (the message states which digest belongs to the binary and which to the artifact, and points at `fnlp pull` for a matching artifact or a matching binary release). `fnlp tokens` without an artifact uses the embedded bytes and reports their digest in `--json`/robot output.
- Deterministic: same input bytes + same binary → byte-identical data output (ordering, ids, counts).

## Constraints
- Two binaries, one entrypoint: this subcommand lives behind `pub fn cli_main() -> ExitCode`; `src/main.rs` and `src/bin/fnlp.rs` stay thin one-line shims.
- Dependency allowlist only (clap for CLI, serde/serde_json for JSON, sha2 for digests); no new crates. No Rayon in the release graph; no network; no model weights required for this command.
- Robot mode: stable versioned schema, line-oriented NDJSON, no human decoration mixed into machine output.
- License mechanics: embedded tokenizer bytes carry Apache-2.0 attribution via the license bundle; this bead must not strip or duplicate that plumbing.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) golden CLI fixtures (human, --json, robot NDJSON) frozen and green; (b) the embedded-vs-artifact hash-check proven by a test that presents a deliberately mismatched tokenizer copy and asserts the typed fail-closed error with both digests; (c) robot output validating against the frozen `robot schema` JSON-schema fixture (contract test).
- Counts/ids agree with the A_TOK_L0 engine by construction (same code path); a smoke differential over the L0 corpus is included in the e2e run.

## Tests
- Unit: flag parsing; BOS on/off counts; empty input; stdin vs file; multi-file ordering; invalid-UTF-8 input handling per the engine's decode_text/bytes contract.
- Property: arbitrary input bytes → command exits 0 or typed error, never panics; NDJSON output always parses line-by-line and validates against schema.
- E2E: golden transcripts for human/--json/robot modes with digests logged; tokenizer-mismatch artifact test (fabricated small artifact stub with a wrong tokenizer digest → typed error, exit code asserted, both digests present in stderr/robot error event). Detailed logging: every e2e failure prints the full argv, env snapshot (NO_COLOR/CI/TERM), and byte-level diff of expected vs got output.
- CI posture: no weights needed; nothing reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL (the artifact-mismatch test uses a fixture stub, not a real model download). Named artifact: `tests/cli_tokens.rs` (golden transcripts for all three modes, property tests, the mismatch-artifact case), ending with `CLI_TOKENS RESULT=PASS|FAIL modes=<human,json,robot>`.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on the [P1] SP BPE encode/decode engine (A_TOK_L0): counts/ids must come from the L0-exact engine; shipping a CLI over a pre-gate tokenizer would publish wrong counts.
- Robot-skeleton bead (franken_nlp-5e3): robot-mode NDJSON events, the frozen `robot schema` fixture, and the contract-test machinery this CLI's robot output validates against are built there (error.rs exit-code semantics arrive transitively through it).

title: [P1] Build chat-template typed AST + builder with L0 byte-exact fixture matrix
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). The pinned chat template uses `<|im_start|>` / `<|im_end|>` role framing, `<think>` / `</think>` reasoning markers (`enable_thinking` default ON), `preserve_thinking`, and BOTH XML and JSON tool-call branches [OBSERVED@pin]. We do NOT ship a Jinja interpreter (no `minijinja` — the allowlist forbids it): the template is ONE fixed program, and we implement *it* as a typed Rust builder. This bead is anchor A_TPL_L0 — every prompt any task ever builds flows through it.

## Contract
- Typed AST in `src/template/`, covering the complete pinned accepted surface: `Conversation`, `Message` (roles `system|user|assistant|tool`), `MessageContent` (plain string OR iterable content parts), `ContentPart` (text and the pinned media kinds), `AssistantReasoning` (`reasoning_content`, embedded `<think>` extraction), `ToolDefinition`, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`.
- Builder renders `apply_chat_template` BYTE-EXACTLY across the complete accepted mode matrix:
  - First-position system enforcement + the DEFAULT SYSTEM TEXT when no system message is supplied.
  - Non-leading system messages handled exactly as the pinned template handles them.
  - Media-reminder rendering exactly (the template inserts reminder text for media parts).
  - Assistant `reasoning_content` and embedded `<think>…</think>` extraction; `preserve_thinking` true/false (prior-turn thinking preserved vs stripped).
  - Tool serialization in BOTH branches: XML tool-call form and JSON tool-call form, plus `ToolDefinition` listing.
  - CONSECUTIVE TOOL-RESULT GROUPING (adjacent tool messages group exactly as the template groups them).
  - The EXACT generation suffix (the assistant-start + thinking-marker tail for generation), including the `enable_thinking` on/off variants.
- REJECTION BEFORE TOKENIZATION: unknown roles, unknown mapping shapes, unknown content-part kinds, and malformed tool-call structures reject with typed errors BEFORE any tokenizer call. There is no permissive fallback rendering.
- Output is the rendered prompt string/bytes; tokenization of that output is the tokenizer engine's job (ids covered by L0's template half).
- L0 FIXTURE MATRIX (this bead's gate): byte-exact equality vs the pinned reference `apply_chat_template` outputs across the OQ-7 matrix — content arrays, media-reminder branches, default system text, non-leading system, adjacent tool responses, prior-turn thinking preserved/removed, both tool formats, empty/malformed fields (the malformed rows assert typed rejection, matching the archived accepted-mode census).

## Constraints
- No Jinja/template-language interpreter of any kind; one fixed program. Dependency allowlist only; serde/serde_json may serialize the AST but the rendered bytes are produced by our code, not a serializer's canonical form.
- Only trusted template code may emit role/think/tool control markup — this builder is that trusted code; the UntrustedDocument encoder bead consumes its `TemplateControlIds` discipline.
- G1 > G2: byte-exact or reject; no "similar enough" rendering. Presets are data; prompts are versioned — rendered-prompt hashes feed the prompt-template hash in every task envelope.
- Unknown forms forward-reject (fail closed), never best-effort.

## Evidence / gates
- **Gate L0 (template half)**: the frozen byte-exact fixture matrix green (every accepted mode) + typed-rejection tests green (every unaccepted form). Anchor **A_TPL_L0**. Fixtures carry digests; the conformance harness records pass/fail per matrix cell.
- The complete accepted mode matrix (not just happy paths) is enumerated in a table in the module docs, mirroring the archived census, so matrix coverage is checkable.

## Tests
- Unit: each AST node's construction/validation; first-position system logic incl. default text; generation suffix with thinking on/off; XML vs JSON tool branch selection; tool-result grouping across 2/3/N adjacent results; reasoning extraction edge cases (empty think block, think markers inside content as PLAIN TEXT — they are content here, not control).
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary JSON-shaped conversation values → builder returns Ok(rendered) for accepted forms or typed Err BEFORE tokenization for everything else; never panics; rendering is deterministic (same AST → same bytes, asserted by repeated-render digest equality).
- E2E: full fixture-matrix differential with detailed logging — on any mismatch print matrix-cell id, expected/got byte lengths, first diverging byte offset, and a hex+escaped-text window of ±64 bytes. Golden files under tests/fixtures with digests.
- CI posture: fixtures committed; no weights; nothing SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Fixture regeneration is the oracle script's job, not CI's. Named artifact: `tests/l0_template_matrix.rs` (unit + property + full matrix differential), emitting one `L0T cell=<matrix-id> RESULT=PASS|FAIL` line per cell and a final `L0_TEMPLATE RESULT=<verdict> cells=<n> rejects=<m>` summary.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on the [P1] SP BPE encode/decode engine (A_TOK_L0): the template gate includes tokenized-prompt id checks and the rejection boundary is "before tokenization", so the tokenizer surface must exist and be L0-exact first.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_FIXTURES — the pinned reference `apply_chat_template` renderings across the mode matrix are Phase −1 fixture artifacts. A_CTL_CENSUS — the archived accepted-AST/mode-matrix census and the TokenizerSpecialIds/TemplateControlIds registries define what "complete accepted surface" means; building against guessed registries is forbidden.

title: [P1] Implement UntrustedDocument encoder excluding all TemplateControlIds
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Two token registries are normative: `TokenizerSpecialIds` (ids whose tokenizer metadata says `special=true`: `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, end-of-text, base special pieces) and `TemplateControlIds`, which ADDITIONALLY contains template-significant added tokens — `<think>`, `</think>`, `<tool_call>`, `</tool_call>` — that carry `special=false` AT THE PINNED REVISION [OBSERVED@pin]. Generic `skip_special_tokens` handling therefore CANNOT police the untrusted-document boundary. Only trusted template code may emit role/think/tool control ids; documents are untrusted and must never smuggle them.

## Contract
- Implement the `UntrustedDocument` constrained encoder in `src/tokenizer/`: encode an untrusted document segment such that the emitted token id sequence
  1. EXCLUDES every member of the complete `TemplateControlIds` registry (superset of `TokenizerSpecialIds` for this purpose — exclusion covers BOTH registries' ids), including the `special=false` think/tool markers; and
  2. `decode_bytes(ids)` reproduces the document's EXACT original bytes (using ordinary and byte pieces).
- If exact byte preservation without any forbidden id is impossible for a given input, the encoder REJECTS with a typed preflight error. It never silently weakens the boundary (no dropping bytes, no substituting lookalikes, no permitting "just this one" control id).
- Literal marker TEXT stays ordinary content: a document containing the characters `<think>` or `<|im_start|>` encodes to ordinary/byte pieces that decode back to those exact bytes — the string survives, the CONTROL ID does not appear.
- The registry is loaded from the archived control-id census, never hand-listed in code; a test asserts the encoder's forbidden set is exactly the registry (no drift).
- Honesty boundary stated in API docs and enforced in claims: this proves MARKER CONTAINMENT only. It is NOT a prompt-injection firewall — instruction-shaped prose still steers the model; that is measured per-task by matched clean/attack scorecards elsewhere. All derived output remains untrusted data.

## Constraints
- Fail closed (reject, never degrade). No configuration flag may disable the exclusion for untrusted segments.
- Dependency allowlist only; no unsafe; no Rayon in the release graph.
- Deterministic: same document bytes → same id sequence (required for prefix caching and replay).
- The encoder must be the ONLY path by which document text enters a prompt; template builder code composes trusted control ids around it (typed trust boundary, doctrine #22).

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) the byte-preservation + full-exclusion property proven over the document corpus (every fixture: ids contain no registry member AND decode_bytes == original bytes, or a typed rejection); (b) FULL-REGISTRY FUZZ green — for EVERY id in `TemplateControlIds` (and every `TokenizerSpecialIds` member), adversarial documents built from its literal text, byte-split variants, and surrounding context never produce that id; (c) the registry-equality test vs the archived census. Results recorded in the conformance harness; this is the §9.3 metamorphic invariant "untrusted-segment token ids exclude every control id while decoding to the same document bytes".

## Tests
- Unit: plain text; text containing each literal marker string (`<think>`, `</think>`, `<tool_call>`, `</tool_call>`, `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`); markers split across artificial chunk boundaries; markers embedded mid-word; empty document; pure-binary (byte-fallback) documents; a constructed impossible case asserting typed rejection (if none exists for this vocab, the test documents that the rejection path is still exercised via an injected shrunken registry).
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary bytes → (ids exclude full registry AND decode_bytes(ids) == input) OR typed rejection; never panics. Registry-driven fuzz: seeds derived from every registry member's text and its UTF-8 prefixes/suffixes.
- E2E: encode→template-compose→decode round trip showing document bytes preserved and control ids present ONLY at trusted template positions. Detailed logging: on violation print the offending id, its piece text, byte offset in the document, and the ±32-byte context; on rejection print the typed reason.
- CI posture: corpus + registry fixtures committed; no weights; nothing SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named artifact: `tests/untrusted_encoder.rs` (unit + property/fuzz-seed replay + the encode→compose→decode e2e), ending with `UNTRUSTED RESULT=PASS|FAIL docs=<n> violations=<m>` plus the per-violation detail lines specified above.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on the [P1] chat-template typed AST + builder (A_TPL_L0): the trusted/untrusted composition seam and the control-id discipline are defined by the template builder; the encoder must slot into that seam, not invent its own.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_CTL_CENSUS — the complete archived `TemplateControlIds`/`TokenizerSpecialIds` registries are the authority for the forbidden set; hand-listing ids is forbidden.

title: [P1] Implement hf-bf16-eager forward pass with pinned cast points
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: a dense looped decoder with 22 physical layers executed in 2 loops (44 logical layer executions/token), KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, and final RMSNorm after EACH pass (loop 2 consumes loop-1 normalized output). hidden 3072; 48 query : 8 KV heads; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (config overrides hidden/heads=64 — q_proj 3072→6144, k/v_proj 3072→1024, o_proj 6144→3072); SwiGLU 10752; RMSNorm eps 1e-5; split-half RoPE θ=7e7; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head. Fidelity claims are PROFILE-SCOPED: the pinned HF oracle executes bf16 with explicit cast points, so the `hf-bf16-eager` profile OWNS all HF-match claims. This bead builds that profile's forward pass (anchor A_FWD) — the semantic reference execution every later optimized/quantized backend is judged against.

## Contract
- Implement the reference forward pass under the `hf-bf16-eager` numerics profile in `src/native_engine/`: embed → [22 layers → final RMSNorm] ×2 with KV slot = layer + loop×22 → lm_head, greedy argmax.
- Values are bf16 with the PINNED CAST POINTS, exactly:
  - **Embedding**: `embed_tokens(input_ids)` row STAYS bf16 (no widening) [OBSERVED@pin].
  - **RMSNorm** (eps 1e-5): reduce (sum of squares / rsqrt / scale) in f32, then CAST BACK to bf16.
  - **Softmax** (attention scores): computed in f32, then CAST BACK to the activation dtype.
  - **RoPE**: frequency/cos/sin tables constructed in f32, then CAST to the q/k dtype at application; θ=7e7, head_dim 128, split-half rotation.
  - **Logits**: EXPORTED as f32 (the pre-processor logit vector is f32; 166,144 × 4 = 664,576 bytes).
- Attention: GQA 48 query : 8 KV heads @ head_dim 128 (6 query heads per KV head), scale 1/√128, additive causal mask, eager (non-fused) semantics matching `attn_implementation="eager"`.
- MLP: SwiGLU gate/up 3072→10752, SiLU, elementwise mul, down 10752→3072; residual adds around attention and MLP per the pinned source.
- No bias anywhere; no sliding window; untied lm_head 3072→166,144.
- Cast discipline is centralized (named cast helpers per site) so the cast schedule is auditable and cannot drift silently; the profile enum value `hf-bf16-eager` selects this schedule.

## Constraints
- G1 > G2, profile-scoped: this path exists for correctness, not speed. It must be simple, readable, and obviously faithful; optimizations belong to later backends judged against it.
- head_dim is 128, NOT hidden/heads=64 — any 64-derived buffer/table here is catastrophically wrong (doctrine #4).
- The loop is the architecture: never collapse to 22 logical layers; final RMSNorm runs after EACH pass; no embedding re-injection (doctrine #3).
- Dependency allowlist + pinned FrankenSuite only (bf16 handling through pinned ft-core/ft-serialize surfaces — no `half` crate). No Rayon in the release graph; leaf kernels never spawn. `unsafe_code = "deny"` outside enumerated SIMD/mmap islands (none needed here).
- No silent numerics changes: any deviation from the pinned cast schedule is a DISCREPANCIES.md event with rollback, not a code tweak.

## Evidence / gates
- Anchor **A_FWD**. Closes on: L1 green for every op under the hf-bf16-eager tolerance vectors (thresholds from the measured oracle floor); L2 green across all 44 post-layer outputs + both post-loop norm states on the trace fixtures; L3 green (f32 exported logits within measured oracle tolerance AND exact argmax over the stable set); L4 greedy-exact over the oracle-reproducible prefixes (full gates land in the L2/L3-L4 harness beads — this bead must pass the portions that exist and provide the taps they need).
- Every claim is scoped `hf-bf16-eager`; no cross-profile claim is made here.

## Tests
- Unit: per-op reference tests (RMSNorm f32-reduce/bf16-cast; RoPE table f32-then-cast at positions {0,1,many}; softmax f32; GQA head-grouping 48:8@128; SwiGLU; residual), each against tiny hand-checkable tensors AND against spec-engine values; cast-schedule audit test asserting the named cast helpers are used at exactly the pinned sites.
- Property: forward is deterministic (same input → bit-identical outputs, single-threaded); KV writes land in slot layer+loop×22 (asserted via instrumented cache); loop-2 input equals loop-1 post-norm output bit-exactly within this implementation.
- E2E (model-gated): tiny-prompt forward vs committed oracle fixtures (logit digests, argmax sequence). Without the weight artifact these report **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** — never fake-pass. Detailed logging: per-execution max-abs/max-rel/ULP stats per (loop, layer) tap and first-divergence location on failure. Named artifact: `tests/bf16_eager_forward.rs` (per-op units incl. the cast-schedule audit, properties, model-gated fixture e2e), ending with `BF16_EAGER RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL taps=<n>` and naming the first diverging (loop, layer, point) on failure.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on the [P1] 44-slot KV cache + loop runner bead: the forward pass executes on that scheduler/cache; building it first prevents two divergent loop implementations.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_CENSUS — tensor name→shape→byte census (4,169,800,704 params / 8,339,601,408 bf16 payload bytes) is the authority for every buffer size and load check. A_SCAFFOLD — needs the crate skeleton, numerics-profile enum, and error/CI surfaces.

title: [P1] Implement diagnostic-f32 forward pass as structural bisect oracle
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, hidden 3072, 48:8 heads with head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), SwiGLU 10752, eps 1e-5, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). Fidelity is profile-scoped (§ numerics profiles: `hf-bf16-eager`, `diagnostic-f32`, `strict-quantized-vN`, `fast-vN`). `diagnostic-f32` is the STRUCTURAL BISECT ORACLE: a full-precision f32 execution used to localize where a divergence enters (structure vs rounding). It is deliberately NOT required to token-match bf16 — where greedy tokens flip between bf16 and f32, those flips are captured as NAMED FIXTURES, not treated as failures.

## Contract
- Implement the `diagnostic-f32` forward path in `src/native_engine/`, selected by the numerics-profile enum:
  - bf16 weights (and the bf16 embedding row) are WIDENED ONCE at load/entry to f32 per the profile's rule; thereafter the entire forward — embed row use, RMSNorm, RoPE tables and application, attention scores/softmax/weighted sum, SwiGLU, residuals, lm_head — runs in f32 end-to-end. No bf16 round-trips anywhere downstream of the single widening.
  - Same architecture semantics as the reference: 22 layers → final RMSNorm → same 22 layers → final RMSNorm; KV slot = layer + loop×22; GQA 48:8 @128 scale 1/√128; additive causal mask; logits f32.
- STRUCTURAL BISECT ROLE: the path exposes the same taps as the L2 harness (per-(loop,layer) post-layer outputs, both post-loop norms, pre/post attention/MLP bisect points) so a failing hf-bf16-eager or optimized run can be bisected against a numerics-insensitive structural reference. A structural bug (wrong KV slot, missed boundary norm, RoPE half-swap) shows up in diagnostic-f32 identically; a pure-rounding difference does not.
- TOKEN-FLIP FIXTURES: run the greedy corpus under both reference profiles; where diagnostic-f32's greedy stream diverges from hf-bf16-eager's, freeze the (prompt, position, bf16 token, f32 token, logit gap) tuple as a named divergence fixture. These fixtures are the profile's L4 contract — expected, documented, and stable; an UNLISTED flip is a regression.
- diagnostic-f32 meets its OWN L3 contract: logits within the f32-oracle tolerance measured from the pinned oracle's diagnostic-f32 fixture generation.

## Constraints
- Profile honesty (G1 > G2, profile-scoped): never present diagnostic-f32 agreement as HF parity — `hf-bf16-eager` owns HF-match claims. Never "fix" a bf16/f32 flip by nudging numerics; record it.
- The optimized release path may use f32 activations as a named, evaluated choice — but THIS path is the diagnostic profile, not a production fast path; keep it simple and readable.
- Allowlist deps only; no Rayon in the release graph; no unsafe. head_dim 128 everywhere (never 64).
- No silent numerics changes; cast/widen sites centralized and audited like the bf16 path's.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) L1/L2 green under diagnostic-f32 tolerance vectors (thresholds from the f32 oracle fixture floor); (b) L3 green under the f32-oracle tolerance; (c) the token-flip fixture set generated, committed, and green (re-run reproduces exactly the listed flips on the fixture corpus); (d) bisect-oracle utility demonstrated by a seeded-structural-bug test: intentionally mis-slot KV (layer+loop×22 broken), drop a boundary norm, and swap RoPE halves in a test double — the harness must localize each to the correct (loop, layer/boundary) tap.
- Recorded in the conformance harness; fixtures under tests/fixtures with digests.

## Tests
- Unit: single-widening audit (no bf16→f32→bf16 round trips downstream — type-level where possible, else instrumented); per-op f32 reference tests vs the scalar spec engine (which is also logical-f32, so agreement here is tight).
- Property: determinism (bit-identical repeat runs, single-threaded); tap availability at all 44 + 2 + bisect points.
- E2E (model-gated): greedy corpus under both profiles → flip extraction and comparison against the committed flip fixtures; logit-tolerance run vs f32 oracle fixtures. Reports **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact. Detailed logging: per-tap metric vector (max-abs, max-rel, ULP, cosine) and, for flips, the full (position, tokens, top-5 logits both profiles) record.
- Seeded-bug bisect tests run WITHOUT the model (spec-engine-backed), so the bisect machinery is CI-proven even in ordinary CI. Named artifacts: `tests/diag_f32_forward.rs` (units/properties/model-gated e2e) with the flip fixtures under `tests/fixtures/token_flips/`; runs end with `DIAG_F32 RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL flips_expected=<n> flips_observed=<m>`.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on the [P1] 44-slot KV cache + loop runner bead: shares the one loop scheduler/KV binding; a second private loop implementation would fork the architecture.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_CENSUS — buffer/tensor shapes from the machine census. A_SCAFFOLD — numerics-profile enum, error surfaces, CI harness hosting.

title: [P1] Build 44-slot KV cache + two-loop runner with boundary norm
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d. THE LOOP IS THE ARCHITECTURE: 22 physical layers are executed TWICE per token (44 logical layer executions); `_get_loop_cache_layer_idx(layer, loop) = layer + loop × num_hidden_layers` = layer + loop×22, so the KV cache has 44 INDEPENDENT slots per position, not 22; `skip_loop_final_norm=false`, so the SAME final RMSNorm runs after EACH 22-layer pass and loop 2 consumes loop-1's NORMALIZED output directly — there is no embedding re-injection and no loop-boundary projection [OBSERVED@pin]. Positions/cache positions/masks/RoPE positions are the same logical positions in both passes. head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024), 8 KV heads, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half. Per position KV = 44 × 2(K,V) × 8 heads × 128 × 2 B = 180,224 bytes = 176 KiB/token bf16. Everything else in Phase 1 (both reference forwards, L2's 44 taps) executes ON this runner, so it lands first.

## Contract
- Implement in `src/native_engine/` (looprun + kv):
  - **Loop runner**: the straight-line plan `for loop_idx in 0..2 { for layer in 0..22 { layer_forward(layer, kv[layer + loop_idx*22]) } hidden = final_rmsnorm(hidden) }` — implemented ONCE, truth-pack line-backed, with no re-injection/boundary projection and the SAME positions/masks/RoPE positions in both passes.
  - **44-slot KV cache**: 44 slots × 8 KV heads × head_dim 128 per position for K and V; append semantics for decode; per-slot addressing exactly `layer + loop×22`.
  - **Per-(loop,layer) binding resolved at engine build**: the runner holds a prebuilt binding table (loop, layer) → KV slot + weight refs; ZERO hash-map or dynamic lookups in the hot loop.
  - The runner is profile-agnostic: it drives whichever layer_forward the selected numerics profile provides (hf-bf16-eager, diagnostic-f32, later quantized), so there is exactly ONE loop implementation in the codebase.
  - **Loop-boundary fixture**: a named property/fixture asserting loop-1 post-final-RMSNorm output ≡ the hidden state entering loop-2 layer-0 (bit-exact within an execution), plus KV-slot-occupancy assertions (prefill of T tokens fills exactly 44×T slot-positions; slots 0–21 written in loop 0, 22–43 in loop 1).
- Buffer sizing derives from the census numbers (hidden 3072, KV head dim 128×8) — never from hidden/heads=64.

## Constraints
- Doctrine #3 verbatim: never size/schedule as a conventional 22-layer model; L2 has 44 layer outputs PLUS two norm states.
- Doctrine #4: head_dim 128 (q 3072→6144); any 64-based KV stride is catastrophically wrong.
- No Rayon in the release graph; leaf kernels never spawn; the runner itself is straight-line control flow (parallelism arrives in later phases via asupersync-owned teams, not here).
- Allowlist deps only; no unsafe; system allocator; inner token/layer loops make no general allocator calls once buffers are built (allocation-count test later hardens this — design for it now).
- Implemented once: no second loop implementation may ever appear (the scalar spec engine in tests/ is the deliberate independent exception, and it lives outside src/).

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) the loop-boundary fixture green; (b) KV slot-binding property tests green (slot = layer + loop×22 for all 44 combinations, resolved-at-build table matches the formula); (c) prefill→decode append semantics green (T-token prefill then 1-token decode appends position T in all 44 slots); (d) the two reference-forward beads successfully execute on this runner (their L-gates are their own evidence). Recorded in the conformance harness.

## Tests
- Unit: binding-table construction (all 44 entries); boundary-norm invocation count (exactly 2 per token forward); no-reinjection check (loop-2 input pointer/value equals loop-1 norm output, not the embedding); position/mask reuse across passes.
- Property: for random T (1..=64), prefill fills exactly the expected slot/position set; append-after-prefill equals one-shot prefill of T+1 (within a fixed profile, bit-exact); binding table is a pure function of (loop, layer).
- E2E: spec-engine cross-check on tiny random weights — runner-driven forward equals the independent tests/spec_engine forward bit-exactly in logical f32 (no model download needed). The spec engine is built by the sibling bead franken_nlp-80z (scalar f32 spec engine under tests/spec_engine); this cross-check test lands with whichever of the two beads merges second and reports SKIPPED_NO_SPEC_ENGINE truthfully until then. Model-gated fixture runs report **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without weights. Detailed logging: on any slot/boundary violation, log (loop, layer, computed slot, expected slot, position) and the first diverging value's coordinates. Named artifacts: `tests/looprun_kv.rs` (unit + property suites) and `tests/spec_cross_check.rs` (the spec-engine E2E, reporting SKIPPED_NO_SPEC_ENGINE until franken_nlp-80z merges); both end with machine-parseable `LOOPRUN RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_*` lines.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Scaffold bead (franken_nlp-uxw, cross-epic A_SCAFFOLD): looprun/kv land in the src/native_engine/ module tree, with the numerics-profile enum home, error surfaces, and CI harness created there.
- Test-time want, not a blocker: franken_nlp-80z (tests/spec_engine) supplies the independent forward used by the E2E cross-check; deliberately NOT a dependency edge so both root beads stay independently buildable.
- No intra-epic blockers: this is the epic's root implementation bead (both forward-pass beads depend on it, not vice versa).
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract target(s) looprun_kv green in the 24/26-green no-fail-fast suite (only canonjson + dependency_policy red)

title: [P1] Build scalar f32 spec engine under tests/spec_engine
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, hidden 3072, 48:8 heads @ head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024), SwiGLU 10752, eps 1e-5, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). The verification methodology needs an INDEPENDENT-ENOUGH in-repo check: a deliberately simple, readable, executable specification that localizes failures and prevents two optimized paths from merely agreeing on the same bug. HF Python remains the semantic authority; this spec engine (anchor A_SPEC) is the readable second implementation that every kernel harness (P1's L1 and P3's scalar/i64 oracle work) diffs against.

## Contract
- Implement under `tests/spec_engine/` (NOT under src/ — it is dev/test-only code and must never enter the release binary or become production fallback):
  - **Deliberately simple logical f32 tensors**: plain `Vec<f32>`-backed row-major tensors; no packing, no SIMD, no clever layouts; clarity beats speed everywhere.
  - **Direct 22×2 loops**: literal nested `for loop in 0..2 { for layer in 0..22 { … } final_rmsnorm; }` — the loop schedule visible in ten lines.
  - **Explicit 44-slot KV**: a plain indexed structure with slot = layer + loop×22 spelled out.
  - **Dense GQA expansion**: reference attention expands 8 KV heads to 48 by explicit repetition (6 query heads per KV head), computes full dense per-head attention with scale 1/√128 and additive causal mask — the naive, obviously-correct form.
  - **Stable scalar reduction order**: every sum (dot products, sum-of-squares, softmax normalizer, weighted V) is a single sequential scalar loop in a documented fixed order, so its results are deterministic and citable as "the canonical scalar order".
  - Complete op set: embed lookup, RMSNorm (eps 1e-5), RoPE θ=7e7 split-half @128, GQA attention, SwiGLU (gate/up 3072→10752, SiLU, mul, down), residuals, final norm, lm_head 3072→166,144, greedy argmax (lowest-token-id tie break).
- API: run a forward (prefill and single-token decode) over arbitrary small logical-f32 weights AND over the real widened weights, exposing per-(loop,layer) taps, both post-loop norms, and logits — the same tap names the L2 harness uses.
- SHARES NOTHING with the optimized engine: no packed/SIMD code paths, no shared kernel modules — only public types where unavoidable. A structural test asserts spec_engine does not link src/native_engine kernel internals.

## Constraints
- Dev/test only, NEVER production fallback (the plan says this verbatim); it must not be reachable from `cli_main()`.
- Simplicity is a requirement, not a style preference: no optimization PRs are accepted against it; changes are only for spec fidelity.
- head_dim 128 (never 64); the loop schedule and boundary norms exactly as pinned; no Rayon; no unsafe; std only.
- HF remains the semantic authority — spec-engine agreement is localization evidence, not parity proof by itself.

## Evidence / gates
- Anchor **A_SPEC**. Closes on: (a) spec-engine forward on tiny random weights agrees bit-exactly with hand-computed values for each op (unit goldens); (b) spec-vs-native cross-check harness runs (native reference forwards diff against spec taps within the L1/L2 metric vectors); (c) the no-shared-implementation structural test green; (d) taps exposed at all 44 + 2 + bisect points. Downstream: the L1 harness bead and P3's scalar/i64 oracle harness consume this engine as their readable reference.

## Tests

Detailed logging: every diff prints op name, (loop, layer) tap, index coordinates, expected/got, and abs/rel/ULP delta. Named artifacts: the engine module lives at `tests/spec_engine/` with its suites in `tests/spec_engine_goldens.rs` (per-op goldens, properties, tiny-model E2E, and the no-shared-implementation structural test); runs end with `SPEC_ENGINE RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL ops=<n>`.
