title: [P1] Build L1 per-op differential harness with per-profile tolerance vectors
description:
## Background franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, hidden 3072, 48:8 heads @ head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). The parity ladder is L0–L5; this bead builds **L1 — the per-op differential harness**: every kernel implementation vs the matching profile's scalar/oracle implementation, op by op, BEFORE whole-forward comparisons can be trusted. Fidelity is profile-scoped (`hf-bf16-eager` / `diagnostic-f32` / quantized profiles): each op gets tolerance thresholds derived per profile from the MEASURED oracle nondeterminism floor (established by ≥5 independently launched oracle processes at ≥2 preregistered thread counts) — never guessed, and NEVER cosine similarity alone. ## Contract - Build the L1 harness in `tests/` (conformance harness module): - **Integer ops: EXACT.** Any integer kernel (int8/int4 MAC paths arriving in later phases; embedding index-select; argmax over ties) must match the reference bit-for-bit; a single differing element fails. - **Float ops: named metric VECTOR per op** — max-abs error, max-rel error, max ULP distance, AND cosine similarity, evaluated together (cosine alone is explicitly insufficient); plus dedicated NaN/Inf/signed-zero behavior vectors (inputs containing NaN, ±Inf, −0.0 propagate/compare per the reference's own behavior, asserted explicitly, not skipped). - **Thresholds per (op × profile)**: a committed threshold table keyed (op, numerics_profile) with provenance — each threshold derives from the measured oracle floor fixtures (`hf-bf16-eager`, `diagnostic-f32`, quantized when those profiles land). The table file records the derivation (floor statistic + margin rule); harness refuses to run an op whose threshold row is missing (fail closed, no default tolerance). - **Op coverage**: RMSNorm (eps 1e-5), RoPE (θ=7e7, split-half, hd 128), softmax, GQA attention components (QKᵀ scores, weighted V), SwiGLU pieces (gate/up/down GEMV+SiLU+mul), residual add, embedding row gather, final norm, lm_head projection, argmax/top-k selection — every op the reference forwards use, each diffable in isolation over both tiny synthetic tensors and real-shape tensors (3072/6144/1024/10752/128/166,144). - **References**: the scalar spec engine (tests/spec_engine) is the in-repo comparator; committed oracle per-op fixtures are the external comparator where the fixture set provides them. - Harness API is reusable: later SIMD tiers (Phase 3) and quantized backends plug the same op ids and get the same metric/threshold machinery. - Output: per-op report rows (op, profile, metric vector, threshold, PASS/FAIL, fixture digests) in both human and machine-readable (JSON) form. ## Constraints - G1 > G2: L1 gates land BEFORE optimized kernels; a kernel without its L1 row cannot ship (doctrine #1). - Never cosine alone; never a tolerance without measured-floor provenance; integer means exact (doctrine: integer stages are exact; each floating stage has a named metric/tolerance contract). - Allowlist deps only; harness code is test-only; no Rayon; deterministic execution (fixed seeds for random tensor generation, seeds logged). - Fail closed on missing thresholds/fixtures — a missing row is an error, not a skip. ## Evidence / gates - Closes on: (a) the harness running the complete op inventory for `hf-bf16-eager` and `diagnostic-f32` against spec-engine + available oracle per-op fixtures, all green; (b) the threshold table committed with derivation provenance for every row; (c) NaN/Inf/signed-zero vectors present for every float op; (d) machine-readable report emitted and archived by the conformance run. This IS gate L1 for the two reference profiles; quantized rows are added by later epics using this same harness. ## Tests - Unit: metric implementations (max-abs/max-rel/ULP/cosine) against hand-computed values, including ULP across exponent boundaries and signed-zero handling; threshold-table loader rejects missing/duplicate rows. - Property: metric symmetry/monotonicity sanity; random-tensor differential runs are seed-reproducible (same seed → same report digest). - E2E: full L1 sweep both profiles; report golden (structure, not float values) frozen. Model-gated portions (real-weight op fixtures) report **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact; synthetic-tensor portions always run. DETAILED LOGGING: every failure logs op, profile, seed, tensor shapes, worst-element coordinates, expected/got values, all four metrics, and the threshold row cited. Named artifact: `tests/l1_per_op.rs` (harness entry; machine-readable report written as JSON + human summary), emitting one `L1 op= profile=

RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL` line per row and a final `L1 RESULT= rows=` summary. ## Dependencies & rationale - Depends on the [P1] scalar f32 spec engine (A_SPEC): the in-repo per-op comparator; without it L1 would compare optimized code only against itself. - Reference-fixtures bead (franken_nlp-6gi, cross-epic A_FIXTURES): the external comparator side — per-op oracle fixtures and the measured-floor-derived threshold provenance — is that bead's committed corpus; an L1 gate with no oracle-side fixtures could go green against a shared in-repo bug.

title: [P1] Build L2 44-execution harness with loop-boundary equality fixture
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d. THE LOOP IS THE ARCHITECTURE: 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions per token; KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; the final RMSNorm runs after EACH pass, so an implementation can produce plausible text while applying the boundary rule in the wrong place — which is exactly why the ladder names **L2: per-execution comparison at all 44 taps plus both post-loop norm states**. The pinned HF source overwrites `last_loop_all_hidden_states` at the end of each loop and returns only the final loop's collection [OBSERVED@pin], so standard `output_hidden_states=True` CANNOT capture loop-1 taps; the oracle side uses side-effect-free forward hooks (the trace-hook protocol) proven non-perturbing (traced ≡ untraced logits/tokens). head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), hidden 3072, SwiGLU 10752, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half.

## Contract
- Build the L2 harness in the conformance suite, comparing OUR engine taps against the trace-hook fixtures:
  - **All 44 post-layer outputs** — every (loop ∈ {0,1}, layer ∈ {0..21}) hidden state after the layer's residual add.
  - **Both post-loop final-RMSNorm states** — after loop 1 and after loop 2 (two additional named states; L2 is 44 + 2, never 44 alone).
  - **Named pre/post attention and pre/post MLP bisect points** within layers, exactly the tap set the trace-hook fixtures provide, so a divergence bisects to attention vs MLP vs norm within a specific (loop, layer).
  - **Loop-boundary equality fixture**: loop-1 post-final-norm state ≡ the captured loop-2 input hidden state, asserted as a NAMED equality fixture under the SAME traced execution (this is a structural identity in the traced data and in our engine; it pins the boundary-norm rule to the right place).
  - **Prefill→decode KV-append coverage**: the fixture set includes prefill and one-token-append KV tensors for all 44 slots; the harness compares our KV contents per slot.
  - Metric contract: per-tap PROFILE-SPECIFIC metric vector (max-abs/max-rel/ULP/cosine against the (op-class × profile) threshold rows from the L1 threshold machinery) for `hf-bf16-eager` and `diagnostic-f32`; both profiles run the full tap sweep.
- Output: per-tap machine-readable report (tap id = loop/layer/point, metrics, threshold row, PASS/FAIL, fixture digest) + human summary; first-divergence bisect helper that walks taps in execution order and names the earliest failing tap.

## Constraints
- Never collapse to 22: the harness enumerates 44 + 2 states by construction; a fixture set missing any tap is a hard error, not a partial pass.
- Tolerances come from the L1 threshold table (measured-floor provenance); no ad-hoc epsilons.
- Raw floating-point fixture digests are never presented as portable cross-host proof; comparisons are metric-based, digests only identify fixture files.
- Test-only code; allowlist deps; deterministic; fail closed on missing fixtures/thresholds.

## Evidence / gates
- **This IS gate L2.** Closes on: (a) full 44+2+bisect tap sweep green for both reference profiles on the committed trace fixtures; (b) the loop-boundary equality fixture green; (c) KV-append comparison green for all 44 slots (prefill T then append); (d) seeded-structural-bug detection demo (mis-slotted KV / dropped boundary norm / swapped RoPE halves each localized to the correct earliest tap) — proving the harness actually bisects. Archived as the conformance run's L2 section.

## Tests
- Unit: tap-id enumeration (exactly 44 post-layer + 2 norm + the named bisect points); fixture-loader validation (missing tap → typed error); bisect-walker ordering.
- Property: report determinism; tap comparison is order-independent (parallel-free, but shuffling comparison order changes nothing).
- E2E (model-gated): the real fixture sweep — reports **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without weights/fixtures, never fake-passes. Spec-engine-backed synthetic sweep (tiny weights, self-generated trace) always runs in CI to keep the harness executable. DETAILED LOGGING: per-tap metric line; on failure the earliest failing tap, its metrics vs thresholds, worst-element coordinates, and the upstream tap's status (to distinguish propagation from origin). Named artifact: `tests/l2_44exec.rs` (tap sweep + loop-boundary fixture + KV-append + seeded-bug bisect demo), emitting per-tap `L2 tap=<loop>/<layer>/<point> RESULT=...` lines and a final `L2 RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL states=<n>/46 bisect_points=<m>` summary (46 = 44 post-layer + 2 norm states).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P1] hf-bf16-eager forward (A_FWD): supplies the engine taps under the profile that owns HF-match claims.
- Depends on [P1] diagnostic-f32 forward: the second profile's taps; the structural bisect pairing is the point of L2.
- Depends on [P1] L1 per-op differential harness: threshold rows/metric machinery are L1's; L2 must not fork its own tolerance logic.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_TRACE — the non-perturbing 44-execution trace-hook protocol and its fixtures (traced ≡ untraced proof) are produced there. A_FIXTURES — the committed fixture corpus (per-(loop,layer) dumps, both post-loop norms, KV appends) this harness consumes.

title: [P1] Land L3/L4 gates, determinism gate, and census loader
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, hidden 3072, 48:8 heads @ head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half, vocab 166,144 → f32 logits vector 664,576 bytes, untied lm_head). This bead lands the Phase-1 exit gates above L2: **L3 (logits)**, **L4 (greedy tokens)**, the **scoped determinism gate**, and the **census loader** CI artifact. Params total 4,169,800,704 = 8,339,601,408 bf16 tensor-payload bytes; the two published safetensors files total 8,339,624,720 bytes (exactly 23,312 bytes of container/header overhead).

## Contract
- **L3 gate (logits)**: compare the F32 EXPORTED PRE-PROCESSOR logits (before any sampler/processor touches them; full 166,144-entry vector, 664,576 B) against oracle fixtures. For `hf-bf16-eager`: within the measured-oracle-floor tolerance AND EXACT ARGMAX over the stable set (the fixture positions whose argmax was stable across the oracle's nondeterminism-floor runs). For `diagnostic-f32`: within its f32-oracle tolerance. Thresholds come from the L1 threshold table (measured provenance, fail closed if missing).
- **L4 gate (greedy tokens)**: greedy decoded stream AFTER THE COMPLETE PROCESSOR STACK (the full ordered logit-processor pipeline in play for greedy — EOS/min-length/stop handling and any reference-active processors; argmax tie break = lowest token id) must be EXACT over the ORACLE-REPRODUCIBLE PREFIXES for `hf-bf16-eager` (the frozen stable prefixes from the oracle floor audit; no claim past the stable prefix). `diagnostic-f32` flips are recorded as named divergence fixtures (its own contract), not failures.
- **Determinism gate (Phase-1 scope)**: batch-1 semantics under ONE NAMED numerics profile — repeated identical runs (fresh process, same artifact/profile) produce bit-identical token streams and identical exported logits; the gate names the profile in its report. (Batch-M≡batch-1 and prefix-fork≡cold are LATER epics' gates; this bead must not claim them.)
- **Census loader**: load-time verification of the machine-readable census — every tensor name → shape → byte size (totals: 4,169,800,704 params; 8,339,601,408 payload bytes; 23,312 container overhead), fail-closed on ANY extra, missing, or mis-shaped tensor, including the absence-assertions (no mHC/depth/LoopSplit/n-gram tensor families may appear in the 201-name index). CI runs the loader against the census artifact; drift fails CI.
- All gate reports are machine-readable (JSON rows: gate, profile, corpus/fixture digest, result) and archived by the conformance run.

## Constraints
- G1 > G2, profile-scoped: `hf-bf16-eager` owns HF-match claims; `diagnostic-f32` is not required to token-match bf16; no blanket claims across profiles.
- Determinism is scoped (doctrine #9): semantic greedy output exact under a named profile; NO cross-machine floating-point byte-identity claim; canonical-bytes claims (ordered output, scrubbed metadata) are separate later surfaces.
- The product default is greedy for reproducibility; parity gates run greedy where the oracle is deterministic. Sampling parity is NOT claimed here (seeded-sampler contract is a different surface).
- Fail closed everywhere: missing fixture/threshold/census row = error, not skip. Allowlist deps only; test/CI code.

## Evidence / gates
- **This closes the Phase-1 exit**: L0 exact (tokenizer+template beads), L1–L3 green for both reference profiles, L4 exact on hf-bf16-eager oracle-reproducible prefixes with diagnostic-f32 meeting its structural/logit contract, 44-tap + both-norm + KV-append fixtures green (L2 bead), determinism gate green, census loader green. The conformance harness archives every gate row; this bead's close reason cites the archived run id.

## Tests
- Unit: stable-set extraction from floor fixtures; argmax tie-break (lowest id); processor-stack ordering for greedy; census loader against (a) the real census fixture, (b) mutated censuses (one tensor removed / added / reshaped / renamed → each a distinct typed error naming the tensor).
- Property: determinism-gate machinery detects an injected nondeterminism (a test double with a racy accumulator must FAIL the gate); L3 comparator is symmetric and seed-reproducible.
- E2E (model-gated): full L3/L4/determinism sweep on the fixture corpus — **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact, never fake-passing; census loader e2e always runs against the committed census JSON. DETAILED LOGGING: L3 failures log position, worst logit index, expected/got, metric vs threshold; L4 failures log the first diverging position, both tokens, both top-5 logit sets, and whether the position was inside the stable prefix; determinism failures log the two run digests and first diverging byte. Named artifacts: `tests/l3_l4_gates.rs`, `tests/determinism_gate.rs`, and `tests/census_loader.rs` (the census e2e always runs; the loader is release code exercised through it); each emits machine-parseable `L3|L4|DETERMINISM|CENSUS RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL ...` summary lines archived by the conformance run.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P1] L2 44-execution harness: L3/L4 sit above L2 in the ladder; certifying logits/tokens before the 44-tap sweep is green would invert the ladder and mask structural bugs (cross-epic fixture/trace flows arrive through L2's wiring).
- Census-generator bead (franken_nlp-7xa, cross-epic A_CENSUS): the census loader verifies every load-time tensor against the committed machine-readable census artifact (201 names; totals 4,169,800,704 params / 8,339,601,408 payload bytes / 23,312 container overhead); without that artifact the loader gate has no authority to check against.
- Oracle-floor bead (franken_nlp-snp): the L3 "stable set" and the L4 "oracle-reproducible prefixes" are DEFINED by docs/truth-pack/oracle_floor.json; certifying L3/L4 without the measured floor would invent tolerances (never derived from two observations).

title: [P3] Build measured dispatch-table framework + robot backends reporting
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions/token, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), SwiGLU 10752, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Phase 3 ships per-arch int8 SIMD tiers; this bead builds the frame they all plug into. Doctrine: **measured-faster wins; hardware capability is NOT a routing decision** (franken_ocr shipped Apple Silicon defaulting to LLVM-autovec over SDOT/SMMLA for some dense int8 shapes because measurement said so). One `int8_gemm` / `int8_gemv` / `int4_gemv` entry set, capability-detected once, but SELECTED per fixed shape and regime from a measured dispatch table. This bead is anchor A_DISPATCH.

## Contract
- **Dispatch framework** in `src/native_engine/` (dispatch + backends reporting):
  - Tier registry covering the full catalog: A1 (aarch64 SMMLA `vmmlaq_s32`, gated on the OS actually advertising FEAT_I8MM), A2 (aarch64 `dotprod` SDOT `vdotq_s32`), A3 (aarch64 LLVM-autovec i32 MAC — first-class, not fallback), X1a (`avx512f`+`avx512vnni` zmm VPDPBUSD), X1b (X1a features + `avx512vl` 256-bit EVEX-VNNI), X2 (`avxvnni` `_mm256_dpbusd_epi32`), X3a/X3b (`avx2` exact decompositions), S (scalar i32 MAC — always available, bit-exact floor).
  - **Dispatch table keyed (ISA, shape, regime)**: shape from the fixed model dims (K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}; fixed N set; dynamic M bucketed), regime ∈ {prefill/GEMM, decode/GEMV, batched-decode skinny-M}. Table rows are MEASURED choices with provenance (benchmark id, host class, date); hardware capability only defines the CANDIDATE set, never the selection.
  - **Detection-gated execution only**: capability detection uses the platform's reviewed runtime feature-detection surface once at startup; OS/firmware exposure is authoritative (AVX-512 can be absent despite CPU family support; FEAT_I8MM must be OS-advertised, never inferred from a marketing name). There is NO in-process "guarded smoke instruction" probe — no portable, dependency-free way exists to run an unsupported instruction "guardedly" in-process without risking the very SIGILL the selftest exists to prevent; a child-process ISA probe is out of scope until an approved OS surface can contain and report SIGILL/structured exceptions.
  - **Forced tiers fail BEFORE dispatch**: `--force-tier`/env-forced requests for an undetected tier return a typed error pre-dispatch; they never reach kernel code and never fault. Forced paths for proof runs on SUPPORTED tiers remain available.
  - **`fnlp robot backends`** (versioned NDJSON/JSON): reports detected features, the selected kernel id + tile geometry per (shape, regime), benchmark-table provenance, WHY any wider tier lost (measured numbers or "no measurement — conservative default"), and requested-vs-observed placement fields where relevant. Human mode summarizes; robot mode is schema-stable.
  - Fallback ladder: with no measured row, selection falls to the widest DETECTED tier's conservative default or S, and the report says so explicitly; absence of a benchmark row is never invented as a measurement.

## Constraints
- Capability never routes (doctrine #6); measured-faster wins; a narrower tier may be the shipped default on a wider-capable CPU.
- No model-name/vendor-name routing tables — feature detection only.
- Allowlist deps only; `unsafe_code = "deny"` — the dispatch layer itself is safe code (unsafe lives only inside the enumerated SIMD kernel islands of the tier beads). No Rayon in the release graph; dispatch never spawns.
- Robot-mode ergonomics: stable versioned schema, stdout data / stderr diagnostics, `NO_COLOR`/`CI`/`TERM=dumb` honored.
- Local tuning (Phase 6) may later overlay validity-domain-keyed rows; this bead's table format must carry the keying (binary/kernel ABI, artifact recipe, CPU/ISA, OS exposure) so tuning cannot turn a transient into a machine constant.

## Evidence / gates
- Anchor **A_DISPATCH**. Closes on: (a) tier registry + detection green on at least aarch64 (Apple) and x86-64 (Zen 3) CI/dev hosts, with unsupported tiers absent from candidates; (b) forced-unsupported-tier typed pre-dispatch failure test green; (c) `robot backends` output validating against its frozen JSON-schema fixture and showing selection provenance; (d) dispatch-table load/lookup property tests green (missing row → declared conservative fallback, never a fabricated measurement). Selection-quality evidence (actual measured rows) accrues from the tier + gauntlet beads and lands in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.

## Tests
- Unit: table lookup precedence; candidate-set construction per detected-feature combinations (feature sets mocked via injected detection results); forced-tier validation (supported → honored; unsupported → typed error, no dispatch); schema of `robot backends` events.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary (ISA-feature-set, shape, regime) queries never panic and always return either a detected-tier selection or S; table files with unknown/duplicate/corrupt rows reject cleanly.
- E2E: `fnlp robot backends` golden transcript per host class (digest-logged); a differential asserting the selected kernel for each fixed shape actually executes (smoke matmul through the dispatcher on detected tiers only). DETAILED LOGGING: every selection logs key, chosen tier, provenance id, and losing candidates with their recorded numbers; failures print the full detection vector. Named runnable driver for the whole kernel cluster: `scripts/e2e_backends_matrix.sh` — enumerates detected tiers (S always; A1/A2/A3, X1a/X1b/X2, X3a/X3b where detected), force-runs each over every fixed (shape, regime) differential vs tier S, and emits one NDJSON row per (tier, shape, regime) with timestamps, expected-vs-actual output checksums, explicit SKIPPED_UNSUPPORTED_ISA rows, the full CPU feature vector, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line; the tier beads' dispatcher-driven smoke runs ride this driver.
- No model weights needed; nothing here is SKIPPED_NO_MODEL (kernel smoke uses synthetic tensors).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SCAFFOLD — needs the crate skeleton, robot-schema plumbing, and error/exit-code map to host the dispatcher and `robot backends`.
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract target(s) dispatch green in the 24/26-green no-fail-fast suite (only canonjson + dependency_policy red)

title: [P3] Implement scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle harness
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072), SwiGLU 10752, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). Every SIMD tier in the Phase-3 catalog (SMMLA/SDOT/autovec/VNNI/AVX2) must be proven EQUAL to one canonical answer. This bead builds that authority: **scalar reference kernels (tier S) plus an i64 oracle harness** — the bit-exact floor every tier is differentially tested against, and the overflow-proof instrument for every intermediate.

## Contract
- **Tier S scalar kernels** in `src/native_engine/`: plain scalar i32-accumulating int8 GEMM and GEMV (and the int4→int8 unpack feeding the same MAC) over the model's fixed weight-side shapes — K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}, the fixed N set (6144, 1024, 3072, 10752, 166,144), dynamic M/T — in the canonical algebra (s8 weights, zero-point 0). Portable, cross-compiles everywhere, always in the dispatch candidate set, and IS the shipped floor on hosts with nothing better.
- **i64 oracle harness** (test-side): recompute every dot product/accumulation chain in i64 and assert (a) equality with the i32-path result after the canonical narrowing rules and (b) that NO i32 intermediate exceeded i32 range. Bounds to verify against, at K=10752 (worst K): full-domain S8×S8 ≤ 176,160,768; offset-domain raw U8×S8 ≤ 350,945,280; the 128·Σw correction ≤ 176,160,768; conservative raw+correction ≤ 527,106,048 — all with >4× headroom vs 2^31−1 = 2,147,483,647. The harness proves these numerically for every model K, every int4 group case, row sums, and every tail length, not just cites them.
- Domain: ALL stored i8 bit patterns (−128..=127) — the converter currently targets [−127,127], but the proof covers the full domain so correctness is not secretly coupled to a quantizer convention.
- The harness API is the shared differential fixture generator for the tier beads: given (shape, seed, domain profile) it yields input sets — exhaustive small vectors, randomized property vectors, all-extreme full-K vectors (all −128, all +127, mixed extremes), alternating signs, offset-correction extremes, and every tail length — with expected i64-verified results.
- Bit-exact floor: tier S results are the DEFINITION of correct for integer paths; SIMD tiers must equal them exactly (integer SIMD ≡ scalar/i64 is a release invariant).

## Constraints
- Integer stages are exact — no tolerance anywhere in this bead (G1 > G2). Overflow is proven, not assumed (doctrine #10: integer bounds cover every intermediate).
- Safe Rust only (scalar code needs no SIMD island); checked/widening arithmetic in the oracle; release-path scalar kernels use the canonical narrowing rules, with debug assertions against the i64 shadow in test builds.
- Allowlist deps; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; deterministic (accumulation order fixed and documented — the canonical scalar order).
- No production dependency on test-side oracle code.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) tier-S GEMM/GEMV green vs the in-repo readable reference (spec-engine-adjacent logical math) on all fixed shapes; (b) the i64 oracle proving the bound set above for every model K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752} and every generated input class with ZERO i32-range violations; (c) the differential fixture generator adopted by at least one consumer test (the harness self-test) with seeds logged. Recorded in the conformance harness; this bead is the floor cited by every subsequent tier bead's L1-integer row.

## Tests
- Unit: tiny hand-computed GEMM/GEMV goldens; tail lengths 0/1/W−1/W/W+1 at various W; int4 unpack pairs (both nibbles, sign handling) feeding MAC equality.
- Property: for random shapes within the fixed-K/N family and random i8 inputs over the FULL domain, scalar i32 result == i64 shadow result after canonical narrowing, and max |intermediate| stays within the proven bound; seed-reproducible.
- Exhaustive: all-extreme full K=10752 vectors (documented worst cases) checked against closed-form expected values (e.g. 10752 × (−128 × −128) = 176,160,768 exactly).
- E2E: fixture-generator determinism (same seed → same fixture digests). DETAILED LOGGING: any violation logs shape, seed, element index, i32 value, i64 value, running-intermediate max, and the bound it approached/violated. No model weights involved; nothing SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_SPEC — the P1 scalar spec engine is the readable logical-math reference these kernels are first checked against (independent implementation, shared-nothing).
- [P0] crate scaffold (franken_nlp-uxw, direct): tier-S kernels land in `src/native_engine/` inside the scaffolded crate and the i64 harness rides its test tree; wired directly so this cluster's readiness never depends on the spec-engine bead's own dependency wiring.

title: [P3] Plumb canonical quant algebra with XOR-0x80 offset correction
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, SwiGLU 10752, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). Cross-ISA bit identity for int8 is a THEOREM first, then a test: **one canonical quantization algebra** that SDOT/SMMLA consume directly and that x86 U8×S8 instructions reach through an exact offset identity. This bead builds that shared plumbing so every tier implements the same math and AVX2 is never allowed a different answer.

## Contract
- **Canonical algebra**, implemented once in `src/native_engine/` and consumed by all tiers:
  - Weights and logical activations are **s8 with zero-point 0**. Signed tiers (SDOT/SMMLA, scalar) accumulate `Σ qx·w` directly.
  - **x86 offset identity**: U8×S8 instructions (VPDPBUSD, vpmaddubsw-based paths) reinterpret each activation byte as `u = qx XOR 0x80` (= qx + 128 in u8), accumulate `Σ u·w`, then subtract the correction `128·Σw` per output row — algebraically EXACTLY `Σ qx·w`. The identity, its i32 bounds (at K=10752: raw ≤ 350,945,280; correction ≤ 176,160,768; conservative sum 527,106,048 < 2^31−1 with >4× headroom), and its proof obligations are documented at the definition site.
  - **Offline row sums `Σw`**: canonical row sums are derived from the SEMANTIC LOGICAL weights at convert/pack time, stored per output row. Every native packed copy's row sums are protected by that copy's physical section/file digest and CHECKED against freshly recomputed sums from the packed bytes before dispatch (a corrupt or stale correction table must fail closed, not corrupt results silently). Digest coverage is integrity evidence for the physical copy — it is NOT mislabeled as independent semantic identity.
  - **Integer identity ends before dequantization**: the exact-integer contract covers everything up to the i32 (i64-shadowed) accumulator including offset correction; from there a SEPARATELY FIXED scale-application order governs float work (which scale multiplies when, in what order across row/column/group scales), and int4 group summation order is likewise fixed. These orders are named constants of the algebra, not per-kernel choices.
- Plumbing deliverables: the activation offset transform (s8→u8 XOR 0x80) as a shared utility; row-sum table format + digest binding + pre-dispatch verification; the scale-order specification as code (one function applied by every tier's epilogue); int4 group-sum order specification.
- Full-domain guarantee: all stored i8 bit patterns (−128..=127) are covered; converter's current [−127,127] target is a convention, not a correctness dependency.

## Constraints
- One algebra, no per-tier variants (G1 > G2): a tier that cannot implement this algebra exactly does not ship.
- Fixed scale-application order — changing it is a numerics change requiring DISCREPANCIES.md + rollback, never a silent edit.
- Fail closed on row-sum/digest mismatch before dispatch (typed error naming the section and digests).
- Safe Rust here (no SIMD island needed for plumbing); allowlist deps (sha2 for digests); no Rayon; deterministic.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) the offset-identity property proven exhaustively on small K and by i64-shadowed property tests on full K=10752 (raw − 128·Σw == signed dot, for full-domain inputs including −128 weights and both correction extremes); (b) row-sum verification wired: a mutated packed section or mutated row-sum table each produce the typed pre-dispatch failure; (c) scale-order and int4-group-order spec functions adopted by the tier-S epilogue with fixture-locked outputs; (d) bound checks green (no i32 intermediate exceeds range across the generated worst cases). Recorded in the conformance harness; cited by every U8×S8 tier bead.

## Tests
- Unit: XOR 0x80 ↔ +128 equivalence over all 256 byte values; correction arithmetic at extremes (Σw = ±10752·127 and ±10752·128); row-sum recompute vs stored table on synthetic packs; digest-binding round trip.
- Property: random full-domain vectors at K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752} and tails — signed dot == offset dot − 128·Σw, i64-shadow verified, seed-reproducible; scale-order function is deterministic and order-sensitive tests prove reorderings change results (i.e. the order genuinely binds).
- Fuzz: corrupt row-sum tables / truncated sections → typed rejection, never wrong math.
- DETAILED LOGGING: identity violations log K, row, seed, signed dot, raw dot, correction, difference; digest failures log section id + both digests. No model weights; nothing SKIPPED_NO_MODEL (synthetic packs), though an artifact-backed check joins later int8 epics.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: the identity is proven against the scalar/i64 authority and the fixture generator; plumbing without that floor would be unverifiable.

title: [P3] Implement NEON SDOT (A2) + SMMLA (A1) tiled int8 tiers
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, fixed GEMM shapes K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752} / N ∈ {6144, 1024, 3072, 10752, 166,144}, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). Apple Silicon / ARM64 (M4/M5) is a first-class target. This bead builds the two explicit-SIMD aarch64 tiers: **A2 (SDOT)** and **A1 (SMMLA)** — with the mandatory register/cache blocking and packed K-panels (the un-blocked-SMMLA trap from prior art: matrix-engine instructions without blocking/packing lose to autovec).

## Contract
- **A2 — NEON dotprod tier**: int8 GEMM/GEMV using SDOT (`vdotq_s32`), gated on runtime detection of aarch64 `dotprod`. Register-blocked and cache-blocked; consumes offline-packed K-panels (packing layout defined with the prepacked-GEMM bead's converter contract; this bead may start on test-side packers producing the same layout).
- **A1 — SMMLA tier**: int8 GEMM using SMMLA (`vmmlaq_s32`), gated on the OS ACTUALLY ADVERTISING FEAT_I8MM (runtime detection surface; NEVER inferred from a chip's marketing name — at the audited frankentorch pin there is no SMMLA path, so this is new code). GEMV may use SMMLA or SDOT, whichever the measured table selects per shape. Register/cache blocking + packed K-panels mandatory, as for A2.
- Both tiers implement the CANONICAL algebra (s8×s8, zero-point 0 — SDOT/SMMLA consume it directly, no offset correction needed) and must be BIT-EXACT equal to tier S scalar / i64 oracle over the full i8 domain, every fixed shape, and every tail.
- Tail handling: dynamic M/T/N-remainder tails via proved masked/cleanup paths, tested at 0, 1, W−1, W, W+1 lanes and at buffer boundaries.
- Both register as dispatch-table candidates keyed (ISA, shape, regime) with measured-entry provenance; NEITHER is assumed faster than A3 autovec — franken_ocr shipped autovec over SDOT/SMMLA for some shapes, and selection is the benchmark's job, not this bead's.
- Unsafe policy: intrinsics live in an enumerated SIMD module island with scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` still denied, every unsafe block carrying a local `// SAFETY:` proof (detection-gated execution, in-bounds panels).

## Constraints
- Parity first: no tier lands without its bit-exact gate vs scalar/i64 (doctrine: integer SIMD ≡ scalar/i64 is a release invariant).
- Capability never routes: detection defines candidacy; the measured table selects. Forced-tier proof runs supported; forced-unsupported fails before dispatch.
- Register/cache blocking + offline pre-packing are MANDATORY for the matrix-engine path (the un-blocked-SMMLA trap); no unpacked "temporary" variant may ship.
- Nightly toolchain stdarch intrinsics; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; allowlist deps only.
- Measured-faster wins; losers go to docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md / docs/PERF_LEDGER.md rather than being deleted-and-forgotten.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) L1-integer EXACT differential green for A2 and A1 vs tier S / i64 oracle across: exhaustive small vectors, randomized full-domain property vectors, all-extreme full K=10752 vectors, alternating signs, and every tail length (the shared fixture generator from the scalar/i64 bead); (b) detection-gating tests green (A1 absent from candidates when FEAT_I8MM is not OS-advertised — asserted via injected detection); (c) dispatch registration green with provenance rows; (d) initial sustained benchmark rows recorded per (shape, regime) on an accessible Apple host into the PERF_LEDGER (numbers may lose to A3 — that outcome is valid evidence, not failure). No hardware access → the bench rows are explicitly marked blocked, and no performance claim is made.

## Tests
- Unit: microkernel tile correctness on hand-checked tiny tiles; panel-packing layout round-trip (pack → unpack == original logical weights); tail masks at 0/1/W−1/W/W+1.
- Property: random (M, K, N) within the fixed family × full-domain i8 → tier result == scalar == i64 shadow, seed-reproducible; page-boundary-adjacent buffers (allocation placed so panels end at page edges) never over-read (asserted via bounds-checked test allocator).
- E2E: dispatcher-driven smoke matmul on detected hardware; SKIP with explicit `SKIPPED_UNSUPPORTED_ISA` (not silent pass) on hosts without dotprod/i8mm. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log tier, shape, tile coords, lane index, expected/got, panel digest, and the detection vector. Model weights not required (synthetic + packed fixtures); artifact-backed runs come with the int8 epic.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] dispatch-table framework (A_DISPATCH): tiers register as candidates and are reachable only through detection-gated dispatch.
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: the bit-exact floor and fixture generator these tiers are proven against.
- Depends on [P3] canonical quant algebra plumbing: the s8 algebra, scale-order epilogue, and (for mixed paths) row-sum machinery are shared, not re-implemented.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — real packed int8 weights/panels come from the int8 artifact epic; until then synthetic packs stand in.

title: [P3] Implement autovec tier A3 as first-class Apple candidate
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, fixed GEMM shapes K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). Hard-won prior art: **franken_ocr SHIPPED Apple Silicon defaulting to LLVM autovectorization over hand-written SDOT/SMMLA for some dense int8 shapes because that is what measurement said.** Tier A3 — carefully shaped safe Rust that LLVM vectorizes — is therefore a FIRST-CLASS Apple candidate in this project, not a fallback, and it competes in the dispatch table on equal terms.

## Contract
- **A3 — autovec tier**: int8 GEMM/GEMV kernels written in SAFE Rust (no intrinsics, no unsafe island) structured for LLVM auto-vectorization: fixed inner-K loops over the model's compile-time-known shapes (K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}), i32 accumulators, iterator/chunk patterns known to vectorize, no aliasing obstacles, 64-byte-aligned packed inputs shared with the other tiers' panel format where that helps codegen.
- Implements the canonical s8 algebra (zero-point 0, direct signed accumulation); BIT-EXACT equal to tier S scalar / i64 oracle over the full i8 domain, all fixed shapes, all tails (integer math — vectorization order cannot change exact integer sums; the gate proves it).
- Registered as a dispatch candidate on aarch64 (and available generally — autovec is portable); candidacy everywhere, selection only by measurement.
- Codegen guardrails: benchmarks + (dev-side) assembly inspection notes record whether the hot loops actually vectorized on the pinned nightly; a toolchain bump that de-vectorizes shows up as a benchmark regression in the ledger, not a silent slowdown.
- Portable target-feature baseline: built with the portable baseline + runtime dispatch; NEVER `target-cpu=native`.

## Constraints
- Measured-faster wins (doctrine #6): A3 may beat A1/A2 per shape and, when it does, the table records A3 with the reason; when it loses, the row goes to the ledger. No pride-of-authorship routing in either direction.
- Integer SIMD ≡ scalar/i64 release invariant applies to autovec output exactly as to intrinsics.
- Safe Rust ONLY — this tier must not grow an unsafe island (its whole point is the safe portable candidate); allowlist deps; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn.
- The 5×-slower hand-SIMD lesson (doctrine #5): glue stays autovectorized; this bead does NOT hand-vectorize non-MAC glue.

## Evidence / gates

- The franken_ocr precedent is cited in the ledger row rationale as PRIOR expectation, never as this project's measurement.

## Tests
- Unit: tiny hand-checked tiles; tail lengths 0/1/W−1/W/W+1; alignment-variant inputs (aligned and deliberately misaligned logical views) all exact.
- Property: random full-domain i8 inputs across the fixed shape family → A3 == scalar == i64 shadow, seed-reproducible.
- E2E: dispatcher-driven smoke on any host (A3 is portable, so this runs in ordinary CI on both arches); benchmark harness smoke (short run) proving the bench plumbing works without claiming numbers. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log shape, seed, element coords, expected/got, and the compiler version/flags (codegen identity matters for this tier). No model weights; nothing SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] dispatch-table framework (A_DISPATCH): candidacy/selection and `robot backends` reporting.
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: the exactness floor and fixture generator.

- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — real packed weights arrive from the int8 artifact epic for artifact-backed differentials/benchmarks.

title: [P3] Implement AVX2 X3a exact low-7/high-bit vpmaddubsw decomposition
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, fixed shapes K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}, vocab 166,144). The reference AMD dev box is **Zen 3 (AVX2, no VNNI)**, so AVX2 must be FIRST-CLASS AND EXACT. The `vpmaddubsw` hazard is INTRA-INSTRUCTION: it multiplies unsigned×signed bytes and saturates the ADJACENT-PAIR i16 sum inside the instruction — under the converter's [−127,127] weight convention a raw pair reaches 2·255·127 = 64,770, and over the full i8 domain (w = −128) 2·255·128 = 65,280; both blow past i16::MAX = 32,767, and NO downstream accumulation cadence can restore bits lost inside the instruction. The failure is data-dependent and silent. Raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` is therefore BANNED — not an approximate mode, not a fast path, banned. This bead builds **X3a**, the exact low-7/high-bit decomposition that keeps byte-dot throughput anyway.

## Contract
- **X3a kernel** (int8 GEMM/GEMV, `avx2`-gated) implementing the exact decomposition over the canonical algebra's offset domain (`u = qx XOR 0x80`, u ∈ [0,255]):
  1. Split each offset activation byte: `lo = u & 0x7f` (∈ [0,127]) and `hi = u >> 7` (∈ {0,1}).
  2. `dot(lo, w)` via `vpmaddubsw`: each adjacent pair is bounded by 2·127·128 = **32,512** ≤ i16::MAX = 32,767 → CANNOT saturate. Accumulate pairs into i32 (`vpmaddwd` with ones / widening adds).
  3. `dot(hi, w)` via `vpmaddubsw`: pair bound 2·1·128 = **256** → cannot saturate. Widen to i32, SHIFT LEFT 7 (hi contributes u's bit-7 weight, 128·hi·w = (hi·w)<<7), and add to the lo accumulation.
  4. Subtract the offline row-sum correction **128·Σw** (canonical-algebra plumbing) to land exactly on `Σ qx·w`.
  - i32 safety: raw offset dot ≤ 350,945,280 and correction ≤ 176,160,768 at K=10752 (conservative sum 527,106,048 < 2^31−1, >4× headroom); the accumulation cadence (how many pair-sums before i32 widen) is chosen so no i16→i32 stage can overflow, proven by the i64 shadow.
- Register/cache-blocked, consuming the packed K-panel layout; tails at every length via proved cleanup.
- BIT-EXACT equal to tier S scalar / i64 oracle over the FULL i8 domain (including w = −128), all fixed shapes, all tails.
- Registered as dispatch candidate X3a; the primary Zen 3 candidate, with X3b the independent exact alternative — MEASUREMENT chooses per shape.
- Unsafe policy: enumerated SIMD island, scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` denied, per-block `// SAFETY:` proofs.

## Constraints
- **Raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` is BANNED** as any shippable mode; the decomposition or an equally exact route is the only way this instruction may appear (doctrine #7). A test corpus containing saturation-triggering data (pairs > 32,767 raw) must exist and pass ONLY through the exact route.
- Parity first: no landing without the exact gate. Integer SIMD ≡ scalar/i64 is a release invariant.
- Capability never routes; measured-faster wins; Zen 3's real wins are many-core batch GEMM + cache/NUMA + prepacking, not pretend-VNNI.
- Nightly stdarch; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; allowlist deps.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) L1-integer EXACT differential green vs scalar/i64 across exhaustive small vectors, randomized full-domain property vectors, ALL-EXTREME full K=10752 vectors, alternating signs, OFFSET-CORRECTION EXTREMES, and every tail length — including a dedicated saturation-adversarial class (activation bytes 0xFF against weight ±127/−128 patterns) that would corrupt a raw-vpmaddubsw implementation; (b) a negative control: the test harness demonstrates the adversarial class DOES diverge under a quarantined raw-vpmaddubsw test double (proving the corpus has teeth), while X3a stays exact; (c) dispatch registration + provenance rows; (d) sustained bench rows vs X3b on the Zen 3 box recorded in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md (either winner is fine; the loser is ledgered).
- G0 heritage: the Zen-3 AVX2 exact-construction spike (both candidates on the actual Threadripper) is the architectural precedent this bead productionizes.

## Tests
- Unit: pair-bound arithmetic goldens (32,512 and 256 bounds hit exactly by constructed inputs, no saturation); shift-7 recombination on hand values; correction application; tiny tiles hand-checked.
- Property: random full-domain inputs, all fixed K/N, every tail → X3a == scalar == i64 shadow; seed-reproducible; page-boundary buffers never over-read.
- E2E: dispatcher-driven smoke on AVX2 hosts; `SKIPPED_UNSUPPORTED_ISA` (explicit, not silent) elsewhere. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log shape, tile/lane coords, u/lo/hi values, raw pair sums, correction term, expected/got, and CPU feature string. Synthetic packs; artifact-backed runs join the int8 epic.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] dispatch-table framework (A_DISPATCH): candidacy, forced-tier proof runs, backends reporting.
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: exactness floor + adversarial fixture generator.
- Depends on [P3] canonical quant algebra plumbing: the XOR-0x80 offset domain and the digest-protected 128·Σw row sums ARE that bead's machinery.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — real packed weights for artifact-backed proof/bench.

title: [P3] Implement AVX2 X3b sign-extend vpmaddwd exact route
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, fixed shapes K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}, vocab 166,144). The reference AMD box is Zen 3 (AVX2, no VNNI), and the plan requires TWO independent exact AVX2 constructions: X3a (low-7/high-bit vpmaddubsw decomposition) and **X3b — this bead**: sign-extend both operands to i16 and use `vpmaddwd`, whose i16×i16 adjacent-pair products sum into i32 WITHOUT any saturation hazard (max pair 2·128·128 = 32,768 fits i32 trivially; `vpmaddwd` accumulates into i32 natively). X3b costs more unpack/half-lane work but has a SHORT proof and serves as an independent oracle-quality SIMD path — two exact routes that agree with scalar/i64 and with each other make a silent encoding bug in either construction nearly impossible to miss.

## Contract
- **X3b kernel** (int8 GEMM/GEMV, `avx2`-gated):
  - Sign-extend activation bytes (s8, zero-point 0 — the canonical algebra directly, NO offset domain and NO 128·Σw correction needed on this route) and weight bytes to i16 lanes (`_mm256_cvtepi8_epi16`-class ops).
  - `vpmaddwd` multiplies i16 pairs and adds adjacent products into i32 lanes; accumulate i32 vectors across K; horizontal-reduce per output element in a fixed documented order.
  - i32 safety: per-pair ≤ 2·128·128 = 32,768; K=10752 worst-case accumulation ≤ 176,160,768 (S8×S8 full-domain bound) — well under 2^31−1; proven by the i64 shadow, not assumed.
  - Register/cache-blocked over the shared packed K-panel layout; every tail length via proved cleanup paths.
- BIT-EXACT equal to tier S scalar / i64 oracle over the FULL i8 domain (including −128 on both operands), all fixed shapes, all tails; ALSO differentially tested against X3a (exact == exact, a free cross-check).
- Registered as dispatch candidate X3b; MEASUREMENT chooses X3a vs X3b per shape/regime — X3b is not "the slow safe one" by fiat; if it wins a shape, it ships for that shape.
- Unsafe policy: enumerated SIMD island, scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`, `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` denied, per-block `// SAFETY:` proofs.

## Constraints
- Independent construction discipline: X3b shares panel formats and the algebra's epilogue with X3a but NOT its lane-math helpers — the value of two candidates is independence; a shared decomposition helper would collapse them into one proof.
- Raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` remains BANNED everywhere; X3b must not quietly route through it for "fast segments".
- Parity first; integer SIMD ≡ scalar/i64 release invariant; capability never routes; measured-faster wins with losers ledgered.
- Nightly stdarch; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; allowlist deps.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) L1-integer EXACT differential green vs scalar/i64 across exhaustive small vectors, randomized full-domain vectors, all-extreme full K=10752 vectors, alternating signs, and every tail length; (b) X3a↔X3b cross-differential green on the same corpus; (c) dispatch registration + provenance; (d) sustained per-shape bench rows vs X3a on the Zen 3 box recorded in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md (the per-shape winner enters the dispatch table; the loser's row is retained as evidence).
- G0 heritage: the Zen-3 both-constructions spike is the precedent; this bead productionizes the second construction.

## Tests
- Unit: sign-extension lane goldens (including −128); vpmaddwd pair arithmetic on hand values; horizontal-reduction order fixture (documented fixed order, digest-locked); tiny tiles hand-checked.
- Property: random full-domain inputs across fixed K/N and tails → X3b == scalar == i64 shadow == X3a; seed-reproducible; bounds-checked test allocator proves no over-read at page-boundary panels.
- E2E: dispatcher-driven smoke on AVX2 hosts; explicit `SKIPPED_UNSUPPORTED_ISA` elsewhere. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log shape, tile/lane coords, i16 lane values, accumulator state, expected/got, CPU feature string, and whether X3a agreed (to localize which construction broke). Synthetic packs; artifact-backed runs join the int8 epic.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] dispatch-table framework (A_DISPATCH): candidacy/selection/reporting.
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: exactness floor + fixture classes.
- Depends on [P3] canonical quant algebra plumbing: s8 semantics and the fixed scale-application epilogue (X3b needs no offset correction, which the algebra's documentation makes explicit per route).
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — real packed weights for artifact-backed proof/bench.

title: [P3] Implement VNNI tiers X1a zmm / X1b ymm / X2 with masked tails
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, fixed shapes K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}, vocab 166,144). AVX-512 WIDTH IS NOT DESTINY: Zen 4 commonly executes 512-bit work through double-pumped 256-bit datapaths; Zen 5 (Threadripper 9000) advertises a native full 512-bit datapath; Intel frequency/power behavior varies by generation. VNNI supplies the exact U8×S8→i32 primitive (`VPDPBUSD`) plus 32 registers and masks — width and semantics are orthogonal. This bead builds all three VNNI tiers and the benchmark discipline that keeps them honest.

## Contract
- **X1a — zmm VNNI**: `VPDPBUSD` 512-bit tiles, gated on OS-exposed `avx512f` + `avx512vnni`; selected only where the 512-bit path wins the SUSTAINED bench for that (shape, regime, host family).
- **X1b — ymm EVEX-VNNI**: same VNNI semantics at 256-bit EVEX (requires X1a features + `avx512vl`); keeps the VNNI instruction/register file while avoiding a losing 512-bit width on a given shape/host.
- **X2 — AVX-VNNI**: `_mm256_dpbusd_epi32` under `avxvnni` (client Intel/AMD without full AVX-512); feature-detected, never vendor-name routed.
- All three consume the canonical algebra's offset domain: `u = qx XOR 0x80`, accumulate `Σ u·w` via VPDPBUSD, subtract the digest-protected offline correction `128·Σw` → exactly `Σ qx·w`. i32 bounds at K=10752: raw ≤ 350,945,280, correction ≤ 176,160,768, conservative sum 527,106,048 < 2^31−1 (>4× headroom).
- **Masked tails**: AVX-512 masked loads/stores (and X2's cleanup) handle M/N tails; EVERY masked case is tested at 0, 1, W−1, W, W+1 lanes AND at page boundaries (buffers placed flush against protected pages to catch over-reads). K padding, where a tile wants it, is CONVERTER-DEFINED zero padding recorded in the tile contract with digest coverage — kernels never invent padding.
- **Benchmark keys are separate per microarchitecture**: Zen 4 (double-pumped) vs Zen 5 (native 512) vs Intel generations are distinct dispatch/bench keys; for every hot shape compare zmm-VNNI vs ymm-VNNI (where available) vs AVX2 vs scalar over a SUSTAINED forward — never a 5 µs microbench — after warmup, recording clocks where observable, joules/doc where available, p50/p95/p99, and thermal steady state. A narrower tier may be the shipped default on a wider-capable CPU.
- OS/firmware exposure is authoritative (AVX-512 can be fused off / VM-masked); detection-gated candidacy; forced-unsupported fails before dispatch.
- BIT-EXACT vs tier S scalar / i64 oracle over the full i8 domain, all fixed shapes, all tails; unsafe intrinsics confined to the enumerated SIMD island with per-block SAFETY proofs.

## Constraints
- Doctrine #14 verbatim: benchmark sustained zmm/ymm/AVX2/scalar per host/shape; firmware/VM exposure authoritative; no model-name tables.
- Parity first; integer SIMD ≡ scalar/i64; capability never routes; measured-faster wins; losers ledgered in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md / docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.
- AMX is OUT of v1; AVX512-BF16 is not part of the int8 correctness story; do not scope-creep either into this bead.
- Nightly stdarch; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; allowlist deps.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) L1-integer EXACT differential green for X1a, X1b, X2 vs scalar/i64 across exhaustive small, randomized full-domain, all-extreme full K=10752, alternating-signs, offset-correction-extreme, and every-tail-length classes; (b) the masked-tail matrix green at 0/1/W−1/W/W+1 and page boundaries for every masked path; (c) detection/candidacy tests green (each tier absent without its exact feature set — injected-detection tests); (d) sustained per-(shape, regime, host-family) bench rows recorded on accessible Zen 4/Zen 5/Intel hosts with p50/p95/p99 + thermal-steady-state notes; hosts we lack are marked blocked with NO performance claim (no hardware, no claim).

## Tests
- Unit: VPDPBUSD lane arithmetic goldens; offset+correction epilogue; mask-register construction per tail; tiny tiles hand-checked per tier.
- Property: random full-domain inputs × all fixed shapes × all tails → each tier == scalar == i64 shadow, seed-reproducible; cross-tier agreement (X1a == X1b == X2 where all detected).
- E2E: dispatcher-driven smoke per detected tier; explicit `SKIPPED_UNSUPPORTED_ISA` elsewhere; bench-harness smoke proving sustained-run plumbing (duration, warmup, steady-state detection) without claiming numbers. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log tier, shape, mask pattern, lane coords, raw/correction/final values, expected/got, and the full detection vector; bench rows log exact command, env, thread count, and CPU feature string. Synthetic packs; artifact-backed runs join the int8 epic.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] dispatch-table framework (A_DISPATCH): per-family keys, candidacy, forced-tier handling, backends reporting.
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: exactness floor + fixture generator.
- Depends on [P3] canonical quant algebra plumbing: the offset identity and digest-protected row-sum corrections are that bead's machinery.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — real packed int8 panels for artifact-backed proof and the sustained benches.

title: [P3] Build prepacked fixed-shape tiled GEMM + batched skinny-M decode GEMM
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions/token — prefill compute is ×2, ≈12.6 GFLOP/token; KV slot = layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752). Prefill is compute-bound and dominates scoring/classification throughput; decode at batch M is a SKINNY GEMM (M×K · K×N), which is exactly where a tiled kernel beats M independent GEMVs. The generality-tax wedge: weight-side shapes are compile-time-fixed, so the converter pre-packs arch-specific interleaved tiles OFFLINE (the llama.cpp "aarch64 repack" lesson done at convert time, not load time) and the runtime never reshuffles.

## Contract
- **Prepacked fixed-shape tiled int8 GEMM** (prefill/batch) + **batched skinny-M decode GEMM**, built over the SIMD tiers:
  - **Offline per-arch interleave**: packing happens in the converter's native-pack stage (artifact pipeline stage 4); this bead defines/consumes the pack contract — tile layout id, interleave order, alignment (64-byte), and any padding — and provides the test-side packer producing byte-identical layouts for synthetic weights.
  - **Per-layer contiguity**: layer[i]'s full weight set (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072, gate/up 3072→10752, down 10752→3072) laid out as ONE sequential range per loop pass (prefetch-friendly, NUMA-placeable), without claiming how many cache-line reads the microkernel performs — logical layout, measured traffic.
  - **Tile geometry specialized to K ∈ {3072, 6144, 10752}** and the fixed N set; register/cache blocking chosen from a BOUNDED OFFLINE CANDIDATE SET per (ISA, shape, regime) — initial panel sizes from L1/L2 capacity arithmetic, but ONLY measured winners enter the dispatch table (no inherited "256 KiB is right everywhere" constant).
  - **Converter-defined zero padding ONLY where the selected tile contract records it**; dynamic M/T/candidate tails remain real and are handled by proved masks or cleanup kernels — padding is never invented at runtime.
  - **One microkernel family serves both regimes**: the same packed panels feed prefill GEMM and batched skinny-M decode GEMM (M small, e.g. compatible decode rows batched layer-major); per-regime dispatch rows may still differ.
- Exactness: tiled results BIT-EXACT equal tier S scalar / i64 oracle for every (tile geometry × shape × tail) — blocking must not change integer sums; every packed layout is differentially tested against the LOGICAL weights (packing preserves logical tensors, a metamorphic invariant).
- Registered in the dispatch table per (ISA, shape, regime) with measured provenance.

## Constraints
- Register/cache blocking + offline pre-packing are MANDATORY (the un-blocked-SMMLA trap); no load-time repack in the release path.
- G1 > G2: parity before perf rows; measured-faster wins; losers ledgered.
- 64-byte alignment for all packed weights/activations; scales SoA; system allocator; inner loops make no general allocator calls.
- Leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon in the release graph (batch-team parallelism is a LATER epic's asupersync-owned surface; this bead's kernels are single-team leaves).
- Allowlist deps; unsafe only inside the already-enumerated SIMD islands of the tier beads — the tiling/packing logic itself is safe code.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) pack↔logical differential green (pack(synthetic W) unpacks/reads back to exactly W; a corrupted pack fails its digest check); (b) L1-integer EXACT green for every candidate tile geometry vs scalar/i64 on all fixed shapes and adversarial tails (0/1/W−1/W/W+1 rows/cols, page-boundary panels); (c) skinny-M decode GEMM exactness for M ∈ {1..smallset} incl. M=1 ≡ GEMV-path results bit-for-bit; (d) sustained per-(ISA, shape, regime) bench rows for the bounded tile-candidate set recorded in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md with winners entering the dispatch table and losers retained.
- The tile contract (layout id, interleave, padding, digests) is written into the pack-format docs consumed by the converter epic — contract drift fails the differential.

## Tests
- Unit: packer layout goldens (tiny matrices → exact expected byte order per layout id); padding-contract cases (padded K tiles verify zeros and digest coverage); per-layer contiguity assertion (offsets of all 7 layer matrices form one sequential range per loop pass).
- Property: random synthetic weights × every tile geometry → tiled == scalar == i64 shadow, seed-reproducible; M-sweep property (result independent of M-blocking for fixed rows).
- E2E: dispatcher-driven prefill-shaped GEMM and skinny-M decode GEMM smoke per detected tier; bench-harness sustained-run smoke. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log layout id, tile coords, panel digest, row/col/lane, expected/got; bench rows log exact command/env/threads/CPU features. Synthetic packs suffice here; artifact-backed packed weights come from the int8 artifact epic — those runs report **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] canonical quant algebra plumbing: pack format carries row-sums/scale-order metadata defined there.
- Depends on [P3] NEON SDOT/SMMLA tiers (A1/A2): the aarch64 microkernels the tiling drives on Apple hosts.
- Depends on [P3] AVX2 X3a: the primary Zen 3 microkernel the tiling drives on the reference AMD box.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — production packed weights are converter artifacts; the offline interleave ships there, against this bead's contract.

title: [P3] Build native 48:8 GQA prefill + 44-deep decode GEMV attention
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions; KV slot = layer + loop×22 → the KV cache is 44-DEEP (176 KiB/token bf16 = 180,224 B across 44 slots); final RMSNorm after EACH pass; attention is GQA **48 query : 8 KV heads at head_dim 128 EXPLICIT** (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024, o 6144→3072 — SIX query heads per KV head), scale 1/√128, additive causal mask, f32 softmax; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half; vocab 166,144. At the audited frankentorch pin, `sdpa_forward_f32` is DENSE PER-HEAD — usable ONLY as an L1/reference adapter with an explicit KV-repeat; materializing 6× KV in the production path is forbidden. This bead (anchor A_GQA) builds the native attention kernels.

## Contract
- **Prefill: native 48:8 GQA attention kernel.** Computes causal attention for 48 query heads over 8 KV heads (grouping 6 query heads per KV head) WITHOUT materializing repeated KV (no 6× copies): iterate KV-head-major, apply each KV head's K/V panels to its 6 query heads. Scale 1/√128; additive causal mask; softmax in f32 per the profile's cast contract. The dense frankentorch SDPA + explicit KV-repeat adapter remains available strictly as the L1 REFERENCE comparator — it is never the production claim path and never ships as the default.
- **Decode: GEMV attention over the 44-deep KV.** Per step, per (loop, layer): q GEMV → RoPE → scores against that slot's K (8 KV heads × 128; six query heads blocked per KV head) → ONLINE SOFTMAX (streaming max/sum renormalization over the position scan) → weighted V accumulation → o GEMV. Logical addressing is `[loop-layer][head][position][128]`; the physical paged order is selected by benchmark while preserving sequential position scans and 64-byte alignment (the KV-page/slab design is a later epic's surface; this kernel consumes the logical addressing contract).
- Numerics: floating path with a NAMED metric/tolerance contract per profile (attention is float work — L1 thresholds from the measured oracle floor; max-abs/max-rel/ULP/cosine + NaN/Inf/signed-zero vectors, never cosine alone). Reduction order per row is FIXED and documented (required later for batch-invariance).
- Both kernels handle ragged/growing context lengths, position offsets for decode append, and the same-positions-both-loops rule (loop passes reuse identical logical positions).
- Registered in the dispatch framework per regime (prefill-attention, decode-attention).

## Constraints
- NEVER materialize 6× KV in production (memory and bandwidth fraud on a 44-deep cache); the repeat adapter is L1-only.
- head_dim 128 everywhere (q rows are 6144 = 48×128; KV rows 1024 = 8×128); any 64-derived stride is catastrophically wrong.
- The loop is the architecture: decode touches slot layer+loop×22, never a 22-deep view.
- Online softmax is the decode contract (bounded state over long scans); post-parity candidates (tiling crossover, int8 QKᵀ) are LATER, behind explicit selectors — out of scope here.
- Leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon; allowlist deps; unsafe only in enumerated SIMD islands if/where used; G1 > G2 with profile-scoped claims.

## Evidence / gates
- Anchor **A_GQA**. Closes on: (a) L1 green vs the dense-SDPA+KV-repeat reference adapter AND the scalar spec engine's dense GQA expansion, under per-profile tolerance vectors, across context lengths {1, 2, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65, long}, all 44 slots exercised; (b) decode-vs-prefill consistency: decoding token T+1 after a T-token prefill produces attention outputs equal (within the profile contract) to a T+1 prefill's last position — per (loop, layer); (c) online-softmax equivalence: streaming result matches two-pass softmax bit-for-bit under the fixed reduction order on the same inputs; (d) a memory assertion that the production prefill path allocates NO repeated-KV buffer (allocation-count/high-water test); (e) bench rows (prefill attention throughput, decode attention per-token cost vs context) recorded per host in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.

## Tests
- Unit: tiny GQA cases hand-checked (2 KV heads × small dims scaled analogues plus real-shape smoke at 48:8@128); causal-mask edges (position 0, single token, full context); grouping map (query head h → KV head h/6) exhaustive over all 48.
- Property: KV-head-major iteration == dense-repeat reference within tolerance for random inputs; online softmax invariant to score-block partitioning; NaN/Inf propagation matches reference behavior; seed-reproducible.
- E2E (model-gated): attention taps inside the L2 44-execution sweep on real fixtures — reports **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact; synthetic runs always on. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log (loop, layer, kv head, query head, position), metric vector vs threshold, softmax max/sum state, and whether the dense adapter agreed (localizing kernel vs harness).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle: harness/fixture machinery and the integer floor for any quantized sub-paths later; the scalar attention comparator discipline rides the same differential harness.
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_FWD — the hf-bf16-eager reference forward (P1) defines the semantic attention behavior and cast points this kernel must reproduce; its taps are the comparison surface.

title: [P3] Build RoPE θ=7e7 split-half tables + q/k projection-epilogue fusion variant
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, hidden 3072, 48:8 heads @ head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024), vocab 166,144, max positions 262,144). RoPE here is **θ = 7e7 (70,000,000), head_dim 128, SPLIT-HALF rotation** (rotate_half convention: the head vector's first 64 and last 64 lanes pair as (x_i, x_{i+64}) — NOT adjacent-pair interleaving), and the reference constructs frequency/cos/sin tables in f32 then casts to the q/k dtype at application [OBSERVED@pin]. Positions are the SAME logical positions in both loop passes. The advertised 262,144-position limit is an observed model limit, not a promise — tables are built only to the ADMITTED runtime context cap (default per-sequence cap 8192; admission-certificate governed).

## Contract
- **RoPE table builder** in `src/native_engine/`: precompute inv_freq (θ = 7e7; inv_freq[j] = θ^(−2j/128) for j ∈ 0..64), then cos/sin tables in f32, sized EXACTLY to the admitted context cap (never 262,144 up front); table growth on re-admission is an explicit rebuild, not a hot-path reallocation.
- **Application kernel**: split-half rotation applied to PROJECTED q and k (after q/k GEMV, before KV write / score use), per head (48 q heads, 8 kv heads @ 128), f32 tables cast to the working dtype at application per the active numerics profile's cast contract. Decode applies position P's row; prefill applies rows 0..T; both loop passes reuse identical positions.
- **Projection-epilogue fusion VARIANT**: a second implementation fusing RoPE into the q/k GEMV epilogue — rotate in-register before the KV write, so rotated q/k never round-trip through memory. This is the PROJECTION's epilogue (RoPE applies to projected q/k), not a norm fusion. It is a measured CANDIDATE behind the standard fusion discipline: bit-exact/tolerance-proven vs the unfused route (same profile), DEFAULT OFF until the ledger shows a win per (ISA, shape).
- Exactness contract: unfused vs fused must be equivalent under the profile's L1 metric contract (f32 work: identical operation order → expect bit-equality where the fusion preserves order; any reorder must be proven within tolerance and documented); table values differential-tested against the scalar spec engine's direct computation and oracle fixtures.

## Constraints
- θ is 7e7 — not 1e4, not 5e5; head_dim 128 — a 64-lane table is catastrophically wrong (doctrine #4); split-half, never adjacent-pair interleave (a plausible-text-producing bug the L2 taps exist to catch).
- Tables only to the admitted cap (memory admission precedes allocation, doctrine #15); no silent 256K reservation.
- Fusion is gated by the isomorphism/equivalence proof and default off until measured (one lever at a time, 5-pass keep/revert, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE for losers).
- Allowlist deps; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; safe Rust (autovec glue) unless a tier's SIMD island genuinely absorbs the epilogue.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) table-value differential green vs spec-engine direct computation and committed oracle RoPE fixtures (f32 tables; cast behavior per profile) including positions {0, 1, cap−1} and every j lane; (b) application-kernel L1 green for q and k at real shapes across prefill and decode-append paths; (c) fused-vs-unfused equivalence green per the stated contract on every (ISA, shape) where the variant exists; (d) admitted-cap sizing test green (cap C → table rows exactly C; position ≥ C is a typed error, not a wrap); (e) bench rows for fused vs unfused recorded in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md; the variant defaults ON only for shapes where the ledger shows a win, else stays off with the loser row retained.

## Tests
- Unit: inv_freq goldens at j ∈ {0, 1, 63} against closed-form θ^(−2j/128); rotation goldens on hand vectors (verifying the split-half pairing (i, i+64) explicitly against a wrong adjacent-pair double-check); position-0 identity checks (cos=1, sin=0 lanes).
- Property: rotation preserves per-pair vector norm in exact arithmetic (within f32 tolerance); applying position P then examining both loop passes uses identical table rows; fused == unfused per contract for random inputs; seed-reproducible.
- E2E (model-gated): RoPE-bearing taps (pre/post attention bisect points) inside the L2 sweep — **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without fixtures/artifact; synthetic paths always run. DETAILED LOGGING: failures log position, head, lane j, table values (cos/sin), input/output lanes, metric vector, and fused/unfused agreement to localize table vs application vs fusion.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle harness: the shared differential-harness machinery and fixture discipline this bead's comparators ride on (RoPE itself is float, but the harness/fixture generator and metric plumbing are that bead's deliverables).

title: [P3] Build fusion catalog behind per-fusion isomorphism proofs
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions/token, KV slot = layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, hidden 3072, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, SwiGLU 10752 (gate/up 3072→10752, down 10752→3072), vocab 166,144, untied lm_head → greedy needs argmax over 166,144 f32 logits = 664,576 B). Because no framework boundary forbids it, adjacent dataflow can fuse — but ALGEBRA AND DEPENDENCIES still do. The catalog is bit-exact-or-proven fusions, EACH gated by its own isomorphism proof, EACH default OFF until measured faster (one lever at a time; losers to NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE).

## Contract
Implement the four catalog fusions as selectable variants behind the dispatch/selection machinery, each with proof + measurement:
1. **Gate/up shared input quantization**: gate and up projections (both 3072→10752) share ONE quantized input row and one max-scan; pairwise SiLU×up writes the canonical intermediate scratch — replaces duplicate input quantization + separate activation/multiply buffers, while PRESERVING the global down-proj activation-scale contract (the fixed scale-application order from the canonical algebra).
2. **Norm → shared activation quantization**: RMSNorm output feeds ONE shared quantization consumed by q/k/v (and separately by gate/up at the layer's second norm) — norm scratch/max scan once, one quantized row reused, replacing per-projection re-quantization.
3. **Residual + next-norm sum-of-squares**: the residual add accumulates the NEXT RMSNorm's sum-of-squares in the same pass, followed by the still-required normalization pass — removes one full read of the hidden row; it does NOT pretend RMSNorm is single-pass.
4. **lm_head GEMV → argmax (greedy)**: fused projection+argmax over 166,144 rows with the specified lowest-token-id tie break and explicit NaN/Inf policy, no materialized softmax and no materialized full logit vector when nothing else needs it — replaces full-vector write + separate scan. (When logprobs/processors need the vector, the unfused route runs; the fusion never changes observable semantics.)
- **Isomorphism proof per fusion**: integer segments bit-exact; float segments preserve the canonical per-row reduction order so results are bit-identical to the unfused route under the same profile — any fusion that must reorder float reductions is NOT eligible for strict profiles and either keeps order or is dropped. Proof = differential equality corpus + a written order-preservation argument in the fusion's docs.
- **Default OFF until measured**: each fusion is a dispatch-selectable variant; it defaults on ONLY for (ISA, shape, regime) rows where the ledger shows a sustained win; losers stay implemented-but-off with their NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/PERF_LEDGER rows, or are reverted per the 5-pass loop.

## Constraints
- Bit-exact gate: fused == unfused under the active numerics profile (strict profiles demand bit-identity via preserved order); batch-invariance discipline (M=1 vs M>1 reduction-order rule) must survive every fusion.
- One lever at a time: each fusion lands/benches separately; never a combined "fusion pack" measurement authorizing all four.
- The scale-application order and down-proj activation-scale contract are the canonical algebra's fixed constants — fusion 1 and 2 must consume them, not redefine them.
- Leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon; allowlist deps; unsafe only within existing enumerated SIMD islands.
- Honest ledgering: every accepted default-on row cites its measurement; every loser is retained as evidence (doctrine #11).

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on, PER FUSION: (a) the equality corpus green (fused == unfused bit-exact for integer paths and order-preserving float paths, across fixed shapes, tails, and adversarial values incl. NaN/Inf for fusion 4's policy); (b) the written order-preservation/isomorphism note in the fusion docs; (c) sustained A/B bench rows (fused vs unfused, per ISA/shape/regime, p50/p95/p99, warm steady state) in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md; (d) default-state table showing ON only where measured-faster, with every OFF/loser row ledgered. A fusion missing any of (a)–(d) stays off and the bead does not close on its account until (a)–(b) exist and (c)–(d) record the honest outcome (a measured loss with a retained ledger row is a VALID close).

## Tests
- Unit: per-fusion tiny goldens (shared-quant scale equality; SoS accumulation vs separate-pass; argmax tie break lowest-id; NaN/Inf policy rows); scale-order conformance (fusions 1–2 produce byte-identical scale metadata to unfused).
- Property: random inputs × all fixed shapes → fused == unfused (bit-exact where contracted), seed-reproducible; fusion 3 equivalence across residual magnitudes including denormal-adjacent values; fusion 4 equals separate GEMV+argmax on random logit landscapes including exact ties.
- E2E: full-forward differential with each fusion toggled individually and all-on vs all-off (model-gated runs report **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact; synthetic-weight forwards always run).
