DETAILED LOGGING: failures name the fusion, shape, row, first diverging element, both values, and the active profile; bench logs record exact command/env/threads/CPU features.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] prepacked fixed-shape tiled GEMM: fusions attach to the production GEMM/GEMV epilogues and prologues; fusing a pre-final kernel would demand rework.
- Depends on [P3] native 48:8 GQA + decode attention (A_GQA): fusion 2's shared-quant feeds q/k/v around the attention kernel's contract, and forward-level equality corpora need the native attention path in place.

title: [P3] Build R1 latency gauntlet harness vs pinned llama.cpp baseline
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 layers × 2 loops → 44 logical executions/token, ≈12.6 GFLOP/token prefill-side, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44-deep KV at 176 KiB/token bf16, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT, vocab 166,144, untied lm_head). Phase 3's exit requires **gauntlet R1 — the latency benchmark pillar**: fair, receipted comparisons against the nearest-format peer. The strongest baseline is a PINNED, TESTED official `ggml-org/llama.cpp` revision at/after the Nanbeige support commit `b77d646…` (upstream expands 22 physical layers into 44 logical executions with distinct KV slots and loop-boundary norm), run CPU-ONLY. Honest, measured everything: no cherry-picked microbenches, no unfair thread/allocator asymmetries, losers stay in the ledger.

## Contract
- Build the R1 harness (benches/ + scripts) producing receipted A/B latency comparisons:
  - **Baseline pinning**: exact llama.cpp revision, RECORDED build flags, thread count, and the GGUF quant recipe used — all in the receipt; nearest-format pairing names peers honestly (our int8 vs the Q8_0 class) with the format difference stated in the receipt rather than hidden — never "matched quantization", because the formats are not numerically identical; matched-footprint and matched-quality views are additional labeled rows, not substitutes. CPU-only on both sides.
  - **Fairness controls**: same host, same thread counts (or both sides' own measured-best, both recorded), allocator identity recorded, same prompt corpus, thermal steady state established before measurement.
  - **Randomized paired A/B post-warmup**: interleaved randomized run order after warmup, measured at thermal steady state (steady-state detection criterion recorded), enough repetitions for stable percentiles; report distributions and confidence intervals, NEVER best-of-N.
  - **Metrics**: p50/p95/p99 per stage/regime (prefill tokens/s at fixed lengths; decode ms/token at batch 1; end-to-end task-shaped runs), plus ENERGY where the platform exposes it (recorded joules/doc or explicitly "unavailable").
  - **Separate attribution columns**: the report distinguishes what differs — format/recipe, kernel selection, threads, allocator — so a win/loss is attributable, never a mushy aggregate.
  - **Ledgering**: every comparison lands in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md (artifact-graph format: claim_id, evidence, fixture hashes, CPU feature string, exact command+env, disposition); LOSING rows (where we are slower) are recorded in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md / PERF_LEDGER.md and STAY there — slower rows are evidence, not embarrassment. A repository `.bench-history` ratchet retains every accepted baseline row so a regression is a mechanical diff, and the §10.2 loop is binding on every comparison this harness certifies: freeze claim/SHA/host/workload/counters first, change ONE causal lever, prove its equivalence/tolerance contract, then keep only when the confidence interval AND the practical threshold both win (otherwise restore baseline and retain the patch/commands/results as negative evidence).
  - Host matrix: accessible M4/M5 (Apple) and Zen 3/4/5 hosts; NO HARDWARE → NO CLAIM (the row is marked blocked, never extrapolated).
  - Output: machine-readable receipt rows + human summary; receipts name the ExecutionIdentity projection (artifact recipe, numerics profile, backend semantic version, host class) so no number floats free of its validity domain.

## Constraints
- G1 > G2: R1 runs only on parity-green configurations (a fast wrong build measures nothing); the receipt cites the parity run it rode on.
- Thread/allocator/precision fairness controls are mandatory (doctrine #11); `target-cpu=native` never ships and never benchmarks as "ours".
- No performance claim without a receipt row; public claims map to docs/CLAIMS.json (later governance surface) — this harness produces the evidence, not the marketing.
- llama.cpp stays an out-of-repo baseline binary (fork-only upstream relationship; we never vendor its code); the authors' `nanbeige42` fork is lineage, NOT an independent second baseline vote.
- Allowlist deps in our code; the baseline's own build is scripted + pinned but external.

## Evidence / gates
- Closes on: (a) the harness executing a full R1 sweep on at least one accessible host per family we possess, producing receipted p50/p95/p99 rows for prefill and decode with attribution columns and (where available) energy; (b) baseline pinning proven (revision, flags, threads, GGUF recipe in every receipt; re-run reproduces within stated noise bounds); (c) randomization/warmup/steady-state machinery validated by a self-test (injected thermal ramp → harness refuses to certify until steady); (d) ledger entries written in the artifact-graph format with losers present. Phase-3 exit language: R1 measured fairly on accessible M4/M5 and Zen 3/4/5 hosts; every winner AND loser ledgered.

## Tests
- Unit: receipt-row schema validation; attribution-column completeness (a row missing thread/allocator/flags fields is rejected); percentile math goldens; steady-state detector on synthetic traces (ramping vs stable).
- Property: run-order randomization is seed-logged and reproducible; paired-difference computation invariant to A/B labeling swap (sign flips, magnitude identical).
- E2E (model-gated): a short real sweep against the pinned baseline on the local host — reports **SKIPPED_NO_MODEL** without the artifact and SKIPPED_NO_BASELINE without the pinned llama.cpp build, each explicitly, never fake-passing. DETAILED LOGGING: every run logs exact argv, env, thread count, CPU feature string, temperature/steady-state samples where readable, and per-repetition raw timings (retained as fixture data for reanalysis). Named entrypoint: `scripts/e2e_gauntlet_r1.sh` — drives the baseline build/pin check, warmup/steady-state establishment, the randomized paired sweep, and receipt emission; per-stage timestamps and per-repetition raw rows are logged, SKIPPED_NO_MODEL / SKIPPED_NO_BASELINE are emitted explicitly, and the run ends with a machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line (rows produced, ledger paths, skips).

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P3] prepacked fixed-shape tiled GEMM: R1's prefill/batch numbers measure that surface; benchmarking pre-tiling kernels would ledger obsolete rows.
- Depends on [P3] native 48:8 GQA + decode attention (A_GQA): decode latency includes attention over the 44-deep KV; without the native kernel the numbers measure the L1 adapter (forbidden in production claims).
- Cross-epic (via bead_wants): A_INT8 — R1 runs on the real int8 artifact recipe (nearest-format pairing needs the actual `.fnlpq` int8 artifact and its recipe id).

title: [4C] Harden fnlp batch daemon: ordering, epochs, doc_error isolation, SIGINT drain, backpressure
description:
## Background
`fnlp batch` is the long-running NDJSON daemon: `{id, text, task_args?}` requests on stdin, results on stdout, weights loaded once. It is the amortized corpus path for the one-model wedge — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: 22 physical layers × 2 loops (KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots), final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024), vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, split-half RoPE θ=7e7. BF16 KV costs 180,224 B = 176 KiB/token/sequence, so reloading per invocation is prohibitive and the daemon is the product's throughput backbone. Phase 4A delivered the skeleton; this bead hardens it to the frozen §8.3/§8.4 contract.

## Contract
- **Completion-order default:** every result carries the caller `id` plus an engine-assigned monotonic `request_seq`. Every nonempty stdin line receives a checked `request_seq` BEFORE parsing; every event or parse error caused by that line echoes it, so a reused caller id can never make completion-order output ambiguous. Sequence overflow cleanly ends admission (no wraparound).
- **`--ordered` mode:** canonical byte replay requires `--ordered`, a DECLARED maximum reorder window (a documented, admission-bounded cap), and telemetry-free output: volatile run ids/timings/host counters omitted; canonical JSON (recursive UTF-8-byte key order, pinned serializer number/string escaping, non-finite floats rejected).
- **Numbered epochs:** duplicate caller ids are rejected within an epoch; the seen-id set is CAPPED (bounded memory) and resets ONLY after a drained `flush`. Flush events are numbered corpus/cluster boundaries.
- **doc_error isolation:** one malformed document emits exactly one typed `doc_error` with its sequence position; stream framing is never corrupted; the daemon continues. An ADMISSION rejection (memory/budget/size caps) is distinguishable from a parse failure: its typed payload names the exact violated certificate/budget term (the same named term the admission certificate prints in `robot plan`), so an agent can correct the request without diffing logs.
- **EOF** requests a graceful drain: admitted work completes, final flush, `run_complete`.
- **SIGINT policy:** first SIGINT closes admission and requests cooperative cancellation; a second SIGINT shortens the CLI grace policy but is NEVER described as safely preempting Rust/OS threads. The process emits no success receipt and does not reuse an in-process buffer before the compute completion latch fires (the pinned blocking contract: an already-running pool closure may outlive its cancelled wrapper, so the closure is tracked to an actual-completion latch and treated as outstanding drain work).
- **Backpressure pauses stdin reads** — bounded queues, no unbounded buffering; input is bounded by line/document/token/schema/output size caps before admission.
- Exit-code policy per §8.5: 0 ok, 1 generic, 2 usage, 4 input decode/parse, 5 budget/timeout, 6 cancelled, 9 admission/resource, 10 typed task no-result. CancelKind mapping: Timeout/Deadline/PollQuota/CostBudget→5; User/Shutdown/ordinary ParentCancelled→6; ResourceUnavailable→9; RaceLost escaping as a root terminal result is an invariant failure (1 + crashpack). A panic is a supervised failure producing `run_error` + nonzero status, never laundered into a per-document error.

## Constraints
G1>G2, profile-scoped (hf-bf16-eager / diagnostic-f32 / strict-quantized-vN / fast-vN). Determinism is scoped: NEVER promise byte identity for completion-order NDJSON. Asupersync owns every request region: one owned region/child Cx per admitted request or bounded batch epoch; the run crosses `Cx::spawn_blocking` once and uses one `Cx::scoped_cpu` region; leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon anywhere in the release graph; re-entrant calls fail typed/fast. Direct non-suite deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. stdout is data, stderr diagnostics; NO_COLOR/CI/TERM=dumb honored. Presets are data.

## Evidence / gates
Frozen robot-schema contract test (schema_version on every event: run_start, stage, doc, doc_error, token, flush, run_complete, run_error). Ordered-mode byte-identity replay fixture (same canonical metadata profile) and completion-order per-id semantic-equivalence fixture. SIGINT/second-SIGINT scenarios as deterministic asupersync Lab runs with seed-bound chaos; failing interleavings replay from seed + crashpack (never a one-off CI ghost). Gate evidence recorded with the Phase-4C exit set (R2/R3 gauntlet receipts).

## Tests
- Unit: epoch numbering, seen-id cap + reset-only-after-drained-flush, request_seq monotonicity and overflow-ends-admission, reorder-window bound enforcement.
- Property/fuzz: malformed NDJSON lines → exactly one doc_error and the stream survives; giant lines / invalid UTF-8 / duplicate ids / output amplification hit caps BEFORE allocation.
- Lab: EOF drain, first/second SIGINT, backpressure pause/resume, cancellation-at-every-stage; oracles for quiescence/obligation-leak/loser-drain; `many_docs_without_deadlock` watchdog.
- E2E soak with detailed stderr logging: per-event seq, epoch, queue depths, admission decisions, cancel reasons (CancelKind chain retained in robot envelope). Model-gated e2e reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL, never fake-passes. The soak/chaos e2e ships as the named runnable `scripts/e2e_batch_daemon_chaos.sh`: pipes a mixed valid/malformed/duplicate/giant-line corpus plus SIGINT/EOF/backpressure scenarios against the daemon, logs every event with (caller id, request_seq, epoch), logs scenario id + seed for every injected chaos scenario (replayable from the log alone), and ends with one machine-parseable summary line (docs in / ok / doc_error / rejected-by-term counts, exit code).

## Dependencies & rationale
- EP_P4C rollup (epic tracks this task).
- wants A_SCHED: the 4A scheduler core (layer-major batching, morsels, admission) is the engine this daemon feeds; hardening semantics sit on its cancellation/drain behavior.

## Ordered milestones (implement strictly in this order; each milestone independently reviewable and testable)

1. **`request_seq` assignment + completion-order default.** Deliverable: every nonempty stdin line receives a checked engine-assigned monotonic `request_seq` BEFORE parsing; every event or parse error caused by that line echoes it (reused caller ids can never make completion-order output ambiguous); sequence overflow cleanly ends admission with no wraparound. Test evidence: unit request_seq monotonicity and overflow-ends-admission; the completion-order per-id semantic-equivalence fixture. Next milestone assumes: unambiguous per-line sequencing underneath error isolation and epochs.
2. **`doc_error` isolation + input caps.** Deliverable: one malformed document emits exactly one typed `doc_error` with its sequence position, stream framing is never corrupted, and the daemon continues; input bounded by line/document/token/schema/output-size caps before admission. Test evidence: property/fuzz — malformed NDJSON lines yield exactly one `doc_error` and the stream survives; giant lines / invalid UTF-8 / output amplification hit caps BEFORE allocation. Next milestone assumes: a framing layer that survives hostile input.
3. **Numbered epochs + duplicate-id policy.** Deliverable: duplicate caller ids rejected within an epoch; the seen-id set CAPPED (bounded memory) and reset ONLY after a drained `flush`; flush events as numbered corpus/cluster boundaries. Test evidence: unit epoch numbering, seen-id cap, and reset-only-after-drained-flush; duplicate-id property/fuzz rows. Next milestone assumes: epoch semantics on which ordered replay and drain behavior rest.
4. **`--ordered` mode canonical replay.** Deliverable: `--ordered` with a DECLARED maximum reorder window (documented, admission-bounded) and telemetry-free output — volatile run ids/timings/host counters omitted; canonical JSON (recursive UTF-8-byte key order, pinned serializer number/string escaping, non-finite floats rejected). Test evidence: the ordered-mode byte-identity replay fixture (same canonical metadata profile); reorder-window bound enforcement unit; scope discipline — completion-order NDJSON is never promised byte identity. Next milestone assumes: the deterministic output contract is fixed before lifecycle hardening perturbs timing.
5. **Backpressure + EOF drain.** Deliverable: backpressure pauses stdin reads (bounded queues, no unbounded buffering); EOF requests a graceful drain — admitted work completes, final flush, `run_complete`. Test evidence: Lab EOF-drain and backpressure pause/resume runs with quiescence/obligation-leak oracles; the `many_docs_without_deadlock` watchdog. Next milestone assumes: clean quiescence paths that signal handling can reuse.
6. **SIGINT policy + completion latch.** Deliverable: first SIGINT closes admission and requests cooperative cancellation; second SIGINT shortens the CLI grace policy but is NEVER described as safely preempting Rust/OS threads; no success receipt is emitted and no in-process buffer is reused before the compute completion latch fires (the already-running pool closure is tracked to an actual-completion latch and treated as outstanding drain work). Test evidence: SIGINT/second-SIGINT scenarios as deterministic asupersync Lab runs with seed-bound chaos; failing interleavings replay from seed + crashpack; loser-drain and cancellation-at-every-stage oracles. Next milestone assumes: correct lifecycle terminal states for exit-code mapping to classify.
7. **Exit codes, CancelKind mapping, robot-schema freeze + soak.** Deliverable: §8.5 exit codes 0–10 with the CancelKind map (Timeout/Deadline/PollQuota/CostBudget→5; User/Shutdown/ordinary ParentCancelled→6; ResourceUnavailable→9; RaceLost escaping as a root terminal result = invariant failure, 1 + crashpack); a panic is a supervised failure producing `run_error` + nonzero status, never laundered into a per-document error. Test evidence: the frozen robot-schema contract test (schema_version on run_start, stage, doc, doc_error, token, flush, run_complete, run_error); E2E soak with detailed stderr logging (per-event seq, epoch, queue depths, admission decisions, cancel reasons with the CancelKind chain in the robot envelope); model-gated e2e reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; gate evidence recorded with the Phase-4C exit set (R2/R3 gauntlet receipts).

title: [4C] Restructure daemon internals as supervised children with typed ack discipline
description:
## Background
The hardened `fnlp batch` daemon (and, when jobs are enabled, the durable-job writers) has long-lived internals: admission feeder, scheduler pump, output writer, journal writer, spool writer. For the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) these processes hold the only weights copy and all in-flight work, so their lifecycle/restart semantics must be typed and model-checked, not incidental.

## Contract
- The daemon's long-lived internals — admission feeder, scheduler pump, output writer, and (when jobs are enabled) journal + spool writers — are **supervision candidates**: where the OQ-35 pinned-surface census RATIFIES the supervision/GenServer surfaces, they run as named children of ONE supervised tree with explicit restart policy and deterministic start/stop order. Absent ratification, the §3.3 explicit region tree with hand-rolled restart-on-error is the proven fallback. Either way, restart behavior is part of the model-checked lifecycle — never an incidental loop hidden inside a worker.
- REQUIRED admission, state-transition, output-delivery, journal, and spool operations use `call` (a tracked reply obligation) or a reserve→permit channel followed by an explicit processing/commit acknowledgement. A durable writer replies only AFTER the declared sync/commit point.
- `cast` is restricted to explicitly acknowledgement-free telemetry or declared latest-value notifications: async `cast().await` waits for bounded mailbox capacity but success proves ENQUEUE ONLY; nonblocking `try_cast` applies the configured overflow policy (`Reject` returns `Full`; `DropOldest` is allowed only for an explicitly lossy stream and its drops are COUNTED). Neither form is ever mislabeled a processing acknowledgement.
- Any later AA-R1 resident experiment sits under the same tree with registry name-leases, never an ambient service locator.

## Constraints
Asupersync pin truths (do not overclaim): GenServer cast acknowledges enqueue only; futurelock detection is a bounded witness, not a semantic-deadlock proof; all eleven CancelKind variants (User, Timeout, Deadline, PollQuota, CostBudget, FailFast, RaceLost, ParentCancelled, ResourceUnavailable, Shutdown, LinkedExit) preserved to the policy boundary; Lab oracles cover async state, NOT native scoped_cpu OS-thread interleavings — the bounded team-state model covers those; TLA+ export is TLC INPUT only. No Rayon in the release graph; leaf kernels never spawn; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. Required state transitions never ride on fire-and-forget messaging.

## Evidence / gates
- OQ-35 census outcome recorded (ratified surface list or explicit fallback decision) before the supervised-tree form ships.
- Deterministic Lab scenarios run to `run_until_quiescent_with_report()` asserting region/task/obligation/cleanup invariants, cancellation propagation, loser drain, no futurelock witness within named schedule/idle bounds; failing seeds attach crashpacks into the evidence ledger.
- Bounded team-state model covers the scoped_cpu OS-thread half; native hostile stress/replay validates the abstraction seam.

## Tests
- Unit: child start/stop order determinism; restart policy per child; reserve→permit accounting; overflow policies (Reject→Full, DropOldest drop counters exact).
- Property: no required operation completes via cast; every `call` reply obligation resolves or is a typed leak caught by the obligation oracle.
- Lab chaos: kill each named child at every lifecycle stage; assert deterministic restart and no lost/duplicated required acknowledgement; logging records child name, restart cause, and CancelKind chain.
- Model-gated paths report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL rather than fake-passing.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [4C] batch daemon hardening: it defines the concrete feeder/pump/writer processes and their required-op set being supervised.
- wants A_G0_CENSUS: the Phase-0 pinned-surface census (OQ-35) decides whether supervision/GenServer surfaces are ratified or the §3.3 region-tree fallback rules.

title: [4C] Build durable jobs core: snapshot commitment, execution key, HMAC commitments, cache authority
description:
## Background
Durable jobs (`fnlp job start/status/resume/verify/materialize`) are the opt-in corpus execution contract, distinct from the live `fnlp batch` pipe. For the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit, q 3072→6144; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), corpus runs are expensive (2 loop passes / 44 physical-layer executions per token position), so resumability must be exact and privacy-preserving. This bead builds the identity/commitment/cache-authority core; the commit protocol is a separate bead.

## Contract
- `fnlp job start` canonicalizes a replayable manifest and freezes (a) a **corpus-snapshot commitment** over ordered input ids/bytes/normalization and (b) a **semantic execution key** covering: artifact + packing; tokenizer/template/prompt/grammar/TaskIR including dependency scopes; task args; calibration/policy; numerics/KV/thinking/sampling INCLUDING the effective seed and addressable-sampler version; output schema; engine semantic version. This is an ExecutionIdentity projection (§4.3.1) — every cache/receipt key derives from the one ExecutionIdentity.
- **Per-job random 256-bit secret** + **domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 commitments** (RFC-2104/4231, mandatory RFC vectors, over the approved `sha2` primitive — never `SHA256(secret || value)`) for input bytes, normalized bytes, and result bytes. Raw SHA-256 of private content NEVER leaves owner-only job state (raw digests of low-entropy documents invite dictionary and cross-job equality attacks). The secret never enters telemetry, public receipts, or filenames. Public receipts expose: random job id, execution identity, item counts, commitment root. Trusted public artifacts, repo-shipped prompts, and release assets keep ordinary SHA-256 — they are not secrets.
- **Snapshot-wide item-id uniqueness** proven BEFORE execution, using a bounded external-sort/index when the corpus exceeds memory. (The live batch daemon's windowed duplicate rejection is a different, weaker contract.)
- **Cache authority by stage scope:** `ItemLocal` may reuse an exact item key; `PartitionReduce` must rerun its deterministic reduce when the complete child-set digest changes; `CorpusGlobal` authority is valid only for the exact snapshot. Adding one item preserves exact unaffected ItemLocal entries but invalidates/recomputes every changed PartitionReduce/CorpusGlobal authority.
- fsqlite records `pending → admitted → running → result_committed → materialized`. Default journal tables contain ids, digests, state, attempts, metrics, errors — NEVER input text or output bytes; resume requires the original manifest. `--spool-input`, `--spool-results`, and incremental result caching are explicit owner-only privacy/storage choices with byte/retention budgets and inspect/purge commands.

## Constraints
fsqlite, never rusqlite; fsqlite tables never contain document/prompt/output text. Durability authority boundary: an owned checksummed spool/materializer may promise one canonical committed record per item; arbitrary stdout promises only stable ids + documented at-least-once replay. Job persistence opt-in, metadata-only by default. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon in the release graph. Secret handling: non-Debug/non-Clone wrapper, minimized copies; process-memory/debugger resistance and compiler-proof zeroization are explicitly NOT claimed.

## Evidence / gates
- HMAC-SHA-256 passes RFC-2104/4231 vectors (mandatory fixture).
- ExecutionIdentity projection differential: cache keys, receipt keys, and the semantic execution key derive from one identity; any field change (including effective seed / sampler version) changes the key.
- Dependency-scope mutation invariant fixture: item-only snapshot change preserves exact unaffected ItemLocal entries and invalidates PartitionReduce/CorpusGlobal (a §9 metamorphic invariant, Phase-4C exit gate).
- Privacy gates: journal-content field allowlist test; no raw private-content hash or snippet in telemetry/exported receipts; inspect/purge behavior proven.

## Tests
- Unit: manifest canonicalization; key field-level diff; domain-separation labels; commitment-root construction.
- Property/fuzz: duplicate item-id detection including the out-of-memory external-sort path (population/order invariance); low-entropy input corpora show no equality leakage across jobs (different jobs → different commitments for identical bytes).
- E2E: job start → status over a small corpus with detailed stderr logging of state transitions, counts, and scope-cache decisions; model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [4C] batch daemon hardening: jobs ride the hardened daemon execution/admission semantics (epochs, drain, cancellation).
- wants A_EXECID: the ExecutionIdentity type (§4.3.1) is the single identity every job key/receipt projects from.

title: [4C] Implement spool-first/journal-second commit, recovery, and resume/verify/materialize
description:
## Background
A database transaction cannot atomically commit an external spool append, so durable jobs need a normative commit order and a recovery discipline. This is the exactly-once authority boundary for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half): when the job owns a checksummed spool and materialization it can promise ONE canonical committed record per item; raw stdout can promise only stable ids and at-least-once replay.

## Contract
Normative **spool-first, journal-second** protocol — five steps, in order:
1. Encode ONE canonical framed result: item id + execution identity + length + keyed (HMAC-SHA-256) result commitment.
2. Append the frame to the same-job result spool.
3. Flush/sync the spool per the declared durability mode.
4. Commit `(spool_generation, offset, length, commitment)` plus `result_committed` in fsqlite.
5. Only then acknowledge durable completion.

- **Recovery** scans only to the last journal-authorized frame, independently validates framing and commitments, truncates or quarantines any uncommitted/torn tail, and NEVER trusts a valid-looking spool record absent its committed journal pointer. Interrupted pre-commit states are retryable.
- Input spooling follows the same spool-first/journal-second order. Directory-entry durability/replacement semantics are documented per platform — never waved through as "fsync makes it atomic".
- **Materialization** derives only from committed pointers and is itself staged, synced, and atomically published; `materialize --ordered` writes one canonical record per item.
- **`resume`** refuses ANY execution-key mismatch with a field-level diff (a caller label alone is not identity; wrong pseudonym/commitment secret fails before emitting mixed output).
- **`verify`** checks journal/spool/materialization consistency end-to-end.
- Output paths follow the §8.6 local-output transaction: owner-controlled parent, exclusive `create_new` staging, no symlink/reparse/device targets, owner-only permissions, sync + same-directory activation.

## Constraints
Durability has an authority boundary (owned spool = exactly-once per item; stdout = at-least-once). fsqlite never rusqlite; journal tables never contain input text or output bytes. Durable writers reply only after the declared sync point (call / reserve→permit + commit ack — never cast). Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon. Honest durability status reported (declared durability mode, platform semantics), never a blanket atomicity claim.

## Evidence / gates
- Kill/disk-full/corrupt-tail injection at EVERY transition (pending→admitted→running→result_committed→materialized) shows **uninterrupted ≡ resumed** semantic output in ordered deterministic mode — a Phase-4C exit gate.
- Where the OQ-35 census ratifies them, these campaigns run as seed-bound Lab chaos scenarios (deterministic cancellation/delay/budget-exhaustion injection + reusable crash/restart scenario definitions) so a failing interleaving replays from its seed and crashpack.
- Wrong-key resume-refusal fixture with field-level diff output.

## Tests
- Unit: frame encode/decode; spool_generation/offset/length bookkeeping; staged materialization publish.
- Fuzz: torn-tail/truncated/bit-flipped spool frames → recovery truncates/quarantines, never accepts; journal-without-spool and spool-without-journal divergences detected by `verify`.
- E2E: kill -9 at each step 1–5 boundary, restart, `resume`, byte-compare ordered materialization vs uninterrupted run; disk-full via quota injection; detailed logging of every recovery decision (frame offsets, quarantine paths, truncation points). Model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. This matrix ships as the named runnable `scripts/e2e_job_kill_resume.sh`: for each of the five protocol steps it logs the kill-point id, every recovery-state transition (scan → validate → truncate/quarantine → resume) with frame offsets, and the uninterrupted-vs-resumed byte-compare verdict, ending with one machine-parseable summary line per (kill-point, outcome); seed-bound Lab variants log scenario id + seed so failures replay from the log alone.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [4C] durable jobs core: the execution key, HMAC commitments, and fsqlite state machine this protocol commits against.

title: [4C] Ship fnlp resolve: lexical blocking, LLM pair scoring, deterministic clustering
description:
## Background
`fnlp resolve` canonicalizes entity mentions across a corpus (the companion to source-grounded `ner`). On the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), every scored pair costs a complete two-loop invocation (2 passes / 44 physical-layer executions per token position), so blocking is the cost lever and determinism is the correctness lever.

## Contract
- Pipeline: **lexical blocking → LLM pair scores within blocks → deterministic clustering**.
- Determinism at flush: mentions sorted by `(document_id, byte_start, type, surface)`; canonical pair order; frozen scores; exactly ONE named clustering rule. Final output is independent of arrival order and completion order.
- Daemon semantics: `resolve` collects mentions and emits deterministic FINAL clusters only on a numbered flush/EOF transaction. Provisional incremental clusters may be emitted only as explicitly provisional events — never as final results.
- Cache authority: mention/pair caches are `ItemLocal` (exact item key reuse); clusters are `CorpusGlobal`, bound to the complete snapshot digest and snapshot-qualified — never return a stale global cluster because one document hash was unchanged. Adding a document preserves exact unaffected ItemLocal entries but invalidates/recomputes cluster authority.
- Realized cost reporting: candidate-pair count and model invocations are reported (structural witnesses), so avoided pairs and their risk (a missed pair can corrupt a cluster) stay visible.

## Constraints
G1>G2 profile-scoped; valid-by-construction output (G8): budget/cancel/resource failure is a typed no-result (exit 10), never partial success. Cache authority follows dependency scope (doctrine #25). Presets/prompts are versioned data carrying prompt-template hashes. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn. AA-B1 (MinHash/LSH blocking) is a later gated card — this bead ships exhaustive type-compatible pairs or the simple proven lexical blocker as the deterministic baseline/fallback.

## Evidence / gates
- Arrival/completion-order independence fixture: shuffled input orders → byte-identical flush output under `--ordered`.
- Snapshot-id stability fixture: same frozen snapshot → same cluster ids; item-only change → new snapshot authority (dependency-scope mutation invariant, Phase-4C exit gate).
- §9.6 scorecard hooks produced here (executed by the [4C] eval campaign bead): blocking recall reported BEFORE clustering scores; pairwise P/R/F1; B³/CEAF-class metrics where licensed labels permit; overmerge/undermerge rates; singleton behavior; runtime vs candidate-pair count.

## Tests
- Unit: mention sort key, canonical pair ordering, the named clustering rule on hand-built fixtures (incl. ties).
- Property: clustering rule is a deterministic function of the frozen score set; permutation invariance over input order; provisional events never alter final clusters.
- E2E: multi-document NDJSON run through `fnlp batch` with flush boundaries; detailed logging of block sizes, pair counts, score provenance, cluster decisions. Model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_resolve_flush.sh`: multi-document NDJSON through `fnlp batch` with numbered flush boundaries and shuffled arrival orders, logging block sizes, candidate-pair counts, snapshot digests, and one machine-parseable cluster row per flush; order-independence asserted by byte-comparing `--ordered` outputs across shuffles; SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- wants A_TASKCORE: rides the shared task-core (TaskIR stages, typed prompt-segment/trust ABI, presets, robot task envelope) from Phase 4B.

title: [4C] Ship fnlp sentiment: distribution and sampled modes
description:
## Background
`fnlp sentiment` is the dimension-scoring task — the swiss_army_llama descendant (the project owner's own prior work; methodology/prompts/presets reused freely WITH attribution). On the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), a single-step distribution read is dramatically cheaper than sampling — but its probability semantics must be stated exactly (§6.10 score spaces).

## Contract
- **Presets:** focus areas (e.g. reviews, earnings calls, support tickets), each defining adjective dimensions, audience/context, and a `[-100,+100]` interpretation with 0 = indeterminate. Running `fnlp sentiment` WITHOUT `--focus-area` is an exit-2 usage error that LISTS the shipped focus-area presets (name + one-line description) and shows one worked command; an unknown focus area lists the valid names. Every imported swiss_army_llama datum gets an origin hash so later edits are auditable.
- **Mode A `--mode distribution`** (candidate default ONLY after quality proof): one shared-prefix-cached prefill per `(doc, dimension)`; a closed, census-verified single-token bucket vocabulary. Bucket-token identity is census-verified IN the exact answer scaffold INCLUDING leading whitespace — never by tokenizing the label string in isolation. The fast path computes only bucket rows and reports **`single_step_candidate_conditional`** (the depth-1 form of trie_local_conditional_probability); it must NEVER report "captured mass", because that requires the full 166,144-row denominator. A **full-vocabulary audit path** computes true captured mass on the calibration/test sample and establishes whether the prompt reliably puts probability on the scale. Presets include an explicit `UNSURE/OFF_SCALE` bucket. Single-token opaque labels preferred; multi-token alternatives use a frozen teacher-forced sequence-scoring/length-normalization recipe and separate calibration. Report: normalization mode, E[score], dispersion, entropy, calibration version, abstention/off-scale decision.
- **Mode B `--mode sampled --justify`:** independently implemented N-seed generations with a grammar-locked score plus free-text justification and a preregistered aggregation/interval recipe. Inspired by the prior project's behavior — not copied code/data.
- **Default policy:** both modes are judged independently against held-out human labels/rankings and reliability targets BEFORE distribution mode may become default (task metric + calibration + full-vocab captured-mass + throughput gates all pass; otherwise sampled or abstaining mode stays default). Cross-mode agreement is a diagnostic, never ground truth, and never a reason to force two different estimators to coincide.

## Constraints
Every scoring surface names its probability space (§6.10: full_vocab_sequence_logprob / trie_local_conditional_probability / sequence_score_softmax; mandatory score_space envelope field). Candidate scores are never mislabeled probabilities. Thinking off by default for structured tasks. Prompts/presets are versioned data with prompt-template hashes. Sampling uses the addressable sampler (seeded; RANDOM capability drawn once at admission for unseeded). Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon. Attribution is factual provenance, never a synthesized copyright notice.

## Evidence / gates
- Bucket census fixture: every bucket token verified single-token in the exact scaffold context (incl. leading whitespace) against the frozen tokenizer; failure blocks Mode A.
- Score-space labeling test: fast path emits single_step_candidate_conditional; captured-mass field appears ONLY on full-vocab audit outputs (166,144-row denominator).
- §9.6 scorecard hooks (executed in the [4C] eval campaign): disjoint calibration/test splits with human labels; rank correlation/MAE/reliability/selective risk; captured-mass audit; cross-mode agreement diagnostic; directional negation probes reported as sanity, not law.

## Tests
- Unit: preset parsing, scaffold construction, bucket-row extraction, E[score]/dispersion/entropy math.
- Property: Mode A fast path equals full-vocab path restricted to bucket rows (differential); N-seed Mode B aggregation is a deterministic function of the seed set.
- E2E: both modes over a small labeled fixture corpus with detailed logging (per-dimension buckets, masses on audit path, seeds, aggregation trace). Model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_sentiment_golden.sh`: both modes plus the missing/unknown focus-area usage paths, one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, mode, score_space, dataset/prompt-hash/recipe/thinking-mode, exit code), SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- wants A_TASKCORE: shared task-core (prompt-segment ABI, presets, envelopes) from 4B.
- wants A_SAMPLER: Mode B's N-seed generation requires the addressable, versioned sampler (effective seed + sampler version enter the ExecutionIdentity).

title: [4C] Ship fnlp judge: rubric, faithfulness, order-debiased pairwise
description:
## Background
`fnlp judge` scores text against rubrics, verifies claim faithfulness against a source, and expresses pairwise preference. On the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), judge runs at classify-path cost (NLI-style single-step scoring), making it the local RAG-verification loop batchable over an entire retrieval log.

## Contract
- **Rubric mode:** score texts against provenance-cleared rubric presets. Distribution-style scoring is only a candidate default after the SAME held-out human-label gates as sentiment (task metric, calibration, full-vocab captured-mass, throughput); otherwise sampled/abstaining behavior stays default.
- **Faithfulness mode:** claim (or answer) + source → `{entailed | contradicted | unsupported}` + evidence spans. NLI-style, classify-path cost, batchable over a whole retrieval log.
- **Pairwise mode:** A vs B under a criterion → preference + margin computed from the two candidates' logprobs, **order-debiased by running BOTH orders and averaging** — exactly 2 prefills, still cheap. Feeds eval pipelines and rerank-by-judge.
- **Internal second-reader reuse:** `extract --verify-semantic` may reuse this exact VERSIONED task, but its same-model correlation and per-field claim rendering remain visible in the receipt. Verification is a diagnostic/decision-policy input whose uplift must be measured per extraction domain — never a certificate attached merely because a second forward ran (a second pass of the same model is not independent proof).

## Constraints
G8 valid-by-construction output; typed no-result (exit 10) on budget/cancel, never partial success. Score spaces named per §6.10 (score_space envelope field mandatory). Thinking off by default for structured tasks (bounded explicit override). Prompts/rubric presets are versioned data with prompt-template hashes; rubric provenance recorded. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn.

## Evidence / gates
- Both-order debias fixture: pairwise result invariant under argument swap (preference direction flips consistently; margin magnitude equal), proven on frozen fixtures.
- Faithfulness three-way output validates independently; evidence spans byte-verified against the supplied source.
- §9.6 scorecard hooks (executed in the [4C] eval campaign): licensed/owned entailment label sets; per-mode metrics with recipe id + prompt hash + thinking mode + dataset version.

## Tests
- Unit: rubric preset parsing; three-way label mapping; margin math from paired logprobs; order-averaging.
- Property: pairwise(A,B) and pairwise(B,A) produce mirrored preferences with identical averaged margin; faithfulness spans always occur in source bytes.
- E2E: batch a synthetic retrieval log through faithfulness mode with detailed logging (per-claim verdicts, span offsets, score spaces). Model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_judge_golden.sh`: rubric/faithfulness/pairwise fixtures incl. the both-order debias check, one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, mode, score_space, verdict, dataset/prompt-hash/recipe/thinking-mode, exit code), SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- wants A_TASKCORE: shared task-core (prompt-segment/trust ABI, presets, envelopes, classify-path scoring) from 4B.

title: [4C] Ship fnlp summarize, keyphrases, answer with structural citations
description:
## Background
`fnlp summarize`, `fnlp keyphrases`, and `fnlp answer` complete the v1 task portfolio. On the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), long documents are expensive — bf16 KV is 176 KiB/token and prefill attention is quadratic — so summarize rides the map-reduce spine, and citation claims are typed precisely.

## Contract
- **`summarize`:** length/style presets `--words` / `--bullets` / `--tldr`; long docs run map-reduce over the §7.10 spine; `--cited` makes every bullet carry syntactically valid, **byte-verified source spans — a STRUCTURAL citation guarantee**, explicitly not proof the spans entail the bullet. The stronger word **`grounded` is RESERVED** for a separately qualified task version that passes a locked human factual-support evaluation and an explicit semantic-support policy (§9.6); a same-model judge contributes diagnostics but cannot turn span membership into entailment.
- **`keyphrases`:** ranked phrases, constrained-list output (valid by construction), exact-match anchoring to source bytes, `--max N`.
- **`answer`:** context-limited QA — question + provided passages → answer + byte-valid span citations + calibrated abstain (`answerable: false`, calibrated per §7.8; abstention is a SUCCESSFUL typed result, exit 0 + status "abstained"). Base contract is structural citation validity (spans exist in the supplied passages); `grounded` is claimable only by a version whose locked evaluation measures semantic support of each material claim. **Citation validity and citation support are separate metrics, never conflated.** Retrieval itself is frankensearch's job — `answer` consumes its output NDJSON shape. Invoking `answer` without passages is an exit-2 usage error with a worked example of the expected passage NDJSON.

## Constraints
G8 valid-by-construction; typed no-result (exit 10) on failure, never truncated output as success. Grounded-field verification is independent of the grammar compiler (separate validation module). Thinking off by default. Presets/prompts versioned data with prompt hashes. Map-reduce outputs linked to chunk ids/byte ranges; hierarchical reduce never claims single-context equivalence. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon.

## Evidence / gates
- Structural-citation property: every emitted span byte-verifies against the source/passages via the independent verifier; a failing span is a typed error, not a warning.
- Abstention calibration hook: answerable/abstain decision carries calibration version; uncalibrated builds label the signal `uncalibrated`.
- §9.6 scorecard hooks (executed in the [4C] eval campaign): summarize — length/coverage, citation validity, citation-support precision/recall, human-annotated claim-level factuality subset (any external LLM judge disclosed, never the sole gate); answer — answerability, correctness, citation validity + citation support separately, selective risk; keyphrases — anchoring rate, exact/partial P@K, R@K, duplicate/stem variants, diversity, blinded human usefulness.

## Tests
- Unit: preset parsing (--words/--bullets/--tldr/--max N), citation span plumbing, answerable:false envelope.
- Property/fuzz: constrained keyphrase list always validates; citations always within passage bounds; map-reduce chunk linkage total (every output traceable to chunk ids/byte ranges).
- E2E: long-document summarize through the spine; answer over a passage set including unanswerable cases; detailed logging (chunk boundaries, reduce decisions, span verification results). Model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_task_summarize_golden.sh` covers all three subcommands (long-doc summarize through the spine, keyphrases, answer incl. unanswerable and the no-passages usage error), one machine-parseable row per case (fixture id, chunk count, citation-verification verdict, dataset/prompt-hash/recipe/thinking-mode, exit code), SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [4C] map-reduce spine: summarize's long-doc mode (and shared long-doc handling) executes over it.
- wants A_TASKCORE: shared task-core (segments, presets, envelopes, calibration hooks) from 4B.

title: [4C] Build long-document map-reduce spine (mapreduce.rs)
description:
## Background
`mapreduce.rs` is the shared long-document spine for summarize/extract/score-over-long-docs. On the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), the 44-deep KV makes even 32K context expensive: bf16 KV is 180,224 B = 176 KiB per token per sequence (8K ≈ 1.38 GiB), and full attention is quadratic in prefill. Map-reduce is therefore a PRIMARY operating mode — not an edge case hidden behind the reported 256K maximum, which is not a usability promise.

## Contract
- Pipeline: **deterministic token-budgeted chunking → batched map → task-specific deterministic reduce.**
- Chunking is deterministic under the exact tokenizer (byte spans preserved; chunk coverage/overlap deterministic and testable).
- Every output is linked to chunk ids and byte ranges — full traceability from any reduced claim back to source chunks.
- Conflict/dedup rules, score weights, reduce fan-in, and lossy-summary warnings are VERSIONED data (changing one is a diffable event with an eval re-run).
- Hierarchical reduction NEVER claims exact equivalence to single-context inference — the reduce is its own named, deterministic semantics.
- Map stage batches through the scheduler (R2/R3 regimes); reduce is deterministic given the complete child set (a `PartitionReduce` stage: it must rerun when the complete child-set digest changes).

## Constraints
Determinism is scoped: same chunker version + same reduce version + same numerics profile → same output; batch/prefix equivalence requires the same per-row reduction order. Cache authority follows dependency scope (ItemLocal map outputs; PartitionReduce reduce outputs). Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; memory admission precedes allocation (process-aggregate EngineResources ledger).

## Evidence / gates
- Deterministic-chunking golden: fixed corpus → exact chunk boundaries/coverage/overlap per chunker version.
- Traceability property: every reduced output field maps to ≥1 chunk id + byte range; orphan outputs are a typed error.
- Child-set digest invariant: adding/removing one chunk changes the reduce authority and forces recompute while unaffected ItemLocal map entries are preserved (feeds the Phase-4C dependency-scope exit gate).

## Tests
- Unit: token-budget boundary cases (chunk exactly at budget, tiny tail chunks, overlap math); versioned rule parsing.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary UTF-8 documents chunk without panic; concatenation/permutation of documents never crosses chunk provenance; reduce is a pure function of the ordered child set.
- E2E: long synthetic document through map-reduce with detailed logging (chunk table, per-chunk map status, reduce decision trace, fan-in used). Model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- EP_P4C rollup only; consumed by [4C] summarize/keyphrases/answer (dep from that bead). Built on the 4A scheduler/batching primitives already required by the epic's daemon work.

title: [4C] Gate tool mode behind OQ-10 parser conformance corpus
description:
## Background
Nanbeige4.2-3B's chat template (im/think markers, XML/JSON tool branches) supports tool calling, but fnlp ships tool mode only behind evidence. The wedge model (HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) emits tool-call text in two pinned formats (XML and JSON branches of the template); parsing that text robustly is an empirical contract (OQ-10), not a prose claim. Template-side RENDERING landed in Phase 1; this bead is the PARSER side and its conformance corpus.

## Contract
- Build the OQ-10 conformance corpus for BOTH pinned formats (XML and JSON tool-call branches):
  - exact accepted tool-call ASTs (golden fixtures);
  - malformed calls (broken tags/braces, wrong nesting);
  - duplicate arguments;
  - nested and multiline argument values;
  - adjacent calls (back-to-back, no separator);
  - calls mixed with natural-language prose;
  - missing delimiters (unterminated call at EOS/budget);
  - the documented parser RECOVERY POLICY for each malformation class.
- Tool declaration/rendering/parsing is COMPILED IN only when OQ-10 is EVIDENCED (line-backed parser contract + this corpus + its eval gates green). Before that gate, `--tools` returns a typed unsupported-surface error — absent or a versioned `surface_not_built` error ONLY where the frozen robot schema explicitly describes that state. Never a success-shaped stub.
- `fnlp` parses and emits tool-call DATA but NEVER executes tools.
- Parser success is a separate metric from tool-selection quality (the model choosing the right tool is a different, later question).

## Constraints
G8: a parsed tool call validates or is a typed parse failure; no unconstrained retry loop. Forced tokens ≠ forced bytes; template control ids are emitted only by trusted template code (untrusted segments exclude every TemplateControlIds member or reject). Presets/templates are versioned data. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon. Every parser boundary rejects duplicate JSON object keys rather than accepting parser-dependent overwrite semantics.

## Evidence / gates
- OQ-10 register row flips to EVIDENCED only with: archived line-backed template/tool-format evidence, the complete conformance corpus committed, and parser pass/fail rows published per malformation class (§9.6 tool-call parsing scorecard: exact accepted-call ASTs, malformed XML/JSON, duplicate arguments, nested/multiline values, adjacent calls, mixed prose, missing delimiters, recovery policy — for both formats).
- Frozen robot-schema fixture describes the `surface_not_built` state for `--tools` pre-gate; contract test proves the pre-gate behavior.

## Tests
- Unit: AST construction per format; recovery-policy state machine per malformation class.
- Property/fuzz: arbitrary text → parse-or-typed-error, never panic, never a silently dropped or half-accepted call; duplicate-argument and duplicate-key rejection.
- Golden: the full corpus replayed with exact expected ASTs/errors; UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 with mandatory diff review.
- E2E (model-gated, SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without artifact): generate with tool declarations under the pinned template and parse the emission; detailed logging of every parse decision and recovery action. The corpus replay ships as the named deliverable `tests/tool_call_parser_conformance.rs`: every malformation class for BOTH formats, one machine-parseable row per case (format, class, expected/actual AST-or-error, recovery action).

## Dependencies & rationale
- wants A_TPL_L0: the L0-exact template builder (Phase 1, OQ-7 AST matrix) renders the tool branches this parser must round-trip against; parser conformance is meaningless without the pinned rendering side.

title: [4C] Run 4C eval scorecards and durability chaos campaigns
description:
## Background
Phase 4C exits only when the remaining v1 portfolio has published scorecards and the durability story is proven under chaos. Kernel parity proves faithful execution of the wedge model (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) — but not useful tasks. This bead runs the §9.6 eval campaigns for resolve/sentiment/judge/summarize/answer/keyphrases and the §8.4 durability chaos campaigns, producing the Phase-4C exit evidence.

## Contract
Scorecards (each states model recipe id, thinking mode, prompt hash, dataset version; every dataset first enters docs/eval/DATASETS.md with immutable source, exact license text/terms, allowed use/redistribution, preprocessing digest, unit of analysis, dev/calibration/test ids, contamination/leakage risks; "fetch by hash" is not permission; only repo-authored or explicitly redistributable data is committed):
- **resolve:** blocking recall reported BEFORE clustering scores (a good clustering score cannot hide blocking false negatives); pairwise P/R/F1; B³/CEAF-class cluster metrics where licensed labels permit; overmerge/undermerge rates; singleton behavior; deterministic snapshot-id stability; runtime vs candidate-pair count.
- **sentiment:** disjoint calibration/test splits with human labels/rankings; rank correlation/MAE/reliability/selective risk; full-vocab captured-mass audit (the 166,144-row denominator); cross-mode agreement as a diagnostic only; directional negation probes as sanity reports.
- **judge:** licensed/owned entailment label sets for faithfulness.
- **summarize:** length/coverage; citation validity; citation-support precision/recall; human-annotated claim-level factuality subset (external LLM judge disclosed, never the sole gate).
- **answer:** answerability; answer correctness; citation validity and citation support as SEPARATE metrics; selective risk.
- **keyphrases:** source-anchoring rate; exact/partial P@K and R@K where references exist; duplicate/stem variants; diversity; blinded human usefulness on owned data.
- Every document-consuming task includes matched clean/adversarial-content fixtures (role-marker text, refusal steering, false-negative steering, value steering, tool-call bait); content-injection resistance is an empirical per-task attack-success metric — never a firewall claim.
- **Chaos campaigns:** kill / disk-full / corrupt-tail injection at every durable-job transition, run as seed-bound lab chaos scenarios (deterministic cancellation/delay/budget-exhaustion injection; reusable crash/restart scenario definitions) proving **uninterrupted ≡ resumed** in ordered deterministic mode; failing interleavings replay from seed + crashpack.

## Constraints
Quality regressions gate releases at the same rank as parity regressions. Preregistered point estimates and confidence intervals on locked data; no post-hoc metric shopping. A user scorecard is never promoted into a universal project claim. Task-quality claims name dataset, prompt hash, recipe id, thinking mode. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite. Model-gated: ordinary CI reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; armed runs record artifact digest.

## Evidence / gates
Phase-4C exit set: uninterrupted ≡ resumed equivalence green; dependency-scope mutation invariants green; privacy/storage tests green; full v1 portfolio scorecards published; R2/R3 gauntlet receipts green. Scorecards land in the ledger/registry flow (PERF_LEDGER rows for R2/R3; claims stay ≤ registry state).

## Tests
This bead IS the test campaign; its own meta-tests: dataset-registration validator (DATASETS.md row complete before use); scorecard schema validator; chaos scenarios replayable from recorded seeds; detailed logging of every campaign run (dataset digests, split ids, seeds, crashpack ids). SKIPPED_NO_MODEL for all model-gated rows. Campaign runners are named deliverables: `scripts/e2e_4c_scorecard_campaign.sh` drives every §9.6 scorecard and emits one machine-parseable row per task carrying dataset version+digest, prompt hash, recipe id, and thinking mode (SKIPPED_NO_MODEL rows explicit, never silently absent); the durability chaos campaign reuses `scripts/e2e_job_kill_resume.sh` scenario definitions with scenario id, seed, and crashpack id logged per run.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [4C] resolve, [4C] sentiment, [4C] judge, [4C] summarize/keyphrases/answer: the campaign evaluates those shipped surfaces.
- wants A_EVALFW: the eval framework/harness (datasets registry, scorecard machinery, locked-split handling) this campaign executes on.

title: [P5] Implement int4 per-group quantization (g32/g16) via proven int8 MAC paths
description:
## Background
Int4 halves weight traffic versus int8 for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit, q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half; 4,169,800,704 params = 8,339,601,408 bf16 payload bytes). Decode is memory-bound (R1), so int4 is the traffic lever — but v1 stays on the PROVEN int8 MAC paths: no target tier gets a new packed-int4 multiply-accumulate.

## Contract
- **Uniform per-group baselines:** int4 with group sizes g32 and g16 (per-group scales), produced as staged immutable artifacts alongside the int8 chain (int8-mlp → int8-mlp-attn → int8-all precedent; prior-artifact activation is the real rollback — no env var may claim to restore bf16 weights not in the file).
- **In-register unpack int4 → int8 feeding the SAME proven MAC paths.** No v1 target tier (AVX2, AVX-512-VNNI zmm/ymm, NEON/SDOT, scalar) implements a packed-int4 MAC.
- **Per-group i32 accumulators with their own proved bounds.** Method as at K=10752 for int8 (S8×S8 ≤ 176,160,768; raw U8×S8 ≤ 350,945,280; +correction ≤ 176,160,768; conservative sum 527,106,048 < 2^31−1 with >4× headroom): derive and prove the analogous per-group bounds for g=32 and g=16 int4 values against i64, covering every model K, row sum, tail, and SIMD tier.
- **Dequantize per group, then add in increasing-group f32 order; scales are NEVER pulled outside the sum.** The group-order f32 accumulation is part of the named numerics contract (strict-quantized-vN).
- **Canonical nibble order:** one documented packing (which nibble is element 0), enforced by the format writer and asserted by the reader; any deviation is an artifact integrity error (exit 7).

## Constraints
G1>G2 profile-scoped: int4 recipes carry preregistered logit/argmax/token/task budgets under strict-quantized-vN; deliberate divergence from bf16 is a separate preregistered decision, never a blanket BF16-token-identity claim. AVX2 is first-class and exact — raw saturating vpmaddubsw is banned; use the proved low-7/high-bit decomposition or widened signed-i16 route. Integer stages exact vs scalar/i64. Measured-faster wins (dispatch tables record measured choices; forced paths remain for proof runs). Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; unsafe only in enumerated SIMD islands with SAFETY proofs.

## Evidence / gates
- Bounds memo: per-group i32 bound derivation for g32/g16 checked against i64 brute force over full int4 domain; committed with the kernel.
- L1 same-recipe integer-exact gate: every SIMD tier ≡ canonical scalar/i64 for the unpack+MAC+per-group path; L2/L3 named tolerance vectors for the f32 group-sum stage; L4 quantized-vs-bf16 token agreement MEASURED, not presumed.
- Format: allocation of groups/scales recorded in .fnlpq; nibble-order assertion fixture; conversion-twice identity.

## Tests
- Unit: nibble pack/unpack round-trip; group boundary tails (K not divisible by group size); scale placement.
- Property/differential: random int4 weight tiles × int8 activations — SIMD ≡ scalar ≡ i64 exactly; group-order f32 sum deterministic and permutation-sensitive test documents the fixed order.
- Fuzz: malformed int4 artifact headers/groups rejected loudly (exit 7).
- E2E (model-gated, SKIPPED_NO_MODEL): int4-g32/g16 artifacts load and decode a frozen prefix; detailed logging of tier dispatch, bounds mode, group stats.

## Dependencies & rationale
- A_INT8 (franken_nlp-of3): the int8-all stage artifact is the packing/parity precedent and the staged-chain anchor int4 artifacts sit alongside.
- A_FMT_W (franken_nlp-rsk): the .fnlpq writer must carry per-group scales/allocation tables and the canonical nibble order.
- [P3] scalar reference kernels + i64 oracle (franken_nlp-9tn): every bounds memo and exactness gate here is proved against that oracle.
- [P3] canonical quant algebra (franken_nlp-8lu): the XOR-0x80 offset domain, row-sum correction, and scale-application epilogue the unpack+MAC path reuses.
- [P3] dispatch-table framework (franken_nlp-pwu): int4 tier variants register as measured dispatch candidates with forced-path proof runs.
- Per-tier wants (not blocking edges): the proven int8 MAC tiers themselves — AVX2 X3a franken_nlp-fms / X3b franken_nlp-3am, VNNI franken_nlp-gzh, NEON franken_nlp-hpt, autovec franken_nlp-g2n — each tier's int4 unpack variant lands only after that tier's int8 exactness gate is green; a tier missing at the time simply has no int4 variant yet.

title: [P5] Run AA-Q1 joint bit allocation under footprint budget
description:
## Background
AA-Q1 (joint rate-distortion bit allocation): with int4 baselines shipped, each tensor of the wedge model (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752) can choose its own precision under a footprint budget. Because each physical layer executes in BOTH loops, a tensor's quantization error propagates twice through different contexts — sensitivity is JOINT, not separable.

## Contract
- **Choice set per tensor:** {bf16, int8, int4-g32, int4-g16} under an explicit footprint byte budget, optimized against held-out task metrics.
- **One-at-a-time sensitivity curves only SEED the search** — loop reuse and cross-tensor interactions make separable water-filling a heuristic, never a conclusion.
- **Complete candidate artifacts are evaluated end-to-end** (development-set search first, then full candidate artifacts on disjoint calibration/test) — never a per-tensor proxy alone.
- **Gates:** exact footprint accounting; mean error PLUS the mean loss among the worst 10% of documents (upper-tail CVaR at confidence 0.90); repeated-seed stability of the search outcome.
- **Allocation table + provenance recorded in the .fnlpq artifact** (which tensor got which representation, and why — search manifest digest).
- **No claim of global optimality without a valid dual bound.** Absent a bound, the claim is "best found under budget X with search budget Y".
- Fallback: the best UNIFORM recipe inside the same byte budget.

## Constraints
Alien-artifact contract: EV=(Impact×Confidence×Reuse)/(Effort×AdoptionFriction) ≥ 2 to enter implementation; fixed search/profile budget declared before execution — exhaustion means no promotion, never a best-so-far default; evidence dir carries env.json, manifest.json, repro.lock (+ LEGAL.md if external IP informed the work). Quantization stages are immutable artifacts; rollback = activating a prior artifact. Preregistered budgets on locked data; mean metrics stay visible. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon.

## Evidence / gates
- Search manifest (candidate space, budget, seeds) frozen before running; repeated-seed stability rows published.
- Candidate-vs-uniform paired comparison on locked calibration/test with confidence intervals; footprint bytes exact per candidate.
- Allocation table digest present in the shipped .fnlpq; recommendation record with hotspot evidence, EV factors, interaction matrix, rollback command.

## Tests
- Unit: budget accounting arithmetic (checked; bytes per representation per tensor); allocation-table serialization round-trip.
- Property: any generated candidate respects the byte budget exactly; allocation table ↔ artifact contents consistency validator.
- E2E (model-gated, SKIPPED_NO_MODEL): build one small-budget candidate end-to-end, evaluate on the locked split harness, verify CVaR@0.90 + mean gates computed as specified; detailed logging of search trajectory, seeds, and per-candidate metrics.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P5] int4 per-group quantization: the int4-g32/int4-g16 representations are choice-set members and their proofs must exist first.
- wants A_EVALFW: held-out task metrics, locked splits, and paired-comparison machinery come from the eval framework.

title: [P5] Enforce AA-T1 tail-aware quality gate (CVaR only)
description:
## Background
AA-T1 (tail-aware quality gate): quantized recipes for the wedge model (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752) can look fine on mean metrics while quietly destroying the worst documents. The tail gate makes that failure mode a first-class release blocker without importing a zoo of tail statistics.

## Contract
- **CVaR is the ONLY tail objective** for per-document quality loss. Do not stack EVT/large-deviation/e-process terminology on the same quantity — redundant tail methods are forbidden (no subsystem composes more than three mathematical families without a written compatibility review; here the answer is one).
- **Preregister before measuring:** α (the tail confidence level, e.g. CVaR@0.90 = mean loss among the worst 10%), the per-document loss definition, the grouping/unit of analysis, the bootstrap interval procedure, minimum subgroup sizes, and the paired candidate-vs-baseline test on locked data.
- **Mean metrics remain visible** alongside every tail number so a tail win cannot hide a broad regression (and vice versa).
- **Deterministic fallback** when a candidate fails the tail gate: keep the uniform recipe, or promote the offending tensors one precision tier.
- The gate integrates with AA-Q1 candidate evaluation (its CVaR@0.90 gate) and with release scorecards: a recipe that fails preregistered tail budgets does not ship as default.

## Constraints
Use CVaR alone for quality-tail optimization (Alien-Artifact contract; "alien" means rigorous evidence, not elaborate vocabulary). Preregistered point estimates and confidence intervals on locked data; no post-hoc α shopping. Quality regressions gate releases at the same rank as parity regressions. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite.

## Evidence / gates
- Preregistration record (α, loss, grouping, bootstrap recipe, subgroup minima) committed BEFORE the first gated measurement; any change is a new preregistration.
- Paired candidate/baseline tail + mean rows on locked data with bootstrap intervals, published in the perf/quality ledger; failing candidates recorded with their fallback disposition.

## Tests
- Unit: CVaR estimator on hand-computed small samples (exact enumeration goldens); bootstrap interval reproducibility under fixed seed.
- Property: CVaR@α ≥ mean for loss distributions (sanity invariants); subgroup-minimum enforcement refuses under-sized groups with a typed INSUFFICIENT_DATA-style result rather than a silent estimate.
- E2E: run the gate over a synthetic per-document loss table with a planted heavy tail; verify gate fires, mean stays visible, fallback disposition recorded; detailed logging of α, n, tail set membership, and interval endpoints. Model-dependent loss production is SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without an artifact.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P5] AA-Q1 joint bit allocation (loose): Q1 is the primary consumer — the gate's preregistered CVaR@0.90 evaluates Q1 candidates; building the gate against Q1's candidate stream keeps the two consistent.

title: [P5] Build AA-U1 calibration and uncertainty layer
description:
## Background
AA-U1 (task uncertainty) / §7.8: raw logprobs from the wedge model (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752) are NOT confidence claims. Calibration is product semantics — the substrate for abstention, selective automation, and the user-owned `calibrate` surface — not kernel control.

## Contract
- **Split discipline:** every calibrated task has disjoint development, calibration, and locked-test ids. Temperature/isotonic parameters fit ONLY on calibration data; ECE/Brier/selective-risk are reported ONLY on the locked test.
- **Conformal methods** (abstention/prediction sets) are used only where the exchangeability/unit-of-analysis assumptions are WRITTEN and checked, with a NAMED population; coverage is stated for that dataset/population and finite sample — never universally. No e-process ornament.
- **Artifact keying:** recipe, prompt, label set, thinking/numerics mode, calibration digest, and validity date key the calibration artifact (all deriving from the one ExecutionIdentity).
- **Shift handling:** distribution shift invalidates the coverage claim and falls back to raw scores labeled `uncalibrated` or to conservative abstention — NEVER silent extrapolation. Shift indicators and validity/expiry conditions are named in the artifact.
- **Abstention semantics:** calibrated abstention is a SUCCESSFUL typed result — exit 0 with `status:"abstained"`; exit 10 remains reserved for executions that cannot produce a valid task result at all.

## Constraints
Constraint pressure is not confidence (legal-mass/margin diagnostics cannot authorize acceptance without task-specific calibration). A sample is not authority by itself. Reliability claims name dataset, prompt hash, recipe id, thinking mode. Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon. No online learning; refitting is an explicit, versioned event.

## Evidence / gates
- Phase-5 exit contribution: calibration validity/coverage measured and scoped per task; reliability/ECE/Brier/selective-risk rows on locked tests with confidence intervals published per calibrated task.
- Exchangeability memo per conformal use (written assumption + named population) archived with the artifact; absent memo = no conformal claim.
- Shift-invalidation fixture: a deliberately shifted eval stream flips output labeling to `uncalibrated`/conservative abstention.

## Tests
- Unit: temperature/isotonic fitting on synthetic distributions with known answers; ECE/Brier arithmetic against hand-computed goldens; artifact key derivation.
- Property: fit never touches test ids (split-leak detector); prediction-set coverage on synthetic exchangeable data within tolerance of nominal.
- E2E: calibrate a toy task end-to-end (dev/cal/test), verify locked-test-only reporting and validity-date/shift behavior; detailed logging of split digests, fitted parameters, coverage computations. Model-gated runs SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- wants A_EVALFW: locked splits, dataset registry, and metric harness are eval-framework machinery this calibration layer builds on.
- This bead IS anchor A_CAL: downstream consumers (eval/calibrate/qualify CLI, DecisionPolicy, verify-semantic, P6 registry closure) hang off it.

title: [P5] Ship user-owned fnlp eval/calibrate/qualify
description:
## Background
Assay becomes a USER surface: `fnlp eval`, `fnlp calibrate`, `fnlp qualify`. Users of the wedge model (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 explicit; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752) need to prove a candidate artifact/recipe is good enough on THEIR data before activating it — without their scorecards ever becoming universal project claims.

## Contract
- **`fnlp eval`:** consumes versioned task-shaped NDJSON and emits the same digest-bound metrics the project uses internally (dataset digest, split ids, recipe id, prompt hash, thinking mode on every scorecard).
- **`fnlp calibrate`:** requires a disjoint calibration split (refuses overlapping ids); produces the §7.8/AA-U1 calibration artifact keyed by recipe/prompt/labels/mode/digest/validity date.
- **`fnlp qualify`:** paired candidate-vs-active replay under CALLER-DECLARED gates; writes a receipt scoped to host + dataset + config (never a portable universal certificate).
- **`fnlp models activate --require-qualification`:** accepts ONLY an exact matching receipt (same host/dataset/config scope, same digests); the previous content-addressed configuration remains available — installation and activation are distinct; rollback is activation of the prior artifact.
- **Refusals:** dataset overlap/duplicate detection between splits; tiny samples return `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` (typed, never a confident number); stale-digest substitution (metrics computed against bytes that no longer match the declared digest) is rejected.
- User corrections enter only an explicitly named local suite; a user scorecard is never promoted into a universal project claim.

## Constraints
G8 typed results; abstention/refusal semantics per §8.5 (INSUFFICIENT_DATA is a typed successful refusal, not a fake metric). Receipts follow the .fnlpr completeness grades (Replayable / StructuralReplay / VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied / AuditOnly); exported receipts never expose raw SHA-256 of private/low-entropy content (per-receipt HMAC commitment or omitted identity with lower grade). Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; stdout data/stderr diagnostics; robot NDJSON versioned.

## Evidence / gates
- Phase-5 exit contribution: qualification receipts and stale-digest rejection PROVEN; activation rollback tested.
- Frozen robot-schema coverage for eval/calibrate/qualify events; golden scorecard fixtures.
- Overlap/duplicate/tiny-sample/stale-digest negative fixtures all pass.

## Tests
- Unit: NDJSON task-shape validation; gate declaration parsing; receipt scope fields.
- Property/fuzz: malformed eval NDJSON → typed errors, never partial scorecards; split-overlap detector catches planted duplicates (including near-duplicate ids).
- E2E: full loop — eval a candidate, calibrate, qualify candidate-vs-active, activate --require-qualification, roll back; verify receipt scope matching rejects a receipt from a different host/dataset/config; detailed logging of digests, gate evaluations, receipt ids. Model-gated runs SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_assay_qualify_cycle.sh`: the full loop plus every refusal fixture (split overlap, tiny-sample INSUFFICIENT_DATA, stale digest, foreign-scope receipt), one machine-parseable row per phase (digests, gate verdicts, receipt id, exit code), SKIPPED_NO_MODEL explicit.

## Dependencies & rationale
- Depends on [P5] AA-U1 calibration: `calibrate` is the user-facing wrapper over that machinery, and `qualify` consumes its validity semantics.
- wants A_TASKCORE: evaluated/qualified subjects are the task surfaces; task envelopes and identity plumbing come from the task core.

title: [P5] Implement offline DecisionPolicy and review spill
description:
## Background
