Deliver `scripts/fetch_model.sh` (Unix) and `scripts/fetch_model.ps1` (Windows), human-run, out-of-band. Because they are explicit provisioning tools (not inference/library code), they MAY use system `curl` / PowerShell web APIs.
- Default destinations (revision-scoped): Unix `${HOME}/.cache/franken_nlp/source/Nanbeige4.2-3B/f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d/`; Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\franken_nlp\source\Nanbeige4.2-3B\f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d\`.
- Every URL is `https://huggingface.co/Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B/resolve/<immutable-revision>/<canonical-filename>`; follow redirects under a pinned credential/host policy; honor `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`; retry transient failures.
- Destination must be an owner-controlled, non-shared directory on ONE filesystem. One revision lock guards the closure.
- Resume: each `.partial` is exclusively created as a regular file (never symlink/reparse/device); resume allowed ONLY when a side journal binds exact URL + revision + name + length + digest to that secure partial. Verify exact length AND SHA-256, sync, then same-directory rename.
- `--check-only` (`-CheckOnly` on Windows) fully REHASHES the existing closure from the revision-scoped directory; "file exists" or "size matches" alone is never a cache hit.
- Per-file progress + operator guidance (binding UX contract): every file logs a start line (name, expected bytes, URL), periodic progress lines (bytes-so-far / expected), and a completion line with observed length + SHA-256; on ANY interruption or failure the script prints the EXACT resume instruction — the verbatim re-invocation command with the same `--dest` — plus the journal path and a note that the journal makes the retry resume rather than restart. Documented exit-code contract (both scripts): 0 = complete/verified; 1 = digest/length verification failure (names file + expected + observed); 2 = usage/flag error; 3 = network failure after retries (names URL + attempt count); 4 = preflight refusal (insufficient disk; prints needed vs available bytes).
- Invalid old files are QUARANTINED with their observed digest recorded (e.g. moved to a `quarantine/` sibling with a journal entry), never silently overwritten. Deleting them is forbidden.
- Non-default `--revision` requires an explicit flag, labels the download untrusted until a new truth-pack revision is reviewed, and cannot reuse the default recipe/catalog identity.
- Preflight computes PEAK free space (source closure + staging + journals + margin), repeated before work; no hard-coded "10 GB should be enough".

title: [P-1] Measure oracle nondeterminism floor (>=5 processes x >=2 thread counts)
description:
## Background
Before any tolerance can be honest, the oracle's OWN nondeterminism must be measured. Every L1–L4 float tolerance for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops → 44 KV slots; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144) is derived from this floor — never invented, never inherited from prose (OQ-14).

## Contract
Measure the pinned CPU oracle's nondeterminism floor:
- At least FIVE independently launched processes (fresh interpreter each; never five loops in one process) at EACH of at least TWO preregistered thread counts (e.g. 1 and a preregistered multi-thread value; the exact pair is preregistered before running).
- Per run capture: logits for the fixture prompts, per-(loop,layer) taps where cheap, greedy token streams, and the full env/thread record.
- Compute per-metric variance/max-abs spread across runs. If ANYTHING varies: apply the preregistered additional-repetition/convergence rule to bound its confidence interval and identify the exact stable prefix; freeze ONLY the stable prefix as exact goldens. No tolerance distribution is ever derived from two observations; no unstable suffix is promoted as an exact golden.
- Output `docs/truth-pack/oracle_floor.json`: per-metric (logit max-abs, per-tap spreads, first-divergence token position per prompt, per thread count) measured floor + the derived tolerance vectors that L1/L2/L3 gates will consume, each tagged with the run count that produced it.

## Constraints
Tolerances derive from MEASURED variance only (G1>G2; profile-scoped fidelity: this floor is the hf-bf16-eager authority; the separately recorded SDPA variance run may not redefine eager semantics). Preregistration (thread counts, repetition rule, convergence criterion) is committed BEFORE the measurement runs. Determinism is scoped: cross-machine float byte identity is never implied.

## Evidence / gates
Phase −1 exit: "OQ-14's oracle floor is measured". The L4 gate's "oracle-reproducible prefix" is DEFINED by this artifact (the exact stable prefix per prompt). Downstream L1/L3 tolerance vectors cite oracle_floor.json by digest.

## Tests
(1) Model-gated measurement campaign (SKIPPED_NO_MODEL otherwise): ≥5 processes × ≥2 thread counts complete; artifact records run count, thread counts, and per-metric spread. (2) Analysis unit tests on synthetic run data: identical runs → zero floor; injected divergence at token k → stable prefix = k, unstable suffix excluded from goldens; two-observation input → analysis refuses (guard against the never-from-two rule). (3) Preregistration check: thread counts and repetition rule file committed before result files (CI compares timestamps/ordering in the artifact). Logging: per-run digests, per-metric tables, first-divergence positions. Runnable artifact: `scripts/measure_oracle_floor.py` (campaign runner + analysis) — `--analyze-only` re-runs the analysis over recorded run files; `--self-test` exercises the synthetic-data unit tests (2) including the two-observation refusal, model-free. Logging: stderr, per-run start/end timestamps + env/thread record, final `ORACLE_FLOOR RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL runs=<n> thread_counts=<list>` line; a preregistration-ordering failure (3) names the out-of-order file.

## Dependencies & rationale
- oracle-closure bead: the floor is a property of the exact frozen environment; measuring before the closure locks would produce unusable numbers.

title: [P-1] Generate profile-tagged reference fixtures (hf-bf16-eager, diagnostic-f32, sdpa variance)
description:
## Background
The profile-tagged reference fixtures are the frozen ground truth every Rust parity gate (L0–L4) compares against, for Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22×2 loops → 44 KV slots layer+loop×22; final RMSNorm after each pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Fidelity claims are profile-scoped: hf-bf16-eager owns HF-match claims; diagnostic-f32 is the structural bisect oracle (not required to token-match bf16); hf-bf16-sdpa exists only to measure backend variance.

## Contract
Run `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures.py` in the locked oracle closure and commit the fixture corpus under tests/fixtures/ + docs/truth-pack/:
- Numerics matrix: hf-bf16-eager AND diagnostic-f32 fixture sets; plus a separately recorded hf-bf16-sdpa VARIANCE run (may not redefine eager semantics). EVERY fixture names its dtype and attention backend.
- Per-execution traces via the trace harness: post-embed; per (loop, layer) for all 44 executions; BOTH post-loop norms; pre-lm_head; logits.
- Prefill → decode KV-append traces for all 44 slots.
- Greedy token streams for the golden prompt corpus (frozen only on the oracle-stable prefix per the measured floor).
- Template renderings across the full mode matrix (thinking on/off, preserve_thinking, tools xml/json, system default text, media reminders).
- Tokenizer id sequences over the multilingual/code/special adversarial corpus (slow SentencePiece reference, use_fast=False).
- Sampled streams at fixed seeds where reproducible (distributional reference only).
Every fixture file carries: profile tag, oracle closure digest, generator commit, prompt/corpus digest, and generation command.

## Constraints
Raw floating fixture digests are never presented as portable cross-host proof. Greedy exactness fixtures freeze only the measured-stable prefix. Product default is greedy; the sampled fixtures never become parity gates. Fixture corpora are repo-authored or redistribution-safe; tokenizer/template fixtures embed no third-party licensed text.

## Evidence / gates
Phase −1 exit: "capture smoke fixtures (greedy streams, per-(loop,layer) dumps, both post-loop norms, KV appends, template renderings, tokenizer corpora)" + "profile-tagged traces green". These fixtures are the comparison surface for Phase 1 L0–L4, the G0 tokenizer/template spike, and the P2 conversion smoke checks.

## Tests
(1) Model-gated generation run (SKIPPED_NO_MODEL otherwise) with a manifest listing every fixture + digest. (2) Completeness assertions: 44 (loop,layer) taps + 2 norm states per traced prompt; each fixture tagged with profile+backend; sdpa files tagged variance-only. (3) Loader round-trip: fixture reader parses every committed file; unknown profile tag rejects. (4) Consistency: greedy stream prefix agrees with the floor artifact's stable-prefix length per prompt. Logging: fixture inventory table (name, profile, bytes, digest). Runnable artifact: `scripts/gen_reference_fixtures.py` is the generator; `--verify` re-hashes every committed fixture against the manifest and runs completeness/round-trip/consistency checks (2)–(4) WITHOUT the model (always runnable in CI); full generation is the model-gated path. Logging: stderr, per-fixture timestamps, final `REF_FIXTURES RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_MODEL fixtures=<n> missing=<list>` line; verification failures print fixture name + expected-vs-observed digest.

## Dependencies & rationale
- oracle-closure bead: fixtures are meaningless before the environment closure is frozen.
- trace-harness bead: the 44-tap/KV-append captures and the no-perturbation guarantee come from it.
- (soft) floor-measurement bead: stable-prefix freezing consumes the measured floor; generation may start earlier but goldens freeze only after the floor exists.

title: [P-1] Census TokenizerSpecialIds + TemplateControlIds registries (forbidden set = template controls)
description:
## Background
Two token registries are normative for Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (vocab 166,144; bos 166100, eos 166101, pad 0; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128). The untrusted-document boundary (doctrine #22) and the reasoning/tool parsers depend on getting this exactly right: at the pinned revision the think/tool markers carry `special=false`, so generic `skip_special_tokens` handling can NEVER be the containment authority (OQ-20).

## Contract
Deliver two censused registries as committed truth-pack artifacts (canonical JSON) + their generator:
- `TokenizerSpecialIds`: every id whose tokenizer metadata says `special=true` — `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, end-of-text, and the base special pieces — with id, surface string, source file (tokenizer_config.json 10,990 B / special_tokens_map.json 623 B / added_tokens.json 174 B, digests per the conversion manifest), and the metadata line that proves the flag.
- `TemplateControlIds`: a SUPERSET registry additionally containing every template-significant added token — `<think>`, `</think>`, `<tool_call>`, `</tool_call>` — which are `special=false` AT THE PIN [OBSERVED@pin], each with id, surface, and the template/config evidence line.
Normative statement embedded in both artifacts and the docs: the FORBIDDEN set for untrusted-document encoding is the complete TemplateControlIds census, never the tokenizer special flag. An untrusted segment must decode to the original bytes while excluding every TemplateControlIds member, or reject.

## Constraints
Registry content is extracted from the pinned files by tool, never hand-typed; every entry carries file+line/JSON-path evidence. The registries are the SINGLE source consumed later by tokenizer/specials.rs and the UntrustedDocument encoder — no parallel hand-maintained lists. License Apache-2.0 settled; tokenizer bytes embedded later carry attribution.

## Evidence / gates
OQ-20 promotion (registry completeness) and the Phase −1 exit item "census TokenizerSpecialIds and the complete TemplateControlIds registry". Phase 1's L0/untrusted-encoder work and Phase 4B's injection gates cite these artifacts by digest. Gate: generator replay from the pinned tokenizer files reproduces the committed registries byte-identically.

## Tests
(1) Generator replay test: byte-identical regeneration from the pinned source files. (2) Content assertions: think/tool markers present in TemplateControlIds with special=false provenance; im_start/im_end present in BOTH registries; TokenizerSpecialIds ⊂ TemplateControlIds; bos=166100/eos=166101/pad=0 recorded. (3) Negative: a synthetic tokenizer_config with a new added token missing from the registry fails the completeness check. (4) Docs lint: any doc/text claiming "skip_special_tokens" as the boundary authority fails a grep-based policy test. Logging: per-entry id/surface/source-evidence table. Runnable artifact: the generator is `scripts/gen_token_registries.py` — `--check` re-extracts from the pinned files and byte-compares against the committed registries (test 1); `--self-test` runs assertions (2)–(4) hermetically. Logging: stderr, per-step timestamps, final `TOKEN_REGISTRIES RESULT=PASS|FAIL specials=<n> controls=<n> drift=<none|file>` line; failures print the exact missing/extra entry with its source-evidence path.

## Dependencies & rationale
- fetch-scripts bead (franken_nlp-mzr): the registry generator extracts from the locally fetched pinned tokenizer files (tokenizer_config.json 10,990 B / special_tokens_map.json 623 B / added_tokens.json 174 B), acquired and digest-verified by scripts/fetch_model.sh; generating the NORMATIVE forbidden-set registries from unverified bytes would launder drift into the untrusted-document boundary. The conversion-source manifest pins the same digests in parallel — CI cross-checks both.

title: [P-1] Archive complete chat-message AST + template mode matrix (OQ-7)
description:
## Background
`fnlp` implements the pinned chat template as ONE FIXED PROGRAM, not a Jinja interpreter, for Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (vocab 166,144; `<|im_start|>`/`<|im_end|>`, `<think>`/`</think>`, enable_thinking default ON, preserve_thinking, XML/JSON tool branches; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128). ## Contract
Archive `docs/truth-pack/chat_ast.json` (+ prose spec) materializing the full pinned branch surface of the template in tokenizer_config.json (10,990 B, digest 3edfa64a0826a77e9412b9008f1febf3fe906a68fd616b6de4cd15897a8c8518):
- Roles: `system|user|assistant|tool`; first-position system enforcement and the EXACT default system text bytes when absent.
- Content forms: plain string AND iterable content parts; every accepted part kind; the EXACT media-reminder rendering per media part kind.
- Assistant `reasoning_content`; embedded `<think>` extraction; `preserve_thinking` semantics (prior-turn thinking kept vs stripped).
- Tool branches: JSON and XML tool-call serialization forms; tool role results; CONSECUTIVE tool-result grouping rules.
- The exact generation suffix appended for generation prompts (including thinking-mode variants).
- Rejection surface: unknown roles, mapping shapes, part kinds, malformed tool-call structures — enumerated as MUST-REJECT-BEFORE-TOKENIZATION cases.
Each AST node/branch carries the template source span (line/offset in the pinned template string) proving it. Companion: the mode matrix enumeration (thinking on/off × preserve on/off × tools none/xml/json × content string/parts × system present/absent/default) used by the fixtures bead.

## Constraints
The archive documents the PINNED template only; no generalization to a template language. Byte exactness matters: default system text, whitespace, and suffixes are recorded as exact bytes, not prose. Unknown forms are rejection cases, not "best effort".

## Evidence / gates
OQ-7 promotion: the complete accepted AST/mode matrix archived. Phase 1 template builder (L0 exact) and the Phase −1 template-rendering fixtures both cite this artifact; the template-rendering portion of OQ-10 (tool-call RENDERING, not parsing) is evidenced here to the extent Phase 1 requires.

## Tests
(1) Span-replay validator: every AST branch's quoted template span matches the pinned template bytes (re-extracted from the archived tokenizer_config.json). (2) Coverage assertion: every `if`/branch construct in the pinned template string maps to ≥1 AST node or an explicit exclusion entry — no unmapped branch. (3) Cross-check: the mode matrix enumerates every combination the fixtures bead renders; missing combination fails. (4) Negative: the MUST-REJECT list is nonempty and includes unknown-role/unknown-part/malformed-tool-call cases. Logging: branch → span → AST-node mapping table. Runnable artifact: all four checks ship as `scripts/validate_chat_ast.py` (truth-pack tooling, runnable by hand and in Phase −1 CI), logging per-check timestamps to stderr and ending with one machine-parseable line `CHAT_AST RESULT=PASS|FAIL checks=<n> failures=<list>`; on failure it prints the offending branch id, the quoted template span, and expected-vs-actual bytes.

Oracle-rendered confirmations arrive with the fixtures bead, which depends on this archive's matrix.

title: [P-1] Record benchmark source conflicts (HMMT 82.8 vs 82.1) and promote OQ-1..9/16/25
description:
## Background
The truth pack never silently selects the most favorable number, and no [OBSERVED@pin] claim may drive Phase 1–2 implementation without promotion. title: [P0] Enforce unsafe-code lint policy: deny defaults, enumerated islands, policy test
description:
## Background
Memory-safety governance for the franken_nlp crate (one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops → 44 KV slots; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144). The only unsafe code this project will ever hold is enumerated SIMD islands and the opt-in mmap island; policy must make any other unsafe a build failure, not a review nit.

## Contract
- `Cargo.toml` `[lints.rust]`: `unsafe_code = "deny"` AND `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "deny"`.
- Crate roots additionally carry `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` — deliberately `deny`, NOT `forbid` (forbid cannot be locally overridden by the enumerated islands).
- Enumerated island policy: only listed SIMD modules (future kernels under native_engine/) and the opt-in mmap module (artifact/weights mmap island) may opt into scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`. Islands NEVER allow `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn`, so every unsafe operation stays inside an explicit `unsafe {}` block with a local `// SAFETY:` proof comment.
- Policy test (compile-time + source-scan): parses the source tree; FAILS on (a) any `#![allow(unsafe_code)]`/`#[allow(unsafe_code)]` in a module not on the checked-in island allowlist, (b) any allow of `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` anywhere, (c) any other lint relaxation of the two governed lints, (d) an `unsafe` block without an adjacent `// SAFETY:` comment inside an island.
- The island allowlist is a committed data file the policy test reads; adding an island is a diffable event.

## Constraints
Deny-not-forbid unsafe (doctrine/toolchain rule). NUMA/huge-page/topology/QoS experiments are NOT permission for new unsafe islands — they need a ratified safe FrankenSuite surface or stay off. Integer kernels differential-test against scalar/i64; mmap gets separate range/lifetime/immutability tests (later phases; the policy test only enforces the lint structure now).

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: deny-by-default unsafe policy in place; the policy test runs inside scripts/check.sh. Every later kernel bead inherits this gate — an unlisted island fails CI before review.

## Tests

title: [P0] Pin exact dated nightly toolchain + CI rustc/LLVM/target-feature recording

The toolchain pin for franken_nlp (one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). title: [P0] Build SUITE.lock + SUITE_ROOT_PATCHES.lock generation and check tooling
description:
## Background
Reproducibility plumbing for franken_nlp's pinned FrankenSuite universe (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). The trap this bead exists to close: **Cargo does not inherit a dependency repository's root `[patch]` entries** — the pinned frankentorch root carries a `[patch.crates-io]` entry for `block` that would silently VANISH when frankentorch is consumed by Git revision, changing the effective build.

## Contract
- `SUITE.lock`: generated, checked manifest recording every pinned FrankenSuite dependency (ft-kernel-cpu, ft-core, ft-serialize, asupersync with only the runtime/network/TLS features actually used, optional fsqlite/fsqlite-types) with exact immutable Git revision, selected features, and source identity. Floating `0.3.x` prose is not reproducibility.
- `SUITE_ROOT_PATCHES.lock`: generated closure of every root-level `[patch]`/source replacement in the pinned suite repositories that is RELEVANT to the actually selected release feature graph. Tooling must: compute the selected feature graph; determine which reviewed root patches are relevant (the frankentorch `block` patch is the known live example); mirror required patches into the franken_nlp root manifest at exact revisions; REFUSE irrelevant or stale copies; and fail CI when a pinned suite root changes its patch closure without a plan revision.
- Cross-checks: the generated locks are verified against `cargo metadata`, `cargo tree -e features`, `Cargo.lock`, and the root `Cargo.toml`; `Cargo.lock` and `SUITE.lock` must agree.
- Developer overrides: local /dp or ~/projects checkouts selectable only through an UNTRACKED override file; a preflight refuses the override unless its HEAD equals the reviewed pin. No absolute/local path in any committed manifest.
- Deliver the generator + checker as repo tooling (invoked from scripts/check.sh), plus the two committed lock files.

## Constraints
Committed public manifest uses immutable git+rev so a fresh clone builds without sibling directories. Mirror ONLY feature-graph-relevant patches — an irrelevant mirrored patch is a refused error, not harmless noise. Adopting any asupersync-workspace substrate crate (franken_kernel/franken_evidence/franken_decision/frankenlab) is an explicit SUITE.lock decision recorded via the OQ-35 census, never a silent import.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: checked suite-pin manifest in place; Cargo.lock/SUITE.lock agreement enforced in CI. The G0 probes and all later kernel work build against exactly these pins.

## Tests
(1) Generator determinism: two runs produce byte-identical locks. (2) Agreement test: revision/feature drift between Cargo.lock and SUITE.lock fails with a named diff. (3) Patch-closure tests: fixture suite root with a relevant patch → mirrored; irrelevant patch mirrored in root → refused; suite root patch closure changed vs recorded → CI fail. (4) Override preflight: override pointing at wrong-HEAD checkout refused with expected/observed revisions. (5) Path lint: committed manifests contain no absolute/local paths. Logging: full computed feature graph + patch relevance verdict per patch. Named artifacts: `scripts/check_suite_lock.sh` (wraps the generator in --check mode; the scripts/check.sh section) plus `tests/suite_lock.rs` covering cases (1)–(5); each run logs per-check timestamps and ends with `SUITE_LOCK RESULT=PASS|FAIL drift=<none|summary>`; agreement failures print the exact revision/feature diff lines.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: locks/tooling operate on the crate manifest and pinned deps introduced there.
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract test target (suite_lock) fully green in the no-fail-fast suite run (23 targets, 18 green); per-bead evidence per close policy

title: [P0] Add dependency-policy test: three-family allowlist + no-Rayon release graph
description:
## Background
The dependency perimeter of franken_nlp (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144) is deliberately tiny and machine-enforced: three non-suite families + pinned FrankenSuite, and Rayon banned from the ENTIRE release graph because it would create a second ambient scheduler beside asupersync.

## Contract
A dependency-policy test (runs in scripts/check.sh) that:
- Parses `Cargo.lock` + `cargo metadata` and FAILS if any new DIRECT non-suite root appears beyond exactly: `clap` (CLI parsing only), `serde`+`serde_json` (typed API/NDJSON/schema/manifest data only), `sha2` (SHA-256 integrity, canonical ids, HMAC-SHA-256 pseudonym primitive) — plus the pinned FrankenSuite surfaces (ft-kernel-cpu, ft-core, ft-serialize, asupersync, optional fsqlite/fsqlite-types).
- Explicitly asserts the named forbidden crates never appear as direct deps: thiserror, anyhow, ctrlc, rayon, half, memmap2, uuid, num_cpus, any allocator crate, tokenizers, tiktoken, minijinja, llguidance, rusqlite, reqwest, hyper.
- **Rayon assertion is graph-wide, not direct-only**: `cargo tree` (and metadata graph walk) over the RELEASE feature graph must contain no `rayon`/`rayon-core` node anywhere — transitive included. (At the pins: asupersync's Rayon entry is dev-only; ft-kernel-cpu's unconditional Rayon is exactly what the no-Rayon leaf surface work must eliminate — until then this test documents/blocks the release graph state.)
- Records transitive deps selected by the pinned suite + three roots into a supply-chain manifest (committed, diffed) — recorded is NOT permission to depend on them directly.
- Benchmark/oracle tooling stays outside the release dependency graph (test asserts release graph only; dev-deps are separately listed).

## Constraints
Adding a fourth family requires explicit owner approval AND a plan revision — a written justification alone is insufficient; the test has no bypass flag. Typed errors use std. Networked code is asupersync-only (tls-webpki-roots); no reqwest/hyper ever.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit + permanent CI gate: allowlist test green; no-Rayon release-graph assertion green (or, until the frankentorch no-Rayon leaf surface lands, the test pins the exact current violation as a known-blocked entry that FAILS release builds — never silently passes).

## Tests
(1) Happy path: current graph passes with the supply-chain manifest byte-stable. (2) Negative fixtures (synthetic metadata JSON): new direct root → fail naming crate; rayon appearing transitively in release graph → fail with the full dependency path printed; forbidden crate as direct dep → fail. (3) Dev-vs-release split: a dev-only dependency does not trip the release assertions. Logging: full direct-root inventory + rayon search path trace per run. Named artifact: `tests/dependency_policy.rs` (cargo test, invoked via scripts/check.sh) with the synthetic negative fixtures as in-test JSON documents; on failure it prints the offending crate and the full dependency path, ending with `DEP_POLICY RESULT=PASS|FAIL violation=<crate|none>` on stderr.

title: [P0] Create scripts/check.sh single CI entrypoint (fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, doc links, UBS)
description:
## Background
One CI entrypoint for franken_nlp (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). Once the crate exists, `cargo test --locked` is a hard green-bar gate; CI invokes `scripts/check.sh` as its SINGLE test step, and the Phase-2 batch-verify swarm loop runs the same script centrally.

## Contract
`scripts/check.sh` runs, in order, failing fast with clear sectioned output:
1. `cargo fmt --check`
2. `cargo check --locked --all-targets` (and greps its output to FAIL on any "present in multiple build targets" warning)
3. `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
4. `cargo test --locked`
5. Doc-link validators: every intra-repo markdown link and every plan/docs cross-reference (docs/*.md, README) resolves; dead links fail with file:line.
6. Bounded UBS: `ubs --diff` (working tree) with a documented time bound; UBS exit >0 fails the script. Gracefully SKIP with a loud notice when the `ubs` binary is absent (CI records SKIPPED_NO_UBS rather than fake-passing).
7. The policy tests wired by sibling beads as they land (lint policy, dependency policy, suite-lock agreement, toolchain expectation) — check.sh is their single execution home.
Also: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` invokes exactly `scripts/check.sh`; the script is POSIX-sh/bash clean, honors `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, prints per-section wall-clock timing and a final machine-parseable summary line per section (`CHECK section=<name> result=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_<REASON> time_s=<t>`), and exits nonzero if any section failed.

## Constraints
Never create a fake empty crate to manufacture a green bar (crate exists from the scaffold bead). Model-gated tests report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL, not pass. Builds may route through rch when available but the script must not require it. No section may be silently skipped — every skip is a named, logged state.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: CI runs check.sh green on the scaffold; the script is the Mandatory-Checks authority (AGENTS.md) and the Phase-2 batch-verify entrypoint for the implementation swarm.

## Tests
(1) e2e: check.sh exits 0 on the clean scaffold; each section's PASS line present. (2) Negative: introduce a fmt violation in a temp copy → section 1 fails, later sections not run (fail-fast) with correct exit code; a broken doc link fixture → section 5 fails with file:line. (3) Skip semantics: PATH without ubs → SKIPPED_NO_UBS logged, script still enforces sections 1–5. (4) Warning grep: a fixture cargo-output containing the multiple-build-targets warning fails section 2. Logging: per-section timing + verdict summary block. Named artifact: the negative/skip/warning-grep cases (2)–(4) live in `scripts/test_check.sh`, which runs check.sh against scratch fixture trees and asserts both the exit codes and the machine-parseable section lines; it ends with `CHECK_SELFTEST RESULT=PASS|FAIL cases=<n>`.

title: [P0] Implement duplicate-key-rejecting canonical JSON primitives
description:
## Background
Canonical JSON primitives for franken_nlp (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). Duplicate-key JSON is an attack/ambiguity vector at every boundary (manifests, NDJSON, schemas, receipts), and canonical bytes are load-bearing: digests (ExecutionIdentity projections, manifest hashes, golden fixtures) are computed over them. serde_json alone silently last-wins on duplicate keys — unacceptable.

## Contract
A small module (e.g. src/canonjson.rs or textutil-adjacent, name per tree conventions) providing:
- **Rejecting parse layer**: a serde_json-based entry (custom Visitor/Value construction) that REJECTS duplicate object keys at ANY depth with a typed error naming the JSON path. This layer is mandatory at every parser boundary in the crate: manifests, NDJSON requests, schema inputs, config snapshots, robot echo — direct `serde_json::from_str` on external input becomes a policy violation (grep/policy test enforces the chokepoint).
- **Canonical writer**: sorted keys (byte-lexicographic on UTF-8 key bytes), one pinned escape form per character class (documented table; e.g. mandatory short escapes, \uXXXX form pinned for control chars, no gratuitous escaping), no non-finite floats (NaN/Inf REJECT with typed error, never null-ified), stable integer formatting, no trailing/insignificant whitespace. Never accepts arbitrary `serde_json::Value` maps for authority-bearing structures — writers use typed structs + BTreeMap only where the schema declares key order.
- Both layers are pure std+serde/serde_json (allowlist-clean) and allocation-bounded (document caps: max depth, max string length hooks for boundary callers).

## Constraints
Deps: serde/serde_json only (approved family). Canonical bytes are specified, not delegated to an unspecified map serializer (plan §5.2 discipline). Non-finite floats reject; duplicate keys reject; no lossy fallback anywhere. This module underlies later digest computation, so byte-stability across versions is a compatibility promise from day one.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: duplicate-key-rejecting JSON primitives in place. Downstream consumers: ExecutionIdentity digesting, robot NDJSON emission, manifest/lock tooling, golden fixtures — all cite this module as their serialization authority.

## Tests
(1) Unit: duplicate key at top level / nested / inside arrays-of-objects → typed error with exact path; valid input parses identically to serde_json. (2) Writer goldens: a fixture struct covering every field type, escape class, sorted-key case, and alignment produces byte-exact committed output; NaN/Inf rejected. (3) Property/fuzz: parse(write(x)) == x for arbitrary typed values (no non-finite floats); writer output re-parses under the rejecting layer; random duplicate-key injections always reject. (4) Policy test: source scan proves no raw `serde_json::from_str`/`from_reader` on external input outside the chokepoint module. Logging: fuzz failures print the minimized input. Named artifacts: `tests/canonjson.rs` (units, writer goldens, policy scan) and dev-only fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/canonjson.rs` (round-trip + duplicate-key injection); the test run ends with `CANONJSON RESULT=PASS|FAIL` and every rejection error asserts its JSON path appears in the Display output.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: module lands in the crate tree created there.

title: [P0] Implement ExecutionIdentity type + docs/COMPATIBILITY.md + invalidation property test
description:
## Background
One canonical, versioned `ExecutionIdentity` value is constructed before admission and reused by task envelopes, prefix/grammar caches, durable jobs, qualification receipts, benchmarks, and ledgers — for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops → 44 KV slots layer+loop×22; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144). Manual partial lookalikes are how a cache key eventually omits thinking mode, grammar version, calibration, or packing semantics — this type makes that impossible.

## Contract
- `ExecutionIdentity` struct (plan §4.3.1) with EXACTLY these fields: `source_revision`, `logical_model_digest` (logical_model_sha256), `artifact_format`, `quant_recipe`, `packing_set_digest`, `tokenizer_digest`, `template_digest`, `task_spec` + `taskir_digest`, `prompt_digest`, `grammar_compiler_version` + `schema_digest`, `numerics_profile` (hf-bf16-eager | diagnostic-f32 | strict-quantized-vN | fast-vN), `kv_dtype`, `sampler_version`, thinking/tool mode, `calibration_digest`, `decision_policy_digest`, `backend_semantic_version`, and — where fast-vN semantics require it — `host_class` + `compiler_identity`.
- Subsystems derive DOMAIN-SEPARATED keys from this one structure (named projection constructors, e.g. prefix-cache key, semantic job key, receipt identity); no manual partial assembly. Digesting goes through the canonical JSON writer + sha2.
- A SEPARATE `ProvenanceIdentity` (source_root_sha256, fnlpq_file_sha256, release_manifest_sha256, license_bundle_sha256, converter/build provenance, publisher-attestation status) for artifact/release receipts. Legal-notice bytes are intentionally NOT part of logical_model_digest or semantic cache authority.
- `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`: for EVERY field, which caches/receipts/goldens/calibration artifacts/job stages a change invalidates.
- Property test: mutate every field in turn, assert the DOCUMENTED invalidation behavior (each named projection changes exactly when its documented fields change, and stays stable otherwise) — the doc and code are cross-checked mechanically (doc table parsed by the test).

## Constraints
No subsystem may hand-roll a partial identity (later policy test hook). Correcting a modification notice must not pretend the model computation changed (legal bytes outside semantic identity). Deps: std + serde/serde_json + sha2 only. Versioned type: a schema-version field + frozen serialization golden from day one.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: canonical ExecutionIdentity type + docs/COMPATIBILITY.md + field-mutation property test green. §6.7 prefix-cache key, §8.4 semantic job key, and §9.7 receipt identity are named projections defined here.

## Tests
(1) Property test as contracted: every field mutation vs every projection, matrix asserted against the parsed COMPATIBILITY.md table; a doc/code mismatch fails naming field+projection. (2) Domain separation: two projections over the same identity never produce equal digests (domain tags differ). (3) Serialization golden: canonical bytes of a fully populated identity frozen; any field addition/rename breaks the golden deliberately. (4) ProvenanceIdentity: notice-only change alters license_bundle/file digests but no ExecutionIdentity projection. Logging: full mutation-matrix table on failure. Named artifact: `tests/execution_identity.rs` (property/domain-separation/golden/provenance tests, parsing docs/COMPATIBILITY.md at test time); failures print field, projection, and expected-vs-actual digest prefixes, ending with `EXEC_IDENTITY RESULT=PASS|FAIL mismatches=<n>`.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: type lands in the crate tree.
- canonical-JSON bead: identity digesting is defined over the duplicate-key-rejecting canonical writer; without it the digest bytes are unspecified.

title: [P0] Write docs/PLATFORM_SURFACES.md per-target OS-facility registry
description:
## Background
franken_nlp's three-family dependency slogan survives only if platform facilities are governed, not improvised (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). Mmap, madvise, huge pages, NUMA placement, QoS, file locking, owner-only permissions, Windows ACLs, and peer-credential local IPC are NOT licensed merely by calling them "audited islands".

## Contract
Create `docs/PLATFORM_SURFACES.md`: a per-target registry (the 5 release targets: linux x86-64/gnu, linux aarch64/gnu, macOS aarch64, macOS x86-64 or as recorded by the dist matrix, windows x86-64/msvc — exact triples per the scaffold's CI record) listing, for EVERY promised OS facility:
- the exact API/ABI authority (syscall/API family and semantics relied on);
- whether `std` or a pinned FrankenSuite crate exposes it (and which);
- any manually declared symbols (target: NONE — no handwritten platform ABI enters release code);
- minimum OS/ABI version (min glibc / min macOS / min Windows);
- safety invariants and the fallback when unavailable;
- the feature/subcommand BLOCKED when no approved portable surface exists.
Initial rows (status may be "blocked/off" — honesty over coverage): opt-in mmap island; file locking + create_new + same-directory rename/sync semantics (model root, fs_tx); owner-only permissions/Windows ACLs; madvise/huge pages (off until a ratified suite surface); NUMA/topology/QoS (off; logical parallelism falls back to std::thread::available_parallelism); cgroup/job-object-aware memory discovery (or explicit-budget refusal); peer-credential local IPC (research-only, AA-R1). A validator script checks table structure + required columns and that every row names a fallback and a blocked-feature entry.

## Constraints
An unavailable reviewed surface DISABLES the optimization or REFUSES the operation — never silently weakens ACLs, locking, or memory safety. FrankenNLP never reaches through to transitive sysinfo/libc. The registry is the gate later beads (mmap island, fs_tx, tune, jobs) must update before shipping their facility.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: "every promised OS facility is exercised by target-native tests or explicitly marked blocked/compiled out" — this registry is the checklist that exit item is audited against, and the G0 model-root crash-semantics probe records its findings into these rows.

## Tests
(1) Validator: table parses; every row has all seven columns non-empty; every "available" row names its std/suite authority; every "blocked" row names the blocked feature. (2) Cross-reference: rows referenced by G0 probe ADRs exist (checked once those ADRs land). (3) Doc-link check: registry linked from AGENTS/plan-adjacent docs sections resolves (check.sh doc validator). Logging: validator prints the full facility × target matrix with status. Named artifact: `scripts/validate_platform_surfaces.py` (structure validator, wired into the check.sh doc section; the cross-reference check activates once G0 ADRs exist); ends with `PLATFORM_SURFACES RESULT=PASS|FAIL rows=<n> incomplete=<list>` and each incomplete row names its missing column.

title: [P0] Implement error.rs exit-code map 0-10 with CancelKind policy boundary
description:
## Background
Typed errors and stable exit codes are the policy boundary where asupersync's four-valued `Outcome::{Ok,Err,Cancelled,Panicked}` collapses for CLI callers (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). Agents script against these codes; they are frozen contract from Phase 0.

## Contract
`src/error.rs`: `FnlpError` (typed, std-only — no thiserror/anyhow) → stable exit codes, documented in-file:
- `0` ok · `1` generic · `2` usage · `3` model not found · `4` input decode/parse error · `5` budget/timeout · `6` cancelled · `7` artifact integrity/format/version mismatch · `8` schema/recipe compile error · `9` admission/resource limit · `10` structured task no-result.
- Calibrated model abstention is a SUCCESSFUL typed result: exit `0` with `status:"abstained"`. Code `10` is for an execution that cannot produce a valid task result at all (unsatisfiable required source field; missing mandatory thinking close delimiter) — never ordinary abstention.
- CancelKind mapping (all eleven pinned variants preserved in the diagnostic/robot envelope until this boundary): `Timeout`/`Deadline`/`PollQuota`/`CostBudget` → 5; `User`/`Shutdown`/ordinary `ParentCancelled` → 6; `ResourceUnavailable` → 9; `FailFast`/`LinkedExit` → the underlying typed error's code when known, else 1 (never generic user cancellation); `RaceLost` is an internal loser-drain reason and must NOT escape as a root terminal result — if it does, that is an invariant failure: exit 1 + crashpack evidence.
- A panic is NEVER laundered into a per-document error: it is a supervised failure producing `run_error`, nonzero run status, and heavier evidence (doc_error is for per-item input problems only).
- Exit-code table also emitted machine-readably (consumed later by `robot schema` and docs); one authority, no duplicate tables.

## Constraints
Preserve `Outcome` severity through join/drain/latch to this boundary — adapters attach context but never flatten Cancelled/Panicked early (doctrine #31). Exit code semantics are frozen pre-1.0 contract: changing one is a versioned breaking event. std-only error types (allowlist).

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: error/resource map present. Robot skeleton and every CLI subcommand consume this single mapping; the frozen-schema golden covers the machine-readable table.

## Tests
(1) Unit: every FnlpError variant maps to its documented code; table test covers all codes 0–10 with a construction for each. (2) CancelKind matrix: all eleven variants (`User,Timeout,Deadline,PollQuota,CostBudget,FailFast,RaceLost,ParentCancelled,ResourceUnavailable,Shutdown,LinkedExit`) → asserted code, including FailFast/LinkedExit with and without a known underlying error, and RaceLost → invariant-failure path (1 + crashpack marker in diagnostics). (3) Abstention: abstained result exits 0 with status field; no-result exits 10. (4) Panic path: an injected panic in a harness run produces run_error + nonzero, never a doc_error. Logging: mapping table printed on any mismatch. Named artifact: `tests/exit_codes.rs` (variant table, CancelKind matrix, abstention/no-result split, panic path via a harness subprocess asserting the real process exit code); ends with `EXIT_CODES RESULT=PASS|FAIL cancelkinds_covered=<n>/11` on stderr.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: error.rs lands in the crate tree created there.

title: [P0] Build robot NDJSON skeleton, robot schema self-description, frozen-schema golden
description:
## Background
Robot mode is the agent-first product surface of fnlp (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144): versioned, line-oriented NDJSON with a self-describing schema. The contract freezes early so agents can build against it; Phase 0 ships the skeleton + schema + golden contract test, not the full engine.

## Contract
- `src/robot.rs`: versioned NDJSON event skeleton with event types `run_start`, `stage`, `doc`, `doc_error`, `token`, `flush`, `run_complete`, `run_error`. Envelope fields: schema version, event type, caller id echo where applicable, and engine-assigned `request_seq` echoed on per-request events. stdout carries DATA ONLY; stderr carries diagnostics — never mixed; no human decoration in robot mode.
- `fnlp robot schema` self-describes the contract: emits the machine-readable schema (event types, fields, exit-code table from error.rs, schema version) as valid versioned JSON. `robot health` and `robot backends` emit valid versioned JSON skeletons (honest stub content: e.g. capability/thread-inventory placeholders marked unpopulated).
- Frozen-schema golden contract test: a committed JSON-schema fixture; a contract test validates EMITTED events against the frozen fixture; `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` with mandatory diff review is the only update path. Schema version bumps are deliberate, diffable events.
- Honor `NO_COLOR`, `CI`, `TERM=dumb`; bare `fnlp` prints help (never a TUI); explicit exit codes from error.rs.
- Emission goes through the canonical JSON writer (duplicate-key-rejecting layer guards any request parsing).
- Error locability (binding): every `doc_error`/`run_error` caused by request input names the offending input line — `input_line` (1-based NDJSON line number), byte offset where known, and the duplicate-key JSON path when the canonical parser rejected it — so an agent can jump straight to the bad line; stderr diagnostics echo the same line number, and raw input content is never echoed into data events beyond what the caller sent.

## Constraints
Stable versioned schema is the point — no field renames without a version bump. Determinism where possible: event field order canonical, no timestamps in canonical-replay mode paths (telemetry fields marked volatile in the schema). Panic → run_error (never doc_error) per the error-map contract.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: `robot schema|health|backends` emit valid versioned JSON; robot skeleton + frozen-schema golden green; empty-pipeline e2e skips green without weights (SKIPPED_NO_MODEL reported truthfully).

## Tests
(1) Contract test: every emitted event type validates against the frozen schema fixture; an added/renamed field without golden update fails. (2) Unit: request_seq echo present on doc/doc_error/token/run_complete; stdout/stderr separation asserted by capturing both streams. (3) Golden: `robot schema` output byte-stable (scrubbed of volatile fields); UPDATE_GOLDENS path exercised in a test that verifies the diff mechanism itself. (4) e2e: robot run with no model reports the skip state as a typed event, exit code truthful; NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb produce byte-identical data streams. Logging: schema validation failures print event + violating field path. Named artifacts: `tests/robot_contract.rs` (contract + unit + golden tests) with the frozen fixture at `tests/fixtures/robot_schema.golden.json`; the e2e (4) additionally feeds a malformed NDJSON line (duplicate key, invalid UTF-8) and asserts the emitted error event carries `input_line` + JSON path; the contract test ends with `ROBOT_CONTRACT RESULT=PASS|FAIL events=<n>` on stderr.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: robot.rs + CLI wiring land in the crate tree.
- canonical-JSON bead: emission/parse layers are the duplicate-key-rejecting canonical primitives.
- error-map bead: robot events and the schema embed the exit-code table and run_error/doc_error semantics defined there.

title: [P0] Scaffold optional metadata-only fsqlite store (no content columns, never rusqlite)
description:
## Background
Optional persistence for franken_nlp (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144): metadata/job-state history on fsqlite, disabled by default. Durability has an authority boundary (doctrine #19) and privacy is structural: content never enters tables.

## Contract
- `src/storage.rs`: an opt-in, feature-gated (and runtime-config-gated) metadata store on `fsqlite`/`fsqlite-types` — NEVER `rusqlite` (policy test already bans it; this bead adds the working skeleton).
- Schema skeleton (jobs/items/state/attempt/metrics/error tables) with a FIELD ALLOWLIST: ids, digests/commitments, state enums, attempt counts, metrics, typed error summaries. NO document text, NO prompt text, NO output/result bytes, NO file paths containing user content names beyond owner-chosen manifest paths — enforced by a schema-level test (column-name/type allowlist) plus an insert-boundary type that simply cannot carry content fields.
- Disabled mode opens NO database file at all (assert: zero filesystem touch when off).
- Durable job content spools are SEPARATE, explicit, owner-only files (plan §8.4, later phase) — storage.rs documents that boundary now and exposes no content-writing API.
- Store open/close lifecycle owned by the engine/CLI layer; owner-only permissions on created files (via the PLATFORM_SURFACES-governed surface; refuse where unavailable rather than weaken).

## Constraints
fsqlite is a pinned FrankenSuite surface (SUITE.lock). Metadata-only by default is a privacy CONTRACT, not a default setting users stumble past: content persistence later arrives only via explicit `--spool-*` flags in jobs.rs, never via storage.rs tables. No hidden input/output retention.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: optional metadata-only fsqlite store present. §8.4's spool-first/journal-second protocol (Phase 4C) builds on this skeleton; the privacy allowlist test becomes a permanent CI gate.

## Tests
(1) Unit: enabled store creates the schema; all tables' columns are within the allowlist; an attempted content-bearing column in a test schema fixture fails the allowlist test. (2) Disabled mode: no file created (temp-dir scan before/after). (3) Round-trip: job/item state transitions persist and reload; typed error summary stored without message content beyond the typed code/context allowlist. (4) Permission check (unix): created DB file is owner-only (0600-class), or the operation refuses on platforms without the governed surface. Logging: schema dump + allowlist verdict per column. Named artifact: `tests/storage_policy.rs` (allowlist scan, disabled-mode filesystem scan, round-trip, unix permission check); ends with `STORAGE_POLICY RESULT=PASS|FAIL columns_checked=<n>` and any violation names table.column + its type.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: storage.rs + feature wiring land in the crate tree with the pinned fsqlite dep.
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract test target (storage_policy) fully green in the no-fail-fast suite run (23 targets, 18 green); per-bead evidence per close policy

title: [P0] Run G0 probes 1-3+9: HTTPS/range matrix, spawn_blocking->scoped_cpu seam, EngineResources broker, model-root crash semantics
description:
## Background
G0 executable architectural ratification, cluster A: the asupersync foundation seams plus filesystem crash semantics, BEFORE any API/format freeze (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops → 44 KV slots; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144). These are minimal bounded spike probes — not production-looking mocks. A failed probe revises the architecture before downstream APIs crystallize.

## Contract
Four probes, each emitting an ADR (exact command, source/host pin, raw evidence digest, decision, killed alternatives):
- **Probe 1 — asupersync HTTPS/Range/redirect/resume fixture matrix** (before `fnlp pull` may depend on it): webpki-bundled vs platform trust roots; `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` behavior; private-mirror auth input + redaction; redirect host/scheme policy + cross-origin credential stripping; TLS name validation + minimum protocol; `Accept-Encoding: identity` for range/length-authenticated assets + rejection of unexpected content encodings; exact `206`/`Content-Range`/body-length semantics; IPv4/IPv6 + DNS failure behavior; enterprise/private-CA support or an explicit unsupported statement; cancellation mid-transfer. No README claims proxy/CA compatibility before these fixtures pass (OQ-33).
- **Probe 2 — `Cx::spawn_blocking` → whole-request/epoch `Cx::scoped_cpu` seam**: a CONFIGURED real blocking-pool handle with executor-heartbeat proof (runtime heartbeat progresses while the coordinator is busy — the pinned inline fallback is lab/test behavior, never a production success); one admitted team; exact coordinator/child width arithmetic (pinned `worker_cap` caps SPAWNED CHILDREN — probe establishes whether the coordinator counts); SEALED team formation (fixed team created behind an entry gate, spawn phase irrevocably ended, then workers released); no spawn after start/latch/cancellation (pinned ScopedCpu::spawn checks the numeric cap but NOT the drain latch — hostile interleaving must prove no post-start/post-latch worker); bounded checkpoints; disconnect-safe panic drain; wrapper-cancel vs actual-closure completion (closure owns lease/buffers until its completion latch fires); explicit request-region vs process-supervisor ownership of the post-cancel tail; re-entry refusal (typed ReentrantCall); no per-op thread creation; no-Rayon release graph/leaf path; scope-startup latency at request and batch-epoch granularity.
- **Probe 3 — one-time `EngineResources` broker**: racing first install (many threads; exactly one wins); compatible reuse; field-level `ResourceConfigConflict` on incompatible later request; same-digest weight sharing (one Arc); cgroup/job-object-aware memory discovery or explicit-budget refusal; AGGREGATE two-phase memory reservation across many engines (reserve→commit/abort); cancel/failed-allocation rollback; no engine lock held while queued for admission.
- **Probe 9 — model-root lock/`create_new`/sync/rename crash semantics on EVERY target family** (linux/macOS/windows): non-reentrant content lock; `create_new` staging; no symlink/reparse/device targets; same-filesystem sync+rename; kill-injection at each step; observed durability/replacement semantics recorded per platform into docs/PLATFORM_SURFACES.md rows.

## Constraints
Probes are bounded spikes in a probe area (e.g. tests/ or a dev-only bin), never release code; they may not add dependencies outside the allowlist/suite. Never enter the seam under an engine lock; never nest runtimes; leaf closures never spawn. Evidence is raw + digested; ADR decisions are binding on later beads.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: every G0 item ratified (ADR) or explicitly blocked with no dependent surface claiming readiness. Downstream anchors: pull.rs (probe 1), orchestrator/batchsched (probe 2), EngineResources (probe 3), fs_tx.rs + activation (probe 9).

## Tests
The probes ARE tests, but each must include: (1) deterministic-lab runs for async halves (seeded, replayable; crashpack on failure); (2) hostile native interleaving stress for the seam (post-latch spawn attempt, cancel/panic joins, heartbeat liveness); (3) kill-matrix table for probe 9 with per-step observed state; (4) fixture HTTP server matrix for probe 1 (206, wrong Content-Range, gzip-injected body, redirect with credentials, proxy env combinations). DETAILED LOGGING: every probe logs command, env, host pin, per-case verdict; failures retain seeds/crashpacks. Model weights not required — all probes run weightless (report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL only where a case genuinely needs weights; none should). Named artifacts: probe harnesses under `tests/g0/` (`probe1_https_matrix.rs`, `probe2_seam.rs`, `probe3_broker.rs`, `probe9_fs_crash.rs` — dev-only bins where a kill-matrix needs a child process); each probe emits per-case `G0_PROBE<N> case=<id> RESULT=PASS|FAIL seed=<s>` lines and one final summary line per probe, mirrored into the ADR evidence directory.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: probes compile against the pinned suite deps and land in the repo tree created there.

title: [P0] Run G0 probes 4-8+10: tokenizer/template spike, loop fixture, mask memory, reduction order, converter RSS, Zen-3 AVX2
description:
## Background
G0 executable architectural ratification, cluster B: the model-shaped and kernel-shaped spike probes for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots layer+loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT q 3072→6144, k/v 3072→1024; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Each probe kills a design assumption cheaply before APIs freeze.

## Contract
Six probes, each emitting an ADR (exact command, source/host pin, raw evidence digest, decision, killed alternatives):
- **Probe 4 — tokenizer/template exactness spike**: a minimal SentencePiece-BPE encode + template-render slice proving our approach reproduces reference token ids / rendered bytes on the Phase −1 fixture corpora (spike scope: enough coverage to ratify the design, not the full Phase-1 implementation).
- **Probe 5 — loop-boundary scalar fixture**: a tiny scalar forward slice proving the boundary semantics: 22 layers → final RMSNorm → 22 layers (loop 2 consumes loop-1 NORMALIZED output) → final RMSNorm; KV bound at layer + loop×22; validated against the Phase −1 trace taps (both post-loop norm states).
- **Probe 6 — 166,144-row mask/projection memory + dense/sparse crossover**: legal-mask bitset = 20,768 B; full logits f32 = 664,576 B; measure mask-AND and row-sliced projection cost dense vs sparse across legal-set sizes; record the measured crossover for §6.10/§7.3 design.
- **Probe 7 — M=1/M>1 reduction-order invariance**: prove which candidate reduction orders make batch-M ≡ batch-1 bitwise for the fixed shapes (K ∈ {3072, 6144, 1024, 10752}); record the canonical per-row reduction-order contract batching must preserve.
- **Probe 8 — converter range access + measured peak RSS**: checked bounded range reads over a large synthetic safetensors file (shard-scale lengths); prove one-tensor/bounded-panel streaming with measured peak RSS ≪ whole-file copy (the pinned ft-serialize loader copies whole files — quantify the gap); record the peak-RSS formula inputs (largest source panel + largest f32 panel + scratch + output buffer + parser metadata + margin).
- **Probe 10 — both exact Zen-3 AVX2 constructions ON THE REAL Threadripper**: X3a low-7/high-bit decomposition (pair bounds: lo ≤ 2×127×128 = 32,512; hi ≤ 256) and X3b sign-extend `vpmaddwd` widened-i16 route; both proved EXACTLY equal to scalar/i64 over the full i8 domain (exhaustive small-K + adversarial full-K at K=10752: S8×S8 ≤ 176,160,768; raw U8×S8 ≤ 350,945,280; +correction ≤ 176,160,768; sum 527,106,048, >4× i32 headroom); raw saturating `vpmaddubsw` is BANNED (clips inside the instruction; no accumulation cadence repairs it); record measured throughput of both on the actual Zen 3 Threadripper host (host pin in the ADR).

## Constraints
Probes are bounded spikes, never production kernels; SIMD probe code lives in an enumerated unsafe island or uses safe portable_simd where possible, with scalar/i64 differential harnesses. Measured-faster wins — capability is not routing; probe 10's numbers seed the Phase-3 dispatch priors, not final decisions. AVX2 exactness is a hard rule: raw saturation is not a shippable approximate mode.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: each probe's ADR ratified or explicitly blocked. Downstream: Phase 1 tokenizer/template + looprun (probes 4, 5), §6.10 lmhead + §7.3 mask design (probe 6), §6.7 batching contract (probe 7), §5.2 converter contract (probe 8), §6.5 X3a/X3b candidates (probe 10).

## Tests
Each probe includes its differential harness: (4) token-id/byte equality vs fixture corpora with per-divergence logging; (5) tap-by-tap comparison vs Phase −1 trace fixtures including the loop-1-post-norm ≡ loop-2-input equality; (6) memory measurements logged per legal-set size with the crossover table; (7) bitwise-equality matrix per reduction order candidate; (8) RSS measurement transcript vs whole-copy baseline; (10) exhaustive/adversarial equality vs scalar/i64 with counterexample printing (must be zero), plus i16 pair-bound assertions (32,512 / 256). Model-gated cases (probes 4/5 need Phase −1 fixtures) report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL/SKIPPED_NO_FIXTURES truthfully when absent. Named artifacts: probe harnesses under `tests/g0/` (`probe4_tok_tpl.rs`, `probe5_loop_boundary.rs`, `probe6_mask_memory.rs`, `probe7_reduction_order.rs`, `probe8_converter_rss.rs`, `probe10_avx2_exact.rs` — probe 10's SIMD body in its enumerated island or safe portable_simd); each emits per-case `G0_PROBE<N> case=<id> RESULT=PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED_NO_FIXTURES` lines plus a final summary, with measurement tables archived into the ADR evidence directory.

## Dependencies & rationale
- ADR framework bead (franken_nlp-oma): every probe's output is a G0 ADR (schema, evidence digests, ratification registry); without that framework the six decisions have no validated record to land in.
- scaffold bead (franken_nlp-uxw): probe harnesses land in the repo tree/toolchain created there.
- Phase −1 reference fixtures (franken_nlp-6gi, cross-epic want wired by orchestrator): probes 4 and 5 compare against the profile-tagged tokenizer/template corpora and trace taps.

title: [P0] Run G0 probe 11: OQ-35 asupersync leverage census (ratify or record absent)
description:
## Background
G0 probe 11 = the OQ-35 asupersync leverage census: an executable audit of exactly what the pinned asupersync foundation provides, so franken_nlp (wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B @ f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22×2 loops → 44 KV slots; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144) claims neither more nor less than the pin delivers. Names are exact contracts, not permission to infer stronger semantics (doctrine #32).

## Contract
One census campaign; EVERY item below ratified at the pin with an ADR, or recorded ABSENT with the hand-rolled fallback named:
- **Lab surfaces**: deterministic LabRuntime (same seed → same execution), oracle suites (quiescence, obligation leaks, loser drain, cancellation protocol), seed-bound chaos, crashpack replay artifacts, `VirtualTcp`. Scope honesty: Lab covers async state, NOT native scoped_cpu OS-thread interleavings (bounded team-state model owns those).
- **Capability rows**: sealed `[SPAWN, TIME, RANDOM, IO, REMOTE]` with monotone `Cx::restrict` [OBSERVED@pin]; project aliases (pull = spawn/time/IO + TLS entropy, never REMOTE; inference = no network; greedy/leaves = no RANDOM; leaf = cap::None or checkpoint-only view) + COMPILE-FAIL tests proving widening after restriction cannot compile and `Cx::current()` cannot regain dropped effects.
- **Budget mapping**: typed `Budget` (deadline, poll quota, cost quota) + `CapabilityBudget` (memory/CPU/IO/cleanup/artifact bytes) unit mapping to project units — the executable probe freezes project-unit ↔ asupersync-unit conversion; until then no prose treats milliseconds as a complete budget.
- **Obligation semantics**: two-phase reservations as tracked obligations; leak-response policy = PANIC in lab/CI, logged escalation in production, never silent.
- **Preset truths**: concrete builder values for `current_thread` / `low_latency` / `high_throughput` (at pin, high_throughput doubles deterministic default runtime workers — never blind-pair with a physical-core-wide scoped team); the aggregate thread envelope = runtime workers + max concurrent blocking coordinators + scoped children + ratified helpers.
- **first_ok**: first_ok SELECTION is sequential-in-input-order and NEITHER pinned surface is a sequential mirror — `first_ok_outcomes` only classifies an already-completed outcome vector; `ExecPlan::first_ok` drives ALL children concurrently to completion then picks the first success in input order with no short-circuit and no loser cancel/drain (split documented); the ratified fallback is the explicit ordered for/await loop (what `fnlp pull` uses), captured in a sequential-fallback fixture; any concurrent first-success needs a separately ratified primitive + duplicate-work budget + loser cancel-then-drain proof.
- **bracket**: normal awaited path vs drop-path split — drop-time release is bounded best-effort; durable cleanup stays RAII + explicit await + journal/recovery.
- **GenServer**: `call` = tracked reply obligation; `cast().await` proves ENQUEUE ONLY; `try_cast` overflow policy (Reject → Full; DropOldest only for declared-lossy streams with counted drops).
- **CancelKind**: all ELEVEN variants (`User, Timeout, Deadline, PollQuota, CostBudget, FailFast, RaceLost, ParentCancelled, ResourceUnavailable, Shutdown, LinkedExit`) present and preserved to the policy boundary.
- **DPOR coverage limits**: bounded guided exploration, never "exhaustive" by adjective — receipts publish run/class/budget/saturation coverage.
- **TLA export vs TLC**: export is TLC INPUT only; a bounded-model-check claim requires retained TLC version/config/command/result + property scope + counterexample when one exists.
- **Supervision surfaces**: supervisor/restart policies, registry name-leases — ratified for the batch daemon tree or fallback = §3.3 explicit region tree with hand-rolled restart-on-error.
- **Workspace substrate crates**: `franken_kernel` (type substrate), `franken_evidence` (evidence-ledger schema), `franken_decision` (decision-contract runtime), `frankenlab` (deterministic harness) — each audited for whether the pinned version usefully serves §9.7 registries / §7.8 DecisionPolicy / the deterministic test program; adoption is an explicit SUITE.lock + ADR decision, never a silent import.

## Constraints
Do not overclaim pin truths (bead-conventions rule 10 list is normative). Census probes are bounded spikes; compile-fail tests use the standard trybuild-style mechanism available under the pinned toolchain. Every ABSENT verdict names the hand-rolled fallback that replaces it.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit: OQ-35 census complete — every listed surface ratified-with-ADR or absent-with-fallback; no dependent surface (scheduler, daemon, jobs, pull proofs) may claim readiness on an unratified item. SUITE.lock records any substrate-crate adoption.

## Tests
(1) Compile-fail suite: capability widening, post-restrict regain via Cx::current — must fail to compile. (2) Lab determinism: same seed twice → identical execution trace; chaos failure produces a crashpack that replays. (3) Semantics fixtures: sequential first_ok ordering observed; cast-enqueue-only demonstrated (message enqueued but unprocessed at ack time); try_cast Reject/DropOldest behaviors; all eleven CancelKind variants constructed and round-tripped. (4) Preset probe: recorded worker/blocking values per preset match the ADR numbers. Logging: per-item verdict table (RATIFIED/ABSENT+fallback) with evidence digests. Named artifacts: probe harnesses under `tests/g0/asupersync_census/` with compile-fail cases in `tests/g0/compile_fail/` (trybuild-style under the pinned nightly); the census run emits one `G0_CENSUS item=<name> RESULT=RATIFIED|ABSENT_WITH_FALLBACK|FAIL` line per item plus a final summary line, with evidence digests logged beside each verdict.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead: census probes build against the pinned asupersync revision from the scaffold's manifest.
- G0 cluster-A bead (probes 1-3+9): the seam/broker probes establish the blocking-pool handle, team-formation, and broker facts this census cross-references (heartbeat, envelope arithmetic, obligation rollback) — census items must cite those ADRs rather than re-deriving them.

title: [P0] Define G0 ADR framework: schema, evidence digests, ratification registry + validator
description:
## Background
Phase 0's G0 executable architectural ratification (probe clusters 1-3+9, 4-8+10, and 11) closes with the exit gate "every G0 item has a ratified ADR or an explicit blocked target with no dependent surface claiming readiness" — for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B @ HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). Every probe bead is required to emit "an ADR, exact command, source/host pin, raw evidence digest, decision, and killed alternatives" — but without ONE shared framework, three probe clusters would invent three incompatible formats and the exit gate could not be checked mechanically. This bead owns that framework: the ADR schema, the evidence-digest discipline, the ratification registry, and the validator that makes the Phase 0 exit auditable.

## Contract
- `docs/adr/` layout + numbering: one ADR file per G0 item (11 probes today; the registry enumerates every item), named `ADR-G0-<probe##>-<slug>.md`, plus a template file `docs/adr/TEMPLATE.md`.
- REQUIRED ADR fields (machine-extractable front-matter or fenced metadata block, canonical JSON semantics): `adr_id`, `g0_item` (probe number + name), `status` ∈ {RATIFIED, ABSENT-WITH-FALLBACK, BLOCKED}, `decision` (one-paragraph binding statement), `exact_commands` (the literal command lines run), `source_pin` (repo/suite revisions probed — e.g. the pinned asupersync/frankentorch git revisions from SUITE.lock), `host_pin` (CPU model, OS, rustc -Vv digest for host-sensitive probes like the Zen-3 AVX2 probe 10), `evidence` (list of raw-evidence files with byte length + SHA-256 each), `killed_alternatives` (each named alternative + why it died), `fallback` (mandatory when status = ABSENT-WITH-FALLBACK: the hand-rolled replacement named), `blocked_surface` (mandatory when status = BLOCKED: the dependent surfaces that may NOT claim readiness).
- Raw evidence discipline: probe outputs (transcripts, measurement tables, crashpacks, fixture matrices) live under `docs/adr/evidence/<adr_id>/`; the ADR lists each file with its SHA-256; evidence is append-only (corrections add files, never rewrite archived bytes).
- Ratification registry `docs/adr/g0_registry.json` (canonical JSON, sorted keys): one row per G0 item (all 11 probes, each sub-probe of clusters allowed its own row) with item id, owning probe bead, ADR path, status. The Phase 0 exit check = every row has status RATIFIED or ABSENT-WITH-FALLBACK or BLOCKED, and no row is missing/unknown.
- Validator (wired into scripts/check.sh): parses every ADR's metadata block; FAILS on missing required fields, status/field mismatches (ABSENT without fallback; BLOCKED without blocked_surface), evidence files missing or digest-mismatched, registry rows without an ADR file or ADR files without a registry row, and duplicate adr_ids. Output: full item × status matrix.
- Downstream citation rule (binding on later beads): a bead consuming a G0 decision cites the `adr_id`; census items (probe 11) must cite cluster-A ADRs rather than re-deriving heartbeat/envelope/rollback facts.

## Constraints
ADR decisions are binding on later beads — a failed probe revises the architecture BEFORE downstream APIs crystallize; the framework must make status BLOCKED loud, never a silent gap. Evidence is raw + digested (no summarized-only evidence). The validator is std/allowlist-only repo tooling (may live in the check tooling, not the release binary). Do not overclaim pin truths (e.g. first_ok is SEQUENTIAL; bracket drop-path is bounded best-effort; TLA+ export is TLC INPUT only) — the ADR format records what was OBSERVED at the pin, with commands that reproduce it. Never delete or rewrite archived evidence.

## Evidence / gates
Phase 0 exit gate "every G0 item has a ratified ADR or an explicit blocked target with no dependent surface claiming readiness" is checked BY this bead's registry + validator; the three probe beads' ADRs populate it. The validator running green in scripts/check.sh (with all 11 items present in the registry, statuses legal) closes this bead's framework half; probe beads close their own content.

## Tests
(1) Unit: metadata parser accepts the template and a fully populated fixture ADR; rejects each missing required field with the field named. (2) Status-consistency: ABSENT-WITH-FALLBACK fixture without `fallback` fails; BLOCKED without `blocked_surface` fails; unknown status string fails. (3) Evidence integrity: fixture ADR with a listed evidence file whose bytes are tampered → digest mismatch failure naming file + expected + observed; missing evidence file → failure. (4) Registry reconciliation: ADR file without registry row, registry row without ADR file, duplicate adr_id — each a distinct named failure. (5) e2e: validator over the committed docs/adr/ tree exits 0 and prints the full item × status matrix. DETAILED LOGGING: per-ADR verdict lines with file, field, and digest specifics on every failure. No model weights involved; nothing reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. Named artifact: the validator ships as `scripts/validate_adrs.py` (the scripts/check.sh wiring invokes exactly this; unit/negative fixtures live under `tests/fixtures/adr/`), emitting the item × status matrix to stdout and a final `ADR_REGISTRY RESULT=PASS|FAIL items=<n>/<total> blocked=<list>` line to stderr.

## Dependencies & rationale
- scaffold bead (franken_nlp-uxw): docs/ tree, check.sh wiring, and repo tooling home are created there; the validator runs inside scripts/check.sh.
close_reason: Batch-verified: named contract test target (adr_validator) fully green in the no-fail-fast suite run (23 targets, 18 green); per-bead evidence per close policy

title: [P1] Build unified tokenizer fuzz program: never-panic, reference-parity losslessness, byte-fallback round-trip, control-id exclusion
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots, final RMSNorm after EACH pass, head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144), vocab 166,144, untied lm_head, SwiGLU 10752, RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). The tokenizer stack (SentencePiece-protobuf reader → SP BPE encode/decode → UntrustedDocument encoder) is the single boundary through which ALL external text enters the engine, so §9.3's fuzz obligation names it first. The per-bead property tests (reader limits, engine never-panic, encoder exclusion) are necessary but scattered; this bead builds the ONE maintained tokenizer fuzz PROGRAM — a persistent, structure-aware, corpus-carrying harness that unifies the obligations, so coverage accumulates across runs instead of restarting from random seeds every CI invocation.

## Contract
- One fuzz harness home (e.g. `fuzz/` cargo-fuzz targets or `tests/fuzz/` deterministic harness — the mechanism must work under the pinned dated nightly and be wired into CI as a bounded-time job; the unbounded campaign is a manual/scheduled run).
- Fuzz targets, each with its own persisted corpus + dictionary:
  1. **spm_proto reader**: arbitrary bytes + structure-aware mutations of valid `ModelProto` encodings → parse returns Ok or typed Err; never panics/aborts/hangs; allocation ceiling asserted (no `Vec::with_capacity(attacker_len)`); exercises every limit constant (10-byte varint cap, nesting depth, piece count ~2,000,000 cap, string length, total bytes) and every rejection class (duplicate singular fields, invalid UTF-8 pieces, truncation, trailing garbage, group wire types).
  2. **encode/decode never-panic**: arbitrary bytes/strings → `encode_ids` never panics; arbitrary id sequences over the FULL u32 range (in-range 0..166,144 and out-of-range, which must reject typed) → `decode_bytes`/`decode_text` never panic; `decode_text` yields valid UTF-8 or a typed error/explicit-lossy result — never silent U+FFFD in an exactness path.
  3. **reference-parity losslessness semantics**: the correctness bar is parity with the reference tokenizer's OWN canonical behavior — SP normalization means `decode(encode(x)) == x` is NOT a general property, so the target asserts byte-losslessness ONLY on paths where the reference itself is lossless: byte-fallback round-trip (inputs forced through byte pieces must reconstruct exact bytes), and differential replay over the frozen L0 fixture corpus (fuzz-discovered inputs that tokenize differently from recorded reference behavior on covered classes are saved as candidate corpus entries for oracle adjudication, flagged — not auto-failed — because the oracle is not present in CI).
  4. **untrusted-segment control-id exclusion**: adversarial documents seeded from every `TemplateControlIds` member's literal text (`<think>`, `</think>`, `<tool_call>`, `</tool_call>`, `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, and the full archived registry), their UTF-8 prefixes/suffixes, byte-split variants, and surrounding context → the UntrustedDocument encoder output NEVER contains any registry id AND `decode_bytes(ids) == original bytes`, or the encoder returns a typed rejection; never panics.
- Dictionaries are GENERATED from the archived registries and the pinned piece table (never hand-typed); a drift test fails when the registry artifact changes but the dictionary generator output was not regenerated.
- Corpus management: minimized crash/violation artifacts are committed as regression fixtures with stable names; every fixed finding becomes a permanent unit test; CI replays the full committed regression corpus on every run (bounded, deterministic) even when the fuzz campaign itself is skipped.
- Runbook doc in the harness directory: how to run each target, time budgets, how to minimize, where corpora live, how a finding is triaged into a fixture + fix.

## Constraints
Fuzz tooling may be dev-only, but it must not drag new crates into the RELEASE graph (release dependency families stay clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; the dependency-policy test's dev-vs-release split covers this). `unsafe_code = "deny"` everywhere here. G1 > G2: L0 exactness is the bar — a fuzz target must never encode "close enough" tokenization as acceptable. Forbidden-set authority is the archived TemplateControlIds census (superset of TokenizerSpecialIds; think/tool markers are special=false at the pin), never a hand list. No Rayon anywhere; deterministic replay of the committed corpus (fixed seeds logged).

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: (a) all four targets implemented with generated dictionaries + committed seed corpora; (b) a recorded bounded campaign (wall-time and executions logged per target) with ZERO panics/hangs/allocation-ceiling violations and zero exclusion/losslessness violations, its transcript archived in the conformance evidence; (c) CI wiring green: regression-corpus replay job runs on every CI pass in bounded time; (d) the registry/dictionary drift test green. This is the §9.3 fuzz row for the tokenizer; the L0 gate (l44) and the §9.3 metamorphic untrusted-segment invariant (k2h) remain the correctness authorities this program hammers.

## Tests
