(1) Unit: dictionary generator output contains every registry member's bytes and its prefix/suffix fragments; drift test fails on stale dictionary. (2) Harness self-tests: an injected panic in a test-double target is caught and reported with the minimized input; the allocation-ceiling hook trips on a test allocation bomb. (3) Regression replay: full committed corpus replays clean, deterministically, within the CI time bound; each replayed artifact logs target, input digest, and verdict. (4) e2e campaign (manual/scheduled, bounded): per-target executions/sec, corpus growth, and findings table logged; findings, if any, are minimized and land as named fixtures. DETAILED LOGGING: every violation prints target, minimized input (hex + escaped), offending id/piece/byte offset with ±32-byte context for exclusion violations, and the exact limit tripped for reader violations. No model weights required; nothing reports SKIPPED_NO_MODEL (oracle-adjudication candidates are flagged artifacts, not skipped tests). Named artifacts: targets are `fuzz/fuzz_targets/{spm_proto,tok_encode_decode,tok_reference_parity,untrusted_exclusion}.rs` (matching contract items 1–4) with corpora under `fuzz/corpus/<target>/`; the bounded CI replay is `tests/fuzz_regression_replay.rs`. Every run ends with per-target `FUZZ target=<name> RESULT=PASS|FAIL execs=<n> corpus=<m>` lines and a final summary.

## Dependencies & rationale
- SP BPE engine bead (franken_nlp-l44): targets 2-3 fuzz its real API and replay the L0 fixture corpus; fuzzing a pre-L0 engine would flag its bugs as fuzz noise. (The spm_proto reader arrives transitively via l44's dependency.)
- UntrustedDocument encoder bead (franken_nlp-k2h): target 4 hammers its exclusion/rejection contract with the registry-derived dictionary; the encoder and its typed rejection surface must exist first.

title: [4C] Ship fnlp runs and sync export-jsonl over the metadata-only fsqlite history
description:
## Background
`fnlp runs` and `fnlp sync export-jsonl` (plan §8.2) expose the optional metadata-only fsqlite run history for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). The P0 scaffold built the store skeleton (field-allowlisted tables, disabled by default, zero filesystem touch when off); this bead ships the user-facing history/audit-export CLI over it, landing with the 4C durability wave where run/job metadata becomes real.

## Contract
- **`fnlp runs`**: lists/inspects recorded run/job metadata from the opt-in fsqlite store — ids, timestamps, ExecutionIdentity projections, job state (`pending → admitted → running → result_committed → materialized`), attempt counts, metrics, typed error summaries. Robot NDJSON (`--json`) under the frozen schema; human table otherwise. When the store is disabled: a typed, honest "history disabled" result (exit 0 with explicit status) — NEVER a fake empty history implying the store was consulted.
- **`fnlp sync export-jsonl`**: exports the same metadata as canonical JSONL (recursive UTF-8-byte key order, pinned serializer number/string escaping, non-finite floats rejected; duplicate-key-rejecting on any read-back) for external audit tooling. Export is a pure read: no mutation, no compaction.
- **Privacy (structural)**: output contains ONLY the allowlisted metadata fields — ids, digests/commitments, state enums, attempts, metrics, typed error codes. NO document text, NO prompt text, NO output bytes, NO raw private-content SHA-256 (private content identity appears only as the job's domain-separated HMAC-SHA-256 commitments per §8.4). The export path re-applies the field allowlist as a read-side filter (defense in depth), so a future schema column cannot leak by default.
- Filters: by task, time range, state, artifact/recipe digest; deterministic canonical ordering (sort by run id) so exports are diffable.
- `-o file` goes through the §8.6 local-output transaction: owner-controlled parent, exclusive `create_new` staging, no symlink/reparse/device targets, owner-only permissions, sync + same-directory activation.

## Constraints
fsqlite, never rusqlite; fsqlite tables never contain document/prompt/output text (store-side allowlist is the P0 gate; this bead adds the read-side filter). stdout is data, stderr diagnostics; exit codes 0–10 per the frozen map (10 = typed task no-result; abstention is exit 0 + status abstained — neither applies to a plain disabled-history status). Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon. Disabled-by-default persistence is a privacy contract: `runs`/`export-jsonl` never enable the store implicitly.

## Evidence / gates
Frozen robot-schema coverage for runs/export events (consumed by the P6 CLI/robot contract freeze). Privacy gate: an export over a fixture store seeded with every column class contains only allowlisted fields (scan test), and a deliberately planted content-bearing column in a test schema is filtered AND flagged. Canonical-export determinism golden: same store → byte-identical JSONL regardless of row insertion order.

## Tests
Unit: filter parsing; canonical ordering; disabled-store typed result; read-side allowlist drops unknown columns. Property: export is read-only (store digest unchanged after export); exported JSONL round-trips through the duplicate-key-rejecting parser; permuting row insertion order does not change canonical export bytes. E2E: seed a store via a stub job lifecycle, run `fnlp runs --json` and `fnlp sync export-jsonl -o out.jsonl` through the output transaction on a hostile-directory matrix (symlink/reparse/device/existing-file targets refuse); detailed logging of rows scanned, filters applied, fields dropped. Named runnable `scripts/e2e_runs_export_golden.sh` (model-free, green in ordinary CI): seeds the fixture store via the stub job lifecycle, runs `fnlp runs --json` + `sync export-jsonl` through the hostile-directory matrix, one machine-parseable row per case (rows scanned, fields dropped, store-digest-unchanged verdict, exit code). Model-free: fully green in ordinary CI (no artifact required for metadata history).

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-uby (P0 fsqlite store skeleton): the schema, field allowlist, and disabled-mode contract this CLI reads.
- franken_nlp-040 (durable jobs core): the job state machine and HMAC-commitment fields are the primary real content of the history; the read surface must match that contract exactly.

title: [4C] Implement fnlp job partition/merge v1 refusal per frozen schema (Phase-7 gated)
description:
## Background
`fnlp job partition/merge` is a Phase-7 surface (portable snapshot shards, plan §8.2 phase-7 row), but the v1 CLI must already behave honestly about it: commands do not appear as misleading success-shaped stubs before their phase — an unbuilt experimental command is ABSENT, or returns a versioned `surface_not_built` error only where the frozen robot schema explicitly describes that state. This bead implements that v1 behavior for the job CLI of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), so the P6 contract freeze can describe the gated state and the later P7 implementation replaces a described refusal, not a hole.

## Contract
- Decide and implement ONE of the two doctrine-legal v1 shapes (recorded decision): (a) `partition`/`merge` subcommands ABSENT from the clap surface entirely (unknown-subcommand usage error, exit 2), or (b) present but returning the versioned `surface_not_built` typed error — allowed ONLY if the frozen robot schema explicitly describes that state for these commands.
- If (b): the error names the surface, the gating phase (Phase 7), and the gate (single-host scope semantics proven first — the Phase-4C dependency-scope mutation invariants); robot mode emits it as a schema-described versioned typed event; exit is the typed error class, NEVER 0.
- Whichever shape ships: `fnlp job start/status/resume/verify/materialize` remain fully functional, and help text does not advertise partition/merge as available.
- The refusal state becomes part of the P6 contract freeze (goldens + surface_not_built negative fixtures for every gated/experimental command); the P7 partition/merge bead later replaces this refusal with the real surface as a versioned schema event, never a silent flip.

## Constraints
No success-shaped stubs before their phase (plan §8.2 rule, verbatim-binding); the frozen robot schema is the only authority for describing a not-built state; exit codes 0–10 (exit 10 = typed task no-result does NOT apply here — this is a usage/surface error class); deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; stdout data / stderr diagnostics.

## Evidence / gates
Golden: `fnlp job partition` / `fnlp job merge` invocation transcripts (human + robot modes) frozen; robot-schema fixture describes the state (shape b) or the subcommands are proven absent (shape a). Negative fixture consumed by the P6 contract-freeze suite. Decision record (a vs b) committed with rationale.

## Tests
Unit: dispatch for both invocations returns the decided shape; help output excludes/marks the gated commands. Golden: exact stdout/stderr/exit code for human and robot modes; UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 with mandatory diff review. Property: no code path under `job partition|merge` can reach job execution, spool, or journal machinery pre-gate (policy test on module reachability). E2E: invoke the refusal against a real job directory — job state untouched (digest-compare before/after); detailed logging of the refusal event with schema_version. Model-free: fully green in ordinary CI.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-eas (job resume/verify/materialize CLI): the `fnlp job` command family this refusal lands inside must exist first.

title: [P5] Measure per-task thinking-mode defaults with locked eval artifacts
description:
## Background
Thinking-mode policy (§7.9) for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half; im/think template markers are special=false at pin): the conservative pre-evaluation default is OFF for every structured/batch task (including judge and answer); generate/chat honors the model-template default; each task exposes a bounded explicit override. Phase 5 may promote thinking per task ONLY when a locked eval shows the gain justifies the cost. Thinking multiplies the expensive loop: every thinking token costs 2 loop passes / 44 physical-layer executions plus 176 KiB of bf16 KV, so promotion is a measured economic decision, not a vibe.

## Contract
- **Per-task measurement campaign** over the locked §9.6 datasets: for each candidate task (extract, ner, classify, sentiment, judge, answer, summarize at minimum), run thinking OFF vs bounded thinking ON under the same recipe/profile/prompt hashes and a preregistered protocol.
- **Metrics per task**: task-metric delta (accuracy/F1 per the task's scorecard), selective-risk delta where a calibration artifact exists, p50/p95 latency, output-token and thinking-token counts (structural witnesses count thinking tokens separately), and energy observations where available.
- **Promotion rule**: thinking becomes a task's default ONLY when the locked eval's accuracy/selective-risk gain justifies the p95 latency, energy, and output-token cost under the preregistered thresholds; otherwise the conservative OFF default stays. Either outcome is a recorded decision.
- **Per-task eval artifact** (the §7.9 deliverable): names dataset version, recipe id, prompt hash, thinking cap (token/time), measured deltas and costs, thresholds, and the decision — consumed by CLAIMS/scorecard rows; a promoted task's preset records its thinking default as versioned data (a default flip is a diffable preset event with eval re-run).
- **Invariants stay invariant**: thinking tokens never enter task JSON; prompt caches are keyed by mode; a missing close delimiter fails as a typed no-result (exit-10 family), never partial success. This campaign measures DEFAULTS; it never weakens those rules.

## Constraints
Preregistered thresholds before measurement — no post-hoc shopping; mean and tail both visible; task-quality claims name dataset, prompt hash, recipe id, thinking mode; presets are data; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon; abstention remains exit 0 + status abstained, distinct from exit 10.

## Evidence / gates
Phase-5 exit contribution: "measured thinking defaults" — the per-task decision table (promoted / kept-off) with locked-eval deltas and cost rows archived with the scorecards; PERF_LEDGER rows for latency/token costs; preset diffs for any promoted task; CLAIMS wording never exceeds the measured state.

## Tests
Unit: campaign config parsing (task list, caps, thresholds); witness separation (thinking vs output token counters) asserted on fixtures. Property: OFF-mode runs are byte-identical to pre-campaign behavior for the same seed/profile (the campaign changes nothing until a promotion lands); mode-keyed caches — an ON-mode prefix entry can never serve an OFF-mode request. E2E: campaign harness over a stub task with recorded outputs validates artifact schema and decision arithmetic; armed per-task runs with detailed logging (per-item mode, token counts, deltas, threshold evaluations). Model-gated rows report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-r0a (eval framework core): locked datasets, split discipline, and scorecard identity are the measurement substrate.
- franken_nlp-ngg (task core): the semantic envelope's thinking-mode field and per-task bounded override plumbing under measurement.
- franken_nlp-k45 (generate/chat): the bounded-thinking implementation (caps, close-delimiter no-result policy, mode-keyed caching) the campaign exercises.

title: [P5] Qualify optional non-LLM n-gram language detector behind license and scorecard gates
description:
## Background
Plan §7.4/§7.7 name an optional non-LLM n-gram language detector as the preferred cheap route for language-id — gated, never assumed. On the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half), a full target invocation costs 2 loop passes / 44 physical-layer executions per token position — overkill for most language-id — but the cheap detector ships ONLY if its separate spec clears the §7.7 gates (Phase-5 exit language). Declining is a legitimate recorded outcome.

## Contract
- **Gate set (ALL required before the detector ships or becomes any preset's default):** (1) model-data license + digest recorded — the n-gram profile data is a versioned, licensed artifact like any preset (origin, exact license text, content hash); (2) declared language set (exact list, never "many languages"); (3) preprocessing spec (byte/scalar handling, case/whitespace policy) pinned by digest; (4) locked accuracy/speed scorecard on license-gated datasets plus owned multilingual smoke — per-language accuracy, confusion pairs, and measured throughput. "Wire speed" is not a premeasurement claim.
- **Surface if promoted:** the language-id preset route in `fnlp classify` uses the detector as the cheap path with an explicit escalation/abstain policy to the LLM route; detector output names the detector artifact version and is never blurred with LLM-derived scores (separate provenance; detector scores are labeled likelihood scores, not calibrated probabilities, absent a calibration artifact).
- **If any gate fails:** the detector stays unshipped; language-id remains an LLM classify preset; the decision is recorded with the failing gate named.
- The detector is pure Rust within the existing dependency policy (no new crates); its model data is embedded or installed as a versioned data file, hash-checked at load — never a network fetch at inference time.

## Constraints
Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite — the detector cannot introduce a dependency; presets are data with provenance (origin/license metadata + content hash per file); license-gated acquisition per the eval framework — a dataset or model-data file without archived license terms never enters CI; no Rayon; scorecard claims name dataset versions; no network in the inference path.

## Evidence / gates
DATASETS.md rows for every evaluation corpus; the detector-data license/digest record; the locked accuracy/speed scorecard (per-language accuracy, confusion matrix, p50/p95 throughput vs the LLM route on the same fixtures); the ship/decline decision record. Phase-5 exit: "the non-LLM language-detector artifact only if its separate spec clears the §7.7 gates" — either outcome recorded, with evidence.

## Tests
Unit: n-gram profile load + hash check (mismatch = loud typed error, exit-7 class); preprocessing conformance to the pinned spec; language-set enforcement (input outside the declared set → explicit other/unknown, never a forced in-set guess). Property/fuzz: arbitrary bytes never panic the detector; detection is deterministic per artifact version; mixed-language and short-input fixtures exercise the abstain/escalation policy. E2E: classify with the language-id preset routing through the detector, with detailed logging of detector version, scores, and escalation decisions; comparison harness vs the LLM route on the owned smoke set. Model-free detector tests green in ordinary CI; LLM-route comparison rows report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-r0a (eval framework core): license-gated acquisition and locked scorecards are the gate machinery this qualification runs on.
- franken_nlp-10a (fnlp classify): the language-id preset surface the detector plugs into, and the LLM fallback route it is compared against.

title: [P3] Implement range-reduced vector exp/sigmoid candidate: default-off, ULP-gated, ledger-promoted
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions per token; KV slot = layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); SwiGLU 10752; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half. LLVM generally cannot turn scalar libm calls into the exact vector transcendental sequence we want, so a range-reduced minimax `exp`/`sigmoid` is a CANDIDATE for the two float glue hot sites: softmax (prefill attention and the decode online-softmax scan, ×44 executions per token) and SiLU (the SwiGLU gate activation over the 10752-wide intermediate). It is NOT known-fast here until profiled (doctrine #5: sibling wins are priors, not this project's measurements), it CHANGES NUMERICS, and it can never be described as SIMD≡scalar bit identity.

## Contract
- Implement range-reduced minimax polynomial vector `exp` and `sigmoid` (SiLU = x·sigmoid(x)) as dispatch-selectable variants for the softmax and SiLU sites, DEFAULT OFF everywhere.
- Range reduction, polynomial degree/coefficients, evaluation order, and the reconstruction step are frozen specification (data in the repo), so the approximate path is itself deterministic per doctrine #9 — but it is an APPROXIMATE mode: never promise byte identity with the libm path.
- Named numerics contract per function: declared input domain; max-ULP bound over that domain measured against the reference libm path; explicit behavior at domain edges (exp underflow to 0 for large negatives, overflow policy, ±0, subnormals); monotonicity preservation (x1 ≤ x2 → exp(x1) ≤ exp(x2), same for sigmoid); NaN/Inf propagation policy identical to the reference path or explicitly documented.
- The reference libm scalar path ALWAYS remains available and remains the shipped default; selection is per (architecture, shape, site) via the measured dispatch table, promoted ONLY on ledger wins (sustained A/B, p50/p95/p99, thermal steady state).
- Profile scoping: strict profiles (`strict-quantized-vN`, `hf-bf16-eager`, `diagnostic-f32`) NEVER select the approximate path; it is only eligible inside a `fast-vN`-class profile that carries its own preregistered numeric/token-quality contract, and fast-profile results may not reuse strict-profile cache entries (ExecutionIdentity includes the numerics profile).
- L1–L5 impact is measured, not assumed: L1 metric deltas at the affected ops, L2 propagation across the 44 layer outputs + two loop norm states, L4 greedy-token flips counted — any flip becomes a named fixture bound to the fast profile's contract, never a silent change.

## Constraints
- Default-off until per-arch/shape ledger wins; losers stay implemented-but-off with NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/PERF_LEDGER rows or are reverted per the 5-pass loop (one lever at a time).
- G1 > G2 profile-scoped: no strict-profile claim may ride this path; forced paths remain for proof runs.
- Leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon anywhere in the release graph; direct non-suite deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; SIMD only inside the enumerated unsafe islands policy (deny-not-forbid), portable_simd/autovec preferred where it measures equal.
- Never claim "SIMD ≡ scalar" for this path; the words available to it are the measured max-ULP bound and the fast-profile contract.

## Evidence / gates
- ULP gate: exhaustive-where-feasible + dense-sweep comparison vs reference libm over the declared domain, including range-reduction segment boundaries, subnormals, ±0, large-magnitude negatives/positives, NaN/Inf — measured max ULP ≤ the declared bound, recorded in the kernel's numerics note.
- Monotonicity gate: property runs proving no local inversion across every reduction-segment boundary.
- L1–L5 impact runs recorded (deltas + any token-flip fixtures) under the fast profile.
- PERF_LEDGER rows per (arch, shape, site): candidate vs libm, p50/p95/p99 after warmup at thermal steady state; promotion ADR for any default-on row; NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE row for every loser. Close cites the ULP/monotonicity fixtures + the ledger rows (a measured loss with retained evidence is a VALID close).

## Tests
- Unit: golden values at hand-checked points (0, 1, ln2 multiples, segment edges); underflow/overflow edges; ±0 and subnormal inputs; NaN/Inf policy rows.
- Property/fuzz: random f32 across the full declared domain — |ULP(candidate, libm)| ≤ bound, monotone pairs never invert, seed-reproducible; on failure log input bits, both output bits, ULP distance, and the reduction segment.
- E2E: forward-level A/B with the variant toggled per site under the fast profile — logit deltas and greedy-token flips logged per (loop, layer, position) with DETAILED LOGGING of profile id, dispatch row, and CPU feature string; model-gated runs report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; synthetic-weight forwards always run.

## Dependencies & rationale
- [P3] dispatch-table framework (franken_nlp-pwu): the candidate exists only as a measured, dispatch-selectable variant with robot backends reporting; there is no other legal route to default-on.
- [P3] native GQA attention (franken_nlp-dsr): the softmax consumer site — prefill softmax and the decode online-softmax scan define where the vector exp plugs in and what reduction-order contract it must respect.
- [P3] prepacked tiled GEMM (franken_nlp-53o): the SiLU×up site lives in the production MLP pipeline's epilogue path; landing the candidate before the production pipeline exists would fuse to a throwaway surface.

title: [P3] Run build-recipe matrix: thin/fat LTO, codegen-units, PGO with hashed training corpus
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions per token; KV slot = layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half. Plan §6.14: build-time optimization is a MEASURED release recipe, not "free". Compiler-level levers (LTO, codegen-units, PGO) can move end-to-end latency and instruction-cache behavior on a 44-execution-per-token forward, but each costs build time, reproducibility surface, or both — so they are promoted per target only through the same keep-gate discipline as any kernel lever.

## Contract
- Build the small matrix and measure every cell: {thin LTO, fat LTO} × {codegen-units = 1, one practical parallel value} × {PGO off, PGO on}. Per cell record: clean build wall time, binary size (both `fnlp` and `franken_nlp` shims resolve to the same lib payload), R1 p50/p95/p99 (decode latency via the R1 gauntlet harness), and instruction-cache counters where the platform exposes them. R2–R4 rows are appended as those regime harnesses land; promotion decided on R1 alone must be re-validated when R2–R4 exist (the promotion ADR records this obligation).
- Promote AT MOST one reproducible release profile per target, and only when its end-to-end gain clears the keep threshold (confidence interval AND practical threshold; §10.2 loop). Otherwise the default profile stands and every measured cell is retained as evidence.
- PGO discipline: the training corpus is named and versioned — corpus ids and their ORDER are hashed into the profile identity together with the compiler commit; a PGO profile whose corpus/compiler hash does not match is stale and unusable. Profile data regeneration is a documented, replayable command.
- BOLT is Linux-only RESEARCH, considered only after PGO, and requires a separately replayed profile; it is not part of the v1 matrix.
- `panic=abort` may apply to shipped binaries only when the error/cancellation contract proves no unwinding dependency (asupersync cancel/panic joins and `Outcome::Panicked` handling included); an embedding application's final Cargo profile controls its own library linkage, and the library makes no panic-strategy assumption.
- Portable target-feature baselines plus runtime dispatch are mandatory in every cell; NEVER ship (or benchmark as "ours") `target-cpu=native`.

## Constraints
- Measured-faster wins: no cell is promoted on build-log vibes; losers and their numbers stay in the ledger.
- Reproducibility: the chosen profile per target is committed configuration (Cargo profile + documented env), rebuildable byte-comparably where the toolchain permits, and named in release receipts.
- No new dependencies: the matrix runner is repository scripts over cargo + the existing bench harness; a convenient bench framework name is not permission to add a dependency.
- One lever at a time when interpreting: LTO/CGU/PGO interactions are read from the full matrix, not from a single pairwise diff.

## Evidence / gates
- The complete matrix results table lands in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md: per (target, cell) — build time, size, R1 p50/p95/p99, icache counters or "unavailable", exact command/env/compiler commit.
- Promotion ADR per target naming the chosen profile, its hashes (PGO corpus ids/order, compiler commit), the cleared thresholds, and the R2–R4 re-validation obligation; or an explicit "default retained" disposition with the losing cells ledgered.
- CI proof that the promoted profile builds and passes the locked test suite; release receipts name the profile. Close cites the ledger table + ADR (a "default retained" outcome with full evidence is a VALID close).

## Tests
- Unit: profile-identity hashing (corpus ids + order + compiler commit → stable digest; any reorder changes it); matrix-cell manifest completeness; stale-PGO-profile rejection.
- Property: matrix-runner determinism — same cell spec twice produces identical build configuration and receipt fields (timing values excepted and marked volatile).
- E2E: build at least one non-default cell end-to-end and run the R1 smoke comparison against the default cell with DETAILED LOGGING (cell id, exact rustc/cargo invocations, flags, wall times, binary SHA-256s, bench receipt ids); R1 rows on the real artifact are model-gated and report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL without it — build-time/size/reproducibility rows run without any model.

## Dependencies & rationale
- [P3] R1 latency gauntlet harness (franken_nlp-i9p): the matrix's latency columns are exactly that harness's receipted A/B rows; without it every "faster build" claim is unmeasured.

title: [P2] Implement runtime-gated KV int8 mode: 88 KiB payload, counted scales, long-context gates
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots (KV slot = layer + loop×22); final RMSNorm after EACH pass; attention is 48 query : 8 KV heads at head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (k/v 3072→1024); vocab 166,144; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half. BF16 KV costs 176 KiB/token (180,224 B across 44 slots) — 8K context ≈ 1.38 GiB per sequence. Because KV is PRODUCED AT RUN TIME, KV int8 is the one genuinely runtime-gated quantization choice in the whole design (§5.5): weight-precision stages are immutable artifacts, but this mode is a real switch whose "rollback" is simply turning it off. This bead implements the mode itself; the slab allocator bead only carries its structural accounting.

## Contract
- **Runtime-gated KV int8 mode, OFF by default:** quantize K and V at KV-write time into the slab pages; int8 payload is 88 KiB/token (half of 176 KiB). Scale metadata is COUNTED, never hand-waved: separate f32 K/V scales per (loop-layer, KV head, token) add exactly 2,816 B/token before alignment (44 slots × 8 KV heads × 2 (K,V) × 4 B), or 1,408 B/token with f16 scales, plus padding and page-table overhead. "Approximately halves total KV" may be claimed ONLY after including scale + padding + page-table overhead in the arithmetic.
- **Consumption:** prefill and decode attention read int8 KV by dequantizing in-scan under the active profile's cast contract, preserving the fixed per-row reduction order (batch-invariance discipline). An int8 QKᵀ/scores·V path is a SEPARATE later candidate behind its own selector — out of scope here; the proved higher-precision attention path stays resident and selectable.
- **Selection surface:** engine builder field + CLI flag (a genuinely runtime choice per §5.1[3]); the selector is honest — both representations are producible at run time, so this switch really can restore bf16 KV semantics (unlike weight stages, where only activating a prior immutable artifact can).
- **Identity and caching:** the KV dtype joins the ExecutionIdentity projection used for prefix-cache keys and receipts; bf16-KV and int8-KV cache entries never cross; batch composition may not mix a row's KV dtype mid-sequence — mode is fixed at admission per sequence, and any mixed-batch support prices both accountings explicitly or rejects typed.
- **Admission:** the admission certificate prices int8-KV payload + scale + padding + page-table bytes exactly (mirroring the slab allocator's structural terms); `robot plan` reports the mode's real per-token cost, not "88 KiB".
- **Enable gates (preregistered, before ANY default-enable):** long-context parity budgets — per-profile logit metric vectors and greedy-token agreement at admitted long contexts (at least one ≥8K and one ≥32K point on hosts whose memory certificate admits them) — plus preregistered task-quality budgets on the locked eval sets, plus a measured bandwidth/latency effect that includes the added scale traffic. Until every gate is green the mode is explicit opt-in and documented as such.

## Constraints
- Quantized-KV claims are profile-scoped and preregistered; the mode never inherits a bf16 token-identity claim (doctrine #1). Any accepted divergence gets a docs/DISCREPANCIES.md entry whose rollback mechanism is the runtime switch itself.
- Scale overhead counted in every claim, admission term, and receipt (§6.8); scales live in SoA next to the slabs with 64-byte alignment.
- Leaf kernels never spawn; no Rayon in the release graph; allowlist deps only; unsafe only within enumerated SIMD islands if the dequant-scan vectorizes; G1 > G2.
- Determinism scoped per doctrine #9: the int8-KV path has its own fixed quant/dequant order; batch-M equals batch-1 token-exactly within the mode.

## Evidence / gates
- Accounting fixture: structural bytes computed by admission equal the constants above (88 KiB payload; 2,816 B f32 / 1,408 B f16 scales; measured padding/page-table terms) for representative context lengths — cross-checked against the slab allocator's certificate terms.
- Long-context parity run: bf16-KV vs int8-KV taps per (loop, layer, KV head, position window) under the named budgets; greedy agreement measured, flips (if accepted) preregistered and fixtured.
- Task-budget scorecard on the locked eval sets with recipe id + profile + KV dtype named.
- PERF_LEDGER rows: tokens/s and bytes/token with scale traffic included, per host; NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE if the mode loses. Close cites accounting fixture + parity/task runs (or the honest opt-in-only disposition with gates recorded as not-yet-green).

## Tests
- Unit: per-(loop-layer, KV head, token) scale computation and placement; quant/dequant round-trip error bound per the declared scheme; accounting arithmetic goldens (2,816 = 44×8×2×4; 1,408 f16 halving); mode-fixed-at-admission enforcement; ExecutionIdentity dtype inclusion.
- Property/fuzz: random K/V streams → write/read round-trip within the declared quant error; admission never undercounts actual allocated bytes (allocator cross-check); fork/COW tails preserve dtype and refcounts; seed-reproducible.
- E2E: synthetic long-context decode with mode on/off — DETAILED LOGGING of per-slot dequant taps, scale values, accounting terms, and per-position score deltas; real-artifact long-context runs are model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; the no-model synthetic path always runs. Named artifact: `tests/e2e_kv_int8_longcontext.rs` — the on/off differential harness whose logs carry per-stage timestamps, per-(loop-layer, KV head) byte counts, accounting expected-vs-actual (payload/scale/padding/page-table terms), and a final machine-parseable summary line.

## Dependencies & rationale
- [4A] KV slab allocator (franken_nlp-mki): owns the page/slab geometry and already carries int8-KV structural accounting ("later recipe stage" there — this bead IS that stage's runtime realization); the mode writes into its slabs and must match its certificate terms.
- [P3] native GQA attention (franken_nlp-dsr): the prefill/decode attention kernels are the consumers — dequant-in-scan rides their fixed reduction order and page-scan contract.

title: [P3] Run team-width sweep + NUMA three-policy placement experiments behind ratified-surface gate
description:
## Background
franken_nlp runs exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF revision f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d: 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 logical layer executions per token; KV slot = layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; SwiGLU 10752. Plan §6.13: many-core scaling has TWO axes that are never blindly mixed — latency (parallelize within one forward: row-blocks of each GEMM/GEMV across the admitted team) and throughput (parallelism inside the batched GEMMs; NEVER N concurrent independent forwards creating competing teams). NUMA/topology/QoS facilities are usable ONLY through a ratified safe FrankenSuite surface (AGENTS.md: no `libc`/`sysinfo` reach-through, no new unsafe island); until that surface exists the experiments stay off and the flags reject honestly.

## Contract
- **Team-width sweep (no ratified surface required):** a reproducible 1..available-width sweep per (host, regime) that directly selects the SMALLEST team width within the confidence interval of peak throughput/latency. Decode at batch 1 stops scaling at bandwidth/coordination saturation — the sweep finds where, it never guesses. Physical-core/topology labels are used only when the safe resource probe established them; otherwise results say "logical/effective width". A USL fit may summarize the curve and flag contention but NEVER extrapolates a dispatch cap beyond measured points. No guessed "8–16" default enters code; the selected width lands as a measured dispatch/EngineResources input.
- **NUMA three-policy comparison (multi-CCD/multi-socket TR/EPYC; gated on the ratified surface):** compare explicitly — (a) bind workers+KV to one node and accept fewer cores; (b) interleave shared weights; (c) replicate read-only packed weights per node when the memory budget permits. Facts the design must respect: "local" without worker restriction causes remote reads; replication can double a multi-GB packed-weight footprint, so admission includes the chosen placement (the replicated-weight residency term in the memory certificate); per-node batch shards avoid cross-node writable state and merge only ordered results (per-row reduction order preserved).
- **Fail-honest until ratified:** `FNLP_NUMA` (and any placement flag) REJECTS non-portable modes with a typed error naming the missing ratified surface — never pretending a standard thread was pinned.
- **Apple P/E:** macOS offers NO hard thread-affinity API, so "pin to P-cores" is not a portable guarantee. QoS is a measured optional experiment only through a ratified safe asupersync scheduling-policy surface; otherwise the portable no-QoS scoped team is the only route. `robot backends` reports requested versus OBSERVED effective placement in both cases.
- Every experiment retains the portable fallback (no-placement scoped team) and leaves the G3 no-foreign-runtime claim unchanged.

## Constraints
- Ratified-surface gate is absolute: without the safe FrankenSuite topology/placement (or asupersync QoS) surface, the corresponding experiment does not run and its flag rejects typed; the gate-closed state is a recordable outcome, not a silent skip.
- Two-axes doctrine: sweeps and placements never create competing teams; one admitted `scoped_cpu` region owns the width being measured; the aggregate thread envelope (runtime workers + blocking coordinators + scoped children + ratified helpers) stays certified.
- Doctrine #24: transient NUMA/page-cache observations are not machine constants — placement selections are validity-domain keyed and expire with topology/firmware changes; `fnlp tune` consumes them under its own hysteresis rules.
- Measured-faster wins; every kept placement/width cites its trials; losers ledgered. No Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; no new unsafe islands.

## Evidence / gates
- Sweep evidence: per-host width-vs-throughput/latency curves with confidence intervals, the selected smallest-within-CI width, and the USL fit (labeled diagnostic) in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.
- Placement evidence: three-policy comparison rows (throughput, latency percentiles, remote-read counters where the surface exposes them, footprint deltas including replication) — OR the recorded BLOCKED-on-surface disposition with the FNLP_NUMA typed-rejection test green. Both are honest closes; a placement claim without the ratified surface is not.
- `robot backends` fixture showing requested-vs-observed placement fields populated on macOS (QoS absent → portable route reported) and Linux.
- Admission fixture: replicated-weight residency term appears in the memory certificate exactly when policy (c) is selected.

## Tests
- Unit: smallest-width-within-CI selection arithmetic on synthetic curves (plateau, knee, noisy-flat cases); FNLP_NUMA mode parsing with typed rejection per missing surface; USL-fit no-extrapolation guard (query beyond max measured width refuses).
- Property: sweep determinism given fixed measurement fixtures (same input curve → same selection); ordered per-node shard merge equals single-node result bit-exactly on synthetic integer workloads regardless of shard count.
- E2E: real sweep on at least one multi-core host over the synthetic fixed-shape GEMM workload with DETAILED LOGGING per width (width, observed placement, p50/p95/p99, counter values or "unavailable", thermal state); model-artifact forward sweeps are model-gated → SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; placement E2E runs only where the ratified surface exists and otherwise asserts the typed rejection path.

## Dependencies & rationale
- [P3] prepacked tiled GEMM (franken_nlp-53o): the sweep and every placement policy execute this workload; sweeping a placeholder kernel would measure nothing durable.
- [4A] EngineResources broker (franken_nlp-t4d): team formation, the aggregate thread envelope, and the memory-certificate terms (including replicated-weight residency) are its authority; widths/placements are inputs to it, not side channels around it.
- [P0] PLATFORM_SURFACES registry (franken_nlp-7el): defines per-target what a "ratified safe surface" IS and records topology/QoS facility status — the gate this bead's placement half opens against.

title: [P0] Land frankentorch no-Rayon leaf surface: serial/range leaves, no-spawn proof, release-graph gate
description:
## Background
The release dependency graph of franken_nlp (the one-model wedge: Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops, KV slot = layer + loop×22 → 44 slots; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT (q 3072→6144); vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) must contain NO Rayon — not merely no direct dependency — because Rayon would install a second ambient scheduler beside the asupersync-owned CPU teams. At the inspected frankentorch pin (523aaf82…), `ft-kernel-cpu` makes Rayon an UNCONDITIONAL dependency and routes many public entrypoints through its global pool. The dependency-policy test bead enforces/blocks on this state ("until the frankentorch no-Rayon leaf surface lands, the test pins the exact current violation as a known-blocked entry that FAILS release builds"); THIS bead does the landing. Setting `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` is explicitly NOT a production ownership proof.

## Contract
- Make the required frankentorch leaf surface consumable with zero Rayon in the franken_nlp release feature graph, by exactly one of: (a) upstreaming a no-Rayon serial/range-leaf feature to `ft-kernel-cpu` at a new reviewed pin; or (b) an equivalently narrow pinned FrankenSuite leaf crate/surface exposing only the needed serial/tile leaf functions. The needed leaf set (ADOPT/ADAPT rows): `linear_int8_dynamic_f32` (scalar/SDOT/VNNI baseline), `linear_int8_dynamic_prepacked_f32` (SDOT experiments), `rms_norm_forward_f32`, `sdpa_forward_f32` (dense reference), softmax/SiLU/matmul/argmax primitives, `quantize_per_output_channel_i8`.
- The exposed leaves have exact tile/range ownership and NO internal spawning: a leaf call cannot create a thread, task, or pool job; intra-op parallelism remains owned by the caller's asupersync scoped team.
- Existing Rayon-backed entrypoints may remain as development / out-of-process reference baselines only; they must be feature-partitioned so the release graph never selects them.
- The chosen route is recorded as a `SUITE.lock` decision at exact revisions (with any required root `[patch]` entries mirrored into `SUITE_ROOT_PATCHES.lock`); consuming an unreviewed floating branch is forbidden.
- Deliverable proof: `cargo tree -e features` and the metadata graph walk over the RELEASE feature graph contain no `rayon`/`rayon-core` node anywhere (transitive included), and the dependency-policy test's known-blocked entry is removed rather than suppressed.

## Constraints
Deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; Rayon banned from the ENTIRE release graph (stricter than direct-dep bans); leaf kernels never spawn; G1>G2 profile-scoped; deny-not-forbid unsafe (no new unsafe here); suite upgrades are explicit plan-revision events, never side effects; benchmark/oracle tooling may keep Rayon only OUTSIDE the release dependency graph.

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: (a) release-graph no-Rayon assertion green in `scripts/check.sh` CI with the known-blocked entry deleted; (b) a no-spawn proof test — calling every exposed leaf under a thread-count watchdog shows zero thread/pool creation (process thread inventory unchanged before/after); (c) `SUITE.lock` + `SUITE_ROOT_PATCHES.lock` updated at the new pin and cross-checked against `cargo metadata`/`Cargo.lock`; (d) Phase-0 exit item "no-Rayon release graph/leaf-kernel path" ratified in its G0 ADR. Recorded in the ADR registry and the dependency-policy test fixtures.

## Tests
Unit: feature-matrix compile tests — release features build the leaf surface; dev-only features gate every Rayon-backed entrypoint. Integration: no-spawn watchdog over each leaf (spawn count == 0, logged per leaf with thread ids); `cargo tree` snapshot test over the release graph (golden, diff-reviewed). E2E: `scripts/check.sh` passes with the no-Rayon assertion in enforcing mode; a deliberate re-introduction of the Rayon edge in a scratch branch fails CI loudly (negative fixture). Detailed logging: the policy test prints the offending dependency path on any failure. Model-gated: none required (no weights involved). Named artifacts: `tests/no_spawn_leaves.rs` (thread-inventory watchdog per leaf, logging leaf name + before/after thread ids), the committed release-graph golden at `tests/fixtures/release_graph.golden` (diff-reviewed snapshot), and the scripts/check.sh no-Rayon section; the watchdog ends with `NO_SPAWN RESULT=PASS|FAIL leaves=<n> spawns=<0|list>`.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-b2p: SUITE.lock/SUITE_ROOT_PATCHES.lock tooling must exist to record the new pin/patch closure this bead selects.
- A_G0_SEAM (cross-epic want): the spawn_blocking→scoped_cpu probe defines the exact leaf-call ownership contract the no-spawn proof must satisfy.

title: [P2] Run OQ-31 independent .fnlpq envelope design review before writer/reader freeze
description:
## Background
OQ-31 requires an independent review of the `.fnlpq` on-disk envelope design BEFORE the format freezes, because every later surface (converter, loader, packer, pull, receipts) inherits its decisions. The container serves exactly one model — Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d (22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half; 201 tensors; bf16 logical payload 8,339,601,408 bytes). Draft envelope: 8-byte magic `b"FNLPQ\0\0\x01"`, u32 format_version/required_flags, u64 header_len/section_count/tensor_count/file_len, header_sha256 [u8;32], canonical hash-checked header JSON, ordered binary sections (tensor bytes + scales/row-sums, exact tokenizer.model bytes, tokenizer/config/template source bytes, Apache-2.0 + attribution + modification-notice bundle). This bead is the review deliverable itself — a design gate, not the writer/reader implementation.

## Contract
Produce a written, ratified review record that settles, with named alternatives and reasons-killed:
- **Canonical-header-JSON vs binary-directory authority tradeoff**: confirm or amend "prelude/header/section table is the authority for ranges; JSON never carries raw binary; no base64".
- **Digest-domain taxonomy** (normative names, each with domain framing): `source_root_sha256` · `logical_model_sha256` (domain-framed over ordered logical tensor (name,dtype,shape,canonical logical bytes) records + exact materialized config/tokenizer/template identities; retires the ambiguous `semantic_digest`) · `packing_set_sha256` · `license_bundle_sha256` (legal identity, never model semantics) · `fnlpq_file_sha256` · `release_manifest_sha256`. Verify native repacking changes file/packing digests but never `logical_model_sha256`, and a notice-only correction changes only license/file/release identities.
- **Duplicate-key policy**: duplicate JSON keys, duplicate tensor/section names, and duplicate required section kinds all reject; one pinned UTF-8 escape form; NaN/Inf reject; floating scales live in binary sections with fixed IEEE-bit encoding, never JSON numbers.
- **Packing-set multiplicity**: a PackingSet may hold multiple representations only with explicit duplicate byte cost; dispatch may select only installed representations; arch mismatch is a hard error naming the required derivation, never silent fallback.
- **Malformed-file limits**: prelude validated before ANY variable allocation; `file_len` equals actual regular-file length; `header_len` under a compile-time cap with checked `prelude_len + header_len`; caps on section/tensor count, rank, dimensions, header/config/template/tokenizer/license size, total mapped bytes; unknown required flags/enums reject (no best-effort parse of newer formats); u64 range checks, no overlap, only declared zero-filled alignment gaps.
- Output: an ADR-style record (decision, evidence, killed alternatives) plus the frozen field-by-field envelope spec the writer/reader beads implement; any change it forces is a plan-revision event, not a code tweak.

## Constraints
The review is independent: performed against the §5.2 spec text and hostile-input reasoning, not against a half-built implementation it would rubber-stamp; three-family dependency allowlist unaffected (no new deps for the format — no compression in v1, no base64, no Unicode-normalization library; authority-bearing names restricted to printable-ASCII grammars); G1>G2; license bundle bytes are legal identity only.

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: the ratified review record committed to the ADR/G0-style registry with evidence digests; the frozen envelope spec versioned and referenced by the writer and reader beads; a checklist showing each of the five OQ-31 clauses (authority tradeoff, digest taxonomy, duplicate-key policy, packing multiplicity, malformed limits) explicitly resolved with at least one named killed alternative each. OQ-31 flips OPEN → resolved in the research-decision register.

## Tests
This design bead lands fixtures for its successors rather than code: a golden field-inventory table (every prelude/header field, size, endianness, cap) the writer's golden serializer fixture must cover; a hostile-case checklist (truncated prelude, header_len overflow, overlapping sections, duplicate section kind, unknown required flag, wrong file_len, NaN scale, duplicate tensor name) that the reader's fuzz corpus must include — each case named here so absence in the implementing beads is detectable. Logging requirement forwarded: reader/writer must name the exact failing field/range in every rejection. Named fixture deliverables (concrete files the successor beads consume): `tests/fixtures/fnlpq/field_inventory.json` (the golden field-inventory table: every prelude/header field with offset, size, endianness, cap) and `tests/fixtures/fnlpq/hostile_cases.json` (the hostile-case checklist, one stable id per case) — both referenced by id from the writer/reader suites so a coverage gap is mechanically detectable, not a prose omission.

## Dependencies & rationale
- None upstream: the review consumes the plan's §5.2 draft and can start immediately; it must FINISH before the writer/reader freeze (wired as their blocker, not vice versa).
close_reason: Batch-verified: OQ-31 envelope review frozen (commit c2af23c); field_inventory.json + hostile_cases.json fixtures present per bead contract

title: [4A] Implement typed RequestBudget: meet-composed stage budgets, semantic counters, reserved cleanup
description:
## Background
Every pipeline stage (resolve → load → tokenize → grammar compile → prefill → decode → detokenize/parse → postprocess → emit) of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22; final RMSNorm after EACH pass; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half) receives a typed child `RequestBudget`. The G0 census bead ratifies the mapping from project units to pinned asupersync `Budget`/`CapabilityBudget` units; the EngineResources bead owns the process host and memory ledger. NOBODY yet implements the RequestBudget type itself and its stage plumbing — this bead does.

## Contract
- **Typed `RequestBudget`** combining: the pinned asupersync `Budget` dimensions (absolute deadline, poll quota, cost quota) + `CapabilityBudget` dimensions (memory bytes, CPU units, IO bytes, cleanup budget, evidence-artifact bytes) + engine-owned semantic counters (input/output tokens, grammar states, KV pages, batch rows, emitted bytes).
- **Monotone meet composition**: a child budget is the meet with its parent and may ONLY tighten; widening is a compile/construction error, property-tested.
- **Fail-closed**: required missing or exhausted dimensions fail BEFORE allocation with the typed budget/timeout error (exit code 5 at the CLI boundary; `Timeout`/`Deadline`/`PollQuota`/`CostBudget` CancelKinds map to 5).
- **Reserved cleanup**: cancellation drains through a separately reserved NONZERO cleanup budget; the last unit cannot be consumed in a way that strands obligations.
- **No ambient env reads**: the library never reads process environment; the CLI snapshots `FNLP_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS` once into `NlpEngineBuilder`; embedders set the same field directly. Milliseconds alone are NOT a complete resource budget — the frozen unit mapping from the G0 probe is authoritative.
- **Per-stage declarations**: each long stage declares its maximum uninterruptible work quantum and checkpoint cadence (named tile, per-doc, prefill-morsel, per-decode-step boundaries); these declarations are the data the p50/p95/p99 cancellation-observation-latency gauntlet measures against.
- Budgets thread through the two cost centers (prefill = compute-bound, decode = memory-bound) without merging them: per-stage accounting stays distinct per regime.

## Constraints
Library reads no ambient environment (one-time CLI `FNLP_*` snapshot only); budgets are meet-monotone, never widened by a child; cleanup reserve is mandatory; no Rayon anywhere in the release graph; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; asupersync budget semantics used exactly as ratified at the pin (no overclaiming unratified dimensions — absent facilities use the recorded hand-rolled fallback); G1>G2.

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: (a) meet-monotonicity property suite green (child ≤ parent in every dimension, widening rejected); (b) fail-closed fixtures green for each dimension (deadline, poll, cost, memory, IO, tokens, grammar states, KV pages, batch rows, emitted bytes); (c) cleanup-reserve drain fixture: cancellation during each stage still completes drain within the reserved cleanup budget; (d) env-hygiene test: library call paths perform zero env reads (audited), CLI snapshot happens exactly once; (e) stage-quantum declarations exist for every long stage and are exported to the receipts/telemetry envelope for the gauntlet's cancellation-latency measurement.

## Tests
Unit: meet arithmetic per dimension including saturation/zero; `FNLP_STAGE_BUDGET_<STAGE>_MS` parsing (unknown stage names reject); missing-required-dimension typed errors. Property: random budget trees — every path from root to leaf is monotonically tightening; exhaustion at any node fails before its stage allocates (allocation-count hook). Fuzz: hostile budget values (0, u64::MAX, conflicting deadline/cost) never panic, always typed. E2E: a CLI run with a tiny stage budget exits 5 with the stage named in the diagnostic envelope; cancellation mid-prefill drains within the cleanup reserve and emits the CancelKind chain (model-gated variants report SKIPPED_NO_MODEL). Detailed logging: per-stage budget snapshot + consumption at debug level, volatile fields excluded from canonical output.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-t4d: the EngineResources host provides the process ceilings and two-phase memory ledger that request budgets tighten against.
- A_G0_CENSUS (cross-epic want): the OQ-35 census freezes the project-unit → asupersync Budget/CapabilityBudget mapping and the obligation/cleanup semantics this type encodes.

title: [4A] Implement decode.rs: frozen DecodeParams/DecodeOutput, AR decode loop, streaming hooks
description:
## Background
`src/native_engine/decode.rs` is the module the repository shape assigns the frozen `DecodeParams`/`DecodeOutput` contract, the autoregressive decode loop, and the streaming hooks. Around it everything already has owners — the loop runner (44 slots via layer + loop×22, final RMSNorm after EACH pass), the reference forwards, the sampler (fused greedy in lmhead.rs, seeded draws), the execution compiler, and the generate/chat CLI — but no bead owns the engine-side AR loop that ties them together for the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head → f32 logit vector 664,576 bytes; KV 176 KiB/token bf16 across 44 slots; SwiGLU 10752; RoPE θ=7e7 split-half). This bead builds it.

## Contract
- **Frozen `DecodeParams`**: max new tokens, stop policy (EOS ids, stop sequences, min-length), sampling mode (greedy default | seeded sampling per the addressable-sampler contract), thinking budget hook, logprob-capture request, per-request numerics profile — serde types shared by CLI, library, and NDJSON per the shared-request-types rule. `DecodeOutput`: emitted token ids + decoded bytes, finish reason (stop | eos | budget | cancelled | no-result), optional per-token logprobs (only when the required projection was actually computed), deterministic token counts, and the score-space/normalization fields when scoring surfaces use it. Task finalizers consume exactly this type; freezing it is what lets the Task trait's `finalize(&req, &plan, raw: DecodeOutput, validator)` stay stable.
- **AR loop**: per step — forward next position through the two-loop runner (KV append at all 44 slots), apply the complete ordered logit-processor stack and grammar mask AND via the sampler/execution-compiler primitives, select token, update processor state (penalty windows update for forced tokens too), check stop policy, checkpoint cancellation at EVERY decode step (a declared maximum uninterruptible quantum of one step's work).
- **Streaming hooks**: a bounded, two-phase (reserve→permit) callback/channel surface emitting per-token events that the CLI maps to NDJSON `token` lines with `schema_version` + `request_seq`; no user callback runs while an engine/admission lock is held; a cancelled sender cannot half-deliver.
- **Budget/cancellation integration**: the loop consumes the typed request budget (output-token and emitted-byte counters decrement per step); exhaustion yields finish reason budget (exit 5 at the CLI), cancellation yields the CancelKind chain (exit 6), and a missing mandatory thinking close delimiter yields typed no-result (exit 10) — never a truncated object as success.
- Decode is one of the two profiled cost centers (memory-bound; prefill is the other) and stays separately attributable in telemetry.

## Constraints
Streaming callbacks never run under an engine lock; reserve→permit discipline for every emission (a held permit is an obligation, never carried across an unrelated await); forced tokens ≠ forced bytes (byte-level jump-forward/token healing excluded from the exact path); greedy has no RANDOM authority; per-row reduction order preserved regardless of batch composition; no Rayon; leaf kernels never spawn; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; G1>G2 profile-scoped.

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: (a) the L4 harness driving greedy decode through THIS loop reproduces the oracle-reproducible prefixes exactly under `hf-bf16-eager`; (b) stop-policy fixture matrix (EOS, multi-byte stop sequences straddling token boundaries, min-length suppression, max-token budget) green; (c) streaming ≡ non-streaming byte equality for identical requests (the hook adds no semantic difference); (d) cancellation-at-every-step fixture: cancelling between any two steps loses no committed tokens and emits the correct finish reason; (e) DecodeParams/DecodeOutput schema goldens frozen (diff-reviewed changes only) since downstream task envelopes embed them.

## Tests
Unit: stop-sequence matching across token boundaries (UTF-8 multi-byte splits included); finish-reason mapping table; logprob fields absent unless projection ran. Property: for random stop/budget configs, emitted tokens are a prefix of the unconstrained greedy stream and the finish reason is consistent with the first triggered condition. Fuzz: hostile stop sequences (empty, overlapping, giant) never panic; streaming consumer that stalls exercises bounded backpressure, never unbounded buffering. E2E: `fnlp generate` streams NDJSON token events whose concatenation equals the final text (model-gated: SKIPPED_NO_MODEL; scalar spec engine covers loop structure in CI). Detailed logging: per-step token id, processor-state deltas, budget counters at trace level.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-9tz: the sampler + fused greedy path is the per-step selection primitive this loop invokes.
- A_FWD (cross-epic want): the reference forward pass (embed → 22×2 with KV append → lm_head) is the compute body of each step.

title: [P3] Run R0 load-mode experiment: cold/warm owned-vs-mmap, hostile matrix, gated load_mode=auto
description:
## Background
For a 4+ GB artifact of the one-model wedge (Nanbeige4.2-3B at HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; bf16 payload 8,339,601,408 bytes; int8-everything ≈4.7 GB with bf16 embed; 22×2 loops → 44 KV slots; head_dim 128; vocab 166,144), load/hash/page-fault behavior can dominate one-shot CLI usage even when steady-state decode is excellent. The plan defines regime R0 (cold/warm startup: process start → manifest/census ready → model ready → first token) measured under cold AND warm filesystem cache and under owned versus mmap loading, and permits Phase 3 to promote `load_mode=auto` — content-addressed immutable INSTALLED artifacts opened via the read-only mmap island, locally converted or untrusted artifacts staying owned — only after measurements and hostile-file tests. The reader bead ships the opt-in `FNLP_MMAP=1` island; nobody owns the R0 measurement + promotion decision. This bead does.

## Contract
- **R0 harness rows** per (host fingerprint, artifact recipe, packing set, load mode, cache state): process start → manifest/census ready → model ready → first token, cold filesystem cache (measured with an explicit documented cache-drop procedure per OS, or labeled warm-only where no approved procedure exists) and warm cache, owned buffer vs `FNLP_MMAP=1`. Report p50/p95/p99 across randomized interleaved trials; single-shot usability is never inferred from steady-state tok/s.
- **R1 interaction**: decode-throughput deltas under mmap (page-fault-driven first-loop touch of the packed weights — both loop passes touch the same 201-tensor working set) are measured, not assumed.
- **Hostile/durability matrix under mmap** (promotion precondition): truncation/replacement of the mapped file mid-run, bit-rot (checksum-valid-at-open, corrupted-later), cancellation during first-touch, hostile-local-file cases from the reader's corpus — each fails loudly/typed, never UB; mapping range/lifetime/immutability proofs from the reader island are re-exercised under the auto policy.
- **Promotion decision**: `load_mode=auto` (installed content-addressed artifacts → read-only mmap where the reviewed platform surface exists; converted/untrusted → owned) may be promoted ONLY if the measured R0/R1 evidence clears the keep-gate; otherwise the default stays owned and the negative result is ledgered. Either way the decision, its validity domain (host classes, OS families), and the exact CLI/builder mapping (`FNLP_LOAD_MODE` CLI-mapped; library takes an explicit builder field) are recorded.
- Prefetch advice / huge pages stay OUT: separate experiments gated on a ratified safe FrankenSuite OS surface; absent that surface they remain off rather than reaching through to libc.

## Constraints
Measured-faster wins — capability is not routing; one lever at a time with keep/revert and NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE on a loss; mmap stays an enumerated audited unsafe island (deny-not-forbid elsewhere); no new dependencies (no memmap2 crate — the island uses the already-approved surface); G3 unchanged (no foreign ML runtime); the G1 census + logical-model digest check still runs on load in every mode; deps only clap/serde/serde_json/sha2 + pinned FrankenSuite; no Rayon.

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: (a) R0 distribution tables committed to docs/PERF_LEDGER.md keyed by (host, recipe, packing, load mode, cache state) with the exact commands/env; (b) hostile-file matrix green under mmap (each case typed, named, logged); (c) either a promotion entry (auto default + validity domain + rollback = set owned mode) or a NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE entry retaining owned default — both with the full A/B data; (d) `robot health`/receipts report the effective load mode so R0 claims stay attributable.

## Tests
Unit: load-mode selection logic (installed content-addressed → auto candidate; converted/untrusted → owned; explicit flag always wins); refusal when the platform mmap surface is absent. Integration: truncation/replacement/bit-rot/cancellation injections under mmap return typed integrity errors and never touch freed mappings (island tests re-run under auto policy). Bench: R0 harness produces stable JSON rows consumed by the ledger; warm/cold labeling is explicit in every row. Named entrypoint: `scripts/e2e_r0_load_mode.sh` — runs the (load mode × cache state) grid, logging per-phase timestamps (process start / manifest+census ready / model ready / first token), bytes mapped-or-read with digests at each verification point, expected-vs-actual on any integrity failure, and a final machine-parseable `E2E_SUMMARY` line; model-gated legs print SKIPPED_NO_MODEL. E2E (model-gated, SKIPPED_NO_MODEL otherwise): full pull→load→first-token timing in both modes on at least one aarch64 and one x86-64 host. Detailed logging: per-phase timestamps (manifest/census/model/first-token) at info level in the telemetry envelope only.

## Dependencies & rationale
- franken_nlp-i9p: the R1 gauntlet harness supplies the randomized paired A/B methodology, warmup/thermal discipline, and bench-history ratchet this experiment reuses.
- A_FMT_R (cross-epic want): the checked reader + opt-in mmap island (range/lifetime/immutability proofs, hostile corpus) is the mechanism being measured and promoted.

title: [P5] Audit pinned llama.cpp GGUF tensor mapping and quant tiers as int4 recipe prior (OQ-12)
description:
## Background
OQ-12 (state OPEN; authority "quant prior, not f32 forward"): audit the tested official `llama.cpp` GGUF conversion for Nanbeige4.2-3B — tensor mapping and quant-tier assignments — and trace its lineage to the authors' historical `nanbeige42` fork, so the K-quant `_M`-class recipe lineage can seed OUR int4 allocation hypotheses without ever becoming authority. The model is the one-model wedge (HF rev f56ec5a9650268aa098496734743c25ea778bd2d; 201 tensors; 22 physical layers × 2 loops → 44 KV slots via layer + loop×22 — so every quantized tensor is reused in BOTH passes and sensitivity interactions are joint; head_dim 128 EXPLICIT; vocab 166,144; untied lm_head; SwiGLU 10752). The truth-pack bead pins the llama.cpp revisions; nobody owns the audit itself. Because the GGUF lineage is [REPORTED] evidence with no published per-tensor sensitivity for this architecture, its only legitimate role is hypothesis seeding for the int4/AA-Q1 search.

## Contract
- **Tensor-mapping table**: for the pinned post-support official `llama.cpp` revision (≥ b77d646…), record how each of the 201 census tensors maps into the GGUF conversion (name mapping, any transposes/merges, which tensors are quantized vs kept high precision) — diffed against our census generator's inventory; any GGUF-side tensor with no census counterpart (or vice versa) is a named finding, not silently dropped.
- **Quant-tier table**: per tensor class (embed, norms, q/k/v/o, gate/up/down, lm_head), the tier each relevant preset assigns (Q8_0-class and the Q4_K_M-class `_M` family), including any layer-position-dependent tiering (early/late layers, `down_proj` upgrades) — the exact patterns §5.5 names as hypotheses.
- **Lineage trace**: document the relationship between the official support commit and the authors' `nanbeige42` fork (historical lineage check, NOT an independent vote); note divergences relevant to tensor mapping/tiers.
- **Prior extraction**: a short machine-readable hypotheses file (candidate tensors/classes for higher precision, with the GGUF-lineage evidence pointer per hypothesis) consumable by the int4 baseline and AA-Q1 allocation beads as SEARCH SEEDS ONLY.
- **Explicit non-authority statement** carried in the record: GGUF tiers are a census/prior; our recipe decisions come from held-out task metrics on complete candidate artifacts; nearest-format gauntlet rows (our int8 vs Q8_0 class) are named peers, never "matched quantization".

## Constraints
No llama.cpp code or dependency crosses into the repository (out-of-tree tooling only); the GPL-3.0 rlx differential stays out-of-tree and is not part of this audit; [REPORTED] evidence is labeled as such and never promoted to recipe authority; one-at-a-time tensor curves and inherited `_M` patterns remain hypotheses because the two-loop reuse makes sensitivity joint; deps unchanged (audit artifacts are docs/JSON in the truth-pack style); G1>G2.

## Evidence / gates
Closes on: (a) the mapping + tier tables committed with the exact llama.cpp commit, conversion command, and GGUF file digest(s) recorded; (b) the census diff green (or findings filed); (c) the lineage note with commit ids for both official and fork; (d) the hypotheses file referenced by the int4/AA-Q1 beads' search manifests; (e) OQ-12 flips OPEN → resolved in the research-decision register with this record as evidence.

## Tests
The audit record is validated mechanically: schema-checked JSON (duplicate-key-rejecting parse) for the mapping/tier/hypotheses files; a cross-check script asserting every census tensor name appears exactly once in the mapping table; CI drift guard — if the pinned llama.cpp revision or census digest changes, the record is flagged stale and must be re-ratified (never silently trusted). Logging: the audit tooling prints per-tensor mapping decisions so a reviewer can spot-check against the upstream source.

## Dependencies & rationale
- A_CENSUS (cross-epic want): the 201-tensor census generator provides the authoritative tensor inventory the GGUF mapping is diffed against.
